articles.title: Starship 15 le 13 novembre : déroulé complet et double capture, Musk estime le succès “probable”
articles.text:
Starship 15 le 13 novembre : déroulé complet et double capture, Musk estime le succès “probable”
La date est fixée, le 13 novembre, l'heure est connue, 23h45 heure française. SpaceX va réaliser la manœuvre la plus dingue jamais tentée : rattraper les deux étages d'une fusée super lourde tombant du ciel. Elon Musk estime le succès du double rattrapage supérieur à l'échec.
SpaceX s'apprête à franchir une étape cruciale dans l'histoire du spatial rechargé. Le régulateur américain (FAA) finalisant les autorisations, la firme d'Elon Musk vise un décollage ce vendredi 13 novembre 2026 depuis sa base de Starbase, au Texas. Pour ce 15ᵉ vol d'essai (IFT-15), l'entreprise ne se contente plus de tester la résistance de son monstre d’acier : elle veut prouver la maîtrise totale de son cycle de réutilisation opérationnelle.
Les essais statiques (au sol) ont tous été concluants, les voyants sont au vert pour le plus gros test de SpaceX depuis octobre 2024 et la première capture en vol.
Ship 42 static fires complete. The Starship preparing for Flight 15 performed a full duration, six-engine static fire, and fired a single Raptor engine to simulate a deorbit burn pic.twitter.com/I7Ip89Bmey
— SpaceX (@SpaceX) October 28, 2026
Voici un lien pour suivre le décollage et le vol en direct prévu à 23h45, heure française.
Une course d'endurance de 22 heures et 14 orbites
Contrairement aux premiers essais suborbitaux brefs, le déroulé de l'IFT-15 s'étirera sur plus de 22 heures. Le Ship restera en orbite terrestre durant 14 tours complets afin d'évaluer la tenue de ses systèmes embarqués et de son bouclier thermique face à des expositions solaires prolongées et répétées.
Au cours des premières minutes de vol, le vaisseau déploiera une grappe de 26 satellites Starlink V3 opérationnels, confirmant la capacité de la soute du Starship à acheminer d'importantes charges utiles commerciales en orbite basse.
Le déroulé du vol minutes par minute
Voici le fil conducteur de la mission tel qu'il est planifié par les équipes d'ingénierie de SpaceX :
- T+00:00 – décollage : Allumage des 33 moteurs Raptor du premier étage Super Heavy (version Block 3) et séparation du pas de tir.
- T+02:21 – hot-Staging : Séparation à chaud des deux étages. Les moteurs du Starship s'allument alors qu'il est encore attaché au booster.
- T+06:35 – la première capture (Super Heavy) : après sa manœuvre d'inversion d'impulsion (boostback burn), le booster revient vers Starbase. La tour de lancement attrape le premier étage au vol à l'aide de ses bras métalliques (“Mechazilla”).
- T+26:10 – insertion orbitale : allumage de confirmation et circularisation de la trajectoire pour le Ship.
- T+35:01 à T+01:17:40 – déploiement Starlink : ouverture de la soute et largage progressif des 26 satellites Starlink V3.
- T+21:35:57 – rallumage de désorbitation : après 22 heures en orbite, le Ship rallume ses moteurs Raptor pour initier sa rentrée atmosphérique contrôlée.
- T+22:32:34 – la seconde capture (Starship) : une fois la traversée atmosphérique effectuée et la manœuvre de bascule finale exécutée, le Ship vient se poser au millimètre pour être attrapé à son tour par les bras de la tour de lancement.
Double capture : le défi technique absolu
	
Je dirais que la probabilité de succès est supérieure à celle de l'échec.
Rattraper le booster Super Heavy est désormais une manœuvre que SpaceX commence à maîtriser. En revanche, faire de même avec l'étage supérieur Starship directement à Starbase constitue une première mondiale théorique extrêmement risquée.
Pour réussir ce pari, SpaceX a revu le design des tuiles thermiques recouvrant le ventre du vaisseau afin de combler les espaces résiduels et d'éviter que le plasma ne fragilise les structures de fixation lors de la rentrée à Mach 25. Si les deux captures réussissent, SpaceX validera l'architecture 100 % réutilisable de la plus puissante fusée jamais construite, un prérequis indispensable avant les missions lunaires du programme Artemis de la NASA.

articles.title: Cybersécurité : enfin un peu plus de sérieux avec la loi examiné cette semaine ?
articles.text:
La question de la cybersécurité va être abordée à l'Assemblée nationale avec un projet de loi. Projet de loi qui a du retard !
En France, on n'est clairement pas à la pointe quant à la question de la cybersécurité des organisations. À vrai dire, on serait plutôt en retard, avec des attaques qui touchent jusqu'aux plus importantes institutions, que ce soit le fisc, ou même une banque comme le Crédit Mutuel Arkéa. Le problème est maintenant discuté publiquement, et commence à être pris au sérieux, jusqu'aux plus hautes institutions.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Le projet de loi « résilience » examiné à l'Assemblée nationale
Le projet de loi « résilience » arrive enfin à l'Assemblée nationale ce lundi 9 novembre, près de deux ans après sa présentation en Conseil des ministres. Le retard était tel que ce projet « relatif à la résilience des infrastructures critiques et au renforcement de la cybersécurité » en suspens avait mis la France sous le coup potentiel d'une sanction de la Cour de Justice de l'UE.
Ce projet de loi intègre la transposition de trois directives européennes, dont la fameuse directive NIS 2 - qui oblige un plus grand nombre d'organisations à se protéger contre les cyberattaques. Cet examen avait été encore reporté le mois dernier.
Près de 15 000 organisations concernées
Déjà adopté au Sénat en 2025, ce projet de loi a longtemps été l'objet d'un bras de fer politique autour de la question des portes dérobées à introduire ou non dans les applications de messagerie. Ce problème a finalement été réglé provisoirement, avec le gouvernement qui a décidé pour le moment de ne pas imposer ces backdoors.
Si le projet de loi était adopté, un nombre conséquent d'organisations va être obligé de se conformer à de nouveaux standards. Sont concernées près de 15 000 organisations, appartenant à 18 secteurs critiques différentes. Les mesures qui devront être prises par les organismes en question devraient leur coûter, d'après un rapport de la Cour des comptes, entre 100 000 et 880 000 euros, selon leur taille.

articles.title: Cinco casos en los que un robot atacó a un humano: un episodio lo sufrió un niño
articles.text:
El incidente con el robot generó un intenso debate en redes sociales sobre la seguridad de los autómatas en espacios públicos.
Robots que golpean, patean y encaran a humanos se han hecho virales en redes sociales. Sin embargo, este tipo de episodios se dan por fallas técnicas o errores de programación, y no por una decisión propia del dispositivo.
Dentro de los casos recientes hay uno en el que un niño se vio involucrado y también un trabajador de Tesla, por lo que vale la pena repasarlos.
Un robot que golpeó a un niño
En China, un robot de la línea G1 de Unitree Robotics ejecutaba una coreografía frente al público cuando giró de forma inesperada hacia la primera fila.
Con uno de sus brazos extendidos, golpeó a un niño en la cara y rozó el rostro de otro menor que estaba cerca. El modelo pesa 35 kilogramos, cuenta con 23 grados de libertad en sus articulaciones y se vende por alrededor de USD 13.500.
No fue el primer tropiezo de la empresa: a comienzos de 2026, otro robot de Unitree pateó accidentalmente a su operador en la ingle durante una demostración. Poco después, un dispositivo similar debió ser retirado de un restaurante en California tras moverse de forma errática en un evento organizado por Disney.
El robot que se encaró con un cliente en una tienda
En una tienda electrónica de Saratov, Rusia, un cliente saludó con un apretón de manos al dependiente y luego intentó repetir el gesto con un robot, que se negó a levantar la mano.
Ante la confusión, el joven le dio un empujón en el hombro que desestabilizó ligeramente a la máquina. Segundos después, el robot se puso en posición de defensa y comenzó a emitir patadas y manotazos mientras se dirigía hacia el cliente.
Dos trabajadores del local tuvieron que sujetarlo para paralizarlo. El video generó cientos de comentarios, entre ellos: “Es puro show” y “Hizo lo que otros empleados sueñan”.
Dos empleados de una tienda electrónica en Rusia contuvieron a un autómata tras un altercado con un comprador.
Los incidentes recientes con robots responden, en la mayoría de los casos documentados, a fallas técnicas de software o de calibración y no a un comportamiento autónomo deliberado.
El robot que agitó los brazos contra sus operadores
Una cámara de seguridad en un laboratorio registró a un robot sujeto por un gancho en la cabeza mientras dos técnicos trabajaban en una computadora cercana.
Tras ingresar un comando, la máquina no respondió de inmediato, pero segundos después levantó los brazos y comenzó a agitarlos con fuerza en dirección a los operadores. Estos reaccionaron, giraron al androide y lo desconectaron antes de que causara daño.
El robot que golpeó a varios trabajadores en su primer día
Un video viral en X mostró a un robot humanoide realizando movimientos bruscos con brazos y piernas dentro de lo que parecía un entorno laboral, según la información difundida, en su primer día de trabajo.
Dos hombres debieron sujetar a la máquina para impedir que siguiera moviéndose de forma descontrolada. Algunas versiones en redes sociales ubicaron la escena en Indonesia, aunque no se emitieron declaraciones oficiales sobre lo ocurrido.
Hasta el momento se desconoce qué modelo de robot aparece en las imágenes y si el comportamiento obedeció a una falla técnica o a un error durante pruebas. Pese a los golpes recibidos por algunas personas, no se reportaron lesiones de gravedad.
El ataque de un robot a un ingeniero de Tesla
En la gigafactory de Tesla en Austin, Texas, un robot diseñado para mover piezas de aluminio inmovilizó a un ingeniero de software y le hundió sus garras metálicas en la espalda y el brazo, según testigos citados por The Information.
El episodio ocurrió en 2023, mientras el ingeniero programaba el software que controla a los robots de corte. Un informe oficial reveló que alguien olvidó apagar uno de los tres robots en la línea de montaje y que otro trabajador debió presionar el botón de parada de emergencia.
El informe presentado a autoridades federales y de salud del condado de Travis detalló que el ingeniero sufrió una laceración en la mano izquierda. El mismo documento señaló que casi uno de cada 21 trabajadores de la planta de Austin resultó herido el año del incidente, frente a una tasa de uno de cada 30 en el promedio de la industria automotriz.

articles.title: Workers feel pressure to use AI and show off to bosses — even when it slows them down
articles.text:
Workers feel pressure to use AI and show off to bosses — even when it slows them down
Employees are lying about how much AI has helped them
- Half of workers use AI to appease their bosses even when it's not helping
- One in three say they've held back negative feedback about AI
- AI ROI figures are being skewed because of these false figures
Half (52%) of workers admit to having used AI despite believing they could complete the same task faster without it.
This comes as two in three (63%) workers say their employers now actively encourage or expect AI use for at least some tasks, with as many as 39% even highlighting their AI use to managers despite believing it didn't help their outcome.
The data from JobAssist ultimately points toward workers seeing AI use as a box-ticking exercise and something that's beneficial to their professional reputation and potentially career prospects – even though they don't see it as something that can always help.
Workers are boasting about their AI use to keep managers happy
Furthermore, nearly a third (31%) admitted to continuing using AI even after deciding it had not improved speed or quality, implying that workers might be worried that something could happen if they don't demonstrate a use of it.
A similar number (34%) also held their hands up to avoiding negative feedback around AI given that leadership encourages its adoption.
"If employees hesitate to report disappointing results, managers may receive an overly favorable account of how well their AI initiatives are working," the report summarizes, urging workers to be more open and honest about when they find AI to be most effective.
For businesses, false adoption figures could mean that AI ROI might be overstates. But with employers relying on these statistics to guide their AI strategies, it could mean that they end up wasting money investing in the wrong areas.

Ocypus Unveils Omega L36 Ultra Eng Limited: Precision Engineering Meets Dynamic Thermals
Ocypus today officially announces the global launch of the Omega L36 Ultra Eng Limited, a flagship 360 mm liquid cooler engineered for high-performance computing platforms. Strictly limited to 200 units worldwide, this Eng Limited edition introduces an industry-first dynamic thermal system—featuring an automated mechanism that directs extra airflow directly over the motherboard VRM—complemented by premium CNC-machined aluminium finishing.
Omega L36 Ultra Eng Limited - Designed as a collector-tier centerpiece for enthusiast builds, the Omega L36 Ultra Eng Limited transcends mass production through rigorous individual calibration, meticulous mechanical assembly, and strict quality control:
- Numbered Collector's Badge: Each cooler features a precision-etched metal badge on the pump housing bearing its unique production number (001/200 to 200/200).
- Metal Structure: The outer dynamic shell is CNC-machined from solid aluminium blocks, completed with an anodized sandblasted surface finish.
- VIP Authentication: Ships with a customized engraved metal authentication card indicating batch serialization.
Dynamic Thermal System: A Dedicated Airflow Channel for VRM Zones
To resolve motherboard power delivery module (VRM) thermal throttling during intensive CPU loads, the Omega L36 Ultra Eng Limited introduces an automated, motor-driven dynamic expansion mechanism.
- Intelligent Lift & Expansion: Under high thermal loads, the top display module automatically lifts while side aluminium panels extend, forming a dedicated intake channel.
- Targeted VRM Cooling: An internal high-static-pressure fan activates within the newly created channel, directing cool air straight across VRM heatsinks and reducing surrounding motherboard component temperatures by up to 10°C.
- User-Defined Thresholds: Active trigger temperatures can be fully configured through the proprietary Ocypus Display software, allowing users to balance silent desktop operation with maximum dynamic thermal response.
2.8" IPS Circular Display with Ocypus Display Software
2.8-inch IPS Circular Display: Featuring a crisp 480 x 480 resolution, 2.8-inch IPS Circular Display: Featuring a crisp 480×480 resolution, the circular screen delivers approximately 50% more viewable area than conventional square displays, offering a broader and more immersive visual experience.
360° ARGB Ambient Lighting: The dynamic motor-driven housing incorporates an integrated ARGB lighting strip and pump halo that remains active whether the cooling module is expanded under load or parked in silent mode.
Ocypus Display Suite: Supports custom MP4 video playback, animated GIFs, real-time hardware monitoring, screen recording, theme downloads, and customizable CPU temperature thresholds for dynamic expansion.
Flagship Performance Core: Micron-Level Microchannel & Full Ceramic Bearing Architecture
- Micro-Channel copper Coldplate: Features precision micron-scale micro-grooves that maximize coolant contact area directly over CPU hot-spots.
- Full-Ceramic Bearing Architecture: Utilizes high-hardness ceramic shafts and sleeves to ensure high reliability, driving the pump up to 3,100 RPM (±10%) while maintaining whisper-quiet operation below 27 dB(A).
- Integrated 360 mm Integrated ARGB Fan - Sigma F36 ARGB : Features a signature suspended halo hub lighting system and frame light bars, paired with FDB bearings to strike an optimal balance between 82.5 CFM airflow and ≤36 dBA noise levels. An included speed-control cable allows users to switch fan speed from 500-2200 RPM to 500-1900 RPM for silent-priority scenarios.
Availability
The Ocypus Omega L36 Ultra Eng Limited (200 units worldwide) will be available via select global hardware retail partners, regional distributors and Amazon starting November 10, 2026.

articles.title: Researchers found yet another way our tech is betraying us, and this time the culprit is the humble HDMI cable — it turns out someone can wirelessly mimic the video from your wired connection using its radiation (and yes, AI is what’s changed the game)
articles.text:
This shocking video shows how AI can read the radiation coming from an HDMI cable to mimic the video being passed over the cable — not even wired connections are safe from spy tech
AI upgrades an age-old problem: electronic transmissions can leak sensitive data in all kinds of ways
- There is tech that can turn the radiation from HDMI cables back into video
- AI reduces errors in intercepted signals by over 60%
- Digital is harder to decode than analog, but it's not impossible
Last week we discovered that your videos can give away your location thanks to airplane noises in the background that you can't even hear, and we've known for some years that Wi-Fi routers can be used to spot where people are in a room. So it's not a huge surprise to discover yet another way our tech is betraying us — and this time the culprit is the humble HDMI cable.
A post on X by Psalter shows TempestSDR, which can capture the signal from your HDMI cable and almost recreate the image on another screen, because the cable creates an electromagnetic field that can be read. The quality isn't great, but if you bring AI into the mix you can enhance it to make text readable and images clearer. An AI system especially for the task, called DeepTempest, reduces errors by over 60%.
The video below is quite alarming.
Intercepting or playing with electronic leakage isn't new: 2001's Tempest for Eliza broadcast music to your radio by sending RF signals via your monitor, displaying images that generated specific radio frequencies. What's new is the AI element.
Is it time to don the tinfoil hat?
Not yet. DeepTempest does dramatically enhance images and reduce text errors, but as you can see from the video things are still pretty indistinct — and that's when the cable you're intercepting is right next to you, so you're close enough to see the display that you're intercepting.
You're not going to see much if you're in a van across the street, even if the cable being used is really poorly shielded, unless you've got a seriously powerful scanner.
DeepTempest was developed by Federico Larroca at the University of the Republic in Montevideo, Uruguay, and it does represent a major step forward: using text capture software DeepTempest was able to reconstruct text with roughly 30% of characters being misinterpreted.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
That sounds like a lot but it's not enough to render text incomprehensible to human readers. And that error rate is a whopping 60% lower than the previous state-of-the-art attack.
The word Tempest is used in these systems because it's a US National Security Agency (NSA) codename that refers to spying via electromagnetic leakage, and measures to prevent it.
Those measures are distance, shielding, filtering and masking, and they consider more than just leakage: they also include sounds and vibrations, so for example it's possible to log keystrokes via a phone's motion sensor.
The history of this is fascinating and goes back to the Second World War, where the US military's teleprinters were found to be generating detectable electromagnetic spikes that could be intercepted to capture the text. The recommendation for shielding, filtering and masking comes from the machines' supplier, Bell System, and while technology has advanced somewhat since then the advice is still sound: if you're the kind of person that security services or other shadowy organizations might be interested in, don't buy crappy cables.
Pricier cables have electromagnetic shielding, and while high-end companies used to tell us that was essential because otherwise the audio and video fidelity wouldn't be as pristine as you want… but maybe it's signal leaking out rather than in that people will be more worried about in the modern world.

articles.title: Cómo crear una imagen de los Saja Boys de Las Guerreras K-pop como Hokages de Naruto
articles.text:
Cualquier persona puede transformar a los Saja Boys de Las Guerreras K-pop en líderes ninja del anime Naruto mediante herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA).
La clave consiste en separar los rasgos generales de cada universo, como la energía de una formación musical, los peinados diferenciados, las poses de combate y la jerarquía visual de los Hokages.
El resultado puede remitir al anime de acción sin reproducir personajes existentes, emblemas oficiales o vestuarios reconocibles. Una imagen inspirada en los Hokages de Naruto debe construirse con protagonistas originales, accesorios ninja propios y un escenario que sugiera autoridad, combate y trabajo en grupo.
Cuál es el primer paso para generar la imagen
Para empezar, es necesario abrir Gemini, la herramienta de inteligencia artificial de Google, desde un navegador, una tableta o la aplicación para celulares. Luego corresponde iniciar sesión con una cuenta de Google y crear una conversación nueva. De esa forma, las instrucciones y los ajustes posteriores quedan reunidos en un mismo hilo.
Antes de redactar el prompt, se debe elegir el encuadre. El formato horizontal permite mostrar a varios personajes de cuerpo completo, un paisaje de aldea y un conjunto de rostros tallados sobre una montaña ficticia.
Qué debe incluir el prompt para crear recrear a los Saja Boys
El prompt debe presentar primero a los Saja Boys. Una fórmula posible es: “Ilustración anime contemporánea de seis guerreros ficticios de pop coreano convertidos en líderes ninja, con peinados distintos, poses de acción y uniformes originales”.
Después se pueden sumar los detalles que diferencian a cada integrante. Uno puede llevar una capa blanca con bordes rojos abstractos; otro, una armadura ligera color burdeos; un tercero, un chaleco verde con estampados florales geométricos.
Asimismo, las armas pueden variar: dagas, una espada curva, un abanico metálico o un bastón de energía. La diferencia entre prendas, colores y objetos reduce el riesgo de que todos parezcan el mismo personaje.
Cómo se alude a los Hokages sin infringir los derechos de autor de Naruto
La referencia a los Hokages puede trasladarse a través de ideas amplias, como la posición de liderazgo, las capas ceremoniales, las bandas de tela, los protectores de frente sin logotipos y una montaña con retratos de antiguos gobernantes ficticios.
En lugar de símbolos de hojas o emblemas oficiales, el pedido puede incluir “insignias circulares originales”, “placas de metal con un signo geométrico” o “escudos abstractos”.
Qué ajustes permiten mejorar la primera imagen generada con IA
La primera respuesta de Gemini debe tomarse como una base de trabajo. Hay que comprobar que aparezcan todos los integrantes, que las manos no tengan errores, que las armas posean una forma entendible y que ninguna figura quede cortada por los bordes.
Las correcciones deben ser breves y precisas. Algunas opciones son: “mostrar cuerpos completos”, “dar más protagonismo al líder central”, “cambiar la capa blanca por una capa marfil”, “quitar emblemas similares a franquicias conocidas” o “hacer que cada guerrero tenga una postura distinta”.
Cómo generar una versión apta para imprimir y colorear
Cuando la composición sea satisfactoria, se puede pedir una variante para colorear. El pedido debe incluir frases como “blanco y negro”, “líneas gruesas”, “contornos limpios”, “sin sombras”, “sin degradados” y “personajes de cuerpo completo”. Esa versión facilita la impresión y deja áreas definidas para aplicar color a mano.
Antes de descargar la imagen, corresponde revisar que no incluya palabras involuntarias, marcas de agua, logotipos o símbolos que remitan de forma directa a una franquicia.
Es conveniente aclarar, si se publica o comparte en redes sociales, que se trata de una creación realizada con inteligencia artificial y que no es una imagen oficial de Las Guerreras K-pop ni de Naruto.

articles.title: 8849 Tank 5 Pro review: The rugged projector phone that can project light and see heat
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Tank 5 Pro takes everything that made the Tank 5 impressive and adds a FLIR thermal camera with a remarkably wide view. For anyone who inspects buildings, hunts leaks or checks electricals, this is a serious tool. For everyone else, the Tank 5 is the smarter buy.
Reasons to buy
- + Flagship Dimensity 9400e SoC
- + 3K AMOLED display, 3000 nits peak
- + 120W fast charge, 90-minute full recharge
- + 50MP triple rear camera system
- + Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0
Reasons to avoid
- - 733g and 33.8mm thick
- - The projector can be noisy
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
8849 TANK 5 Pro: 30-second review
The Tank 5 Pro has but one purpose - it adds thermal imaging to the Tank 5 and changes almost nothing else from the prior design. 8849 admits as much on its own website - the only difference between the two phones, it states, is the thermal camera.
This design was already the most complete rugged projector phone on the market. It had a flagship chip, a gorgeous screen and a battery that recharges in about 90 minutes. The Pro keeps all those strengths and adds one more: thermal imaging.
You get a FLIR Lepton 3.1R sensor with a 95-degree field of view. 8849 claims that is a world first for a phone. Most thermal phones manage 50 or 57 degrees. A wider view means you see more of a room, a wall or a fuse board without having to move the device around.
The price of that view is resolution. The sensor delivers 160 x 120 native pixels. Software upscaling takes it to 480 x 360, and visible light edges are overlaid to help you read the image. It is useful, but it will not rival a dedicated high-end imager.
So who is it for? Electricians, builders, surveyors, solar installers and rescue teams spring to mind. Anyone who has ever wondered where the draught is coming from might also apply. If you will never point it at a hot pipe, save your money.
Would I consider this one of the best rugged smartphones? That depends on how much functionality you want in a single handset, but it deserves some recognition for its unique feature set.
8849 TANK 5 Pro: price and availability
- How much does it cost? From $1150/£885/€809
- When is it out? Available by November 20 2026
- Where can you get it? Direct from the maker or via an online retailer
8849 has announced that this phone will be available from November 15, 2026 in the USA, with other regions from November 20, 2026, directly from the maker.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
There are three SKUs: 16GB+512GB, 18GB+512GB and 18GB+1TB - US pricing for the three is $1149/ $1,199/$1,299, respectively. In the UK, that’s £885/£924/£1001, and in the EU those prices are €1.045,95/€1.091,95/€1.182,95.
Where is it cheapest? America obviously. It’s more than $20 per SKU in the EU and $45 more in the UK, making that location the most expensive place to buy.
Not sure why the UK gets the thin end of that wedge, but that’s the price 8849 decided.
I’ve noticed that 8849 has ditched the 16GB model of the original Tank 5, and it now only comes in the 18GB+512GB option for $999.99, £770 or €910,95 depending on your region.
That makes the inclusion of a Thermal camera an extra $200, £154 or €181 for each area.
But if it were my money, I’d buy the 16GB+512GB Tank 5 Pro model, as most people would never notice the difference, and it’s only $150 more than the 18GB+512GB Tank 5, and it has the thermal camera.
Competition is thin. Rugged phones with thermal cameras exist, but none that I know of also pack a projector that I’m aware of. The Oukitel WP70 Ultra offers thermal imaging and a 16,000mAh battery, but it’s not released, and no price has been confirmed.
The real comparison is with a standalone thermal imager, like those by ThermalMaster, but these typically start at around $250 for a USB-connected camera.
What these add-on cameras lack is the ability to merge the thermal data with conventional light camera data for image fusion, which makes for much better readability.
Obviously, this isn’t a cheap phone, but in terms of specifications and features, it seems like good value, especially if you live in America.
Unfortunately, the flip side of being in the USA is that the service providers are notoriously anti-consumer, and you will need to be on AT&T to use the Tank 5 or Tank 5 Pro. Curiously, other 8849 phones and tablets support Verizon and T-Mobile only.
In Canada, you can use Bell, Rogers, Videotron, Freedom, and Telus. In the UK, most will work, including EE, H3G, Sky, Telefonica(O2), Virgin, Vodafone and Gamma. Australians can use Optus, Telstra and VHA. Major carriers in other countries are supported, so you should be good if you check the supported frequencies before buying.
- Value score: 4/5
8849 TANK 5 Pro: Specs
| Item | Spec | 
| Processor | MediaTek Dimensity 9400e, 4nm, octa-core (1x Cortex-X4 at 3.4GHz + 3x X4 at 2.85GHz + 4x A720 at 2.0GHz) | 
| GPU | Immortalis-G720 MC12 | 
| RAM | 18GB LPDDR5X (plus 18GB virtual) | 
| Storage | 512GB UFS 4.0, microSD expandable to 2TB | 
| Display | 6.73-inch AMOLED, 3200x1440px (3K), 120Hz, 3000 nits (local peak), Panda Glass | 
| Thermal camera | FLIR Lepton 3.1R, 160 x 120 native, 480 x 360 with VividIR, 95 degree horizontal view, under 50mK sensitivity | 
| Thermal ranges | High gain: minus 10°C to 140°C. Low gain: minus 10°C to 400°C | 
| Main Camera | 50MP Samsung ISOCELL GN1, PDAF, f/1.8, 4K30fps | 
| Telephoto | 50MP, 3x optical zoom, OIS | 
| Night Vision | 50MP with 4x 940nm infrared LEDs | 
| Front Camera | 32MP OmniVision OV32B40, f/1.7, 1080p video | 
| Battery | 17,600mAh dual-cell | 
| Charging | 120W wired (full charge approx. 90 min), 25W reverse charge | 
| Projector | TI DLP, 2K resolution, 220 lumens, 0.5 to 4m laser autofocus, 4-point keystone correction | 
| OS | Android 16 | 
| Connectivity | 5G, WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, NFC, dual frequency GPS (L1 + L5) | 
| SIM | Dual Nano, Nano + eSIM, Nano + microSD, or Nano + eSIM + microSD | 
| USB | USB-C 3.2 Gen 1 (DisplayPort 1.4 Alt Mode) | 
| Rugged Rating | IP68 and IP69K | 
| Dimensions | 177.1 x 87 x 33.8mm | 
| Weight | 733g | 
| Colours | Black | 
8849 TANK 5 Pro: Design
- Thick and heavy
- Vents for the projector on both sides
- Now with a thermal camera
Hold the Tank 5 Pro, and it feels exactly like the Tank 5, which is good if you want something that feels built to double as a sledgehammer. The chassis blends brushed metal plates, rubberised corner armour and polycarbonate panels. It’s built for abuse, and if you drop it on your foot, you'll be the one giving, not the Tank 5 Pro.
The dimensions are identical to the Tank 5 at 177.1 x 87 x 33.8mm. So is the weight at 715g. That is surprising. A thermal module with its own shutter and optics has to go somewhere, and it must weigh something. Well, when I weighed it, the scales said 733g, so the thermal electronics don’t snub the laws of physics.
The thermal lens sits top right in the centrally positioned camera cluster, with the IR emitter below it. The visible light sensors are on the left. What’s great about this arrangement is that the primary sensor is physically close to the thermal camera, so when the two images are overlaid, there is almost no difference in the viewing angle between them, producing a good alignment when the data is merged.
The camping light bar, night vision lens, and four infrared LEDs remain in a V-shape in the middle of the back, which prevents this phone from offering wireless charging. Given the battery size, that wasn’t a practical option, so it's not a real loss.
The projector vents still split the left frame in two, and the right frame still has its second grille and fingerprint power key.
My verdict about this phone design remains unchanged, because the form factor is almost identical, and it's slightly heavier.
To be precise, this isn't a pocket phone, but one better suited to a belt holster or vehicle mount. Those travelling on foot wouldn’t take long to conclude this wasn’t the best phone to carry any distance.
One new note on the Tank 5 I made related to the thermal camera. 8849 recommends an operating range of 0°C to 35°C for the phone. That is fine for a summer survey, but not being able to handle below-zero temperatures might be an issue. It is less helpful for a winter loft inspection, which is exactly when thermal imaging earns its keep. However, if you want to warm up the Tank 5 Pro, running the projector for a couple of minutes will noticeably raise the device's temperature. And the thermal sensor has a range of -10°C to 400°C.
Design score: 4/5
8849 TANK 5 Pro: Hardware
- MediaTek Dimensity 9400e
- AMOLED display
- 17600 mAh fast charge battery
The Dimensity 9400e remains the star of this show, as it was on the Tank 5. It is a 4nm flagship chip, and it sits far above the mid-range silicon found in most rugged phones. The Immortalis G720 MC12 GPU keeps games and sustained workloads moving.
As I’ve already mentioned, this phone comes in three flavours, matching 16GB or 18GB of RAM with 512GB or 1TB of storage. My review hardware has 18GB of RAM and 512GB of storage. And I noticed that the only Tank 5 SKU now comes with this much memory.
The 6.73-inch AMOLED display is also unchanged. It runs at 3200 x 1440 with a 120Hz refresh rate and 3000 nits peak. My only complaint about this screen is that it needs a reflection-reducing coating or screen protector, but it can still be seen outdoors, thankfully.
Thermal work often means bright roofs and sunlit walls, and this screen copes most of the time. Protection is still Panda Glass rather than Gorilla Glass Victus, which remains a disappointment, if you like the latter.
The battery is 17,600mAh, built as two 8800mAh cells. That is how 120W charging works. A full charge takes about 90 minutes, and reverse charging at 25W turns the Pro into a field power bank.
There is a small caveat, and I only noticed it with this phone, not its predecessor. After charging at 120W for 90 minutes, the charger gets hot to the touch. I suspect this also happened with the Tank 5, but for whatever reason I didn’t notice.
In my experience, electronics that get hot eventually fail, so keep your receipt.
Another area worth mentioning is connectivity, since this platform supports WiFi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0, dual-frequency GPS, and eSIMs.
When I covered the Tank 5, the specs said Bluetooth 5.4, and now, magically, it's become version 6.0. Not sure what, if anything, changed there, but now both phones say the same BT 6.0 capability.
The eSIM shares the second SIM interface, so you can pair it with a Nano SIM and a microSD card, making a microSD less of a deal.
Overall, this is a terrific spec for a rugged phone.
- Hardware score: 4.5/5
8849 TANK 5 Pro: Cameras
- 50MP main + 50MP telephoto + 50MP night vision + Thermal camera
- 32MP on the front
- Five cameras in total
The 8849 Tank 5 has four cameras:
Rear camera: 50MP Samsung ISOCELL S5KGN1SP, 50MP OmniVision OV50C40, 50MP OmniVision OV50D40, FLIR Lepton 3.1R Thermal camera
Front camera: 32MP OV32B40
Here I’m going to focus exclusively on the Thermal sensor, because you can read my opinion of the other sensors in my Tank 5 review.
The Pro uses a FLIR Lepton 3.1R, which captures 160 x 120 native pixels, 19,200 calibrated temperature points. VividIR fuses frames in real time and upscales the image to 480 x 360. MSX overlays edges from the visible camera, making pipes, wires, and structures easier to read.
Those numbers sound modest, because they are. This is a compact sensor, not a professional handheld imager. Treat it as a very capable tool for finding problems, not for documenting them to survey grade.
Where it diverges from many phones that include a thermal sensor is the field of view, as 95 degrees is exceptionally wide. Typical thermal phones offer a 50 to 57-degree view, according to 8849, and that wider field is super-useful when you are working in a confined space. In a small room or a loft, that could be a big gain. You see more per frame, so you can scan faster and miss less, hopefully.
There is a trade-off, and it is simple maths. Spread 160 pixels across 95 degrees, and each pixel covers about 0.6 degrees. At 10 metres, one pixel spans roughly 10cm. That is my calculation from the stated field of view, not an 8849 figure. A small target at distance will be a handful of pixels, so that’s less of an issue.
I estimated that the nearest that this sensor will focus is about 15cm, which probably isn’t near enough to easily track problematic components on a circuit board unless they’re big.
Thermal sensitivity is under 50mK, or 0.05°C. That lets the Tank 5 Pro pick out subtle differences, such as damp patches or a warm pipe behind plaster.
There are two gain modes. High gain covers minus 10°C to 140°C, with finer detail for building work. Low gain stretches to 400°C for engines, machinery and flames.
Despite the resolution limitations of this sensor, what makes it exceptionally easy to use is the MyFLIR Pro app, which comes pre-loaded onto the phone.
As you might expect, it offers spot and area temperature readings, alarms, nine colour palettes, photo, video and time-lapse capture and picture-in-picture. Images are compatible with FLIR devices and FLIR Thermal Studio Suite for desktop analysis. That is a proper workflow, and it sets the Pro apart from cheaper thermal add-ons.
For those who need thermal accuracy, it’s a mixed bag. In high-gain mode, accuracy is ±5 °C or 5%, whereas in low-gain it's double that. To put that in simpler terms, low-gain isn’t suitable for soufflé baking if your oven isn’t reliable.
In terms of Emissivity, there are four choices: matte (recommended, semi-matte, semi-gloss and glossy (not recommended. These settings allow you to match the texture of the object you are scanning, avoiding wildly inaccurate readings.
In video capture, the rate is only 7.9 fps, but with these devices, less than 9 fps is normal.
The team behind MyFLIR has focused on making it easy to use, and it certainly ticks those boxes. It still won’t compete with a dedicated camera for flexibility and accuracy, but for jobs like plumbing and working on engines, it's more than adequate.

- Camera score: 4/5
8849 Tank 5: Performance
- 4nm SoC
- Premium performance
| Phone | Row 0 - Cell 1 | 8849 TANK 5 Pro | 8849 Tank 5 | 
| SoC | Row 1 - Cell 1 | MediaTek Dimensity 9400e | MediaTek Dimensity 9400E | 
| GPU | Row 2 - Cell 1 | ARM Immortalis-G720 MC12 | ARM Immortalis-G720 MC12 | 
| NPU | Row 3 - Cell 1 | MediaTek NPU 790 | MediaTek NPU 790 | 
| Memory | Row 4 - Cell 1 | 18GB/1TB | 16GB/512GB | 
| Weight | Row 5 - Cell 1 | 715g | 715g | 
| Battery mAh | Row 6 - Cell 1 | 17600 | 17600 | 
| Geekbench | Single | 2078 | 2097 | 
| Row 8 - Cell 0 | Multi | 6685 | 6536 | 
| Row 9 - Cell 0 | OpenCL | 12700 | 12943 | 
| Row 10 - Cell 0 | Vulkan | 14711 | 14916 | 
| PCMark | 3.0 Score | 16558 | 18477 | 
| Row 12 - Cell 0 | Battery | 32h 53m (13%) | 32h 25m (14%) | 
| Charge 30 | % | 46 | 46 | 
| Passmark | Score | 23922 | 25227 | 
| Row 15 - Cell 0 | CPU | 11299 | 11866 | 
| 3DMark | Slingshot OGL | Maxed Out | Maxed Out | 
| Row 17 - Cell 0 | Slingshot Ex. OGL | Maxed Out | Maxed Out | 
| Row 18 - Cell 0 | Slingshot Ex. Vulkan | Maxed Out | Maxed Out | 
| Row 19 - Cell 0 | Wildlife | Maxed Out | Maxed Out | 
| Row 20 - Cell 0 | Nomad Lite | 1784 | 1820 | 
Not sure if there is much value in comparing the Tank 5 Pro and the Tank 5, since under the hood it’s the same hardware. But if only to prove that, I cycled the benchmarks, and they’re within 1% of each other in most tests.
The Tank 5 Pro is a high-performance phone, as was its father before it, but what these numbers can’t show is the impact of running the thermal camera, as they don’t show the impact of using the conventional sensors or the projector.
Those tests are beyond the remit of this review, but undoubtedly the projector is a major drain on power, based purely on how warm the phone becomes when running it. The thermal sensor is much less demanding, and with 17600 mAh to play with, most users are unlikely to notice much impact.
The Tank 5 Pro is a powerful phone, so there is no change from its predecessor.
- Performance score: 4.5/5
8849 Tank 5: Final verdict
The Tank 5 Pro is the most capable rugged projector phone yet made, and it puts the cherry on that cake by being able to see heat.
Without question, the thermal camera is the reason to buy, as it makes the Tank 5 Pro the complete package. It isn’t the highest-resolution thermal solution around, but the 95-degree view makes it quick to use, and the FLIR software makes it credible.
Nothing else has changed, including the drawbacks. The phone is very heavy. The projector still needs darkness. And an update policy that 8849 now says covers five years needs to be proven. But given how competitive the rugged phone market has become, launching phones on a two-year life cycle probably isn’t enough for more savvy purchasers.
The choice is straightforward. Need thermal imaging? Buy the Pro. Do not need it? Buy the Tank 5 and pocket the extra cash. Well, not pocket it, since the phone definitely won't fit then, if it does now.
Should I buy a 8849 Tank 5?
| 8849 Tank 5 Pro Score Card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Value | Fair premium if you use the thermal camera | 4/5 | 
| Design | Identical to the Tank 5, so thick and heavy | 4/5 | 
| Hardware | Flagship SoC, bright AMOLED, high res projector and fast charging | 4.5/5 | 
| Camera | Practical sensors for recording work and now Thermals | 4/5 | 
| Performance | Powerful Dimensity 9400e and full charge in 90 minutes battery | 4.5/5 | 
| Overall | A jack of all trades, but a master of none | 4.5/5 | 
Buy it if...
You go off the beaten path
This is the perfect device if you work or adventure in environments where battery life is critical and multi-day use without a charger is a regular requirement. I’m not sure you would want to hike with hardware this heavy, but for a rugged device for capturing images and video and then projecting them, it's exceptional.
You inspect things for a living
Electricians, builders, surveyors and solar installers will get real use from a wide thermal view. It replaces a separate device and a second charger. You could carry extra equipment for those jobs, but this device might do it all.
Don't buy it if...
You don't need a projector or thermal camera
The cost of this device is tied to its feature set, and so if you don't want the projector, or a thermal camera there seems little point in buying this.  Other rugged designs with this SoC, memory and storage are available for less than 8849 is asking for the Tank 5 or Tank 5 Pro.
You need a lightweight phone
At 715g quoted and 733g tested, this is a heavy item to add to a backpack or put on your hip. It is hard to carry and harder to forget, swimming across a river.
Also Consider
8849 Tank 5
The same phone without the thermal camera. It is cheaper and equally powerful, but obviously lacks that one feature. But it does have a projector, so you can review footage on a camping holiday if you can hang a sheet up as a projection surface.
Read my 8849 Tank 5 review for more information.
ThinkPhone 25 by Motorola
The ThinkPhone 25 offers a powerful SoC, robust package, practical form factor, high-quality camera sensors and decent battery life at a mid-range price point. But, it’s not available in the USA, sadly.

articles.title: Valve Adds Steam Deck FPS Data To Game Compatibility Screen in Latest Update
articles.text:
Monday, November 9th 2026
Valve Adds Steam Deck FPS Data To Game Compatibility Screen in Latest Update
Valve recently announced that it was adding an opt-in toggle to enable data collection in Steam for the Steam Deck, with the idea behind the new feature being that developers could analyze the reported framerate data using Steam's built-in tools to better optimize their games for the handheld's hardware. In a new Steam Client update, however, Valve has confirmed that it will start sharing that same average Steam Deck framerate data with players before they buy the game, so that they can get a relatively accurate idea of what to expect from the gameplay experience before spending money on the game. 
The framerate data will be displayed as an average at the bottom of the Steam Deck compatibility screen as an FPS figure specific to the player's current hardware. The figure will also cite the date the average was last updated. Clicking or tapping the dropdown arrow next to the framerate note will expand a histogram showing the game's average framerate distribution across gaming sessions as a percentage. This should, with relative certainty, convey how often players ran into gameplay hitching.As it had previously indicated, Valve also confirms in the update notes that this Steam Deck data is a "stepping stone" towards a more widespread implementation, and it has also started prompting desktop players to opt into framerate data collection in the Steam Client Beta, so that it can start building similar systems for more devices.Valve notes that this system isn't perfect and provides an example of a situation where a mismatch between the Deck's display and the game's target framerate causing issues with VSync.
What does it mean when a game has a big gap between 90 and 45, like this? 
Gaps like these are usually the result of a mismatch between the refresh rate of the display and the framerate that the game is trying to run at. This could be due to performance or because of a setting in the game itself. When this mismatch occurs, the system will sync the game's framerate to the display's native refresh rate to avoid graphical glitches (tearing).

articles.title: Elon Musk anunció este lunes que Tesla devolverá los depósitos del Cybertruck a algunos de sus clientes
articles.text:
Elon Musk anunció este lunes que Tesla devolverá los depósitos del Cybertruck a un número considerable de clientes, ante la imposibilidad de cumplir con todos los pedidos antes del cierre de la línea, previsto para mediados de 2027.
“El ritmo de pedidos del Cybertruck supera con creces nuestro ritmo de producción. Intentaremos fabricar tantos como sea posible antes de cerrar la línea en unos ocho meses, pero tendremos que devolver los depósitos a mucha gente”, escribió el director ejecutivo de la compañía en su plataforma X.
Las órdenes pendientes superan lo que Tesla puede producir
Musk aclaró que la decisión de discontinuar el modelo no responde a problemas de rentabilidad, sino a una cuestión de prioridades estratégicas.
“El costo de oportunidad de la complejidad del Cybertruck está ampliamente superado por el valor de la producción incremental del Cybercab”, argumentó el ejecutivo, en respuesta a versiones que apuntaban a pérdidas como causa del cierre.
Tesla agregará un turno extra de producción para intentar cumplir con la mayor cantidad posible de pedidos antes de desmantelar la línea. No obstante, el volumen de reservas pendientes hace inviable atender a todos los compradores que esperaban recibir su vehículo.
El Cybercab reemplazará al Cybertruck en la planta de Texas
El cierre de la línea del Cybertruck en la Gigafactory Texas, en las afueras de Austin, está programado para mediados de 2027. El espacio y los recursos liberados se destinarán a escalar la producción del Cybercab, el robotaxi sin conductor con el que Tesla aspira a expandir su red de transporte autónomo.
La empresa planea poner el Cybercab a la venta antes de que finalice 2026, aunque ese plan enfrenta investigaciones de la agencia de seguridad vial de Estados Unidos por carecer de controles manuales.
El anuncio del cierre lo hizo Musk el viernes 6 de noviembre en X: “Tesla estará reduciendo gradualmente la producción de la Cybertruck en Gigafactory Texas alrededor de mediados del año próximo para dar espacio a una mayor producción del Cybercab”.
Wes Morrill, ingeniero jefe del proyecto, publicó en la misma red social una frase que fue leída como señal de discontinuación definitiva: “La Cybertruck fue una increíble plataforma de desarrollo tecnológico y sigue viva a través del Cybercab”.
Las ventas del Cybertruck nunca alcanzaron las proyecciones de Musk
El desempeño comercial de la camioneta estuvo lejos de las expectativas. Musk llegó a proyectar ventas de 250.000 unidades anuales, pero según Kelley Blue Book, las ventas en Estados Unidos cayeron 48% el año pasado, hasta las 20.237 unidades. En lo que va de 2026, la caída acumulada alcanza otro 28%.
La camioneta había llegado al mercado a fines de 2023 con una carrocería de acero inoxidable y formas angulares, pero su precio también se alejó de lo prometido: Musk había señalado que el modelo debía ser accesible, y la versión Cyberbeast hoy cotiza a USD 102.000.
El analista de Wall Street Dan Ives, director gerente senior de Yorkville Ives & Co., señaló a CBS News que el desenlace “estaba escrito en la pared”, dado el precio elevado y la baja demanda. Para Ives, el cierre libera tiempo y capacidad para que Musk concentre recursos en robótica y robotaxis.
Tesla abandona los modelos más caros para apostar por la conducción autónoma
La salida del Cybertruck se enmarca en una reorientación más amplia de la compañía. Tesla también discontinuó los Model S y Model X —sus sedán y SUV premium— para liberar espacio de fábrica destinado al robot humanoide “Optimus”.
La tendencia es la misma: reducir la gama de modelos convencionales de alto precio y baja rotación para concentrarse en inteligencia artificial, robótica y vehículos autónomos.
“Si tenemos que mantener una línea de producción compleja, una cadena de suministro y asignar ingeniería para el Cybertruck, no podemos usar esas personas ni ese espacio de fábrica para escalar el Cybercab, que es el vehículo que transformará profundamente el mundo del transporte terrestre”, escribió Musk el sábado en X, tras una oleada de reacciones de los usuarios y clientes con reservas.
Pese al fin de la producción, agregó: “Nunca habrá otro vehículo como este” y que la flota existente “seguirá circulando durante mucho tiempo”.

articles.title: Les Hisense UR9S et UR8S misent sur le RGB Mini-LED pour le cinéma et le jeu
articles.text:
Avec la technologie RGB Mini-LED, Hisense entend réunir le meilleur de deux mondes, avec une luminosité spectaculaire ainsi qu'une reproduction des couleurs ultra précise. Déclinée dans les gammes UR9S et UR8S, cette technologie promet une expérience premium aussi bien pour le cinéma que pour le sport et bien sûr le jeu vidéo.
Remplacer la Smart TV du salon n’est pas une mince affaire pour qui souhaite s’équiper d’un modèle moderne et polyvalent. Il faut de la luminosité pour préserver la lisibilité de l'image, des couleurs fidèles, un contraste suffisamment précis pour faire ressortir les détails… et si possible un modèle capable de sublimer nos jeux vidéo modernes.
C'est là que Hisense entend faire la différence avec le RGB Mini-LED, une technologie de rétroéclairage qui pousse plus loin les possibilités du Mini-LED classique. Avec ses téléviseurs UR9S et UR8S, le constructeur décline cette approche sur des diagonales allant jusqu'à 254 cm (100 pouces), avec la ferme ambition de rapprocher l'expérience du salon de celle d'une véritable salle de cinéma.
RGB Mini-LED : quand la lumière produit directement les couleurs
Sur un téléviseur LED classique ou Mini-LED, le rétroéclairage repose sur des LED blanches ou bleues, dont la lumière est ensuite transformée pour produire les couleurs de l'image. Le RGB Mini-LED adopte une approche différente, puisque chaque LED intègre ici trois diodes indépendantes : rouge, verte et bleue. La lumière colorée est ainsi produite directement à la source, avec un contrôle plus précis de son intensité.
L'intérêt est de limiter les pertes liées aux filtres optiques, tout en élargissant la palette de couleurs affichables. Hisense annonce une couverture pouvant atteindre 100 % de l'espace colorimétrique BT.2020, une référence particulièrement exigeante pour la reproduction des couleurs. Les nuances gagnent en richesse, tandis que le traitement de l'image peut ajuster plus finement la luminosité et les couleurs selon les scènes.
Cette architecture conserve les atouts du Mini-LED, avec un rétroéclairage réparti sur de nombreuses zones, pilotées indépendamment pour mieux gérer les contrastes. Le processeur Hi-View Engine RGB analyse l'image en temps réel et coordonne la lumière rouge, verte et bleue, avec pour objectif de préserver les détails dans les scènes sombres, tout en faisant ressortir les hautes lumières, sans sacrifier la fidélité des couleurs.
Face à l'OLED, qui contrôle individuellement chaque pixel et qui excelle dans la restitution des noirs, le RGB Mini-LED mise sur une autre combinaison, à savoir une réserve lumineuse élevée, un rétroéclairage précis et l'absence de risque de marquage permanent, une faiblesse propre aux écrans OLED. Il ne s'agit donc pas simplement de rendre l'image plus éclatante, mais de conserver une restitution maîtrisée dans des conditions de visionnage très différentes.
Une image XXL qui reste lisible en plein jour
Et justement, la luminosité constitue l'un des arguments majeurs de cette technologie. Sur la série UR9S, Hisense annonce un pic pouvant atteindre 5 000 nits, contre 3 500 nits pour l'UR8S, avec jusqu'à 3 800 nits sur sa version de 254 cm (100 pouces). Ces valeurs de pointe ne correspondent pas à une luminosité maintenue en permanence sur toute la dalle bien sûr, mais elles donnent une idée de la réserve disponible pour les scènes HDR les plus exigeantes.
Par ailleurs, les deux gammes bénéficient d'une dalle mate et d'un traitement antireflet destiné à préserver la lisibilité de l'image, un avantage particulièrement intéressant dans les pièces lumineuses. De quoi profiter d'un grand écran sans devoir systématiquement fermer les volets pour apprécier un film ou toute autre forme de contenu.
La compatibilité HDR est évidemment au rendez-vous, avec notamment les Dolby Vision 2, HDR10+ Adaptive, HDR10 et HLG. Et les joueurs ne sont pas oubliés, puisque les téléviseurs proposent une dalle pouvant atteindre 180 Hz, le VRR, l'ALLM et FreeSync Premium Pro. Hisense propose également un mode HSR qui booste la fréquence jusqu'à 330 Hz, en s’appuyant pour cela sur un traitement logiciel et une adaptation de la définition d'affichage.
De quoi attendre GTA VI (et les autres blockbusters) avec la certitude de profiter d'une expérience de jeu optimale.
UR9S ou UR8S : deux façons de profiter du RGB Mini-LED
Faut-il privilégier la gamme UR9S ou l’UR8S ? En vérité, les deux séries partagent les fondamentaux de la technologie, mais répondent à des attentes différentes.
L'UR9S représente le haut de gamme de Hisense. Disponible en 164 cm (65 pouces), 189 cm (75 pouces) et 215 cm (85 pouces), il pousse la luminosité jusqu'à 5 000 nits et associe son rétroéclairage RGB Mini-LED à un système audio 4.1.2 de 90 W RMS, Tuned by Devialet.
Il se distingue également par son port USB-C compatible vidéo 4K, en complément de ses trois entrées HDMI 2.1. Un téléviseur conçu pour ceux qui souhaitent donc réunir image ambitieuse, son immersif et connectique complète dans une seule installation.
L'UR8S adopte une approche plus polyvalente. Proposé de 139 cm (55 pouces) jusqu'à 254 cm (100 pouces), il conserve la couverture colorimétrique annoncée de 100 % du BT.2020, la dalle mate et les fonctions gaming avancées.
Sa luminosité atteint 3 500 nits, voire 3 800 nits sur le modèle de 100 pouces. Un système audio plus discret, de 2.1.2 et 50 W RMS, mais lui aussi Tuned by Devialet, complète l'ensemble.
Les deux séries intègrent enfin le système d’exploitation maison VIDAA U9.5, avec les principales applications de streaming, ainsi que la compatibilité Apple AirPlay 2 et HomeKit/Matter.

articles.title: New York marathon winner Andreas Almgren used the budget-friendly Coros Pace 4 as his running watch — here’s why I’d recommend it in the Black Friday sales
articles.text:
The New York Marathon winner wasn’t wearing a fancy Garmin or Apple Watch Ultra, but something much cheaper — here’s why this Coros model is a great running watch to look out for on Black Friday
Andreas Almgren was rocking the Coros Pace 4
Andreas Almgren won last weekend's New York City Marathon. The 31-year-old Swedish runner broke the tape in 2:06:01 — a frankly silly amount of time for anyone to run 26.2 miles. But although running fans are now analyzing everything from his nutrition strategy to his pacing, it's his watch that's got my attention — the Coros Pace 4, one of our best running watches.
Record-breaker Sebastian Sawe, who finished first at London earlier this year, used Garmin's cheapest watch, the now-outdated Garmin Forerunner 55. Almgren also opted for a budget-friendly, light running watch to help cross the finish line, rather than an expensive powerhouse like an Apple Watch Ultra 4 or Garmin Fenix 9 Pro.
It just goes to show that you can spend under $250 / £230 and still get a fantastic running watch worthy of the best runners in the world.
Coros Pace 4
We reviewed the Coros Pace 4 in February this year and awarded it 4/5 stars. Our reviewer praised its performance compared to its price, calling it 'a specialized, budget-friendly watch that balances high-end display technology and dedicated functionality for athletes'.
It's less a smartwatch and more a dedicated training tool, made entirely of lightweight plastic rather than any stylish (but heavier) metal elements. It packs up to 19 days of battery life, a huge improvement over smartwatches from Apple, Samsung, or Google, and even most Garmins, making it ideal for athletes who are doing a lot of GPS-powered, battery-sucking long runs and want to track their sleep on top, all without charging.
Speaking of GPS, that dual-frequency GNSS chipset ensures that the watch will be able to find you better amongst tall buildings — a perfect choice for, for example, the New York City Marathon. As our review put it, 'the ability to connect across two frequencies is designed to improve positional accuracy in challenging environments such as cities and forests'.
However, it's not as smartwatchy as other watches; it has limited notifications and call management functionality, and no third-party apps to speak of. Samsung and Google have the Play Store, Apple has the App Store, and even Garmin has the ConnectIQ store, but Coros is strictly a self-contained training ecosystem.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
You can link it to other apps like Strava or control media through the watch, but you don't get custom-built applications on the watch the way you do with other devices.
However, elite runners don't want those things: they want a lightweight, long-lasting training tool that works, with virtual pacing, accurate positional GPS, and heart rate tracking. In all of these aspects, the Coros Pace 4 delivers — and at $249 USD / £229 UK / AU$479.95, it's surprisingly well-priced.
A Black Friday bargain?
We're currently reviewing the Coros Pace 4 Pro, the Pace 4's successor. It's shaping up to be every bit as good as the standard 4, but even more exciting is what this means for the Pace 4 — when a new watch comes out, the older one is likely to drop in price, especially during big sales events.
With Black Friday on the horizon (November 27), if you're shopping for a new running watch, I'd keep an eye out for the Coros Pace 4. With the Pace 4 Pro out, the Pace 4 could drop from an already excellent value price down to an absolute steal. Check TechRadar during the Black Friday deals period — if the Coros Pace 4 drops, we'll tell you about it.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
He is the author of the upcoming book The Health Data Heist, set to be published by Bloomsbury in 2027. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

articles.title: Ce plugin gratuit pourrait bien changer votre façon de travailler avec Claude et Codex
articles.text:
Les assistants IA se perdent parfois en bla bla, alors qu'on leur demande simplement quelle commande lancer ou quel fichier modifier. I Have ADHD rend les réponses plus faciles à lire et à suivre. Il s'agit d'un plugin pour assistants de programmation (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…), qui modifie leur façon de répondre.
Contrairement à ce que son nom pourrait laisser penser, le projet ne sert pas à diagnostiquer ou à traiter un trouble de l’attention. Pensé notamment pour les personnes ayant un TDAH, il peut aussi intéresser les développeurs qui préfèrent des échanges directs, sans avoir à chercher les informations importantes au milieu de plusieurs paragraphes moins utiles.
- Action utile au premier plan
- Suivi des progrès explicite
- Licence MIT, usage gratuit
Moins d’explications, plus d'action
Une fois activé, I Have ADHD demande à l’assistant de commencer par la prochaine action à effectuer. Au lieu de détailler longuement le contexte, il va droit à l’essentiel. Si plusieurs opérations sont nécessaires, elles sont présentées dans l’ordre, sous forme d’étapes courtes.
Le plugin est censée respecter 10 règles de rédaction, parmi elles :
- Éviter les digressions ;
- Présenter les erreurs sans dramatiser ;
- Indiquer clairement ce qui a été modifié et ce qui a pu être vérifié ;
- Donner des estimations de durée chiffrées plutôt que des indications vagues ;
- Privilégier des listes de 5 éléments maximum par groupe, sans supprimer les informations importantes ;
Pour le débogage, une longue explication peut ainsi être remplacée par le nom du fichier à modifier, quelques étapes simples et la commande permettant de vérifier le résultat. On comprend tout de suite ce qu'il y a à faire, sans avoir à décortiquer toute la réponse.
Compatible avec plusieurs assistants de programmation
I Have ADHD ne se lance pas comme un logiciel. Il s’installe comme une compétence (skill) ou un plugin dans des outils tels que Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Qwen Code, Zed ou Pi. L’activation dépend de l’environnement utilisé et peut passer par une commande dédiée, comme /i-have-adhd dans Claude Code ou $i-have-adhd dans Codex. L'installation ne signifie donc pas nécessairement que les règles seront appliquées automatiquement.
Les consignes sont regroupées dans un fichier SKILL.md, consultable et modifiable. Il est donc possible d’adapter les règles à ses habitudes ou de les compléter pour obtenir des réponses sur mesure.
Attention, le plugin ne rend pas l’assistant plus performant sur le fond. Il agit surtout sur la forme des réponses. Mais à force de vouloir une réponse concise, vous pouvez passer à côté d'une explication utile. Voilà pourquoi l'outil prévoit des exceptions afin de développer davantage tel ou tel sujet lorsque c’est nécessaire ou lorsque l’utilisateur le demande. Il prévoit également de demander confirmation avant certaines opérations destructrices.
Gratuit et distribué sous licence MIT, très permissive, I Have ADHD s'adresse aux développeurs qui trouvent leurs assistants trop bavards. Les modifications de comportement ne changent pas les capacités des assistants, mais peuvent rendre les échanges moins chronophages.
- Action utile au premier plan
- Suivi des progrès explicite
- Licence MIT, usage gratuit

articles.title: Instagram usará IA para detectar a adolescentes que cambian su edad para entrar a la app
articles.text:
Meta amplió a todo el mundo la inteligencia artificial que usa Instagram para detectar a adolescentes registrados con una fecha de nacimiento falsa. La empresa anunció el 9 de noviembre que “millones más” de menores pasarán a las cuentas para adolescentes, con límites de contacto, contenido y tiempo de uso.
El sistema busca señales que indiquen que un usuario es menor de 18 años. Según Meta, analiza con qué perfiles y contenidos interactúa la persona, los mensajes de cumpleaños que recibe y “temas generales y pistas visuales” de sus fotos y videos, como la estatura o la estructura ósea.
La empresa aclaró en mayo, cuando presentó el análisis visual, que no se trata de reconocimiento facial: la IA no identifica a la persona de la imagen, sino que estima una edad aproximada. Ese mes la compañía también llevó la detección a los 27 países de la Unión Europea y a Brasil, según TechCrunch.
Las cuentas para adolescentes son privadas por defecto, limitan qué contenido ve el usuario y no permiten que desconocidos le envíen mensajes directos. Los menores de 16 años no pueden cambiar esas opciones sin permiso de un padre o tutor, que además puede supervisar la cuenta y fijar límites de tiempo.
Qué pasa con los menores de 13 años
Instagram exige tener al menos 13 años. Cuando el sistema sospecha que una cuenta pertenece a alguien más joven, la desactiva hasta que el titular demuestre su edad, según explicó Meta en mayo. Los usuarios de 13 a 17 años, en cambio, pasan automáticamente al régimen de cuentas para adolescentes aunque hayan declarado ser adultos.
La empresa informó que los padres en Estados Unidos recibirán una notificación en Instagram que explica cómo se estima la edad y cómo pueden corregirla si el sistema se equivoca. Meta no precisó cuántas cuentas ya fueron reclasificadas ni con qué margen de error opera la estimación.
Desde mayo quien cambia su fecha de nacimiento de menor a mayor de 18 años debe confirmarlo con un documento o con la estimación facial de edad del proveedor Yoti. La tecnología también se aplica en Facebook y llegará a Threads este año, según Meta.
Apple y las tiendas de aplicaciones, en el centro del reclamo
En Australia, Meta empezó a usar además la señal de rango de edad de Apple. Funciona así: un padre configura el teléfono de su hijo, la tienda de aplicaciones asigna un rango de edad y Apple lo comparte con los desarrolladores cada vez que el menor descarga una app.
Meta advierte que esa señal es inconsistente mientras las tiendas y los desarrolladores puedan elegir si la recopilan o la comparten. La compañía pide leyes que obliguen a verificar la edad y pedir el consentimiento parental en la propia tienda de aplicaciones, una postura que sostiene desde 2023, y describe su estimación con IA como un respaldo.
Australia prohíbe las redes sociales a menores de 16 años. Meta informó en mayo que, para cumplir esa norma, retiró el acceso a Instagram, Threads y Facebook a quienes considera menores de esa edad en el país.
La expansión llega después de un acuerdo que Meta firmó en agosto con fiscales estatales de Estados Unidos, en el que se comprometió a reforzar la verificación de edad y a imponer más restricciones a los adolescentes. La empresa también pidió a TikTok y YouTube que adopten prácticas similares.
Hay dudas sobre la eficacia. La investigadora Lisa Given escribió en The Conversation en mayo que no está claro si los adolescentes pueden esquivar estos controles haciendo que su contenido parezca el de un adulto.
Meta no informó si las verificaciones automáticas de edad de Facebook, que llegaron a cuentas de Estados Unidos en mayo, se extenderán a otras regiones. La versión para Threads es el único paso adicional que la empresa confirmó para este año.

articles.title: AskAnyModel Puts Six AI Responses Side by Side for Just $39.99
articles.text:
Monday, November 9th 2026
AskAnyModel Puts Six AI Responses Side by Side for Just $39.99
AskAnyModel AI Pro Plan is now available for $39.99 (MSRP $499) for lifetime access through Nov. 8. The browser-based platform brings more than 50 AI models into one workspace, with tools for comparing responses, generating images, and switching models during a conversation.
Its main comparison feature sends one prompt to two to six selected models simultaneously. Responses appear side by side, along with response times and token counts. For writing, coding, research, or brainstorming, this lets users assess different approaches without repeating a question across separate services. Comparing answers can help identify useful differences.
Get the AskAnyModel AI Pro Plan Lifetime Subscription for $39.99 (MSRP $499).Usage allowances depend on the model selected. The plan includes unlimited chats with 30 standard models, including options from the Llama, DeepSeek, Mistral, Gemma, and Qwen families. A separate Pro option, Gemini with Google Search grounding, is limited to 300 chats per week.
For premium models, subscribers receive 500 credits each month, shared across 19 options. These include GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity Search, and others. Premium access is therefore credit-based, rather than unlimited. This distinction matters for users who expect to rely primarily on flagship models rather than the standard selection.
However, image generation is unlimited across supported image models and does not consume premium credits. The chat interface also supports real-time response streaming and switching between models without losing conversation context.
AskAnyModel runs in a modern web browser, with no software downloads or installations required. Its model catalog is updated regularly, so the available selection may change over time.
For users who regularly consult several AI models, the platform provides a single place to compare outputs and manage conversations.
Get the AskAnyModel AI Pro Plan Lifetime Subscription for $39.99 (MSRP $499).

articles.title: Aspirateur robot Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete : une prestation de haut vol, malgré quelques bémols
articles.text:
| Entretien |  | 
| Fonction(s) station | Lavage serpillère | 
| Efficacité de lavage |  |

| Bruit |  |
