articles.title: Cisco research: Trust, not technology, is now the speed limit on enterprise AI - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cisco research: Trust, not technology, is now the speed limit on enterprise AI
For several years, the conversation about enterprise artificial intelligence has focused on capability: which model is smartest and which GPU is fastest. That made sense when technology was the constraint.
It isn’t anymore. AI can now do far more than most organizations will allow, and the gap is trust.
That’s the core finding of “Permission to Scale: The Critical Role of Trust in Successful AI Adoption,” new research released today at Cisco Systems Inc.’s Cisco Live APJC in Melbourne. Authored by independent researcher Brad Howarth, the study draws on data from 25 Australian organizations.
At Cisco Live APJC, Cisco hosted a press panel to discuss the report. The panel, moderated by Howarth, featured a number of corporate leaders from companies that participated in the report, including Carl Solder, chief technology officer of Cisco ANZ (far left); Anna Tosky, chief people officer at Elmo Software (second from left); Chris Locke, CTO at Flight Center Travel Group (third from left); Naz Wilson, group culture and enablement manager at Funlab (third from right); and Lucio Ribeiro, chief AI officer at TBWA Australia (second from right).
Though a sample size of 25 is small, the results align with conversations I’ve had with corporate leadership. I appreciated the panel’s mix of technologies, human resources and cultural leadership. I also valued the mix of roles, as the biggest barrier to scaling AI isn’t technical but people-related.
Australia is a tough crowd
Australia makes an interesting test case. According to University of Melbourne and KPMG research cited in the report, half of Australians use AI regularly, but only 36% trust it, and just 30% believe its benefits outweigh its risks. That’s the lowest among 47 countries surveyed. If you can build trust in AI in Australia, that work will scale globally. In the press release, Stefan Leitl, vice president and general manager of Cisco Australia and New Zealand, discussed the benefits of winning over this region: “It’s a playbook that travels well beyond Australia.”
The culture pillar is the one everyone skips
Solder noted that among the six pillars in Cisco’s AI Readiness Index, chief information officers and CTOs gravitate toward what they know, namely infrastructure and data, and leave culture for others. He described a customer that invested in infrastructure, governance, data and information technology skills but “didn’t focus on the culture. And they found that there was a big pushback from their employees and customers on using the toolsets they’ve invested in.”
This is something I’ve seen repeatedly: Companies spend millions on AI platforms only to see utilization remain tepid. Howarth discussed an adoption “flywheel” in which successful use creates evidence, evidence builds trust and trust enables broader use. Companies sit around waiting for trust before deploying, and the evidence of trust must be something measurable.
Trust in AI needs to be established with realistic parameters. Many people reject AI after a single mistake, even though in most cases the error rate is much lower than that of people. This mirrors what the automotive industry went through when a Tesla accident would trigger a media storm. The reality is that Tesla’s Autopilot system experiences one crash for about every 7 million miles, compared with human drivers, who average about one crash every 1 million miles.
Perfection isn’t a realistic goal, but being faster and more accurate than others is. Users should understand this going into any kind of trial or proof of concept, as the expectation of perfection can erode trust.
Leadership has to go first
Chris Locke offered a great example of an executive leading by example. The company’s 77-year-old founder, Graham “Skroo” Turner, uses AI every day. “He’s a big Anthropic Claude user,” Locke said. “This is also a guy who once said the internet wouldn’t catch on back in 2000. He may have gotten that one wrong, but he’s betting on AI catching on, so I think he gives us permission to play.”
Ribeiro outlined a more structured approach, describing trust as an equation built on four elements: ownership, competence, consistency and transparency. He was matter-of-fact about why asking a nervous workforce whether it wants AI doesn’t yield an accurate answer. “You never ask a barber if you need a haircut, as the answer is always yes.”
His alternative was honesty. Companies can’t promise to protect every job, but they can promise to make employees “the most prepared, trained, trusted person” if AI disrupts their role.
Funlab, where 79% of the workforce is 21 or younger, relies on peer learning. Its “AI Super Squad” convenes representatives from every department every four weeks. Wilson said early sessions simply clarified which tools were safe, because many employees’ real limitation was “just not knowing whether I am allowed to do certain things or not.”
Calibrated trust is the right goal, but measure it
The report’s central concept is calibrated trust. People need to know when to rely on AI, when to verify its outputs, and when a human must decide. Blindly trusting these systems and their outputs is a significant risk.
During the Q&A, I asked how companies protect against over-trust, especially in high-intensity jobs where people just take the answer and move on. Tosky was candid. “The AI slop. It’s real,” she said. “You ask the employee a question, prompt the AI system and then they send a report without looking at it, and it’s completely wrong. It’s 10 pages you now have to read.”
Elmo keeps a human in the loop on nearly everything, and she argued that the fix starts with redesigning the work. “It’s very unsexy, but start with the process itself, instead of just going, ‘OK, let’s throw a bunch of agents at it.'”
The report recommends that IT leaders adopt a specific practice: Stop treating log-ins as a proxy for trust, and track how often people challenge or override AI outputs. Usage shows people are clicking. Override rates show they’re thinking.
I also raised a contact center concern. AI automates the mundane tasks that served as cognitive breaks for agents, leaving them with nonstop, high-intensity work and higher churn. Tosky called it “AI brain fry” and suggested rethinking metrics and breaks. Wilson added that if AI absorbs routine work, employees lose the repetition that builds context and expertise. That’s a talent pipeline problem few companies are considering.
Agents raise the stakes
AI that drafts content is one thing; agents that act are another. Locke said Flight Centre now has agents handling a small subset of airline ticketing that was previously outsourced offshore, with security engaged from day one. He used AI to book his Uber to the event, but a return flight to Europe? “Not yet.”
Fewer than half of respondents are very or extremely confident that their foundations are ready for more autonomous AI, and more than half say their infrastructure needs upgrading. Cisco’s 2026 Relentless Defense report found that only 36% of Australian organizations apply consistent controls to AI agents and nonhuman identities. In the report, Lendi Group CTO Devesh Maheshwari described the target as “bounded autonomy, where the agent can act on your behalf but cannot go beyond the boundaries you have established.”
This is where Cisco can help its enterprise customers. Solder argues that trust must be enforced at the network and security layers. “Built into the network and security underneath, control stops being the brake and becomes the permission to move faster,” he said. Cisco is betting that its networking, security and Splunk portfolio will become the trust layer for agentic AI, and the report provides a business rationale for that bet.
Lessons learned from down under
As I stated above, the research is qualitative and aligns with what I hear from CIOs globally. My advice for IT leaders:
- Make AI a leadership team project. Include the chief people officer and the chief financial officer alongside the CTO. AI is a cultural change and a commercial transformation, not just a technology project. Companies that leave AI to IT end up with well-built platforms that employees don’t use, exactly the problem Solder described.
- Start small and show your work. Begin with visible, low-risk wins, then publish the results, including error rates. The report’s data showed that working three times faster with no increase in errors did more to win over skeptics than any mandate could. Proof spreads trust faster than persuasion.
- Make the guardrails obvious. Employees should know exactly what they can and can’t do with AI without digging through a policy document. As Funlab learned, much of the early hesitation stemmed not from fear of the technology but from uncertainty about what was allowed. Clear boundaries give people the confidence to experiment.
- Measure the right things. Log-ins show people are using AI, but they don’t show whether they trust it appropriately. Track how often employees challenge, check or override AI outputs. A workforce that never pushes back on AI isn’t a sign of success; it’s a warning sign.
- Fix the foundation before handing over the keys. Upgrade identity, monitoring and controls for agents before expanding their autonomy. Agents operate at machine speed, and most organizations still don’t apply consistent controls to nonhuman identities. Autonomy should follow readiness, not get ahead of it.
The AI winners won’t necessarily have the best models. They’ll have employees, boards and customers who trust the systems enough to let them do more. As Solder put it, “The leaders in our research aren’t scaling AI first. They’re scaling trust.”
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

GTA VI Pre-Orders Far Exceed Expectations Days Ahead of Launch
It's been known since before the actual release date was announced that GTA VI would generate enough hype that there would be ripple effects throughout the gaming industry, with some analysts estimating that the game would generate as much as $4.5 billion in sales in its first week on the market. However, according to Take-Two Interactive's CEO, Strauss Zelnick, in a recent interview with Variety, GTA VI is already exceeding expectations.
Strauss Zelnick via VarietyGrand Theft Auto VI" presales are "running far in excess of our expectations... That's a good thing. That said, we never claim success before it occurs. So we're just days away from beginning to see the fruits of our labor.
Zelnick also added that Take-Two would be "giving more information about how GTA VI performs post-launch," suggesting that the gaming giant is confident in the game's post-launch success. In late October 2026, it was estimated that GTA VI pre-orders had already reached 6.45 million units worldwide, with 74% of those pre-orders coming from PlayStation buyers. Zelnick also confirmed in an August interview that pre-orders for GTA VI Ultimate Edition had surpassed pre-orders for the standard version, at least at that time.

articles.title: Can Jensen Keep His Job? - EE Times
articles.text:
Overnight, the multibillionaire rock star CEO of the world’s biggest technology company admitted to an affair with a Chinese intelligence asset, and no, this isn’t the plot of a sub-standard Bond movie. Can it really be true that someone with Jensen Huang’s intelligence, experience, and judgment got caught by a honey trap, possibly the oldest trick in the book when it comes to espionage?
Huang, 63, admitted an extramarital affair in a letter to Nvidia employees.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” he wrote in the letter. “You deserve better from me. Leading Nvidia is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence.”
Rumors about Jensen Huang and Megaspeed executive Alice Huang (no relation) had been circulating for some time. Megaspeed is a Singaporean cloud provider and major Nvidia customer. U.S. intelligence believes Alice Huang is a Chinese asset, and is reportedly investigating whether Megaspeed may be illegally providing GPUs, AI compute, or both to restricted entities in China.
Jensen has been asked to appear at a closed-door briefing with the House Select Committee on Nov. 18. Nvidia’s board of directors is also beginning an independent investigation.
“The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate,” a statement from Nvidia’s board read.
While it’s unclear how much either U.S. intelligence or Nvidia’s board knew about this affair, and for how long, Nvidia spokespeople had previously appeared to deny the affair to the media, saying Jensen’s interactions with the Megaspeed executive were “not unusual or unexpected,” wording which, in retrospect, makes it sound like someone at Nvidia might have known. Nvidia’s board will now be checking everything the company has said is true to mitigate any legal ramifications.
It’s difficult to believe that someone with Jensen’s experience, and reported $200 billion fortune, underestimated the risks of an affair like this, whether he knew about his paramour’s connection to Chinese intelligence or not. Has the rock star CEO, one of the world’s richest men, known for his commanding leather-clad onstage performances, succumbed to his own hype?
Whether Jensen’s job outlasts this scandal or not, one thing that’s been irrevocably damaged is his public image. He has a cult-like following among tech bros, and is renowned for his charisma and his somewhat unconventional management style, famously keeping around 60 direct reports. Falling prey to a Chinese honey trap reveals a very human vulnerability that hardly fits his image. Fans were quick to defend him on social media both before and after the letter to employees emerged.
Another fan stepping up to publicly defend Jensen’s character was President Donald Trump.
“He’s such an honorable guy, I think he probably has an excuse for it,” Trump told reporters yesterday.
Asked by reporters whether Jensen should stay on as CEO of Nvidia, Trump replied, “Oh yeah, sure.”
The actual risk to U.S. national security seems debatable. While Jensen is an influential adviser to the Trump administration on AI policy, even being seated at the dinner table with Chinese President Xi Jinping on his state visit to the U.S. last month, Jensen himself has always lobbied for selling GPUs to China and is already a big supporter of open source AI models.
In footage filmed last month but released yesterday, Jensen tells Emily Chang that the Chinese “are not our enemies … If we care deeply about the safety of the world with respect to AI, then of course we must open dialogs, we must work with them in every possible way.”
So what would be the reason for targeting Jensen like this?
Could someone so influential be blackmailed with information like this, possibly in return for GPUs? Jensen’s own letter of admission seems to have put that to rest. Perhaps the destabilizing effect of a scandal of this magnitude would be a desirable outcome, though it remains to be seen how this will affect the market. Nvidia stock was slightly down yesterday, but not dramatically so, and something like this is unlikely to affect market demand for Nvidia’s products overall.
While it’s unclear how much U.S. intelligence or Nvidia’s board knew about this affair, it was the letter from the U.S. House Select Committee that brought it into the open. Why do this, and why now? Is someone trying to discredit Jensen as a major influence on the administration, or are they simply fed up with Nvidia skirting or flouting U.S. export controls? Trump is due to travel to China to meet with Xi later this month, and who knows whether Jensen will be invited.
If the CEO of the biggest technology company in the world, also the No. 1 supplier of AI chips with such huge geopolitical implications, is found to be a security risk of any kind, can he continue in his job? On the face of it, it may look like there’s no smoke without firing, but in the end it seems unlikely Nvidia’s investigation will find that the company or Jensen endangered national security, and most likely it will blow over. But given the strong link between Jensen’s public persona and Nvidia’s brand, can one continue to thrive without the other, and if so, is that a problem?

articles.title: Criptomonedas: cuál es el precio de ethereum este lunes
articles.text:
Ether, comúnmente llamada como ethereum, es la moneda digital #2 en cuanto a términos de capitalización de mercado, por lo que se trata de una de las divisas digitales que más despierta el interés entre los mineros (creadores de las criptodivisas).
Ethereum es una plataforma de blockchain de código abierto que se ejecuta con el uso de su moneda nativa, llamada ether o ETH, por lo que a pesar de que la gente usa estos nombres como sinónimos son cosas distintas.
Ether es un token que se utiliza específicamente en la blockchain ethereum para pagar transacciones. Este token es responsable de impulsar casi todo lo que ocurre en la red, misma que puede ser usada por cualquier persona para crear y ejecutar contratos inteligentes, que son programas de software que se ejecutan de manera autónoma y sin la intervención del usuario.
De acuerdo con el portal de Binance, la moneda digital solana actualmente cuenta con 122.2M de unidades creadas.
El costo de la criptomoneda ethereum para este día a las 14:05 horas (UTC) es de 2117.35 dólares. Esto quiere decir que la moneda digital reportó un cambio de -5.33% en las últimas 24 horas, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #2 entre las más populares.
Costo de la criptomoneda Ethereum
Ethereum y su última actualización
Tras varios meses de retraso y con el temor de que ya nunca pasaría, finalmente el 15 de septiembre de 2022 Ethereum llevó a cabo su tan ansiada fusión o actualización al nuevo nivel 2.0 con la promesa de mejorar la experiencia de los usuarios de esta criptomoneda.
“The Merge”, inglés para “La Fusión”, es una transformación en la forma en que Ethereum procesa las transacciones y en cómo se crean nuevos tokens de Ether.
Esta fusión se trata de la combinación de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum con una nueva cadena de bloques separada conocido como proof-of-stake, el cual reduce el consumo de energía de la cadena de bloques de Ethereum en un 99,9 %, según sus propios desarrolladores, lo que la vuelve más “amigable” con el ambiente al tiempo que las transacciones serían más baratas.
Sus defensores creen que la fusión hará que Ethereum resulte favorecido con respecto al máximo rival, Bitcoin, pues podría aumentar su uso.
En el proceso Proof Stake los propietarios de Ether bloquearán cantidades establecidas de sus criptomonedas para verificar nuevos registros en la cadena de bloques, ganando nuevas monedas además de su criptografía “participada”.

articles.title: Cet aspirateur robot Roborock noté 4,5/5 tombe à 549 € d'ici la fin du Black Friday 2026

Black Friday 2026 – L'aspirateur robot Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro à 549,00 € (-21%)
L'aspirateur robot Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro passe sous les 550 € chez Amazon Marketplace soit une baisse d'environ 21% sur le prix habituellement constaté.
Le Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro arrive sur le marché avec la promesse d'un nettoyage plus puissant et une station encore plus automatisée. Davantage compact, doté d'un lavage à l'eau chaude et un système d'aspiration renforcé, il entend succéder au Curv première génération, tout en se rapprochant des modèles haut de gamme de la marque.

- Très bonnes performances d'aspiration sur sols durs et moquettes.
- Lavage efficace sur l'huile et les taches liquides.
- Station très complète.
- Robot plus fin.
- Vidange automatique efficace.
- Niveau sonore contenu.
Points faibles
- Obstacles évités trop largement.
- Franchissement de seuils parfois défaillant.
- Brossette latérale qui repousse certains déchets.
- Nettoyage des coins et bords perfectible.
Le Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Pro renforce clairement les atouts de la gamme Qrevo en proposant un robot plus compact, plus puissant et doté d'un système de lavage plus ambitieux grâce à l'eau chaude à 100 °C. Ses performances d'aspiration figurent parmi les meilleures que nous ayons mesurées, tout comme son efficacité sur les taches grasses et liquides. La station, toujours très complète, assure un entretien quasi intégralement automatisé et se montre irréprochable sur la vidange. Cette montée en gamme ne gomme pas tous les défauts hérités de son prédécesseur. La navigation manque encore de précision : franchissement de seuils hésitant, gestion approximative de certains obstacles et trajectoires qui s'écartent parfois des zones définies. La brossette latérale, trop énergique, nuit ponctuellement à l'efficacité sur les petits déchets. Le Qrevo Curv 2 Pro demeure néanmoins un excellent robot pour celles et ceux qui privilégient la puissance d'aspiration et l'automatisation complète du lavage.

Néanmoins, son efficacité, aussi bien pour aspirer la poussière que pour éliminer les taches, fait oublier les quelques menus défauts d'un appareil aux innombrables paramètres entièrement modifiables.

articles.title: ‘It feels like malware’: This Chrome extension redirects your web searches to monetized results and was promoted by a VPN with 50 million downloads
articles.text:
‘It feels like malware’: This Chrome extension redirects your web searches to monetized results and was promoted by a VPN with 50 million downloads
Because free VPNs need to make money somehow…
Planet VPN has 50 million downloads on Android and says that its free VPN has “no limits on traffic, bandwidth, or time.”
However, free VPNs often come with caveats and need to earn money somehow. In the case of Planet VPN, this may be achieved via Planet Search — a Chrome extension that re-routes users' internet searches through intermediary platforms before they reach monetized Yahoo search results.
Planet Search has 2 million users, according to its Google Web Store page, and its parent company, Free Planet VPN S.R.L., was recently referenced in an investigation by Socket into ‘searchjacking’ apps.
While its role modifying a user's search engine has previously been documented and is identified in the Chrome Web Store, our investigation reveals that the developer was actively funneling users from its VPN product to its Chrome extension until at least mid-January this year.
Planet search, redirect & monetize
According to Socket’s report, these ‘searchjacking’ apps can “take over the browser's default search engine, route every query through a suspicious proxy server, and collect partner referral payments from Yahoo or Bing under a syndication partner ID.”
TechRadar has independently analyzed the source code of Planet Search and confirmed that it changes Chrome’s default search engine — using the chrome_settings_overrides.search_provider manifest key — to planet-search[.]com.
Using planet-search[.]com as the default search engine redirects users’ search queries through several intermediary platforms before landing on Yahoo’s syndication endpoint (/yhs/search) configured with commercial syndication parameters and campaign tracking tags.
While Planet Search states in the Chrome Web Store that it alters default search settings, the listing explicitly promises that “default search results will be provided by Google.” On another page it says the provider will be switched to Microsoft Bing. However, during our tests we consistently landed on Yahoo search result pages.
While TechRadar’s technical analysis traced the redirect hops to a Yahoo search endpoint, Planet Search’s privacy policy discloses that “certain web search services” are provided through CodeFuel, a search monetization platform. The same document also states the service may "gather data related" to usage, specifically citing "search queries" along with "the time and date of your search queries."
The Socket.dev report suggests many of the extensions may have obtained users via paid advertising campaigns. However, our research suggests that in the case of Planet Search, some of its users have been funneled from its VPN product.
Planet VPN's installer promoted the extension
TechRadar’s analysis of older Planet VPN desktop clients confirms that in version V.2.10.69.99, released on January 13, 2026, the app prompted users to install the Planet Search extension at setup.
However, frustration over the extension goes back years, with several people highlighting difficulties removing the tool .One user said they had "tried everything like deleting all of the folders on my PC" to get rid of the extension, while another said "it feels like malware."
TechRadar has not verified whether the current Planet Search extension still uses methods which make it difficult to remove.
How Planet Search may profit
When you enter a query while using the extension, that query is routed via its planet-search[.]com domain and several intermediary domains. The query is then handed off to major search providers (in our case Yahoo) with partner syndication tags (e.g. hspart or hsimp) at the end of the URL.
In search revenue-sharing arrangements of this kind, a user clicking on sponsored ads may generate a referral commission for the ad network, which may then share revenue with the extension publisher. TechRadar could not confirm whether Planet Free VPN receives any revenue from this arrangement.
While common among ad-tech toolbars, routing searches through redirect hops may expose user search intent to third-party commercial networks and is not something normally associated with the digital privacy protections of a VPN.
The free VPN privacy dilemma
All commercial VPNs exist to make a profit. And when an app is free, more often than not, you are what’s generating that profit.
While there are a few reputable free VPN providers, even the most well-established providers come with caveats — whether data limits, the inability to choose servers, or limited access to international servers.
For this VPN, Planet Search may be one way the provider is able to make money, although TechRadar could not confirm whether it earns revenue through the extension. It also offers paid-for tiers and may be monetizing its products in other ways.
Free Planet VPN S.R.L. did not respond to a request for comment before publication.
Sam is VPN Managing Editor at TechRadar. He has worked in the VPN industry since 2018 and has previously written for CNN, Al Jazeera, WIRED, and Deutsche Welle as a freelance journalist. He focuses on VPNs and digital privacy, cybersecurity and internet freedom.
Before joining TechRadar, Sam carried out research on global digital rights issues at Top10VPN. His research has been cited by the United Nations and UK Parliament, as well as publications such as The Guardian, Washington Post and BBC.
- Mike Williams Lead security reviewer

articles.title: Nvidia cracks down on overseas cloud AI GPU rentals for China — partners face 51% non-Chinese quota as black market B300 rack prices surge to $2.8 million
articles.text:
Nvidia cracks down on overseas cloud AI GPU rentals for China — partners face 51% non-Chinese quota as black market B300 rack prices surge to $2.8 million
Rent abroad or buy compliant cards: both of China’s routes to Nvidia compute are running short.
Nvidia-based compute is getting scarce and expensive for Chinese AI labs on both of their main routes, buying export-compliant cards and renting abroad, and the Financial Times reports that Nvidia’s own crackdowns are part of the reason. Nvidia has told cloud partners worldwide that at least 51% of their services must go to non-Chinese firms, while Chinese companies have bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation cards this year to cover the shortfall. Meanwhile, a B300 rack that sells for about $600,000 internationally reportedly fetched $2.8 million in China last month.
Chinese customers have ordered more than 6 million of Nvidia’s export-compliant RTX Pro 5500 cards. That is at least twice the 3 million that the company could reportedly manufacture in 2027. One source told CNBC that it was proposed that Moonshot pay 30% to 50% more upfront, in comparison to a non-Chinese entity.
Many Chinese groups have relied on overseas leases for advanced AI work, which can include model training, and these tech groups have been the biggest clients for data centers in Southeast Asia. Data centers unable to find non-Chinese clients could be forced to pull back supply, and it’s “difficult to find enough non-Chinese clients outside the US,” one Singapore-based group told the FT. While Nvidia hasn’t confirmed or denied its new rule, implementing it would ease criticism from U.S. lawmakers just as Chinese demand is growing.
What Nvidia told partners has come through verbal instructions, via sales and regional teams, and applies globally rather than just in Asia. Existing deals and leases are not changed, but new ones must comply. Nvidia’s whitelist more than halved its authorized Asian buyer count, which encouraged more Chinese groups to lease over other options, including smuggling. On top of this, Fleet Intelligence tracking is now required for Southeast Asian providers that want to become Nvidia Cloud Partners. All of these combined — whitelist, cap, and tracking — may act to alleviate U.S. concerns.
Among companies that have moved to renting, Moonshot has held discussions to rent capacity from neoclouds that host in Europe with Nvidia GPUs. Specifically, it’s looking for Nvidia Blackwell systems, which export controls bar from China; one source said the talks covered clusters of 8,000 or more Blackwell GPUs in Europe. These clusters would handle inference, serving models to end users, and the European talks for them happened after the White House said Moonshot accessed Blackwell chips through a facility in Thailand. The firm has been fervent about its intentions to secure more compute.
Moonshot isn't the only Chinese company looking to secure Nvidia chips for AI training. Tencent has a deal with Oracle to lease 100,000 GPUs in Southeast Asian data centers. ByteDance and Alibaba are also pursuing similar long-term leases, and most of these overseas data centers run chips like the forbidden B300. MiniMax, like Moonshot, also leases significant compute both at home and abroad.
The big reason is that domestic AI chip supply is simply not up to the task, although not for a lack of trying. Huawei is expected to hit 1.6 million chips this year, with about 1 million from Alibaba and Baidu, and 300,000 from Cambricon. Total supply this year will be up to 3.5 million, including about 1 million made overseas, against a demand that far exceeds 5 million. That number could more than double next year.
Part of the problem is that the export-compliant cards Chinese firms have been buying, mostly the RTX Pro 6000D, RTX Pro 5000, and RTX 5090, are mostly useful for simpler work such as prefill. Even so, the discontinued 6000D’s pricing in China has reportedly doubled. Huawei’s Ascend 910C outperforms them in most areas, but these lower-end options are still coveted, partly because of a preference for CUDA over Huawei’s CANN. Nvidia’s programming platform is supported by most AI frameworks and libraries, and much in-house code is optimized for it.
Then there’s the RTX Pro 5500, with 84GB of GDDR7 with ECC and 1,398 GB/s of memory bandwidth. The card runs on a full PCIe Gen 5 x16 interface, draws up to 600 W, and can be split into up to two MIG instances. That still leaves it well short of a B300, which has about 3.4 times the memory and 5.7 times the bandwidth, plus NVLink, which the 5500 lacks.
| What Chinese labs can buy vs. what they rent |  |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU | Memory | Bandwidth | Interconnect | Status for Chinese buyers | 
| RTX Pro 5500 | 84GB GDDR7 | 1.4 TB/s | PCIe Gen 5 x16 | Export-compliant; samples in December, deliveries from Q1 2027 | 
| H200 | 141GB HBM3E | 4.8 TB/s | NVLink | Licensed by the U.S. case by case; Beijing withholding approval for large-scale imports | 
| B300 | 288GB HBM3E | 8 TB/s | NVLink (1.8 TB/s) | Banned for sale to China; rented abroad | 
Indicated orders from China are not precise, but the total of over six million includes more than three million from ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent. The big three ordered at about $11,400 each, for a total sticker price over $35 billion. This is difficult to fill when there may be fewer than three million produced next year, and partners might only actually get 5% to 10% of the original ask. Starting in 2027, much of Nvidia’s TSMC capacity may shift to Rubin, taking more production, while the RTX Pro 5500’s early samples are due in December.
On the legal side, it’s currently easier to rent than to own as current U.S. law does not give regulators broad authority over overseas cloud access. The Remote Access Security Act (RASA), which would extend U.S. export controls to that area, has sailed through the House but has not yet passed the Senate. Those directly affected — neoclouds and related financiers — price in a possible ban regardless, which drives the upfront premium.
China’s side is not completely clean, either, with about 600,000 H200s reportedly stuck in storage in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to the mainland. Beijing is withholding approvals for large-volume imports such as this. Only relatively small quantities have come in during recent months, for some big internet companies, with others coming through intermediaries and indirect routes in small quantities. The price: over $900,000 for an eight-card H200 server in China at the end of last month, about 3x the cost a year ago. This is despite the fact that H200 sales are already under U.S. license.
The first test that will show how many cards will actually land occurs in Q1 2027, when the RTX Pro 5500 is expected in commercial deliveries. For rentals, whether or not the Remote Access Security Act is a factor depends on a Senate vote, which is not yet scheduled. Nvidia’s Q3 results come in soon, on Nov. 17, which could bring some illumination.
With CEO Jensen Huang under scrutiny lately over reports that he was targeted by an alleged Chinese spy, which Nvidia’s board is now investigating, he’s going to feel the heat even more just a day later, when lawmakers have asked him to attend a closed-door briefing. He’s been pushing for laxer controls and more access, so the assumed 51% rule will also be put to the test.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Anthropic acaba de lanzar sus dos modelos de IA más avanzados. Uno tendrá acceso general y el otro estará restringido
articles.text:
Que un modelo de inteligencia artificial sea capaz de resolver problemas extraordinariamente complejos no significa que todas sus capacidades estén al alcance de cualquiera. La diferencia puede estar en el precio, pero también en restricciones que determinan qué tareas puede realizar y cuáles quedan fuera de su alcance. Es una distinción especialmente importante cuando hablamos de programación, investigación científica o ciberseguridad, ámbitos en los que una misma tecnología puede tener aplicaciones muy diferentes. Y también nos obliga a mirar más allá de las cifras de rendimiento para entender qué estamos recibiendo realmente como usuarios.
Con esa diferencia de fondo, Anthropic ha presentado Claude Fable 5.2 y Claude Mythos 5.2, sus dos nuevas versiones de IA diseñadas para afrontar tareas técnicas de especial complejidad. Según la compañía, ambas mejoran en programación, razonamiento y análisis de imágenes respecto a sus predecesoras, además de generar respuestas hasta un 30% más rápido. Sin embargo, la particularidad de este lanzamiento no está únicamente en sus capacidades: aunque comparten el mismo modelo subyacente, Fable llega con disponibilidad general, mientras que Mythos queda reservado a usuarios y organizaciones que cumplen determinados requisitos de acceso.
La clave para entender esta división está en las barreras de seguridad que Anthropic ha incorporado a cada versión. Fable 5.2 incluye filtros que bloquean determinadas actividades de alto riesgo en ciberseguridad, como la generación de código para explotar vulnerabilidades, y buena parte de las relacionadas con investigación biológica. Mythos 5.2 utiliza el mismo modelo sin algunas de esas restricciones, precisamente para que profesionales verificados puedan trabajar en esos ámbitos. Esto no significa que Mythos permita realizar cualquier operación ni que tenga una inteligencia superior en términos generales: la diferencia está en las salvaguardas aplicadas y en el acceso a determinadas capacidades.
Dos modelos, una misma tecnología y diferentes límites
Para quienes quieran utilizar Fable 5.2, hay una primera aclaración importante: disponibilidad general no equivale a acceso gratuito. Anthropic permite utilizarlo en sus plataformas y mediante proveedores como Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud y Microsoft Azure, mientras que en Claude depende del plan contratado y no está incluido en Free. La compañía ofrece temporalmente condiciones especiales para determinados suscriptores de pago. Los desarrolladores también pueden integrarlo mediante una API que cuesta ocho dólares por millón de tokens de entrada y 40 dólares por millón de salida.
Con Mythos 5.2, la situación es distinta: no basta con contratar un plan o pagar por su utilización. Anthropic reserva el acceso directo a profesionales y organizaciones que superen un proceso de verificación, pensado para actividades como la búsqueda de vulnerabilidades informáticas o la investigación biomédica. Los interesados pueden solicitarlo mediante sus programas Cyber Verification y Life Sciences Verification, pero presentar la solicitud no garantiza la aprobación. Existe, además, otra vía para clientes de Claude Enterprise: utilizar Claude Security, una herramienta que incorpora Mythos para analizar código, sin que eso implique disponer libremente del modelo.
Anthropic también ha puesto a prueba hasta dónde puede llegar Fable 5.2 cuando se enfrenta a proyectos que requieren varios días de trabajo. En uno de sus experimentos, el modelo coordinó más de 1.000 subagentes durante ocho días para desarrollar un sistema operativo prototipo que, según la compañía, puede arrancar en un portátil. La empresa también le atribuye la resolución de dos problemas abiertos de física teórica relacionados con los agujeros negros. Los resultados aparecen en dos prepublicaciones científicas, aunque eso no equivale a una validación definitiva mediante revisión por pares.
Más allá de las pruebas publicadas por Anthropic, también tenemos evaluaciones independientes para medir el rendimiento de Fable 5.2. Una de ellas procede de Vals AI, que lo ha situado en primera posición entre 36 modelos en su índice v2.2, con un 71,31%. Por detrás aparecen Claude Sonnet 5.5, con un 70,85%, y Gemini 4 Carbon, con un 70,45%. Este índice reúne pruebas profesionales de programación, finanzas, derecho y fiscalidad, ponderadas según su peso en la economía estadounidense. Las diferencias son pequeñas, por lo que el primer puesto no demuestra una superioridad general ni concluyente.
El lanzamiento también refleja una decisión que va más allá del rendimiento: Anthropic ha optado por ofrecer diferentes condiciones de uso para una misma tecnología según los riesgos que atribuye a determinadas aplicaciones. Es una forma de permitir el acceso a capacidades avanzadas sin abrir indiscriminadamente todas sus posibilidades. La propia compañía reconoce, sin embargo, que las evaluaciones de seguridad previas al lanzamiento no permiten anticipar todos los posibles fallos. La cuestión será comprobar cómo funcionan esas barreras en la práctica y hasta qué punto consiguen prevenir usos perjudiciales sin obstaculizar trabajos legítimos.

articles.title: Apple começa a cobrar por uso extra de IA em apps profissionais • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple começa a cobrar por uso extra de IA em apps profissionais
Pacote adicional custa cerca de R$ 300 e permite continuar usando recursos de IA após o limite mensal.
A Apple começou a cobrar pelo uso adicional de recursos de inteligência artificial em seus aplicativos profissionais. A novidade estreou na plataforma de áudio Logic Pro, que agora oferece um pacote avulso de US$ 50 (cerca de R$ 300) para usuários que esgotarem a cota mensal incluída no software.
O pacote, chamado pela Apple de Pacotes de Utilização de Inteligência, passa a ser consumido após o término do limite mensal. O Creator Studio custa R$ 39,90 por mês no Brasil.
De acordo com o 9to5Mac, a cobrança por enquanto é restrita ao Logic Pro, mas a Apple já indicou que o modelo chegará a outros aplicativos do Creator Studio, como Final Cut Pro e ferramentas do iWork. Além do Brasil, esse pacote adicional está disponível na Alemanha, Canadá, Estados Unidos, França, Índia, México e Reino Unido.
Ferramentas de inteligência artificial têm gerado custos substanciais às empresas de tecnologia atualmente e, por isso, grande parte dos serviços que as utilizam eventualmente adicionam planos para estender os limites de uso. A Apple, no entanto, optou por uma compra avulsa, em vez de uma assinatura mensal.
No Logic Pro, o pacote custa cerca de R$ 300 e adiciona o saldo à Conta Apple utilizada no iCloud. O limite extra não pode ser compartilhado por meio do Compartilhamento Familiar e não substitui o limite gratuito. Assim, segundo a Apple, enquanto o usuário possui acesso á franquia original, o pacote permanece intacto.
Caso parte do saldo comprado não seja usada no mesmo mês, o restante continua disponível. Segundo os termos da Apple, os créditos podem ser acumulados e têm validade de 12 meses a partir da compra.
A cobrança está ligada principalmente às ferramentas que não conseguem executar todo o processamento diretamente no aparelho. Em eventos anteriores, a empresa explicou que recursos mais pesados do Apple Intelligence podem recorrer à infraestrutura em nuvem da Apple e estariam sujeitos a limites de uso.
Segundo o The Verge, no Logic Pro o limite impacta, por exemplo, o novo assistente de IA do aplicativo, que promete entender o projeto e ajudar em tarefas durante a produção musical.
Quando a franquia disponível acaba, essas funções devem ficar indisponíveis até a renovação do ciclo mensal. Com o novo pacote, o usuário passa a ter a opção de continuar usando os recursos sem esperar pelo mês seguinte.
Os termos também preveem redução de velocidade ou restrições em casos de uso automatizado, excessivo ou considerado abusivo.
A expectativa é que a mesma fórmula de pacotes seja expandida futuramente para o público geral em ferramentas nativas dos sistemas operacionais da Apple. Portanto, podemos ver, futuramente, esses limites aplicados em outros serviços usados no dia a dia.

articles.title: On me voit, on me voit plus ! Les haut-parleurs PlayStation Pulse repoussés à quelques jours de leur lancement
articles.text:
Attendues cette semaine, les enceintes sans fil Pulse Elevate de PlayStation n’arriveront finalement pas à l’heure. Sony vient d’annoncer un report de dernière minute, sans communiquer de nouvelle date de commercialisation.
Mauvaise surprise pour les joueurs qui avaient déjà fait la place sur leur bureau pour accueillir les nouvelles enceintes sans fil de PlayStation. Alors que leur arrivée en boutiques était programmée pour ce 12 novembre 2026, soit dans quelques jours à peine, les Pulse Elevate ne seront finalement pas au rendez-vous. Une annonce de dernière minute, relayée notamment par nos confrères de The Verge.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Un retard de dernière minute pour les Pulse Elevate
Pour justifier ce contretemps, Sony évoque un problème rencontré durant la phase de production. Dans un message publié sur son PlayStation Blog, le constructeur explique : « Dans le cadre de nos tests de qualité continus sur les enceintes Pulse Elevate, nous avons identifié un problème de production et avons pris la décision de reporter leur lancement. »
Sony ajoute que ce délai supplémentaire doit lui permettre de garantir « une expérience conforme aux ambitions », avant de présenter ses excuses aux joueurs. En revanche, aucune nouvelle fenêtre de commercialisation n’a été communiquée. Il faudra donc patienter encore un peu avant de connaître la nouvelle date de lancement.
Pour rappel, les Pulse Elevate représentent une première pour Sony Interactive Entertainment, puisqu’il s’agit des premières enceintes sans fil développées par le constructeur. Elles sont compatibles avec la PS5 évidemment, mais aussi avec les PC et Mac, sans oublier le PlayStation Portal.
Des enceintes PlayStation à 219,99 euros qui se font encore attendre
Avec ses Pulse Elevate, Sony mise notamment sur des transducteurs magnétiques planaires, des woofers intégrés et sa technologie sans fil PlayStation Link (déjà étrennée sur les écouteurs Pulse Explore notamment), qui se veut particulièrement réactive.
Un microphone est également intégré à l’enceinte droite, avec une réduction des bruits parasites assistée par la désormais indispensable IA.
Les Pulse Elevate profitent également d’un petit côté nomade, avec une batterie rechargeable, et la possibilité de fonctionner en Bluetooth. De quoi les utiliser au-delà d'un simple bureau gaming.
Les intéressés devront donc prendre leur mal en patience, alors même que des exemplaires review venaient tout juste de parvenir chez certains spécialistes, notamment outre-Atlantique. Côté tarif, les Pulse Elevate s’inscrivent dans la droite lignée du reste de la gamme audio PlayStation 5, avec un prix de 220 euros la paire.

articles.title: Lista de códigos de Free Fire para ganar diamantes y skins gratis este 9 de noviembre de 2026
articles.text:
Garena difundió una nueva lista de códigos de Free Fire para este lunes 9 de noviembre de 2026, con claves que pueden habilitar recompensas sin costo, como diamantes, skins de armas, trajes, cajas y artículos vinculados con campañas temporales.
Como ocurre cada día, los jugadores deben ingresar las secuencias desde el portal oficial de la empresa y con la cuenta habitual del juego. Ningún código asegura una recompensa determinada: aunque algunos pueden otorgar diamantes, otros habilitan objetos cosméticos o pueden dejar de funcionar si ya vencieron o alcanzaron su límite de uso.
Qué códigos de Free Fire están disponibles este 9 de noviembre
La lista para este lunes reúne más de 15 combinaciones. Cada una admite un solo canje por cuenta y debe escribirse en mayúsculas, sin espacios. Si el sistema informa un error, es posible que el código no esté vigente, haya sido utilizado o no se encuentre habilitado para el servidor del jugador.
- ZZZ76NT3PDSH.
- TX4SC2VUNPKF.
- J3ZKQ57Z2P2P.
- Q8M4K7L2VR9J.
- FFPLUFBVSLOT.
- N7QK5L3MRP9J.
- MCPW3D28VZD6.
- FFWCTKX2P5NQ.
- WD2ATK3ZEA55.
- P3LX6V9TM2QH.
- V427K98RUCHZ.
- S5PL7M2LRV8K.
- RD3TZK7WME65.
- E9QH6K4LNP7V.
- TFX9J3Z2RP64.
- RHTG9VOLTDWP.
- ZRW3J4N8VX56.
La vigencia de estas claves puede variar durante el día. Garena establece condiciones diferentes para cada campaña, por lo que un código puede funcionar en una región y no estar disponible en otra. Hay secuencias que se agotan tras alcanzar un número determinado de canjes.
Dónde se ingresan los códigos para reclamar las recompensas en Free Fire
El procedimiento debe realizarse únicamente en Garena Rewards Redemption Site, la página oficial de canje de recompensas de la compañía. Allí se vincula el código con el perfil que cada jugador utiliza dentro de Free Fire, sin necesidad de descargar programas externos ni instalar archivos adicionales.
Antes de iniciar el trámite, conviene comprobar que la cuenta tenga una vinculación activa. El portal permite acceder con opciones que pueden incluir Google, Facebook, Apple, Huawei o VK, según la región. Las cuentas de invitado no suelen ser aptas para este sistema.
Cómo canjear un código en Free Fire
Después de ingresar al sitio oficial, el usuario debe seleccionar el método con el que tiene asociada su cuenta de juego. Es importante revisar el perfil antes de continuar, porque el premio queda ligado al usuario que inició sesión y no puede transferirse después a otra cuenta.
El segundo paso consiste en buscar el campo destinado a los códigos de recompensa. Allí se debe copiar una de las claves, pegarla sin espacios o escribirla de forma manual. Cada código solo puede utilizarse una vez por cuenta.
Qué hacer si el portal muestra un mensaje de error o no permite el canje
Un mensaje de error puede indicar que el código venció, que sus cupos se agotaron o que no está disponible en el servidor correspondiente. Puede ser por un error al transcribir la combinación. Las letras O e I pueden confundirse con los números 0 y 1, una diferencia suficiente para impedir el canje.
La alternativa es revisar cada carácter y probar con otra de las claves publicadas. Copiar los códigos desde una fuente confiable reduce el riesgo de equivocaciones. La región de la cuenta define qué campañas y recompensas pueden activarse, de modo que una secuencia válida para otros jugadores puede no funcionar en todos los países.
Si el sistema confirma la operación, los premios se envían al buzón interno del juego. La entrega puede aparecer de inmediato, aunque Garena contempla un plazo de hasta 24 horas para acreditar diamantes, trajes, skins de armas, cajas u otros objetos.
Durante ese período, el usuario puede ingresar a Free Fire y revisar el apartado de correo o mensajes del perfil. Si el objeto no aparece tras el plazo previsto, corresponde verificar otra vez que la confirmación haya sido emitida para la cuenta correcta y que el código no haya mostrado restricciones de servidor.
Cuáles pautas de seguridad seguir para evitar riesgos
Las páginas, aplicaciones y supuestos generadores que ofrecen diamantes ilimitados o skins sin costo pueden solicitar credenciales, permisos sobre el teléfono o la descarga de archivos no verificados. Esos mecanismos exponen la cuenta a accesos no autorizados y pueden comprometer datos personales almacenados en el dispositivo.
Asimismo, el uso de herramientas que modifican el funcionamiento del juego puede derivar en sanciones. Las cuentas que utilizan programas no autorizados, generadores de recursos o alteraciones de partidas pueden ser suspendidas o bloqueadas.

articles.text:
Monday, November 9th 2026
GTA VI Game Data Suggests PSSR Update With 120 Hz Support and PS5 Pro "High CPU Frequency Mode"
With the GTA VI launch around the corner, more and more information has begun to surface about the upcoming game. The latest news comes from GTAForums user Tex2, who analyzed the GTA VI PS5 metadata, who claims that GTA VI will launch alongside a newer version of PSSR. The biggest takeaways from this update are that the new PSSR game mode improves both the framerate capabilities of the PlayStation 5 and manages to eke out some more CPU performance out of the PlayStation 5. 
The metadata lists PSSR (or MFSR, by Sony's internal references) version 13.60, which builds on the 13.00A found in Assassin's Creed Shadows and Cyberpunk 2077, and the new version will apparently include a 120 Hz mode that drops support for VRR. It may also include a 40 FPS mode as a stop-gap to make up for the lack of VRR, but that hasn't been confirmed by the metadata. It will also enable a CPU High Frequency mode on the PlayStation 5, which may be necessary to enable higher frame rates in GTA VI.

articles.title: 31 ans d'agacement : Windows 11 teste une option pour faire taire les touches rémanentes
articles.text:
Cinq appuis rapides sur la touche Maj, et une fenêtre s’invite par-dessus la partie ou le document en cours pour proposer d’activer les touches rémanentes. Le scénario se rejoue à l’identique, ou presque, depuis Windows 95. Microsoft teste désormais, dans les versions d’essai de Windows 11, la case qui permet de ne plus jamais revoir cette boîte de dialogue.
La faute à un flipper de 1995
Les touches rémanentes rendent un vrai service : elles maintiennent virtuellement Ctrl ou Maj enfoncées, comme une pédale qui resterait appuyée, le temps de presser la touche suivante. La fonction s’adresse à celles et ceux qui tapent d’un seul doigt ou à l’aide d’une tige tenue en bouche. Les touches filtres, elles, ignorent les frappes brèves ou répétées pour amortir les tremblements. Deux raccourcis les déclenchent depuis trois décennies : cinq appuis sur Maj pour les premières, la touche Maj droite maintenue huit secondes pour les secondes.
Lire aussi : Windows 11 27H2 pourrait être la mise à jour majeure que vous attendez tous
Charles Oppermann, arrivé chez Microsoft en 1994 pour piloter l’accessibilité de Windows, raconte avoir écrit ces boîtes de dialogue début 1995. Les enfants de Brad Silverberg, le patron de Windows 95, activaient la fonction à répétition en martelant la touche Maj dans Space Cadet Pinball, le flipper culte de l’époque. La fenêtre de confirmation est née là, présentée dans la documentation de l’époque comme une « précaution contre l’usage accidentel ». Son équipe avait même envisagé une case pour ne plus poser la question ; elle a préféré garder les options d’accessibilité bien en vue.
Une case minuscule, trente et un ans plus tard
Les versions d’essai diffusées le 6 novembre, bâties sur Windows 11 26H2, ajoutent au dialogue des touches rémanentes une case à cocher inédite, libellée « Never turn on Sticky Keys with this shortcut » dans l’interface anglaise. Une fois cochée, le raccourci cesse définitivement d’ouvrir la fenêtre. Les touches filtres reçoivent leur équivalent. Le déploiement s’effectue par vagues au sein du programme de test, sans date encore pour le grand public.
L’option existait en réalité depuis toujours, enfouie dans les réglages d’accessibilité du clavier, où il fallait penser à aller la chercher. Chez Microsoft, une ingénieure de l’équipe Windows glisse d’ailleurs que « ça a toujours été possible ». La nouveauté tient à l’endroit : la case s’affiche au moment exact de l’agacement, dans la fenêtre fautive. Par défaut, rien ne change d’ailleurs pour les personnes qui dépendent de ces fonctions, puisque la question continue de s’afficher tant qu’on ne l’a pas congédiée.

articles.title: On theCUBE Pod: Midterms send shockwaves through AI market - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
On theCUBE Pod: Blue wave sends AI stock plunging
The very blue results of last week’s midterms have sent technology investors into a tailspin.
With many successful candidates running on platforms opposing data centers and calling for greater restrictions on artificial intelligence, investors anticipate a slowdown in AI spending. Tech stocks fell, with a collective loss of $2.5 trillion in market cap, and the Nasdaq dropped more than 5.5%.
“Yesterday was a bloodbath,” said John Furrier (pictured), executive analyst for theCUBE Research. “It was brutal here and the tech stocks got pounded. 41 states had data centers on the ballot. They all lost or won, depending how you look at it. Now it’s so mainstream, it’s a political football. So you’re starting to see the reality of AI. It’s hitting everybody. Everyone is impacted.”
On the latest episode of theCUBE Pod, Furrier and Dave Vellante (pictured, right), chief analyst for theCUBE Research, discussed the fallout from the midterms and whether or not AI companies will really suffer in the long term. They also explored who will own the “system of intelligence” that will govern enterprise AI.
Midterms puts AI investors on shaky ground
After the “bloodbath” last week, the question remains: Can enterprise AI pay for the boom? Despite the shockwaves from the midterms, theCUBE’s researchers are predicting a longer path toward monetization. A recent analysis identified 2029 as the highest-risk year for the AI bubble.
“There’s a clock in terms of the data center monetization and financing and how long it takes to build data centers,” Vellante said. “We know anybody who can sell GPUs is making money but the enterprises aren’t yet self-funding. I had said that by 2026, this year, you’re going to start to see clear evidence of monetization in the enterprise. I think you see it, but you’re seeing it within tech companies.”
Tech companies are applying AI more effectively, according to Vellante, which should not come as a surprise. He thinks the tech titans are in a solid position while neoclouds are taking on a greater share of risk by pioneering a new software model, although not all of them will make it in the long term.
A GPU-based AI economy will shift in the next several years, Furrier believes, which could lead to surprising winners and losers.
“Supermicro [Inc.], good numbers, [Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Arista Networks, Marvell Technology Inc.],” he noted. “My take is this: the infrastructure is evolving beyond GPU-centric computing. Networking, optics, memory, storage, power efficiency. System-level architecture is becoming the strategic advantage, and those bottlenecks are being solved by the companies I just mentioned. You saw the news that Marvell closed a $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum.”
The stock market plunge shows that not everyone is going to make it through the AI era’s eventual slowdown. Public opinion on data centers is mixed, to say the least, so companies will need to establish a foothold in the developing system of AI intelligence to remain competitive.
“Neoclouds like CoreWeave are going to make it through,” Vellante said. “They’re the first movers and they’ve got some quality advantages but they’re going to go through some pain. Hyperscalers are like an ATM. They could dial it down at any point in time … but right now it’s all about growth, it’s about footprint, it’s about market share.”
Predicting the AI era’s winners
Who owns the “system of intelligence”? This layer, which will bridge the gap between intelligent agents and the data systems they depend on, appears to still be in play. Palantir Technologies Inc. has the ontology that could give it the edge, while Snowflake Inc. and Databricks Inc. are still developing the operational systems — though Vellante sees the latter as having one of the best strategies.
“You need determinism to own that system of intelligence,” Vellante said. “So I think it’s wide open. Right now, I think Ali Ghodsi [chief executive officer of Databricks] has the best vision. He’s going after the client surface, he’s going after the system of intelligence, he’s going after the governance catalog, he’s going after the agent action layer, and he’s partnering … with all the frontier model vendors. Whether or not they can pull it off, we’ll see.”
Frontier models are the “wild card,” as Vellante puts it, but at the moment, all the tech companies are trying to get a slice of the pie. Despite the recent market shakeups, Furrier sees AI-native enterprises as the ultimate result of this current period of growth.
“The AI-native enterprise or businesses is going to be the model,” Furrier said. “Everybody wins in that one. Compute providers, hyperscalers, the data platforms that are on the right side, and the application companies, which are basically going to be agentic. That’s going to be the winners on the profit concentration. The control point … it’s not going to be the models, it’s going to be data and context, and the agents will be the proof point.”

articles.title: Los ciberataques a frigoríficos de supermercados europeos dieron la vuelta al mundo. Francia acaba de señalar a un responsable
articles.text:
Cuando pensamos en un ciberataque, es fácil imaginar datos robados, servicios bloqueados o pantallas que dejan de responder. Pero algunos sistemas conectados no se limitan a gestionar información: también controlan máquinas de las que dependen actividades tan cotidianas como conservar alimentos. Los equipos de refrigeración comercial son un ejemplo, porque sus parámetros pueden gestionarse mediante controladores electrónicos y conexiones remotas. Lo ocurrido en Francia ha mostrado hasta qué punto una intrusión puede trasladarse del entorno digital al físico, con mercancías que dejan de ser aptas para el consumo y daños en las instalaciones.
Los hechos se remontan a la noche del 11 al 12 de octubre, cuando los atacantes manipularon sistemas de refrigeración en Francia. Según el informe de las autoridades recogido por Reuters, la campaña tuvo como objetivo unos 700 establecimientos comerciales, principalmente supermercados, aunque también hubo carnicerías y centros de procesamiento de alimentos. El 9 de noviembre, el Gobierno francés dio un paso más al atribuir oficialmente aquella ofensiva a la Guardia Revolucionaria iraní.
El informe conjunto de los servicios franceses de inteligencia y ciberseguridad identifica a Shahid Kaveh como la unidad que habría ejecutado el sabotaje. Los investigadores relacionaron la infraestructura utilizada con otras operaciones atribuidas al grupo, detectaron semejanzas en los procedimientos de intrusión y encontraron rastros de persa y direcciones IP asociadas a dispositivos situados en Irán. El documento también identifica a tres presuntos implicados: Hamid Reza Lashgarian, Mahdi Lashgarian y Reza Salarvand. Estos son los indicios sobre los que las autoridades sustentan su atribución.
Cómo se produjo el ataque
Para entender cómo fue posible, hay que mirar al sistema que controla el frío, no a la puerta del congelador. Muchos equipos comerciales incorporan interfaces de administración que permiten regular la temperatura y gestionar a distancia tareas como el desescarche, el proceso que elimina el hielo acumulado. Según la Fiscalía de París, los intrusos accedieron remotamente a esos controles, activaron ciclos de desescarche anormales y prolongados y desactivaron alertas de seguridad. Algunos dispositivos afectados eran antiguos o utilizaban software desactualizado, aunque no se ha acreditado públicamente qué fallo concreto permitió acceder a cada instalación.
Las consecuencias se hicieron visibles en los pasillos de los supermercados. Reuters documentó cómo los empleados retiraban carne estropeada y helados derretidos para arrojarlos a grandes contenedores, mientras algunos equipos alcanzaban temperaturas tan elevadas que llegaron a incendiarse. El informe francés contabiliza al menos 15 incendios, además de importantes pérdidas de mercancía. Todavía no existe un balance económico definitivo de toda la campaña, pero Thierry Cotillard, presidente de Les Mousquetaires, el grupo propietario de Intermarché, estimó que el coste conjunto para el sector en Francia podría ascender a varias decenas de millones de euros.
El problema tampoco quedó limitado a la campaña francesa de octubre. La agencia europea ENISA confirmó una nueva oleada los días 1 y 2 de noviembre, y Reuters informó de más de 100 establecimientos afectados en Europa. En Francia, un ataque contra equipos de tres instalaciones del servicio de sangre EFS obligó a proteger o trasladar reservas de plasma, sin pérdidas de productos ni consecuencias sanitarias, según la entidad. En Estados Unidos se investigan como posibles ciberataques los fallos registrados en agosto en al menos seis establecimientos de abastecimiento militar. No está demostrado que todos estos incidentes tengan un mismo responsable.
La respuesta de Francia ya ha pasado del terreno técnico al diplomático. El ministro de Exteriores, Jean-Noël Barrot, ha convocado al embajador iraní y ha anunciado que París promoverá sanciones europeas contra los responsables, unas medidas que todavía no deben darse por aprobadas. En paralelo, la Fiscalía ha solicitado órdenes internacionales de detención contra los presuntos implicados. La misión iraní ante Naciones Unidas no respondió a las solicitudes de comentarios de Reuters. Más allá de la investigación, el caso recuerda que la protección de equipos industriales conectados también es una cuestión de seguridad física.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to congressional committee over affair with alleged Chinese spy — says recent reports raise concerns over security protocols and ties to Chinese intelligence
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to Congress over affair with alleged Chinese spy — says recent reports raise concerns over security protocols and ties to Chinese intelligence
"The letter expresses concerns over NVIDIA’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and Mr. Huang’s reported ties to a Chinese intelligence-linked executive of a Singapore-based data center company."
Less than 24 hours after he admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese spy, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been asked to appear before the House Select Committee on China. The Committee issued a letter today, signed by Rep. Brian J. Mast (R-FL), Rep. John Moolenaar (R-MI), and Rep. Eric A. Crawford (R-AK). An X post featuring the letter states that the letter "expresses concerns over NVIDIA’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and Mr. Huang’s reported ties to a Chinese intelligence-linked executive of a Singapore-based data center company."
"Dear Mr. Huang: We are writing to request that you appear before our committees for a joint, closed-door briefing on NVIDIA’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and your interactions with a publicly reported People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence asset: Megaspeed executive Alice Huang," the letter begins.
It goes on to say that recent reports surrounding the affair "raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information. "The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk."
The closed-door hearing is set for November 18, 2026; whether Huang will attend remains unclear. The letter also allows for Huang to set an alternative date during while the 119th Congress is still in session.
On Sunday, Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed. It is alleged that the latter was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information and help China get its hands on Nvidia's AI GPUs, the most powerful of which are banned from export to the country by Washington. Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling $2 billion of AI chips into China.
In a statement to Nvidia employees, Jensen Huang said, "To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." As Huang's statement noted, Nvidia has opened an independent investigation into its CEO's conduct regarding the national security concerns the story has laid bare. The board of directors stated, "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."
Nvidia shares dropped by around 5% in early trading, but have since recovered some of their losses. The company has rocketed to a market capitalization of over $4 trillion as the global hardware leader of the AI boom. Its powerful GPUs are in high demand for both the training of AI models and inference.

articles.title: Black Friday : le pack Nintendo Switch 2 avec Zelda Ocarina of Time est 100 € moins cher que les prix officiels
articles.text:
Sorti le 5 novembre, le remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time est déjà présenté comme l’un des plus beaux jeux de la Switch 2. Quatre jours plus tard, Joybuy l’associe à la console dans un pack à moins de 470 €, de quoi s’équiper d’un coup avant les fêtes et les offres du Black Friday.
Ce pack réunit la Nintendo Switch 2 en version européenne et The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time en version française, le remake du classique de la Nintendo 64 publié pour les 40 ans de la saga. La console est vendue 499,99 € en France depuis la hausse de prix décidée par Nintendo en septembre, et le jeu 69,99 € en boîte sur la boutique officielle.
Joybuy affiche l’ensemble à 469,99 €, soit 100 € de moins que ces deux prix officiels cumulés, sur un produit vendu et expédié par Joybuy, avec la possibilité de payer en trois fois sans frais via Klarna.
Nintendo Switch 2 + Zelda: Ocarina of Time à 469,99 €
Pourquoi choisir ce pack Switch 2 + Zelda ?
- Le remake d’Ocarina of Time, avec des graphismes refaits, des cinématiques doublées et une bande-son réenregistrée par un orchestre.
- Une Switch 2 plus puissante et mieux finie que la première génération.
- Un grand écran de 7,9 pouces, aussi bien en mode portable que sur le téléviseur.
Une console plus musclée qu’au premier jour
La Switch 2 reprend le principe hybride qui a fait le succès de sa devancière, mais avec des moyens nettement supérieurs. Son écran LCD de 7,9 pouces affiche une image plus grande et plus fluide, ses 256 Go de stockage évitent de jongler avec les jeux installés, et les Joy-Con 2 s’aimantent désormais à la console, avec un mode souris inédit. Dans son test de la Nintendo Switch 2, Clubic la décrivait comme une console plus puissante et plus soignée, sans pour autant révolutionner la formule.
Quelques réserves demeurent. Nintendo a fait le choix d’une dalle LCD plutôt qu’OLED, et la technologie des joysticks n’a pas changé, ce qui laisse planer le doute sur le risque de dérive à long terme. La console reste enfin compatible avec la grande majorité des jeux Switch, un atout pour ceux qui possèdent déjà une ludothèque.
Ocarina of Time, un classique entièrement repensé
Bien plus qu’un lifting graphique
Le remake ne se contente pas de rafraîchir les textures. Les cinématiques sont désormais entièrement doublées, de nouveaux dialogues ont été ajoutés, et les musiques de Koji Kondo ont été réenregistrées avec un orchestre symphonique, un aspect que le Journal du Geek place au-dessus de tout le reste. Le jeu tourne à 60 images par seconde, en mode portable comme sur le téléviseur.
Une maniabilité enfin moderne
Les commandes ont aussi été revues en profondeur : la caméra se contrôle librement, le saut dispose d’une touche dédiée, et un journal de quête garde la trace des objectifs en cours, pratique pour reprendre une partie après plusieurs jours. Les menus, longtemps pénibles dans la version d’origine, se montrent beaucoup plus agréables, ce qui rend l’aventure accessible à ceux qui la découvrent comme à ceux qui la connaissent par cœur.
✅ Les points forts
- Un remake salué par la critique, techniquement soigné
- Une Switch 2 plus puissante avec 256 Go de stockage
- Grand écran de 7,9 pouces
- Compatibilité avec les jeux de la première Switch
❌ Les limites
- Écran LCD et non OLED
- Joysticks sans nouvelle technologie anti-dérive
- Un remake jugé un peu sage par certains connaisseurs
Nintendo Switch 2 + Zelda: Ocarina of Time à 469,99 €
Ce pack s’adresse aussi bien aux nouveaux venus sur Switch 2 qu’aux nostalgiques de la Nintendo 64 qui attendaient une bonne raison de franchir le pas. À 469,99 €, il revient presque au prix de la console seule chez de nombreux marchands, ce qui en fait une idée cadeau tout trouvée pour les fêtes.

articles.title: Neha Nagar wants to help people take control of their financial future through her debut book
articles.text:
Neha Nagar wants to help people take control of their financial future through her debut book
'Simple Money Serious Wealth', which sold over 3,000 copies on launch day, is another feather in the cap of this popular finance educator and content creator.
Finance educator and content creator Neha Nagar recently launched her debut book Simple Money Serious Wealth: How to Turn Ordinary Income into Extraordinary Net Worth.
Neha, who has been in the finance field for over a decade and in content creation for about seven years, decided to don the role of an author when she realised that, while people in India know more about money today than earlier, they aren’t necessarily good at managing it.
“Almost everyone has watched a video on SIPs, insurance or tax-saving. They have information, but they don't have a structure. People start investing with excitement, but when markets fall or an unexpected expense comes up, they stop. Often, it's because they never had a plan behind that investment,” Neha tells YourStory.
While a social media platform helps disseminate information, it has its structural limitations. A book, on the other hand, gives the author the space to explain an entire concept elaborately.
“We wanted to help people build their own financial plan, choose products that actually suit their lives, and understand how to structure their money better. For me, social media can introduce people to money. But this book is about teaching them how to manage it,” says the New Delhi-based author.
Her debut book Simple Money Serious Wealth was published on October 24. It sold over 3,000 copies in the first 24 hours, according to a post on the author's Instagram account.
“At a bookstore in the city, we saw people in the 60–70 years age group picking up the book. Some were buying it for themselves, while others wanted it for their children and grandchildren. We also saw students, young professionals, working women, and parents,” she says.
Educating a nation of billions
While embarking upon the book project, Neha thought that having explained finance through videos for seven years, writing a book would be a piece of cake. But she soon realised that was not the case.
“A book has to work even when the author isn’t around. In my videos, if someone doesn't understand something, they can leave a comment and I can respond. But when someone is reading a book alone, every step has to be clear,” says Neha, who was recognised by Hurun India as India's most-followed female personal finance influencer in 2025.
The creator-turned-author believes India is still far away from reaching financial literacy. There are many reasons for this, she says.
One, our education system never teaches students how to manage salary, calculate insurance requirements, save taxes, or plan for retirement.
The second reason is that money isn’t discussed openly in many Indian households. “So, one goes from never being made aware of finance to suddenly stumbling upon an information overload on social media. That transition makes it very hard for people to identify needful information from noise,” she elaborates.
The ultimate reason is fear, says Neha. Many Indians still associate the stock market with gambling. Due to this notion, they do not make attempts to understand different investment options, and a lot of money remains in savings accounts without a clear purpose.
“My goal with Simple Money Serious Wealth is to help people understand their own money, make informed decisions, and take control of their financial future. Because financial independence isn’t just about how much you earn; it’s about how confidently you can manage what you earn,” she says.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Cómo el streaming de deportes y los videojuegos cambiaron el tipo de TV que queremos tener
articles.text:
La conexión a internet es cada vez más estable, por lo que el reto de las marcas está orientado a la calidad de la visualización y el rendimiento de las pantallas para diferentes formatos, para sacarle todo el provecho a las prestaciones de dispositivos externos y suscripciones.
Por qué el deporte en vivo exige 120Hz y paneles OLED
Una pantalla estándar de 60Hz refresca la imagen sesenta veces por segundo, un parámetro suficiente para la televisión analógica, pero insuficiente ante los cambios rápidos de cámara y los pases largos de un partido. El resultado es un efecto estela conocido como motion blur.
Los televisores con 120Hz o 144Hz nativos duplican o triplican esa tasa de refresco, lo que permite que los movimientos rápidos de un balón o de un auto de carreras se vean nítidos. A esto se suma el tiempo de respuesta de los paneles OLED, cuyos píxeles cambian de color en menos de un milisegundo, lo que elimina casi por completo el desenfoque de movimiento.
Ese salto de nitidez explica por qué el fútbol, el automovilismo y los torneos de e-sports en títulos como EA Sports FC impulsaron la renovación de televisores en los hogares: a mayor velocidad de refresco, menor distorsión visual en las jugadas rápidas y más precisión para seguir la pelota o el movimiento del juego en tiempo real.
Para evitar el desgaste prematuro de los diodos por marcadores o barras estáticas de información, los equipos modernos incorporan mecanismos de desplazamiento de píxeles (pixel shift) que neutralizan el riesgo de marcas permanentes en pantalla.
Las exigencias también están en los puertos de entrada
Los videojuegos competitivos y las plataformas interactivas requieren que la acción del control se refleje de inmediato en la pantalla. Eso modificó el diseño de los puertos traseros del televisor.
Los puertos HDMI 2.1 se volvieron obligatorios para transmitir resolución 4K a 120 imágenes por segundo sin pérdida de datos. El Modo Automático de Baja Latencia (ALLM) detecta cuando se enciende una consola o una aplicación de juego y apaga el procesamiento visual secundario para reducir el retraso al mínimo. La revisión de Smart TVs hoy exige priorizar estos puertos junto con tiempos de respuesta inferiores a los 15 milisegundos.
La Frecuencia de Actualización Variable (VRR), presente en tecnologías como G-Sync o FreeSync, sincroniza los hercios del televisor con la consola o la computadora y evita que la imagen se rompa durante las jugadas de mayor velocidad.
El brillo también entró en la ecuación. Los paneles Mini-LED y OLED desplazaron a los LCD tradicionales porque ofrecen negros profundos o brillos extremos, necesarios tanto para un partido bajo el sol del mediodía como para un videojuego ambientado en una escena oscura. El soporte para Dolby Vision y HDR10+ se consolidó como estándar para mapear el color escena por escena.
Procesadores con IA y el consumo en varias pantallas a la vez
El hardware interno del televisor hoy importa tanto como el panel. Los chips con inteligencia artificial reescalan señales de streaming de baja calidad y estabilizan transmisiones deportivas en vivo comprimidas, mientras que sistemas operativos como Google TV, WebOS o Tizen permiten abrir aplicaciones pesadas de streaming y plataformas de cloud gaming sin hardware externo.
Datos de la consultora Deloitte sobre audiencias digitales señalan que más del 70% de los jóvenes de las generaciones Z y Millennial utiliza una segunda pantalla mientras mira un partido en el televisor principal, para revisar mapas de calor, estadísticas tácticas o transmisiones paralelas de creadores en Twitch o Discord.
Esa multitarea exige notebooks con tarjetas gráficas dedicadas y al menos 16 gigabytes de memoria RAM, además de sistemas de ventilación de doble cámara que eviten caídas de rendimiento.
