articles.title: FritzOS 8.50 und 8.51: Was im Update für Fritzboxen steckt – und welche Router es laden dürfen
articles.text:
FritzOS 8.50 und 8.51: Was im Update für Fritzboxen steckt – und welche Router es laden dürfen
Schon seit geraumer Zeit warten Fritzbox-User:innen auf das große Update FritzOS 8.50. Hersteller Fritz hatte erste Neuerungen zunächst mit der Labor-Version 8.40 testen lassen. Jetzt ist die Beta-Phase für erste Fritz-Router vorbei und die finale Version von FritzOS 8.50 wird in immer größeren Schritten für einzelne Geräte freigegeben.
Welche Fritzboxen bekommen FritzOS 8.50 und 8.51 jetzt?
Die Liste der Fritzboxen, die jetzt mit der Release-Version FritzOS 8.50 ausgestattet werden, ist mittlerweile schon stark angewachsen. Unter den Kandidaten befinden sich auch Router und Repeater, die direkt ein Update auf die Version FritzOS 8.51 erhalten. Am Funktionsumfang ändert sich dadurch nichts. Der Hersteller verweist bei den Ankündigungen auf X stets auf die Übersichtsseite von FritzOS 8.50.
In den kommenden Wochen und Monaten dürfte Fritz noch mehr Modelle für die Aktualisierung freigeben. Wer nicht so lange warten möchte, kann wie erwähnt bei manchen Modellen das Labor-Update zu FritzOS 8.40 installieren, das erste Funktionen von FritzOS 8.50 mit sich bringt. Beachte allerdings, dass es sich um Testversionen des Updates handelt, die noch Probleme bereiten können. Diese Modelle dürfen schon die finale Version von FritzOS 8.50 laden:
- Fritzbox DSL/Fiber 7-90 (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritzbox 7530 AX
- Fritzbox 7690
- Fritzbox 7630 (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritzbox 7632 (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritzbx 6690 (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritzbox 6670 Cable (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritzbox 5630
- Fritzbox 5690
- Fritzbox 5690 XGS (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritzbox 4690 (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritzbox 4630 (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritzbox 4050 (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritz Repeater 3000 AX (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritz Repeater 6000 (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
- Fritz Mesh Set 4200 (direkt auf FritzOS 8.51)
Was steckt in FritzOS 8.50?
Die größte Neuerung von FritzOS 8.50 ist ein DNS-Filter. Dadurch kannst du Werbeeinblendungen auf einer Vielzahl von Geräten im Netzwerk einfach ausblenden. Das gilt etwa für Smartphones, Tablets und verbundene Smart-TVs. Daneben bietet die Myfritz-App in Verbindung mit FritzOS 8.50 einen Smart Check. Darüber wird dir in der App der Status deiner Fritzbox und deines gesamten Netzwerks angezeigt. Die App gibt dir zusätzlich Empfehlungen, mit denen du dein Heimnetz verbessern kannst.
Ferner integriert Fritz mit FritzOS 8.50 eine automatische Priorisierung, die Echtzeitverbindungen wie Videoanrufe vor alle anderen Verbindungen stellt. Dadurch wird die nötige Bandbreite für Meetings und Co. freigegeben, falls andere Verbindungen die Leitung belasten. Für alle Smarthome-User:innen integriert FritzOS 8.50 vordefinierte Routinen wie beim Verlassen des Hauses. Bei selbsterstellten Routinen lassen sich künftig auch mehrere Auslöser festlegen und das Geofencing wurde verbessert.
Mit den Fritz Repeatern 3000 AX 6000 sind erstmals zwei WLAN-Verstärker unter den Update-Kandidaten. Anders als die zahlreichen Router profitieren die Gadgets unter anderem laut Winfuture jedoch nicht von neuen Funktionen. Demnach soll das Update vor allem Stabilitätsverbesserungen und Optimierungen beim Speicherbedarf liefern. Außerdem werde die Zusammenarbeit mit Amazon-Geräten und die WLAN-Stabilität beim Wechsel der Verbindungseinstellungen verbessert.

articles.title: Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI Review: Slim OLED gaming that doesn't last long
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI mostly succeeds as a thin-and-light gaming laptop, offering solid RTX 5070 Ti performance, a beautiful 240 Hz OLED display, comfortable input devices, and plentiful ports. Its biggest weakness is ironically its battery life, which falls short of what you'd expect from a system focused on portability.
Reasons to buy
- + Solid gaming performance
- + Beautiful 240 Hz OLED display
- + Comfortable keyboard and touchpad
- + Useful port selection
- + Good upgrade prospects
Reasons to avoid
- - Fans can be noticeable
- - Below average battery life
- - Only Wi-Fi 6E
- - Subpar speakers
- - Too much preloaded software
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Not everyone wants a hulking gaming laptop. Some prefer something stealthier. Acer’s Predator Helios Neo 16S AI aims for portability but still packs a Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus processor and Nvidia RTX 5070 Ti graphics into a sub-five-pound package. It also includes plenty of ports and a beautiful 240 Hz OLED display. That hardware gives it plenty to work with, but the question remains whether the Helios Neo 16S AI can still deliver solid gaming performance while being portable.
Design of the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
Acer’s obsidian black chassis maintains the look of the Predator series – angular, dark, and visible in the dark with its illuminated lid logo. At 14.05 x 10.85 x 0.74 inches and 4.85 pounds, it’s respectably trim for a gaming laptop, though the Gigabyte Aero X16 (14 x 9.9 x 0.78 inches, 4.2 pounds) and the HyperX Omen 15 (13.5 x 9.96 x 0.93 inches, 4.89 pounds) both have about an inch less depth since neither use a rear thermal shelf like Acer.
The build quality is decent – both the chassis and lid show little flex. The stamped aluminum panels on the lid bottom and chassis lid aren’t ultra-premium but still beat plastic. One downside is that the metal shows fingerprints easily, which are difficult to clean off.
Acer provides an impressive port variety across three sides: Thunderbolt 4, three USB-A 3.2, USB-C 3.2, HDMI 2.1, 2.5 Gbps Ethernet, a MicroSD card reader, and an audio jack. The rear ports conveniently leave cables out of sight.
Inside, the laptop offers Wi-Fi 6E, which isn’t as modern as it could be, though the Killer AX1675i card and accompanying Killer Ethernet jack offer simultaneous network connections via Killer Doubleshot Pro for gamers that want to ensure network priority for the games over one connection and all other apps over the other. It’s also notable that Acer includes a zippered, padded travel sleeve.
Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI Specifications
| CPU | Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus | 
| Graphics | Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (12GB GDDR7, 1,612 MHz boost clock, 115 W maximum graphics power) | 
| Memory | 16GB DDR5-6400 (2x 8GB) | 
| Storage | 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD | 
| Display | 16-inch, OLED, 16:10, 2560 x 1600, 240 Hz, G-Sync | 
| Networking | Killer Wi-Fi 6E AX1675i | 
| Ports | Thunderbolt 4, 3x USB-A 3.2, USB-C 3.2, HDMI 2.1, Ethernet, MicroSD card reader, audio | 
| Camera | 1080p IR | 
| Battery | 92 WHr | 
| Power Adapter | 230 W (barrel connector) | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 Home | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 14.05 x 10.85 x 0.74 inches (357 x 276 x 18.8 mm) | 
| Weight | 4.85 pounds (2.2 kg) | 
| Price (as configured) | $2,774.99 | 
Gaming and Graphics on the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
We tested the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI with a Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus processor, Nvidia RTX 5070 Ti graphics card, and 16GB of RAM.
Playing 007 First Light, I saw about 65 to 75 frames per second (FPS) in most scenes, with spikes to over 100 FPS in wide open areas. The game remained all-around playable, though it did require using DLSS to achieve these framerates at native 2560 x 1600 with High settings.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Our comparison systems for this Acer are Gigabyte’s Aero X16 (Ryzen AI 7 350, RTX 5070 85W, $1,899.99 when tested, $1,499.99 as of this writing) and HyperX’s Omen 15 (Core Ultra 9 386H, RTX 5070 85W, $2,099.99 when tested, about $3,159.99 as of this writing).
Comparisons will focus on the 1920 x 1080 results, but we also included numbers at each laptop’s native resolution: 2560 x 1600 for the Acer and Gigabyte while the HP uses 2880 x 1800.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Overall, the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI performed significantly better than both the Gigabyte and HyperX laptops. Much of that has to do with its higher-wattage RTX 5070 Ti, though its Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus processor is also more modern.
In Shadow of the Tomb Raider (Highest detail preset), Acer’s 125 FPS at 1080p was on par with the HyperX (126 FPS), though it dominated at its 1600p native resolution, with 76 FPS against Gigabyte’s 60 FPS and HyperX’s 64 FPS.
Acer’s advantage continued in Far Cry 6 (Ultra), where it produced 122 FPS to Gigabyte’s 85 FPS and HyperX’s 107 FPS at native resolution. The lead narrowed in Red Dead Redemption 2 (Medium) where Acer and Gigabyte practically tied at 1080p and were within a few FPS at native (52 FPS for Acer and 49 FPS for Gigabyte). The HyperX remained behind.
The Acer also demonstrated markedly better performance in Cyberpunk 2077 (Ray Tracing Ultra) particularly at native resolution, where its 21 FPS outran Gigabyte (17 FPS) and HyperX (5 FPS).
In Forza Horizon 6 (Extreme), Acer’s 72 FPS at 1080p was strangely lower than HyperX’s 80 FPS, but the results flipped at native, where Acer’s 60 FPS was considerably ahead of HyperX’s 51 FPS.
While not a powerhouse, the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI demonstrates competent gaming performance at its 2560 x 1600 native resolution. Crucially, the extra depth from Acer’s thermal shelf design lets its GPU draw 115 W, considerably more than its Gigabyte and HyperX competitors
We test the sustained performance of gaming laptops running 15 loops of the Metro: Exodus stress test, simulating half an hour of gaming. During the test, the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI averaged 86.82 FPS across all runs. The variance was less than one FPS between runs, indicating stable thermal performance. The Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus ran at an average of 2.94 GHz on its P-cores, 2.16 GHz on its E-cores, and had an average temperature of 73 degrees Celsius. Meanwhile, the RTX 5070 Ti averaged 1.622 GHz and 74 C.
Productivity Performance on the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
Our Predator Helios Neo 16S AI features a Core Ultra 9 290HX processor, 16GB of dual-channel DDR5-6400 memory, and a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD.
The Acer’s Core Ultra 9 290HX produced strong numbers in Geekbench. Its single-core score of 3,349 and multi-core score of 19,313 were well ahead of the Ryzen AI 7 350-powered Gigabyte (2,916 and 14,074) and Core Ultra 9 386H-powered HyperX (2,857 and 15,916). This continued into our 4K-to-1080p Handbrake transcoding testing, which Acer dominated with 2 minutes and 30 seconds. The Gigabyte (3:54) and HyperX (3:39) weren’t even close.
Acer also produced solid numbers in our 25GB file transfer test, averaging 2,034.84 MBps next to Gigabyte’s1,480.57 MBps and HyperX’s far slower 999.57 MBps.
Overall, this Acer is very capable for almost any kind of use. Multitasking will be limited by 16GB of RAM, but Acer sells versions of this laptop with 32GB and it can be upgraded after purchase.
Display on the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
Once glance at this Acer’s display leaves no doubt it’s a key selling point. Its OLED panel technology creates exceptionally vivid colors matched by excellent brightness, and its glossy surface gives it an almost liquid appearance. The 2560 x 1600 resolution is a good balance between detail and what the system’s RTX 5070 Ti graphics card can drive in today’s games. Gamers will also appreciate the smooth 240 Hz refresh rate and Nvidia G-Sync support. (As we’ll see in the battery life section, the screen only supports 240 Hz, resulting in higher-than-expected power consumption.)
Watching nature documentaries on National Geographic, I noted the vibrant colors of tropical scenes and the pitch blacks of the depths of the sea. Gaming was equally immersive – 007 First Light felt supremely fluid and looked sharp. I could even make out the writing on character’s uniform badges without zooming.
The Acer’s display covered a healthy 82.7% of the DCI-P3 color gamut, matching the Gigabyte, although it wasn’t quite in the same league as the HyperX, which also used an OLED panel. It also didn’t match the HyperX in brightness, but with a peak of 372.4 nits in SDR, the Acer boasts solid brightness for OLED. Our 40% HDR testing revealed up to an impressive 608 nits of brightness.
Keyboard and Touchpad on the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
Acer’s keyboard offers a satisfying feel, with ample throw and cushioning without feeling rubbery. In MonkeyType, I reached 116 words per minute with 99% accuracy on my first try, a great result for me on any laptop. The Acer Key app lets you customize the user-customizable key above the plus key, which is handy for creating one-press access to a favorite app or site.
Though the keyboard doesn't feature per-key backlighting, its four RGB zones can be set to many patterns and colors in the PredatorSense app. When changing lighting settings, the app initially says they’re controlled by Windows Dynamic Lighting, but that isn’t the case since Dynamic Lighting says no compatible devices are detected. But once dismissing the warning in PredatorSense, the app provides intuitive if limited control over the zones and lid logo. Each zone can be assigned a static lighting effect or the entire keyboard set in a dynamic pattern: breathing, neon, wave, ripple, combo, snake, and disco, with customizable speed, direction, and brightness. Settings can be stored in profiles.
Acer also did well with the large touchpad, which offers predictable clicking and my fingers glided smoothly over the matte surface.
Audio on the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
Audio performance isn’t a strong point for the Neo 16S AI. Twin speakers embedded in the palm rest barely have enough volume for casual listening, with average clarity and thin bass. In Phil Collins’ “Don’t Lose My Number”, drum hits sounded flat and vocals were somewhat muted.
The speakers are better-suited gaming, offering a decent sense of direction because of their placement on either side of the palm rest, but lack of bass and volume means you'll want a headset. The DTS:X app offers equalizers – without them, the sound is quite tinny. I had the best results leaving the equalizer on Auto.
Upgradeability of the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
With ten Torx T6 screws securing the bottom cover, Acer doesn’t make it easy to get inside the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI. Removing the screws is the easy part – finding an entry point for my plastic pry tool provided harder. I eventually found one at the front corners of the chassis by using mild force. The fact that the side vents are part of the bottom cover compounds the difficulty – I needed to find an opening for my pry tool above those as well. The clips made cringeworthy snapping sounds as they were released, though surprisingly, none cracked off.
The effort is not for naught – Acer offers solid upgradeability, with two SODIMM slots under the black plastic cover in the middle, plus an M.2 2280 SSD slot and M.2 2230 wireless card slot. The battery is also replaceable.
Battery Life on the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
Our battery testing consists of web browsing, running OpenGL tests, and streaming videos with the screen at 150 nits while connected to Wi-Fi. The Predator underwhelmed here despite having a large 92 WHr battery – the HyperX laptop outlasted it by almost two hours and the Gigabyte nearly two and a half hours. Most of the blame goes to Acer’s decision to use a screen locked at 240 Hz; more advanced displays would support a variable refresh rate or at least allow it to be lowered to 60 Hz.
Heat on the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
We measure laptop surface temperatures during 15 loops of the Metro: Exodus stress test. During the test, the Acer’s temperatures peaked at 103 degrees F between the keyboard G and H keys, 81 F on the touchpad, and a toasty 129 F on bottom-center. Fan noise is audible particularly while gaming; hearing softer sounds in games will require using a headset. For daily use, the laptop hardly makes any noise.
Webcam on the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
Acer’s 1080p webcam offers a decently sharp picture – I could make out details in my facial hair and eyes from a few feet away. Highlights are also handled reasonably well. It lacks a physical privacy shutter or e-shutter, but it does have infrared (IR) for facial recognition.
Software and Warranty on the Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI
PredatorSense remains the prominent app on Acer’s Predator gaming laptops. On the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI, it offers power settings, system monitoring, updates, and system settings. Power profiles include quiet, balanced (the default), performance, and turbo. Performance mode indicates it overclocks the CPU and GPU, but doesn’t specify details, while turbo appears to be performance mode but with the fan speeds maxed.
The app’s settings let you disable Nvidia Optimus, set up optimized battery charging, a bluelight shield, and toggle a 30-second keyboard backlighting timeout. Fan control is possible, though the custom option only allows you to set the RPM, not a curve. Most of the settings above plus lighting effects and a sound equalizer can be saved in scenario profiles.
Acer loads many more apps than PredatorSense – too many: Acer Assist, Acer Chroma Tune, Acer Intelligence Space, Acer LiveArt, Acer documents, Acer Jumpstart, Acer Legal Information, Acer My Key, Acer Purified Voice Console, Acer PurifiedView, and Acer QuickPanel create a lengthy list under the Start Menu’s “A” section. Many of them are simply links to the Windows Store.
Some of the apps actually installed are useful, like Acer My Key mentioned earlier. Others could be: Acer Intelligence Space provides many AI-driven features like a meeting assistant, an image generator, a media search tool, and a game assistant that claims to automatically change the color of your crosshair for maximum visibility. I didn’t test all these out – they aren’t specific to the Predator Helios Neo 16S AI – but it seems that they could add value if you’re not already vested in other AI services.
There’s also a decent amount of bloatware, including a McAfee trial, a Dropbox promotion, and Forge of Empires. While easily uninstalled, they simply don’t belong on a laptop this expensive.
Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI Configurations
Our Predator Helios Neo 16S AI includes a Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus CPU, Nvidia RTX 5070 Ti graphics card, 16GB of dual-channel RAM, a 1TB PCIe 4.0 solid-state drive, and a 16-inch 2560 x 1600 OLED display with a 240 Hz refresh rate. It retails for $2,774.99 from Best Buy, though I did see it briefly drop to $1,999.99 during my review period.
Best Buy also offers a 32GB version for $3,199.99, but it was discounted to $2,459.99 during our review period, making it less expensive than our model. Pricing is always in flux with the ongoing memory shortages, but Acer’s list prices are in line with market expectations. At Best Buy, many RTX 5070 Ti models hover around the same price as our model and many are pricier.
Acer also lists a $2,099.99 model on its site with 16GB of RAM, a 1TB SSD, and an RTX 5060, though I didn’t find this model for sale.
Bottom Line
The Acer Predator Helios Neo 16S AI delivers on most of its thin-and-light gaming promise. Its RTX 5070 Ti provides solid gaming performance on its beautiful 240 Hz OLED display, and it follows up with a comfortable keyboard and touchpad, useful port selection, and solid upgradeability.
The trouble is that its portability is undermined by its below average battery life, an ironic shortcoming for a thin-and-light laptop. Audible gaming fans and lackluster speakers are further compromises, but the limited unplugged runtime is the one that those seeking a more portable package ought to be most concerned about.
But if you’re after a relatively slim gaming laptop to take between places where you can plug in, the Helios Neo 16S AI is an otherwise appealing package.
Charles Jefferies is a freelance reviewer for Tom’s Hardware US. He covers laptop and desktop PCs, especially gaming models.

articles.title: 'Opt-in always becomes opt-out later': Windows 11 users will get the choice to integrate Copilot AI in the search box as an optional extra — but users are skeptical about where Microsoft is going with this
articles.text:
Microsoft plans two big interface changes for Windows 11 — one sounds useful, but the other involving AI is seriously divisive
Incoming App Updates panel looks nifty, but Copilot integration being inbound for the search box is controversial
- Windows 11 is getting two further sizeable changes with the interface
- One involves the introduction of an App Updates panel in Settings to help manage third-party software updates more effectively
- The other is an integration of Copilot AI functionality in the taskbar's search box, although this will be an opt-in only feature – however, some users remain cynical about Microsoft's motives here
Microsoft has already made some major changes to Windows 11's interface, and a couple more are now in the pipeline – a hub for managing app updates in Settings, and a more divisive change to bring Copilot functionality to the search box in the taskbar.
First off, the less controversial idea that's apparently being mulled. As discovered by Windows Latest, this is an App Updates panel which is in a recent preview build of the OS (and has been present in testing in the past, it should be noted).
This is in Settings and consists of a hub where third-party apps in Windows 11 can be managed, and you can see what needs updating at a glance – rather than getting individual notifications from apps bugging you at random times, or an update only being actioned when you open the software. (The problem in the latter case being that if you don't use something for ages, you might miss a crucial security fix for an app, leaving your system potentially vulnerable).
Essentially, this is about giving third-party apps the same level of support as software from the Microsoft Store in terms of staying on top of updates, and it's a useful piece of functionality.
If it makes the cut for the release version of Windows 11, that is, and note that developers need to register their app for inclusion – with no software having done so as yet (so this is still relatively early testing).
The other interface introduction that's inbound for Windows 11 as flagged by Windows Central is part of the major revamp for Windows search, and it brings Copilot into the mix. Specifically, Microsoft is going to integrate Copilot functionality with search – but only for those who want it present.
In other words, it will be off by default, and you will need to actively turn on the option to have Copilot AI functionality in the search box.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Windows Central highlighted a Microsoft blog post on 'hybrid intelligence' from last month which explained that: "We will also begin adding the option to integrate the new Copilot with Search on the taskbar, so you can get quick answers inline from Search, and if you want to have a richer conversation, you can jump from Search directly to the full Copilot app. This experience will be opt-in, and will first start rolling out to select markets later this year."
Analysis: Ask Copilot returns – but there are doubters as to Microsoft's intentions here
This Copilot experience rollout could start soon, then, and it will likely be very similar to the 'Ask Copilot' functionality that Microsoft has played around with in testing in the past, effectively acting as a replacement for the search box. Evidently, that felt like too radical a move – it was also an opt-in feature, mind, it's worth noting – so with the new tack, the search box remains, but Copilot can optionally be integrated.
Obviously, the Ask Copilot concept was a very visible addition of AI, and this way, Microsoft is keeping it a lot more low-profile. That's a sensible approach, of course, given that the company has previously promised to cut back on AI clutter in Windows 11 as part of the broad drive to fix the OS which has been happening throughout this year.
While the App Updates panel is certainly a welcome move, this Copilot integration has proved divisive. On the one hand, there's a good deal of predictably negative feeling towards any AI addition for Windows 11, even one that is opt-in only.
Part of the reasoning here is that people are generally suspicious of Microsoft's motives and what'll happen in the future. In other words, a feature gets introduced as opt-in only, but later becomes the default (requiring opting out) – and finally it's baked in as a concrete part of the interface (with no option toggle at all). Despite the 'fix Windows 11' initiative and that whole new leaf which is a genuine effort to improve the OS across many fronts, trust in Microsoft is so low with some folks that they can't help but think the worst of the company.
One Redditor warns: "Opt-in always becomes 'opt-out' later. Be wary of this folks. New search UI looks less trash than the old one though."
Another agrees: "Yup they love to make things mandatory after no one uses a feature."
On the other side of the fence, there are those who are pleased that Microsoft has taken the opt-in route with this functionality.
Another Redditor posts: "Microsoft letting consumers pick if they want Copilot or not is inspiring. Take note of this Apple, and let users delete Apple Intelligence models natively."
Personally, taking into account all the good work that has been done with Windows 11 this year, I think we need to give Microsoft the benefit of the doubt here – especially given those promises about not pushing AI features unduly in Windows 11.
That said, longer-term, who knows where Windows 11 is going with AI agents, and I don't for a minute believe that AI isn't the future of Microsoft's desktop OS – or at least that remains the current thinking of the execs, anyway.

articles.title: Binance ferme les comptes français : retirez vos cryptos pour éviter des frais
articles.text:
Le compte à rebours est lancé. Dans un mail envoyé à ses utilisateurs, Binance rappelle que tous les comptes ouverts en France seront clôturés à la fin de l’année. « Votre compte Binance France sera clôturé à compter du 31 décembre 2026 », met en garde la plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies. Il n’est plus possible de déposer de l’argent, que ce soit en euros comme en cryptomonnaies. Seuls les retraits restent ouverts, sans restriction. Les clients sont donc invités à récupérer leurs fonds avant que la plateforme ne ferme définitivement ses portes « en raison de la cessation ordonnée des activités », indique Binance dans son mail.
À lire aussi : 4 heures pour piller Binance – la plateforme crypto révèle ce qu’il s’est vraiment passé lors de la cyberattaque
Pourquoi Binance ferme ses portes en France ?
La fermeture des comptes français découle directement de MiCA (Markets in Crypto-Assets), le nouveau règlement européen qui encadre le monde des cryptomonnaies. Depuis le 1er juillet 2026, toutes les plateformes doivent disposer d’un agrément délivré par le régulateur d’un des pays membres de l’Union européenne pour avoir le droit de proposer leurs services en Europe.
Binance, la plus grande plateforme d’échange de cryptos au monde, n’a pas réussi à obtenir ce précieux sésame dans les temps. Dos au mur, l’exchange a été obligé de restreindre ses services en Europe cet été. Depuis le 2 juillet 2026, les clients français ne peuvent plus acheter ni vendre de cryptos sur la plateforme. Les utilisateurs français pouvaient seulement retirer leur argent ou le laisser dormir sur leur compte. Il n’était plus possible de se servir de Binance pour faire du trading ou des conversions depuis l’Hexagone. C’est précisément ce que Binance veut désormais éviter.
Des frais mensuels pour faire bouger les retardataires
Quelques mois plus tard, Binance s’adresse aux investisseurs qui ont laissé leurs cryptomonnaies dormir sur sa plateforme. À partir du 29 novembre, Binance va appliquer des frais mensuels sur les actifs laissés sur les comptes d’utilisateurs français. Tous les comptes qui contiennent encore des cryptomonnaies seront ponctionnés de 0,025 % du solde, avec un minimum de 10 USDC.
En clair, presque tous les clients paieront 10 dollars à chaque prélèvement. Il faut en effet détenir plus de 40 000 dollars de cryptos pour que le pourcentage dépasse ce seuil minimal. Un premier prélèvement aura lieu dans les trois jours suivant le 29 novembre, puis un second après le 24 décembre 2026. Les frais seront d’abord prélevés en stablecoin USDC, puis dans les autres cryptos du compte si nécessaire, explique Binance.
Sans grande surprise, ce sont les petits portefeuilles qui vont le plus souffrir de cette vague de frais. Avec 100 dollars de cryptomonnaies sur son compte, un utilisateur perdra d’un seul coup 10 % de son épargne dès le premier prélèvement. Encore pire, les comptes qui ne contiennent plus que quelques dollars se feront tout simplement siphonnés. « Si le solde en actifs numériques disponible sur votre compte au moment du prélèvement des frais est inférieur au montant des frais à prélever, les frais seront limités à ce solde disponible et celui-ci sera prélevé dans son intégralité », explique Binance.
Binance se réserve le droit de siphonner les comptes inactifs
Pour éviter ces frais, les utilisateurs doivent impérativement retirer toutes leurs cryptomonnaies avant le 29 novembre 2026. Cette tactique doit pousser les derniers investisseurs à retirer leurs deniers avant la fermeture des comptes. La plateforme cherche à accélérer le mouvement afin d’éviter que des retardataires détiennent encore des cryptos sur des comptes français à la fin de l’année. Plus il reste de comptes au 31 décembre, plus la fermeture se complique. Après le 31 décembre, Binance considérera leur compte comme « inactif ». La plateforme se réserve alors le droit de disposer des cryptomonnaies restantes.
« Si vous n’avez pas retiré vos crypto-actifs au 31 décembre 2026, ce message constitue une notification de notre intention de considérer votre compte comme inactif, conformément à nos Conditions d’Utilisation. Cela peut entraîner la conversion, le transfert ou tout autre traitement de vos crypto-actifs », prévient Binance.
Que faire avec les cryptos restantes ?
Les clients français ont deux options. Ils peuvent transférer leurs fonds vers une autre plateforme agréée MiCA, ou les envoyer vers un portefeuille auto-hébergé (self custody), comme un hardware wallet de Ledger. C’est d’ailleurs l’option choisie par la majorité des Européens depuis l’annonce de la fermeture cet été. Binance révèle en effet que 70 % des fonds retirés par ses clients européens ont été transférés dans des portefeuilles auto-hébergés.
Avant de lancer le moindre transfert de cryptos, vérifiez bien l’adresse de destination et le réseau blockchain que vous avez choisi. Une seule petite erreur peut entraîner la perte définitive de votre argent. Par précaution, commencez toujours par un petit envoi, en guise de test. Si tout se déroule sans embûche, vous pourrez alors transférer le reste des cryptomonnaies. Armez-vous de patience. Il peut arriver qu’un transfert en cryptos prenne du temps, en fonction de la congestion du réseau. Avant de quitter la plateforme, pensez aussi à télécharger l’historique de vos transactions. Elle vous servira pour votre déclaration d’impôts. Vous devez en effet déclarer toutes vos transactions de cryptos vers des monnaies fiduciaires à l’administration fiscale.
Notez que Binance n’a pas abandonné l’idée de se faire une place sur le continent européen. Le géant des cryptos assure toujours vouloir obtenir l’agrément MiCA pour faire son retour en Europe. En juin dernier, Richard Teng, le patron de Binance, se disait déterminé « à obtenir une licence MiCA dans les mois à venir ».

articles.title: AI is even writing our Christmas cards now — and psychologists say we might be losing something important
articles.text:
1 in 8 Brits have used AI to write their Christmas cards — but are we losing something by letting ChatGPT do the talking?
Christmas cards are supposed to be personal — so why are we letting AI write them?
- 1 in 8 Brits have used AI to write their Christmas cards
- A psychologist warns that there’s a big difference between using AI to spark an idea and getting it to write the whole message
- 80% of Brits say a handwritten card feels more special than a digital message
There's something undeniably special about receiving a handwritten Christmas card at this time of year; but according to a new survey of 2,000 adults, around one in eight Brits (that’s an estimated 8.3 million people) say they’ve used AI tools to help them write sentimental messages in their cards.
The question is, should we really be handing over such a personal task to AI? While I agree that rituals like writing Christmas cards can help to get you in the festive mood, and some people find writing them calming and stress reducing, it’s also a bit of a chore for some; so I can sympathize with people wanting to outsource the job to AI. However, it does feel like there's something inherently wrong with using AI for this task.
Psychologist Eloise Skinner warns that there’s a big difference between using AI to spark an idea and getting it to write the whole message. “Challenging oneself to write a heartfelt, emotional message from their own perspective is much more rewarding and meaningful”, she says. “Many of us will have strong memories of childhood Christmas activities, and it might also make us remember previous family gatherings or positive associations we had in past years.”
Christmas is coming
The study, from festive family holiday specialist Santa’s Lapland, also found that even though the tradition of writing Christmas cards is becoming less popular, with 66% of Brits admitting that they write fewer cards than they used to, there’s a new trend for sending a digital Christmas card, with 46% saying they’re more likely to send an electronic greeting either by social media, text or email.
Once you’re sending a digital message at Christmas, it becomes so much easier to get AI involved, since you’re only a copy and paste away from a message you don't need to devote mental headroom to thinking of yourself. Perhaps that’s another good reason for continuing to send handwritten cards this year — it makes it so much less tempting to turn to AI for help.
Further evidence
If you need any further evidence that you should be writing your own Christmas cards by hand, the study also revealed that four in five (80%) say a handwritten card feels more special than a digital message, while more than six in 10 (61%) say writing cards helps them get into the festive spirit.
If you need some tips, then Skinner recommends starting by listing the things you genuinely want to say to someone, then identifying the ideas that matter most. She also suggests drafting the message in a notes app or journal before writing it in the card, arguing that taking your time is part of what makes the experience meaningful.

After all, if you’re getting ChatGPT to express in words how you genuinely feel, how is that different to simply signing your name under the prewritten message in a card?

articles.title: Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 user’s cables almost melted, even when limited to 500W — 12V-2x6 cables appear to still cause problems, show clear signs of melting
articles.text:
Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 user’s cables almost melted, even when limited to 500W — 12V-2x6 cables appear to still cause problems, show clear signs of melting
12V-2x6 strikes again, but thankfully it didn't take out a GPU this time.
Reddit user u/Doomslayer606 posted about frayed braided sleeving on both 12V-2x6 cables for their two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation GPUs the other day, asking whether it’s normal cable degradation or a sign of overheating. The GPUs were running at 500W, below the maximum 600W power draw, but commenters are confident it’s overheated cables, as the poster reports stiff, cracked, and easily peeling sleeves on only some of the wires.
u/Doomslayer606 posted on r/PcBuild with the title “Did I just save my RTX PRO 6000 GPUs from melting?” with photos of the 12V-2x6 cable’s braided sleeving frayed. The poster asked in the description whether this was normal degradation, a manufacturing issue, or overheating. The poster reported that the damaged braided sleeving felt stiff and peeled off easily, which is a strong indication of heat damage, and the comments were sure that it was.
Luckily, the poster’s GPUs were safe, but the 12-2x6 connectors are notorious for melting due to high power draw. One comment asked if they kept the stock power limit, to which the poster responded that they lowered both GPUs to 500W — another user responded asking why the poster wouldn’t use 300W, but the poster said it would reduce performance by up to 50% and they need to keep up with their deadlines.
Theoretically, the cable should be able to handle 500W, as each positive pin would only handle 6.94 A, which isn’t enough current to significantly heat up 16 AWG wire, but one of the main causes of cable overheating is uneven current distribution across the pins. Since only two of the pins melted on both cables, it’s likely those received high-current spikes often, leading to heat buildup.
Users have suggested aftermarket cables like the Corsair ThermalProtect 12V-2x6 cable that detects overheating cables, and the Thermal Grizzly WireView Pro II or Aqua Computing AMPINEL, which have active current balancing to prevent any wire from taking too much current alone. In a recent story, someone even created a power distributor, distributing the 12 pins into two 8-pin cables with a custom-designed PCB, which lowered the cable temperatures significantly — while another modder had a cursed solution, soldering thick cables directly to the RTX 5090’s power pins.
In an ideal world, consumers shouldn’t need another product or mod their GPUs to stop them destroying themselves. GPUs have only gotten more powerful, but instead of using more or thicker wires, we’re getting fewer wires of the same thickness. Understandably, having multiple 8-pin connectors gets messy, but surely there has to be a better solution. Maybe GPUs have outgrown the Mini-Fit Jr. connectors and need to have their own special connector with thicker pins and thicker wires.

articles.title: Répondre à un nouveau virus en 100 jours, le pari de la France et de son nouveau programme à 100 millions d’euros
articles.text:
Le gouvernement a annoncé lundi le déploiement complet de France Vaccins, un programme de 100 millions d'euros financé par France 2030. Son objectif est de développer plus vite de nouveaux vaccins face aux futures crises sanitaires, avec l'ARN messager et l'IA comme alliés.
Le programme France Vaccins et ses 100 millions d'euros issus de France 2030 entrent en déploiement complet, ont annoncé ce lundi 9 novembre à Orléans les ministres Stéphanie Rist (Santé) et Philippe Baptiste (Recherche). Six ans après le choc du Covid, l'idée fixe consiste à raccourcir le trajet entre la découverte en laboratoire et le premier essai clinique, quitte à convoquer l'IA ou à préparer des infections contrôlées de volontaires. L'annonce intervient un peu plus d'un an après les coupes américaines dans l'ARN messager, alors que le projet de budget 2027 rogne France 2030.
Le vaccin en 100 jours, un chantier d'abord technologique
Il existe un chiffre magique dans le petit monde des vaccins, le 100. C'est le nombre de jours visé pour disposer d'un vaccin après l'apparition d’un nouveau pathogène, virus ou bactérie, là où il avait fallu près d’un an face au Covid. Cette cible, portée par la coalition internationale CEPI avec le soutien du G7 et du G20, mobilise dans France Vaccins 31,2 millions d’euros, répartis entre quatre projets technologiques. Le programme court sur quatre ans, piloté par l’Agence de programmes de recherche en santé, ses fonds étant gérés par l’Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR).
Le pari le plus parlant nous redirige au CHU d'Orléans, où l'équipe de la professeure Chantal Pichon (unité InTheRNA, Inserm et Université d'Orléans) copilote FAR-M100 avec le Vaccine Research Institute. Il s'agit d'un projet, doté de 7,7 millions d'euros, qui doit bâtir une plateforme destinée à accélérer la conception puis le développement préclinique, la phase qui précède l'humain, de vaccins et de thérapies à ARN messager. L'IA y est mise à contribution, sans plus de précision sur son rôle.
Ailleurs, on s'attaque à des verrous moins connus. ImMuCHIPP (9,6 millions, Institut Pasteur de Paris et CIC Cochin-Pasteur) décortique les réponses immunitaires et prépare des études d'infection humaine contrôlée, avec des volontaires exposés à un pathogène sous surveillance, pratique longtemps absente en France. NOSE (5,9 millions, Institut Pasteur de Lille, Inserm et Université de Lille) évalue l'innocuité d'une vaccination par le nez, plus simple à administrer et pensée contre les virus respiratoires. Le CEA, avec ImaBioVac (8 millions), mise de son côté sur l'imagerie de pointe pour suivre le voyage d'un vaccin dans le corps et optimiser son efficacité.
Des candidats vaccins, des cerveaux et 20 millions d’euros qui intriguent
La plus grosse part identifiée du programme, avec 38,5 millions d'euros, finance quatre candidats vaccins dont les travaux ont débuté cette année. Le virus Nipah figure en tête de liste, avec une létalité estimée entre 40 et 75 % et toujours aucun vaccin homologué. Suivent les arénavirus, responsables de fièvres hémorragiques, les virus respiratoires et des arbovirus, transmis notamment par les moustiques, dont la dengue et le Zika. La menace n'est pas alarmante, mais elle existe puisqu'au 2 novembre, rappelle le gouvernement, la France recensait cinq épisodes de dengue locale en 2026, pour huit cas.
L'argent sert aussi à recruter. Un appel à candidatures ouvert ce lundi réserve 10 millions d'euros à trois ou quatre chaires seniors sur cinq ans, pour attirer des pointures internationales. L'occasion est tentante, puisqu'en août 2025, l'administration américaine a annulé 22 projets de vaccins à ARN messager, pour environ 500 millions de dollars. Paris connaît la recette, 41 des 46 lauréats de Choose France for Science sont arrivés des États-Unis.
Si on fait les comptes, plusieurs millions d'euros ne sont pas justifiés dans le communiqué du gouvernement. Aucun industriel ne figure non plus parmi les porteurs cités, alors que l'État promet une filière allant jusqu'à l'industrialisation. Quant à l'enveloppe, elle égale à peu près les 102 millions sur quatre ans de l'European Vaccine Hub financé par Bruxelles, et représente trois mois des 400 millions annuels annoncés par Sanofi en 2021 pour l'ARN messager. Pour la « souveraineté sanitaire » que revendique Stéphanie Rist, on peut parler d'une mise assez prudente.

articles.title: Nvidia probes whether foreign intelligence targeted Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Nvidia probes whether foreign intelligence targeted Jensen Huang
Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company has said its board had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security had been compromised.
Dear Readers,
Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The move follows a New York Times report alleging that a business executive with whom Huang had a close relationship passed information to Beijing.
The company shares slid sharply on Monday following this news.
Nvidia said its board had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security had been compromised.
In other news, Sashikumar Sreedharan, the former MD for India at Google Cloud, has joined AI company Sarvam as President and Chief Business Officer. He will also be on the company’s board. Sreedharan will run Sarvam’s business across enterprises and government and expand its work with digital-native companies, developers and partners.
Meanwhile, the India subsidiary of travel booking platform MakeMyTrip has received Sebi’s approval to launch an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO is expected to comprise a sale of equity shares in MMT India by its parent MakeMyTrip and its wholly-owned subsidiary, ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) Pte Ltd.
Lastly, 2026 is on track to be one of the four warmest years on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- How Bariflo uses AI to help factories treat wastewater
- How these Mothers of Courage are fighting to keep girls in school
Here’s your trivia for today: What was Henry Ford’s original design for a car called? (Scroll down for the answer)
In-focus
How Bariflo uses AI to help factories treat wastewater
Bariflo Cybernetics wants factories to get more use out of their wastewater treatment plants. The Odisha-based startup combines sensors, AI software, and automation to adjust treatment processes, aiming to reduce the energy and chemicals needed to clean water for reuse.
It recently secured Rs 2 crore in milestone-linked funding from energy innovation platform MC² Plus, an initiative led by the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, and is preparing for a pilot with Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), according to founder and CEO Mrityunjay Sahu. The funding comes as Bariflo moves from developing and testing its technology towards commercial deployments. That means persuading industrial customers to invest in upgrades that promise lower operating costs.
Key takeaways
- Founded in 2018, Bariflo initially focused on monitoring and cleaning municipal waterbodies. It subsequently explored aquaculture, including shrimp and fish farming, before concentrating on industrial wastewater treatment and reuse. It is now engaged in making existing treatment infrastructure smarter and more efficient.
- Bariflo’s proprietary IoT sensors monitor wastewater parameters such as pH, total dissolved solids, and flow. Its AI models use the readings to determine chemical dosage and treatment processes at different stages. This automates some decisions that operators would otherwise make manually and helps plants respond as the characteristics of incoming wastewater change.
- The company has conducted pilots with Indian Oil Corporation’s R&D centre in Faridabad. Its planned BPCL pilot will test treatment efficiency, energy consumption, and chemical use in an industrial setting. Founder Sahu hopes successful validation will pave the way for a commercial work order.
Social impact
How these Mothers of Courage are fighting to keep girls in school
Mothers of Courage, a documentary on girls’ education in Bihar, recently won the 2026 UN SDG Action Award in the Creativity category. It captures how women in rural Bihar are challenging social norms to keep girls in school.
Directed by Vandana R Jaikumar and produced by Butterfly Effect Media, the documentary was chosen from more than 7,000 applications from 190 countries and territories.
Key takeaways
- In rural Bihar, mothers are at the centre of a quiet revolution. They are negotiating with their families so their daughters can keep studying. Others are standing up for daughters-in-law who want to return to school. This quiet, stubborn conviction and resilience is the subject of the documentary.
- Mothers of Courage is part of Shikshagraha, a national movement to strengthen public education championed by Infosys Co-founder and former CEO S D Shibulal, and supported by Bengaluru-based non-profits ShikshaLokam and Mantra4Change.
- Urmila Kumari, State Head for Shikshagraha in Bihar, is the living embodiment of the movement. She has spent nearly three decades working for the rights and education of girls and young women. She says the UN recognition belongs to “thousands of women and adolescent girls whose courage and determination have driven the fight for girls' education and rights.”
News & updates
- New GCC: SplashBI, a Georgia (US)-headquartered enterprise data intelligence platform, has opened its global capability centre in Hyderabad. The company plans to invest over $100 million over five to seven years in infrastructure, technology and talent to scale the Hyderabad centre and strengthen its global product engineering and delivery capabilities.
- Age checks: Meta Platforms plans to expand its AI age-estimation technology globally to move millions more teens on Instagram into Teen Account protections, even if they have given birth dates showing they are adults. This comes as the company faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young users.
- AI guardrails: US President Donald Trump said the risks posed by artificial intelligence can be managed but signalled an openness to safeguards, telling CBS’s 60 Minutes that he “doesn’t mind guardrails.”

articles.title: Google Extends Tensor Processor Unit Series with TPU 8tx and 8i Max
articles.text:
Monday, November 9th 2026
Google Extends Tensor Processor Unit Series with TPU 8tx and 8i Max
While we've always co-designed our TPUs in partnership with Google DeepMind, we're now increasingly getting feedback from external organizations on their specific needs. With computing moving from human to agent scale, businesses are asking for accelerators that can reason across AI models' massive context windows. In addition, some highly regulated customers are asking for specialized encryption capabilities for unique workloads.
The new TPU systems we are announcing today address this new reality. Coupled with our recent PyTorch announcements, our aim is to make TPUs more easily accessible to every developer and Cloud customer. By combining modular custom silicon with an open and easy-to-use software stack, we can deliver new hardware and system configurations at the pace of the AI industry.Building the computer around the chip
Today, we're announcing two new TPU systems—and there's an important difference between a new chip and a new system.
Designing a new chip means laying out billions of microscopic transistors on a silicon wafer in a multi-year process bound by the laws of physics and a complex, long-duration manufacturing lifecycle. A system, on the other hand, is about how we bring together the compute, networking, and storage around the chip. This can include how they are packaged with the chips, to quickly meet emerging customer needs and research use cases.
When we built our very first TPU more than a decade ago, we knew AI software would evolve much faster than silicon manufacturing ever could. So we made a foundational bet on system balance and modularity, architecting our TPUs as building blocks as part of our AI Hypercomputer, so engineers could rapidly adjust packaging, high-speed memory, optical networking, and security around them. That approach allows us to deliver specialized supercomputers in a matter of months rather than years.
Specializing for secure, high-context AI
Each system in our eighth-generation TPU portfolio targets a distinct part of the AI lifecycle.
TPU 8t and TPU 8i established the baseline for this generation of chips:
- TPU 8t was designed to be a training powerhouse for massive foundation models with maximum "goodput"—or the useful intelligence delivered per watt of energy used.
- TPU 8i is the reasoning engine, designed to break the memory wall, cutting inter-chip communication delays by up to half.
Now, as enterprises bring autonomous agents into production, we have created two new configurations of these foundational systems to solve two urgent new challenges: hardware-level data security and million-token context scale.
TPU 8tx
TPU 8tx, our third eighth-generation system, is optimized for secure and confidential inference and is also great for small-scale training. It's built for regulated enterprises and governments running frontier or proprietary models and autonomous agents alongside their most sensitive data.
Normally, data is encrypted when stored or sent over a network, but has to be unlocked in memory while a computer processes it. Built on the same silicon as TPU 8t and paired with 5th Generation AMD EPYC CPU hosts, TPU 8tx builds security directly into the hardware layer, keeping sensitive data and model weights protected and isolated even while in active use. And by adopting the same low-latency Boardfly network we created for real-time reasoning, TPU 8tx keeps multistep agents moving, delivering up to 2x lower latency compared to TPU 8t with a near-zero performance penalty.
Pairing training-grade compute with a fast inference network also means organizations can simultaneously run and customize their models on a single system. TPU 8tx enables teams to fine-tune models using their private data, distill large models into smaller ones, and train their agents through reinforcement learning, all without needing to migrate sensitive data between separate clusters.
TPU 8i Max
Our fourth system, TPU 8i Max, is built for a different problem: the memory wall.
When dozens of AI agents work together across an entire software codebase or hours of video at once, memory bandwidth quickly becomes the bottleneck. So we took two low-latency TPU 8i chips and combined them onto a single package.
TPU 8i Max scales compute and memory in lockstep, delivering double the compute, double the SRAM and double the HBM bandwidth of TPU 8i, so processors remain equipped with essential data and so that large workloads do not stall. Further, because TPU 8i Max fits twice the silicon within the existing rack footprint, data centers can deploy significantly more computing power per square foot and per watt.
While flexible across workloads, together the four systems in our eighth-generation TPUs give customers a purpose-built accelerator for every stage of the agentic lifecycle. TPU 8t for scale-up training, TPU 8i for low-latency reasoning, TPU 8tx for confidential computing, and TPU 8i Max for massive context windows and the highest compute density per rack.
Opening up TPUs to every developer
When we launched the first TPU more than a decade ago, there were only a handful of companies running workloads that needed the processing power of a TPU. The use cases were specialized, so engineers would use optimized frameworks and hand-tuned code.
Over the years, as AI has advanced, more and more companies began using accelerators. Now, AI adoption is at a point where TPUs are excellent for a wide range of companies and use cases, and as a result, we've been working systematically to remove barriers to adoption so that TPUs are as easy-to-use as general-purpose hardware.
This investment comes together today across these key areas:
- Opening up TPU development to every PyTorch developer; no code rewrites needed: Last month, we open-sourced TorchTPU, so PyTorch code and Hugging Face models now run natively on TPUs, alongside out-of-the-box TPU backends for leading open-source inference engines like vLLM and SGLang. And to make hardware optimization effortless, our new open-source TPU agent suite (now in preview) plugs directly into coding tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Google Antigravity to automate TPU onboarding in minutes, diagnose bottlenecks, and autotune custom kernels using plain language. For production deployments, our new open-source XLA Serving Engine lets you train models in Python and serve them directly in a low-latency C++ runtime across TPUs, GPUs, and CPUs.
- Industry-leading production performance on InferenceX and AgentX benchmarks:
- In production, what really matters is outcomes on real AI workloads rather than theoretical peak chip speeds. On industry-standard InferenceX and AgentX benchmarks, which test realistic agentic coding and long-context work, our native vLLM-TorchTPU software stack on TPUs achieved state-of-the-art price-performance marks. New evaluations demonstrate these advantages extend across a wide range of frontier open models and open-source serving stacks while maintaining high model accuracy. Upcoming software optimizations on this same hardware will drive those results even further.
- Eliminating idle compute waste for autonomous agents: Because AI agents are stateful, they frequently pause for seconds or hours while waiting on a database lookup, an external software tool, or human feedback. To make our accelerators more power-efficient during those pauses, our new Agent Compute Engine software automatically suspends idle agent sessions and shifts working memory off the chip in milliseconds, cutting operational infrastructure costs.
- Breaking through the memory wall with the model-state layer (TPU Sync): Building the computer around the chip also means unifying memory, storage, and networking in software. As agents reason across million-token contexts and continuous reinforcement learning (RL) loops, memory quickly becomes the bottleneck. We're open-sourcing TPU Sync, the model-state layer for TPU clusters. TPU Sync turns chip HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network into a single, co-designed memory hierarchy—automatically tiering massive KV caches off the chip in milliseconds, streaming context across disaggregated prefill and decode nodes, and synchronizing RL weights to cut KV transfer latency and Time to First Token (TTFT) by more than 90%.
- Scaling distributed workloads across TPUs from a single controller: Now generally available on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), Cloud Pathways brings the Google DeepMind runtime behind Gemini to every Google Cloud customer. Using a single-controller architecture and pathwaysutils, you can orchestrate large-scale TPU systems across multiple slices as if they were one local machine for pre-training, reinforcement learning, and multihost inference. Cloud Pathways keeps long-running jobs moving through hardware disruptions with colocated Python sidecars, sub-minute slice hot-swapping, and elastic resharding.
- Stitching custom TPU topologies on-demand with GKE dynamic slicing: Now generally available, GKE dynamic slicing decouples physical hardware provisioning from logical slice formation using optical circuit switching (OCS) technology. By dynamically assembling TPU cubes into larger topologies (super-slicing) or partitioning them into smaller, isolated workloads (sub-slicing) on-the-fly, this update completely eliminates rigid, manual nodepool recreation cycles. This topology agility slashes job startup times by up to 5x and accelerates fault recovery by up to 4.5x, maximizing overall fleet utilization and workload goodput across all TPUs.
Co-designing with a decade of experience
Shipping four TPU systems and a unified, open software stack in a single year only happens when silicon architects, networking engineers, compiler teams, and Google DeepMind researchers build side-by-side.
Increasingly, we're even tapping into AI to ideate and build the next generation of AI infrastructure. From using Google DeepMind's AlphaChip reinforcement learning system to using Gemini to deliver chip layouts in hours rather than weeks, we're using TPU-powered AI services to rapidly accelerate next-generation TPU hardware development. This is true co-design and a unique Google differentiator.
Source:
				Google blog

articles.title: Tem uma placa de vídeo AMD Radeon? Cuidado com o bug que sobrecarrega o SSD • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Tem uma placa de vídeo AMD Radeon? Cuidado com o bug que sobrecarrega o SSD
Falha faz ferramenta AMD External Events Utility gravar dados continuamente no SSD do computador.
O seu computador tem uma placa de vídeo Radeon e, nos últimos dias, passou a apresentar um comportamento estranho? A causa pode ser uma falha em um driver da GPU que sobrecarrega o SSD. A AMD já reconheceu o problema e deve lançar uma solução em breve.
As investigações feitas até agora apontam que a falha envolve o AMD External Events Utility (atieclxx.exe), uma ferramenta que gerencia teclas de atalho e o FreeSync.
Quando o problema se manifesta, o processo em questão grava dados de modo constante nos SSDs instalados no PC, com taxas de escrita que, de acordo com relatos de usuários afetados pelo problema, variam entre 0,3 e 5 MB/s (megabytes por segundo).
Aparentemente, os dados gravados consistem em informações de diagnóstico, verificações de status e registros de eventos no sistema relacionados à GPU. A falha não está na geração desses dados em si, mas na gravação deles por meio de um processo que parece estar em “loop infinito”.
Como a gravação ocorre mesmo quando o computador está ocioso, há o risco de que essas operações aumentem o desgaste do SSD, levando à redução da vida útil do componente. Para você ter ideia do risco, uma operação de escrita contínua à taxa de 0,3 MB/s pode gerar um volume de gravação de 26 GB por dia. Esse número aumenta para 432 GB a 5 MB/s.
É claro que essas são somente estimativas. O volume de dados informado pelo Windows não corresponde, necessariamente, à quantidade efetivamente gravada nas células de memória do SSD. Mesmo assim, o bug é importante e deve ser tratado pela AMD.
Em um tópico do Reddit que trata do problema, uma representante da AMD reconheceu a falha no mês passado, pouco tempo depois de os primeiros relatos a respeito surgirem. No final do mesmo mês, a AMD lançou os drivers Adrenalin 26.10.2, mas eles não trazem a correção. A expectativa é a de que a solução venha a fazer parte da próxima versão dos drivers.
Ainda não está claro quais versões de drivers são problemáticas ou quais placas de vídeo estão envolvidas com o problema. Por isso, vale a pena checar se há alguma atividade irregular em seu PC.
Para isso, digite resmon no campo de busca da Barra de Tarefas ou do Menu Iniciar do Windows. Na janela que abrir (Monitor de Recursos), vá em Disco. Verifique se o processo atieclxx.exe ou atiesrxx.exe está realizando gravações contínuas.
Se estiver, vale a pena desativar temporariamente o AMD External Events Utility, mas tendo ciência de que isso pode afetar o funcionamento do FreeSync ou das teclas de atalho do Adrenalin.

articles.title: MSI Katana 15 HX B14, análisis: un portátil gaming de los de toda la vida sobrado para jugar, con algún sacrificio
articles.text:
En un contexto en el que los ordenadores comienzan a abrazar nuevas arquitecturas y otros posibles usos (como el de ejecutar modelos de IA generativa en local), los portátiles gaming sobreviven principalmente por la potencia bruta que pueden ofrecernos en un formato más o menos compacto. MSI sabe un par de cosas sobre ordenadores para jugar, y en este caso te vamos a contar qué nos ha parecido una de sus últimas propuestas: el MSI Katana 15 HX B14W.
Entre su catálogo de productos, MSI nos ofrece con esta propuesta un ordenador gaming tradicional, con un chip gráfico potente, una CPU sobrada, configuraciones decentes de memoria RAM (que hoy por hoy nunca está de más), y una pantalla QHD de 165 Hz para que disfrutes de los juegos a un gran nivel. Hay algunas particularidades que conviene tener en cuenta y que te vamos a detallar a continuación. Así que no perdamos más tiempo.
✅ Cómpralo si...
- Quieres un portátil capaz de ejecutar juegos modernos en gran calidad y a resolución QHD a un precio más o menos contenido.
- Valoras una alta tasa de refresco y un generoso conjunto de puertos por encima de un diseño delgado.
- Juegas y trabajas principalmente enchufado a la corriente, y rara vez necesitas llevar el portátil de un lado para otro todo el día.
❌ No los compres si...
- Buscas un acabado prémium, un diseño delgado o un portátil que sea fácil de transportar.
- La calidad de la pantalla te importa, pues para trabajos sensibles al color o en cuanto a brillo, este panel se queda corto.
- Esperas una larga duración de batería, especialmente mientras juegas.
Lo esencial en 30 segundos
El Katana 15 HX B14W es un portátil gaming de los de toda la vida y con un objetivo claro: maximizar rendimiento por lo que pagas por él. Lo podemos encontrar en varias configuraciones, aunque la unidad analizada posee un Intel Core i9-14900HX y una tarjeta gráfica dedicada RTX 5070 (con 8 GB de GDDR7 y un TGP de 115 W). Esta configuración nos permitió ejecutar decentemente todos los juegos probados a 1080p y a QHD en calidad ultra, incluyendo opciones de DLSS y trazado de rayos. La pantalla con 165 Hz de frecuencia de refresco y una generosa cantidad de puertos y conectividad completan un paquete bastante sensato.
Los sacrificios son los que cabría esperar a este precio. El chasis está hecho casi en su totalidad de plástico, pesa 2,4 kg y tiene un aspecto muy convencional, con líneas angulosas no hechas para todo el mundo e iluminación RGB en su teclado. Por otra parte, el panel cumple con lo que se propone, pero tampoco debemos esperar mucho más. Y es que en cuanto a calidad visual, se queda muy por debajo de otras propuestas más interesantes con más brillo, mejor color y otras tecnologías como el OLED. Hay que tener en cuenta que hablamos de una pantalla IPS-LCD convencional que no pretende innovar en absoluto.
Por otro lado, bajo máxima carga, la CPU y la GPU superan fácilmente los 90 °C a pesar de tener los ventiladores al tope (que por otro parte, en este tipo de propuestas, suele ser lo común). Además, la autonomía de la batería va bastante justa para cualquier tarea que vaya más allá de lo básico. Así que si buscas potencia bruta para jugar a un precio razonable y no te importa el diseño ni la portabilidad, es una opción sólida. Si quieres un portátil más equilibrado, este no es tu sitio.
8,0
A favor
- Gran rendimiento para todo tipo de cargas, incluyendo obviamente juegos
- Pantalla QHD de 165 Hz antirreflejos y con VRR
- Hardware puntero: i9 14900HX y RTX 5070
En contra
- La construcción es todo plástico y no se siente prémium
- Panel IPS-LCD que se queda por debajo de otras propuestas en brillo y colores
- Pesa bastante: 2,4 Kg
- Va justo de autonomía, así que implica tener enchufe cerca
MSI Katana 15 HX B14WFK-082XES Portátil 15" FHD Black | Intel Core i9 14900HX, RTX 5060, 32GB RAM, 1TB SSD, Free Dos
Nuestra experiencia con el MSI Katana 15 HX B14W
Un portátil gaming de los de siempre. El Katana no intenta ocultar lo que es. Tiene un diseño anguloso y robusto, un teclado RGB y un cuerpo pesado que claramente está pensado para quedarse sobre un escritorio. Casi todo el chasis es de plástico, con rejillas de ventilación en casi todas las superficies para permitir el flujo de aire. El acabado de la parte trasera es rugoso y ligeramente flexible, una textura diferente a la de la tapa y la base superior, y no transmite una sensación prémium. Con un peso de 2,4 kg y un adaptador de corriente de 240 W que también es grande, este no es un portátil para llevar encima a diario.
Un rendimiento acorde al hardware. Con un Core i9-14900HX y una RTX 5070, los resultados son los esperados:
- Cinebench 2026.1.3 multicore: 6.073 puntos.
- Cinebench 2026.1.3 single core: 656 puntos.
- 3DMark Time Spy: 13.246 puntos.
- 3DMark Steel Nomad: 2.771 puntos (27,72 fps).
En cuanto a los juegos, probamos cinco títulos a 1080p y QHD (2560 x 1440), todos con ajustes en ultra. Además, quisimos ver el rendimiento de los juegos activando DLSS y trazado de rayos en calidad media, siempre que estuviera este ajuste disponible.
El panorama general es bueno. La mayoría de los juegos se mantuvieron por encima de los 60 FPS a QHD con los ajustes al máximo, y el DLSS ayudaba a mantener esas tasas de fotogramas altas cuando activamos el trazado de rayos. En Cyberpunk 2077 y en ARC Raiders, activando DLSS y trazado de rayos rindieron prácticamente igual o mejor que en nativo y a resolución QHD. El DLSS carrileó Dragon's Dogma 2 cuando activábamos el trazado de rayos, un ajuste ciertamente exigente en el título de Capcom.
Marvel's Spider-Man 2 es especialmente exigente en calidad ultra, sobre todo a la hora de renderizar y procesar las grandes multitudes de Nueva York y los edificios mientras nos balanceamos por la ciudad. Por no hablar de que el rendimiento empeoraba de lo lindo al activar el ray-tracing. Incluso a 1080p obtuvimos una media de solo 57 FPS, con un mínimo de 28,7 y unos bajones del 1% alrededor de 22 FPS, mientras que a QHD con trazado de rayos baja a 31,5 FPS.
Spider-Man 2 está lejos de ofrecer una experiencia fluida en ultra a pesar de tener un hardware más que decente, pues con solo 8 GB de VRAM en la GPU, este es un título que expone los límites de esa memoria. Para este título y esta configuración recomendamos encarecidamente activar el DLSS y bajar ligeramente algunos parámetros sin reducir drásticamente el aspecto visual del juego. Tampoco habilitaría el trazado de rayos si priorizas una tasa de fotogramas por encima de los 60 fps (a pesar de que el resultado visual es espectacular).
Calor y ruido. A plena carga, tanto la CPU como la GPU pueden superar fácilmente los 90 °C cuando estamos un buen rato jugando a un título especialmente exigente. Para que el sistema de refrigeración cumpla, los ventiladores se tienen que poner a tope, y eso se traduce en un ruido excesivo. Toda ayuda extra es bienvenida para reducir temperaturas, como colocarlo en una base con ventilación y en un lugar fresco y retirado de otros elementos, aunque poco más podemos hacer por nuestra parte.
Pantalla. El panel IPS tiene una resolución QHD y una tasa de refresco de 165 Hz, lo cual son cifras bastante sólidas para jugar. Aunque el brillo es bajo y los colores no impresionan. Si priorizas la frecuencia, esta pantalla te dará lo que buscas, pero no esperes una alta capacidad a la hora de reproducir color o un contraste soberbio (eso se lo dejamos a los paneles VA, o más aún, a los OLED). Es precisamente en pantalla y en calidad de construcción donde MSI sacrifica para ofrecer una propuesta ajustada en precio acorde a las características.
Conectividad y uso diario. El portátil cuenta con un conjunto decente de puertos en los laterales, que incluye USB-A, USB-C, HDMI, Ethernet y un conector para auriculares. La webcam cumple su función, pero sin lujos, con una calidad de imagen que va justita (720p).
Almacenamiento. El SSD de 1 TB funciona como se espera, con buenas lecturas secuenciales que nos aporta la herramienta CrystalDiskMark, sin tampoco encontrarnos con una unidad sobresaliente.
Autonomía de la batería. Tal y como aparece en la tabla de especificaciones técnicas, nos encontramos con una batería de cuatro celdas y de 75 Wh, con una capacidad de 4.850 mA, y un cargador de 240 W. Este cacharro está capacitado para ejecutar juegos y programas con una gran demanda de recursos, por lo que te puedes esperar una autonomía muy justa en esos momentos. En nuestras pruebas, suerte era si alcanzábamos la hora y media de juego, limitando recursos cuando hacía falta.
Al activar el perfil de ahorro de batería y para tareas de ofimática, el equipo puede alcanzar cifras por encima de las 7 horas. Pero ya digo, es un equipo para tener una toma de corriente cerca en la mayor parte del tiempo.
Ficha técnica del MSI Katana 15 HX B14W
|  | MSI Katana 15 HX B14W | 
|---|---|
| dimensiones y peso | 359 x 262 x 25,5 mm 2,4 kg | 
| Pantalla | Panel IPS de 15,6 pulgadas Formato 16:9 Resolución QHD (2.560 x 1.440 píxeles) 165 Hz con Adaptive-Sync 100% DCI-P3 (típico) Brillo: 300 nits | 
| Procesador | Intel Core i9-14900HX (24 núcleos: 8 P-cores y 16 E-cores, 32 hilos). Frecuencia máxima turbo: 5,8 GHz | 
| Gráficos | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Laptop GPU, 8 GB GDDR7 (hasta 115 W de TGP) | 
| Memoria | 32 GB DDR5-5600 (2 ranuras SO-DIMM) | 
| Puertos | 1x USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 (10 Gbps, DisplayPort 1.4, Power Delivery 3.0) 3x USB-A 3.2 Gen 2 (10 Gbps) 1x HDMI 2.1 1x RJ45 Ethernet (1 GbE) 1x Conector combinado de audio de 3,5 mm (auriculares y micrófono) | 
| Conectividad inalámbrica | Wi-Fi 6E (Intel AX211) Bluetooth 5.3 | 
| Almacenamiento | 1 TB M.2 NVMe PCIe Gen 4 | 
| Batería | 75 Wh Adaptador de corriente de 240 W | 
| Webcam y otros | Cámara 720p Teclado retroiluminado RGB de 4 zonas con tecla Copilot Windows 11 Home | 
| precio | Desde 1.599 euros | 
MSI Katana 15 HX B14W, la opinión de Xataka
El Katana 15 HX B14W cumple lo que promete: un portátil gaming con rendimiento de gama alta por un precio más o menos contenido. La combinación del Core i9-14900HX y la RTX 5070 va sobrada para ejecutar juegos en QHD, y su panel de 165 Hz nos aporta ese extra de fluidez en títulos competitivos. Tampoco echamos en falta conexiones, por lo que estamos hablando de un portátil altamente capaz.
Los sacrificios se encuentran en todas las áreas donde MSI recorta costes, es decir, su construcción en plástico, el peso, la calidad del panel, y una autonomía que no sorprende. El PC no tiene ningún sistema de refrigeración revolucionario, así que cuando exprimimos el hardware se calienta de lo lindo y hace un ruido del que te acuerdas. Son algunos problemas inherentes de los portátiles gaming tradicionales económicos que debemos tener en cuenta siempre que vayamos a decantarnos por alguno.
Y ya que hablamos de precio, es más o menos competitivo, al menos en Europa. Al momento de redactar este texto, la configuración analizada se puede adquirir por unos 1.999 euros (sin sistema operativo). También hay opciones más básicas que parten de los 1.599 euros y que incluyen una RTX 5060 como tarjeta gráfica dedicada.
¿Te lo recomiendo?
Sí, si tu prioridad es el rendimiento en juegos por euro y aceptas sus limitaciones. Para un jugador que quiera ejecutar los últimos títulos en QHD con ajustes altos y que vaya a utilizar el portátil sobre un escritorio, esta es una de las opciones más sensatas. Si valoras el diseño, la portabilidad, una buena pantalla o la autonomía, probablemente serás más feliz con otro portátil, incluso si eso significa gastar más o aceptar menos potencia bruta. Tenerlo todo es prácticamente imposible si hablamos de ordenadores portátiles.

On regrette toutefois une trop forte directivité, limitant l’expérience d’écoute dans divers contextes. Malgré d’autres bémols tels que l’impossibilité de la jumeler à d’autres enceintes Marshall, ou encore une app mobile au potentiel inexploité, la Willen II s’impose comme une mise à jour cohérente, plus mature et plus aboutie.
