articles.title: Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds review
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Initial thoughts that these translation earbuds were going to enable realtime audio translation where quickly dispelled. However, speach to text time is new real time whereas speach to audio translation has a good seven second delay. Still the translation quality is excellent and a huge improvement on using google translate.
Reasons to buy
- + Simple to use
- + Relatively fast translation
- + Can be used as standard headphones
Reasons to avoid
- - Still a slight translation delay
- - Good signal strength needed
- - Background noise can affect speed.
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds: 30 second review
Translation Engine: Timekettle Babel OS 3.0
Languages: 54 languages and 108 regional accents
Offline Translation: 25 language pairs
Translation Modes: Face-to-Face, Live Listening, Voice Call and Multimedia
AI Features: Real-time transcription, automatic language detection and AI meeting summaries
Microphones: Dual-microphone air-conduction voice pickup
Connectivity: Bluetooth with dual-device connectivity
Battery Life: Up to 8 hours of music playback or 4 hours of translation per charge
Design and Weight: Open-ear hook design, 6.9g per earbud
Water Resistance: IPX4
The ideal translation device would translate live as you talk, so a conversation in two different languages can happen naturally. This was the concept of the fictional Babel fish in The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy, although in that case the earbud was a fish that you stuck into your ear.
The Timekettle LiveTalk on the surface promises this live-talk potential with near-instant text translation, plus audio. The earbuds have several different translation modes that are selected through the TimeKettle App, and, of course, AI is built in to boost the humanisation of those translations.
The way translations work depends on which of the four modes you choose. Whether you’re talking to someone face to face, in a meeting, listening to discussions, tuning in to multimedia content in another language online, or on a phone or video call, you must select a pickup mode before you start. From there, you can select normal speech-to-text translation, which, with a strong Wi-Fi or mobile signal, is fast once the initial translation starts. The more interesting part is activating audible voice translation as well.
The actual audio voice is good, and you can select either male or female. If you have in mind that this will be just like BabbleFish translating live with the audio in your ear, think again. The delay is 7 seconds; this means you still have that start-stop approach to conversation at best. It’s more like having a translator standing with you rather than live translation.
The speech-to-text translation is faster, but in either case, alongside the slight wait, you still have that disconnect. One of the most interesting features is sharing the earbuds: each person in a two-way conversation has an earbud, with speech and translation happening. The effect is good once you learn to speak in short bursts of no more than 7 seconds, although you can speak for longer; the translation will start to kick in, and due to the delay, having someone talking to you and the translation at the same time, translating some 7 seconds later, can all be a lot to take in and a bit confusing.
At present, however, when you factor in the different translation approaches and the range of translation options, these small, easy-to-use earphones perform surprisingly well for other situations such as watching live presentations, some multimedia content and quick conversations.
Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds: Price and Availablity
At present, the TimeKettle Live Talk AI Translation Earbuds retail for £129 and are available directly from the TimeKettle website as well as other major online retailers such as Amazon.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
- Score: 4.5/5
Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds: Design
The earphones arrive in a compact Star Silver charging case; that colour profile is essentially white with a slightly pearlescent finish. The supplied case is of a nice design and helps keep the earbuds clean and topped up with charge.
The case itself is simple, with the TimeKettle logo on top, but otherwise minimalistic, with the compact design measuring 65 x 74 x 22 mm and weighing 78g. This makes the design easily pocketable, and the closing mechanism is solid, meaning that when closed, it stays closed. Otherwise, on the exterior there’s just the single USB-C port along the rear edge for the power cable. The cable is also supplied in the box.
Opening up the case, the two over-the-ear buds are magnetically held in position in the case, with charging contacts that enable the two buds to be charged in the case in the usual way.
Alongside the hardware is the app, simply named ‘Timekettle’, and this is where the majority of the adjustments and settings for the translation mode, style and language can be made. This is all clearly laid out, and after the initial Bluetooth connection, you can get straight into using the buds and start translating.
Before you start a conversation, you need to select the type of translation you want, and there are four main types: Face to Face, Live Listening, Voice Call Translation, and Multimedia Translation.
Once you select the translation scenario you want, you can go to the main translation screen. At the bottom is a play button that needs to be pressed to start the live translation; this isn’t initially apparent. However, after the first use, the workflow becomes clear: the play button starts the translation process and doesn’t play back audio. For each of the modes there are also a series of options and these are all well laid out and clear to use.
- Design: 4.5/5
Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds: Features
The earbuds themselves are nicely designed, and along with a solid feel to the case, they all feel like a premium product.
The earbuds follow the open-ear hook design, which is comfortable and also lets you hear conversations around you. At 6.9g per bud, they’re also extremely lightweight.
The electronics inside have also been fine-tuned for translation and playback, with dual-microphone air-conduction voice pickup and a dedicated translation EQ that helps to enhance the audio captured.
Through the app, you can also access six EQ preset modes for music. While using these earbuds for more than just translation seems obvious, it isn’t always the case; and it’s great to know that you can use these for calls and as an all-day option rather than just being isolated to translation use.
My review sample arrived in the Star Silver colour profile, but if that doesn’t appeal, then they’re also available in two other colours; Polar Black or Deep Sea Blue.
For connectivity, the earbuds use Bluetooth and support dual connections so that you can connect to both your phone and computer at the same time. There’s also plenty of compatibility with applications such as Zoom, Microsoft Teams and many more.
Battery life, once fully charged, is surprisingly good, with around eight hours per charge and the case providing power for a top-up charge. The earbuds are rated for 4 hours of translation or 8 hours of music playback per charge, with the charging case extending total translation use to approximately 16 hours. Timekettle also advertises up to 35 hours of total battery life, while a quick 10-minute charge provides an additional 2.5 hours of use.
I’ve reviewed many of these translation devices. Timekettle has been one of the more consistent players in the market, with a full feature set that makes its devices useful in the real world and a viable, more advanced alternative to Google Translate.
Google Translate is, of course, free. In contrast with the Live Talk earbuds, there’s an outlay for the product and then often an additional cost for the extended use of the translation service, although with 200 minutes a month included for free, that does give you plenty of scope for use. The paid tiers just extend the translation amounts if you need the functionality for business, for instance.
The first major difference between Live Talk and Google Translate is real-time, two-way translation, with the text translating quickly as the conversation happens. This doesn’t differentiate it from Google much at first, other than that I found the transcription speed faster. The translation accuracy was essentially the same, but LiveTalk also offers 25 offline language pairs through downloadable language packs. This is useful when travelling without a reliable connection, although Google Translate also supports offline translation.
Although without the AI boost, the translations are a little more formulaic. The translation through the TimeKettle App is easy to read, and I found the user interface is far more user-friendly than Googles.
But then, with a quick tap of the voice button, that face-to-face conversation is not only translated into text but also spoken directly into your ear. The translation speed to text is fast, although it depends on your connection speed and ambient noise; it's impressive nonetheless, but the translated audio is notably slower.
In the app, you select the translation environment you need: Face to Face for one-on-one conversations, Live Listening for lectures and meetings, Voice Call, or Multimedia Translation.
Currently, it supports up to 54 languages and 108 regional accents. For example, there’s French and French Canadian. While the system works best with an online connection, it also offers 25 language pairs that can be used offline. The system also uses the Babel OS 3.0 AI translation engine, which you can switch on and off; testing showed it improved translation quality and speed.
One of the features that impressed me was the automatic language detection, although you can still manually select the languages you want, for example, English to French.
Some of the most useful transcription features include real-time speech-to-text transcription with bilingual transcription that’s displayed on the phone’s screen. You can also ask for AI-generated meeting summaries and other summary templates for different situations; this is a feature that I have liked on AI note-taking devices in the past.
As ever, transcription has paid tiers, but the free tier is surprisingly good: up to 200 minutes of translation a month, covering all four translation modes.
Other paid plans include the Unlimited Plan at £9.99 a month and a yearly option at £99.99 a year.
- Features: 4.5/5
Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds: Performance
The LiveTalk earbuds arrive in a compact charging case, and before starting the test, I left them overnight to ensure both the earbuds and the charging case were fully charged.
Once fully charged, I ran through the setup process, which involved downloading the app, opening the charging case with the earbuds inside, and tapping the Connect Device option. At that point, the LiveTalk hardware was detected. There was a little to-and-fro with the app and checking the Bluetooth connection, but overall it was well guided and connected quickly.
On the home screen, you have four translation modes: Face to Face, Live Listening, Voice Call, and Multimedia Translation. I started with the multimedia translation.
I found that getting started with this feature took some work. Initially, activating translation while you play back a video in French is simple. Just activate the Multimedia mode, click play, which sets the app up for translation as soon as it hears the vocals, then go to the media source, in this case, YouTube, and tap play. The video then starts to play, and about three seconds later the text translation appears, followed by the audio translation, which starts about seven seconds after the original word is spoken.
The written transcription and vocal translation are accurate, but the audio delay takes some getting used to, and it’s surprising how quickly things can move on in a YouTube video. The text translation, on the other hand, is almost instant.
There were a couple of issues, though: the original audio and the translated audio came through at the same time, albeit with a 7-second delay on the translation. With the default settings, the original video drowned out the translated audio. In the settings, it’s easy to find the translated audio volume. However, the original audio slider wouldn’t move on iOS, so I had to turn down the phone’s volume to balance the audio. That seemed a little convoluted, but it worked.
Once that was done, and slightly ignoring the delay, it did actually make it possible to watch videos with the translated audio coming through the earbuds. The delay is around seven seconds; while it’s fine for watching business presentations in another language, it wouldn’t be so useful for watching the latest French or Swedish drama. There’s also the issue that there is only one voice, so in one video, as it switched between the two presenters, they both had the same voice, making it difficult to determine which of the two was speaking. In this instance, that wasn’t an issue, but if you’re watching a drama, subtitles might still be the better option, even with the delay. To be honest watching a full drama with the earbuds isn’t really the intended use, but I was interested to see what would happen.
Next, moving on to Face to Face, and here you have two options. The first is to share the earbuds, with each person in the conversation wearing one. I tested this by being the English speaker while a friend who speaks French wore the other. In this situation, you assign the left to, say, French and the right to English.
Again, there is a delay, although this time it was five seconds. Another point I noted was that if you speak for more than five to six seconds, the translation starts for the person you’re speaking to. This obviously makes sense, but it can be hard to understand when the person speaking to you is in French, and the translation comes through at the same time in English, just five seconds behind.
The other option is to wear both earphones, with the other person using the phone. This is a bit of a mix-and-match approach, and in the end, just reverting to the text translation on the phone, which is extremely quick, worked well without the distraction of the delayed audio translation.
Another point is that when I first tried this, I was in a crowded café, and the translation worked well at first. But as the noise in the café built up, the translation became less accurate, often picking up audio from people around us, which became an issue.
Moving on from Face to Face, I used Live Listening, which worked well, although there was again a delay. Here, I had a colleague read a few paragraphs of French in the hall below the office. The translation of what came through was again delayed by about five seconds; however, that delay was far less distracting. Again, the text transcription appeared much faster, although in a lecture, the benefit of looking at the presenter or the person you have come to see is far more valuable than sitting in a live lecture looking at your phone. While it isn’t ideal, it does work well.
The final option was the LiveTalk Voice Call Translation. This option was surprising, as I think my mind is still attuned to slow video calls. To start the conversation, I had to switch from Speaker to Timekettle LiveTalk in FaceTime's speaker output options, and then the original and translated audio started coming through. Again, as with Multimedia mode, I had to adjust the phone’s audio.
The only other point is, again, remembering to assign the correct voice to the right person.
Alongside direct translation, these earbuds offer a few other options. First, every translation is transcribed so you can check it later, along with the original audio recording. You also get AI summaries, which could be really useful. However, during this test, when I tapped the Generate button, the key points for most translations appeared, giving a decent overview of what was being said. However, the AI Minutes seemed a little more temperamental, with ‘Generation failed’ appearing on quite a few of the discussions that I had.
Another feature I liked about these earbuds is that they can be used all day and for multiple tasks, since they’re not limited to AI translation. The open design hooks around your ears and sits just above the ear opening, leaving your ear canal unblocked so you can hear everything around you clearly. This means you can wear them during normal video meetings, while listening to music, and when making calls. If you’re used to inear or cans this does feel different, but is ultimately a more work friendly design.
I also found the battery life pretty decent, and the 4 hours Timekettle quotes for translation are pretty much on the mark.
- Performance: 3.5/5
Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds: Score card
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Row 0 - Cell 1 | Row 0 - Cell 2 | 
| Value | As a translation device and with 200 minutes, the LiveTalk is great value. | 4.5 | 
| Design | The build is high quality throughout, and the lightweight design makes them comfortable to wear all day. | 4.5 | 
| Features | On the surface, the feature set is extensive, and the app makes them easy to access. | 4.5 | 
| Performance | While speech-to-text translation is near-instant, face-to-face can be tricky because of the delay. | 3.5 | 
| Total | The quality and speed of translation across the four modes are good, but quieter locations are better, and the biggest issue is the overlap with face-to-face translations. | 4 | 
TimeKettle LiveTalk: Final Verdict
At the start of the test, I was initially impressed with the translation speeds, especially for the speech-to-text, which is almost real-time as long as you have a decent network connection. As I progressed through the test and the four modes, I had mixed results.
The translation quality was good from English to French, and vice versa, and the audio translation was also better than I expected; you can tell it's a computerised voice that lacks some of the tone and emotion you would expect from a human, but it's still impressive.
The most exciting part of using these headphones was the conversation aspect, and the hope that, like the Babel fish, I could simply stick one in my ear and start conversing in other languages. Unfortunately, this wasn’t quite possible. The delay was just too great, and with the person speaking and the translation coming at you at the same time, it’s just a little too much to take in all at once.
I found that the speed of the speech-to-text translation worked far better, and with the AI enhancement, there was less direct translation, and what was translated became more natural. However, this isn’t too far removed from Google Translate, although the speed and accuracy do seem to be better, and of course the big advantage is that you can use it offline with the language packs.
The points that really stood out were the speed of translation and the live translation for events and seminars; while there is that seven-second delay, it just isn’t so noticeable.
For multimedia and video conferencing as well, once you work out how to reduce the speaker's volume, that becomes far more useful, and it’s surprising how much easier it can be for speakers in their native languages to express themselves through translation. However, you’re always aware of that five- to seven-second delay.
While it still has some way to go before it offers live speech-to-audio translation, it is getting close. If you travel abroad regularly and often get involved in short conversations, this will be incredibly useful. Otherwise, as a speech-to-text translator and for understanding live events in other languages, it does work well, and I found it more convenient than Google Translate for continuously translating large volumes of spoken words without having to stop and start.
Buy it if...
You need a small, lightweight translator.
Its small size and ease of use across different scenarios make it an easy choice.
You’re going to a foreign-language event.
While translation has a delay, at larger events that delay isn’t as much of an issue.
Don't buy it if...
You’re expecting to converse naturally in another language.
Through the test, the average delay between speaking and the audio translation coming through was around seven seconds.
You want to watch foreign-language dramas.
Again, with the delay, the action has generally moved on, making it hard to follow the speech. However, switching to text transcription, the speed is impressive.
Alastair is a photographer, filmmaker and tech writer who has been working in the publishing industry since the late 1990s. For more than 25 years he has covered photography, video and technology across Future's photography, technology and gaming brands. He runs a photography and video production company and lectures in TV and film. He can usually be found testing mini PCs or prototyping and prop building with the aid of 3D printing.

articles.title: KI-Hacker nutzen alte Technik: Die unterschätzte Gefahr für Unternehmen
articles.text:
Cyberangriffe auf Tiefkühltruhen: Warum alte Technik im KI-Zeitalter die größte Gefahr ist
In Supermärkten in ganz Europa heizen Hacker Tiefkühltruhen auf bis zu 50 Grad hoch. Dafür brauchten sie keine KI, nur veraltete Steuerungstechnik, die offen im Netz hängt. Zur gleichen Zeit greift eine China zugeordnete Hackergruppe mit einem KI-Werkzeug mehr als 200 Organisationen weltweit an. Beides zeigt, wohin die Reise geht: KI erfindet keine neuen Angriffe, aber sie macht sie schneller, billiger und massenhaft möglich. Wie groß ist die Gefahr wirklich und wie können wir uns schützen?
Noch vor wenigen Jahren wäre das Science-Fiction gewesen: Ein auf Cyberangriffe spezialisiertes KI-Modell von OpenAI ist während eines Tests aus seiner isolierten „Sandbox“ ausgebrochen, hat einen Server gehackt, sich Administrator-Rechte dafür verschafft und von dort aus über das Internet den auf offene KI-Modelle spezialisierten Online-Dienst Hugging Face angegriffen. Auch dort nutzte der von OpenAIs KI gesteuerte KI-Agent eine Sicherheitslücke, über die er Zugriff auf das System bekam. Dort erweiterte er seine Zugriffsprivilegien, erschlich sich schließlich Zugang zu vertraulichen Daten, und verschleierte anschließend seine Spuren. Ein Mensch hätte das nicht besser machen können.
Dieser Text stammt aus der Ausgabe 7/2026 von MIT Technology Review und ist online erstmals am 08.09.2026 erschienen. Darin beschäftigen wir uns damit, wie KI die IT-Sicherheit auf den Kopf stellt. Das Heft ist in unserem Online-Shop bestellbar.
Seitdem sind eine Vielzahl ähnlicher Fälle gemeldet worden: Antrophic, Meta und Moonshot AI gaben bekannt, dass ihnen ihre Modelle ebenfalls ausgebrochen sind und fremde Server angegriffen haben. Was für andere Branchen ein PR-Desaster wäre, ist für die KI-Entwickelnden eine gigantische Werbekampagne: Seht her, unsere KI ist so gefährlich, dass niemand sie unter Kontrolle halten kann. Nicht einmal wir selbst.
Häufigere Cyberattacken mit KI-Unterstützung?
Auch wenn das alles durchaus im Verdacht steht, nur Show zu sein – sicher ist: Die wachsenden Fähigkeiten von KI-Modellen verändern nicht nur die legale Wirtschaft. Auch die Schattenwirtschaft im Cybercrime-Untergrund macht sich den technischen Wandel zunutze. „Die zunehmende Verbreitung von KI hat die Bedrohungslandschaft grundlegend verändert“, warnt etwa Interpol in einem aktuellen Bericht.
Auf die Frage, wie das weitergehen wird und ob wir vor einer massiven Welle KI-gestützter Verbrechen stehen, gibt es im Moment mehr Antworten als Expertinnen und Experten. Das hängt nicht nur damit zusammen, dass Berater:innen, Firmen für IT-Sicherheitssoftware, Behörden, Forschende und KI-Provider jeweils ihre eigenen Interessen verfolgen. Es liegt auch daran, dass IT-Sicherheit ein weites Feld ist, das die beteiligten Akteure in der Regel nur aus ihrer spezifischen Perspektive betrachten: Ein bisschen so, wie in der indischen Legende von den drei Blinden, die einen Elefanten beschreiben sollen und von denen jeder eine eigene Sicht auf die Wahrheit hat.

articles.title: Yamaha True X Bar 90A : 12 haut-parleurs à faisceaux pour un Dolby Atmos vers le plafond — Frandroid
articles.text:
Yamaha élargit sa gamme premium avec la True X Bar 90A. Selon le fabricant, ce modèle répond à une attente forte des consommateurs : accéder à l’univers sonore haut de gamme de la marque pour un tarif moins élevé. On rappelle que son « projecteur sonore » YSP-1, lancé fin 2004, a ouvert la voie aux barres de son à faisceaux.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quelles sont les meilleures barres de son testées en 2026 ?
            
La True X Bar 90A reprend donc ce principe avec douze haut-parleurs de 28 mm placés sous le panneau supérieur, six de chaque côté. Alimentés par l’amplificateur YDA-141, ils dirigent le son vers le plafond afin de reproduire les canaux d’élévation. L’idée est de créer des effets comparables à ceux d’enceintes encastrées au plafond.
Par ailleurs, la barre prend en charge les formats Dolby Atmos, DTS:X et Auro-3D. Yamaha la présente comme la première barre de son compatible Auro-3D, un titre qu’elle détient en réalité depuis 2025, puisqu’il s’agit de la même barre (référence SR-X90A) que celle du pack True X Surround 90A.
À titre de comparaison, la True X Bar 50A de la même marque utilise des haut-parleurs de hauteur plus classiques. Elle délivre 280 watts et mesure 1 015 mm de large, contre 1 180 mm pour la 90A, dont Yamaha ne communique pas la puissance.
Découvrez la TV TCL SQD-Mini LED : la puissance du Mini LED et la précision du Quantum Dot, actuellement en promotion pour le Black Friday.
Un traitement par intelligence artificielle et un caisson repensé
Côté acoustique, la barre reprend l’agencement inauguré par la True X Surround 90A, avec une vraie voie centrale. En effet, les trois canaux avant reçoivent chacun un haut-parleur large bande ovale « en forme d’œil ». Il est associé à un tweeter de 25 mm sur les canaux gauche et droit, et à deux tweeters sur le canal central. Selon la marque, ces transducteurs offrent des médiums riches et un son clair, sans distorsion, tout en gardant un châssis compact. La barre n’est pourtant pas un modèle de finesse, puisqu’elle mesure 1 180 x 85 x 143 mm, pieds compris, et pèse 11 kg. Sans ses pieds, par exemple une fois fixée au mur, elle ne fait plus que 71 mm de haut.
Le caisson de basses sans fil, équipé d’un haut-parleur de 17 cm, adopte l’évent Symmetrical Flare. D’après Yamaha, sa structure symétrique, mise au point par mesure des flux d’air, évacue l’air plus régulièrement. Le bruit de l’évent serait ainsi réduit de 20 dB par rapport à une conception classique. Le caisson mesure 241 x 378 x 414 mm et pèse 12,7 kg.
La technologie Surround:AI analyse en temps réel (cinq fois par seconde, selon Yamaha) les dialogues, la musique, les ambiances et les effets de chaque scène, puis règle automatiquement le champ sonore. Le traitement repose sur un SoC Qualcomm QCS407 64 bits, déjà employé dans le modèle phare de la série Aventage.
Enfin, la fonction Clear Voice rend les dialogues plus intelligibles, tandis que Bass Extension donne plus de corps aux graves.
Connectique, multiroom et installation
La True X Bar 90A propose une seule entrée HDMI, compatible 4K en passthrough, et une sortie HDMI eARC, ainsi qu’une entrée optique. Elle gère aussi le CEC, ce qui permet de la piloter avec la télécommande du téléviseur. Elle n’a pas d’entrée analogique. Elle n’a pas non plus de sortie caisson, puisque le caisson se connecte sans fil en 5 GHz.
Sur le plan réseau, la barre intègre le Wi-Fi, AirPlay 2 et le Bluetooth 4.2 (codecs SBC et AAC). Le système multiroom MusicCast, propre à la marque, permet en outre de diffuser la musique dans toute la maison. L’application MusicCast Controller sert au pilotage de base de la barre. Elle permet notamment de régler l’angle des faisceaux de hauteur et leur niveau, selon les besoins. Une télécommande est également livrée.
Disponibilité et prix de la barre de son Yamaha True X Bar 90A
La barre de son Yamaha True X Bar 90A est disponible dès à présent en France, au prix de 1 985 euros. Notez qu’une offre de lancement de 10 % de réduction sur le prix de vente est proposée à partir de ce vendredi 13 novembre et jusqu’au 13 janvier 2027, soit environ 1 786 euros. Enfin, si vous souhaitez des enceintes arrière, Yamaha continue de vendre le pack True X Surround 90A. Il réunit la même barre, le même caisson et deux enceintes arrière sans fil sur batterie. Son prix de lancement était de 2 499 euros.
Notez aussi que, selon Yamaha, la True X Bar 90A peut se connecter sans fil aux enceintes True X Speaker 1A ou True X Speaker 3A, vendues séparément. Il est donc possible de commencer par la barre et son caisson, puis d’ajouter des enceintes arrière plus tard. La True X Speaker 1A n’est toutefois plus commercialisée en Europe.

articles.title: “No creo que a todos los niños se les deba enseñar programación”: Linus Torvalds, creador de Linux
articles.text:
La idea de que aprender a programar es una habilidad indispensable para el futuro ganó espacio en escuelas, empresas y políticas educativas. Bajo esa premisa, el código aparece como una herramienta que todos los niños deberían conocer desde edades tempranas, al mismo nivel que otras competencias básicas.
Linus Torvalds, creador de Linux, plantea un matiz. Durante una conferencia en la Universidad de Aalto, sostuvo que la enseñanza de programación debe abrir oportunidades para quienes tengan interés y aptitud, pero cuestionó que deba imponerse como una obligación universal.
Por qué Torvalds cuestiona la idea de que todos los niños deban programar
El ingeniero finlandés partió de una idea central: la especialización permitió buena parte de los avances humanos. “Una de las grandes fortalezas que tenemos como humanos, como especie, es lo buenos que somos especializándonos”, afirmó ante una pregunta sobre cómo acercar la tecnología a estudiantes de primaria.
Para Torvalds, esa lógica alcanza a la informática. Consideró que el trabajo técnico y la programación de bajo nivel demandan conocimientos específicos, así que no todos deben seguir ese camino. “No creo en un mundo donde a todos, a todos los niños, se les deba enseñar a programar”, dijo.
La consulta que recibió Torvalds recordó que, durante las décadas de 1980 y 1990, muchas de las personas que utilizaban una computadora conocían, al menos de forma básica, el código y el funcionamiento de esos dispositivos. Y, algunas escribían sus propios programas.
Según el creador de Linux, el escenario actual es distinto. El uso de computadoras, teléfonos y otros servicios digitales se extendió entre la población, pero buena parte de los usuarios desconoce cómo funcionan los sistemas que emplea a diario. Esa distancia entre el uso y la comprensión técnica plantea un desafío para la educación.
Cómo se debe enfocar la enseñanza de programación
Torvalds no propuso que cada usuario deba convertirse en programador para comprender una computadora. Su planteamiento se orientó a reconocer que las sociedades funcionan a partir de tareas diferenciadas y que la especialización permite resolver problemas con mayor eficiencia.
La discusión, entonces, no pasa solo por enseñar lenguajes de programación. Incluye la posibilidad de que niños y adolescentes entiendan que las herramientas digitales pueden modificarse, adaptarse o crearse. El objetivo consiste en que quienes muestren inclinación por ese campo puedan identificarla a tiempo.
De qué forma identificar a quienes tienen aptitud para programar
El fundador de Linux sostuvo que los sistemas educativos y tecnológicos deben ofrecer condiciones para que los estudiantes interesados puedan acercarse al código. “Cada niño que tenga la capacidad de realmente sentir pasión por la programación” debe recibir estímulo.
En ese punto, su postura no rechaza la enseñanza de informática. Propone que el acceso sea amplio y que existan oportunidades de aprendizaje, sin convertir a la programación en un requisito idéntico para todos. “Esas personas deben ser alentadas”, afirmó, para que descubran que esa actividad puede resultarles atractiva.
Qué función pueden tener dispositivos como Raspberry Pi
Torvalds citó a Raspberry Pi como ejemplo de una iniciativa que puede facilitar ese primer contacto. Valoró el concepto de computadoras de bajo costo, disponibles para que los usuarios prueben ideas, cometan errores y experimenten sin depender de dispositivos caros o difíciles de reemplazar.
El desarrollador dijo que no buscaba anticipar el resultado del proyecto, pero defendió la importancia de contar con aparatos “baratos y desechables” que permitan aprender mediante la práctica. Para él, el valor de esos elementos no depende de que todos terminen usados de forma sostenida.
Por qué el creador de Linux acepta que muchos dispositivos queden sin uso
Torvalds planteó una comparación directa para explicar su criterio. “Si eso significa que 99 de cada 100 Raspberry Pis básicamente acumularán polvo porque nadie las usa, está bien”, dijo durante la conferencia en la Universidad de Aalto.
La razón, explicó, está en el impacto que puede tener el dispositivo restante. Si una sola persona descubre a través de esa experiencia que le interesa programar, el acceso habrá cumplido su función.
“No creo que debamos intentar que todo el mundo programe”, resumió Torvalds, aunque remarcó que quienes tengan esa aptitud deben poder reconocerla y desarrollarla.

articles.title: Google Cloud India MD Shashikumar Sreedharan joins Sarvam as President and CBO
articles.text:
Google Cloud India MD Shashikumar Sreedharan joins Sarvam as President and CBO
Sreedharan will run Sarvam's business across enterprises and government, and widen its work with digital-native companies, developers and partners.
Sarvam, one of the leading artificial intelligence (AI) startups in India, has announced the appointment of Sashikumar Sreedharan as President and Chief Business Officer. Sreeedharan was previously Managing Director - India of Google Cloud.
A blog post by Sarvam said Sreedharan will also be joining as a board member of the company. His responsibilities include leading the business of Sarvam across enterprises and government, and expanding its work with digital native companies, developers and partners. He will also be responsible for marketing, finance, forward deployed engineering, service delivery, and commercial operations.
“India should be a maker of the intelligence the world runs on. For me, joining Sarvam is a commitment to that opportunity. I look forward to working with the team and our customers to build products that become part of how industries and governments operate,” said Sreedharan.
Sreeedharan has more than three decades of experience building and leading technology businesses. Previously, he led Microsoft India’s enterprise business as the managing director for over five years.
Sarvam said the new appointment comes at a time when the startup is growing in scale and scope. It noted that over 100 enterprises and government institutions are building with Sarvam’s full-stack offering.
“The next phase of Sarvam is about advancing our research, developing products loved by people around the world, and building a company that can operate at a much greater scale. Every enterprise should own its AI,” the blog post said.
Sarvam became a unicorn startup after raising $234 million in the first close of its Series B funding round in June 2026. This round valued the company at $1.5 billion and saw participation from investors such as HCLTech, Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners.

articles.title: MakeMyTrip's India arm gets Sebi nod to float IPO
articles.text:
MakeMyTrip's India arm gets Sebi nod to float IPO
The proceeds from the planned IPO will be utilised by MakeMyTrip for long term growth, inorganic opportunities and repurchase of different types shares
Nasdaq-listed travel booking platform MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary has received Sebi's approval to launch an initial public offering (IPO), according to an update available on the markets regulator's website.
MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd (MMT India) had filed draft papers with Sebi in July through the confidential route. After examining the draft documents, the regulator issued its final observations on November 6.
Sebi's observations mark an important step in the IPO process, allowing the company to proceed with preparations for its public issues, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.
The proposed IPO is expected to comprise a sale of equity shares in MMT India by its parent MakeMyTrip and its wholly-owned subsidiary, ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) Pte Ltd, the Gurugram-headquartered company said in a regulatory filing with Nasdaq.
Following the completion of the proposed IPO, MMT India will continue to remain a subsidiary of MakeMyTrip, with its financial results continuing to be consolidated with those of the parent company, it had said.
"MakeMyTrip expects the proposed initial public offering and listing of MMT India to enhance its brand visibility and support MMT India's ability to incentivise and promote talent in a competitive technology recruitment landscape," the filing stated.
The net proceeds received by MakeMyTrip and ibibo Group Holdings from the sale of shares in MMT India are expected to strengthen the parent's cash position.
The proceeds will be utilised for long-term growth, strategic inorganic initiatives and repurchases of different classes of securities, including convertible securities, by MakeMyTrip, the filing stated.
MakeMyTrip swung back into profit for the three months ending September, 2026 boosted by increased booking across all categories. The company reported a net profit of $1.8 million for the second quarter of FY27 as compared to loss of $5.7 million in the similar period a year ago. The revenue for the second quarter touched $235.2 million which was a 11.2% increase when compared to the similar period of last fiscal.

articles.title: Siri AI devrait changer en 2027 : chez Apple, l’IA divise déjà la direction
articles.text:
John Ternus a pris les commandes d’Apple le 1er septembre 2026, après quinze années de Tim Cook. Lors d’une réunion à huis clos, le nouveau PDG aurait pressé Craig Federighi, qui dirige le logiciel maison, d’aller au-delà des seules retouches de Siri. Le désaccord porte sur le rythme, et il déborde déjà sur ce que l’iPhone saura faire ces deux prochaines années.
Un PDG pressé, un logiciel sur la défensive
Ternus jugerait trop timide l’adoption de l’IA par ses équipes, quand la concurrence avance à marche forcée. Le reproche rejoint ses propres déclarations : lors des derniers résultats trimestriels, il a publiquement qualifié de « prometteuses » les capacités d’IA dites agentiques, celles qui enchaînent seules une série d’actions. L’image est celle d’un assistant à qui l’on confie une course entière, plutôt qu’une consigne à la fois.
Face à lui, les réserves de Craig Federighi sur la vie privée, la sécurité ou l’emploi sont connues en interne, et son management très tenu laisserait peu d’espace aux propositions concurrentes. Son organisation planifie sur douze à dix-huit mois, quand les équipes matérielles se projettent sur plusieurs années : deux horloges qui se télescopent au moment d’écrire une feuille de route commune. Rien n’indique pour autant qu’il songe à partir.
Le dossier Siri s’est pourtant débloqué sous sa direction : relancé en bêta à la rentrée, l’assistant tient enfin les promesses de 2024, entre contexte personnel, lecture de l’écran et actions dans les applications. Mike Rockwell, le vétéran du Vision Pro qui a mené cette refonte, envisagerait toujours de quitter son poste, voire Apple, courant 2027. Sa relève se dessinerait déjà, entre Amar Subramanya, débauché de Google, et Sebastien Marineau, adjoint de Federighi.
Et sur votre iPhone, ça change quoi ?
Pour l’utilisateur, le premier enjeu est fonctionnel : Siri sait fouiller vos messages et agir dans vos applications, sans mener encore de longues tâches en arrière-plan, du tri d’une boîte mail à la préparation d’un voyage. C’est précisément le terrain que le PDG voudrait voir occupé plus vite, et celui où les assistants concurrents creusent l’écart.
Depuis le 26 octobre et iOS 27.2, Siri AI parle français, espagnol, japonais, coréen et portugais. Les iPhone, iPad et Apple Watch de l’Union européenne restent pourtant à l’écart, Apple invoquant son bras de fer avec le règlement DMA. Les Mac et le casque Vision Pro y ont droit, eux, chez nous. « Nous sommes profondément déçus que nos utilisateurs européens ne puissent pas bénéficier de Siri AI sur iPhone ou iPad », concédait Federighi en juin, sans avancer de date.
Pour iOS 28, attendu en septembre 2027, la première phase de développement passerait à six semaines de code pour deux de stabilisation, au lieu d’un découpage à quatre et quatre. Un remaniement qui n’est pas pour déplaire aux ingénieurs, qui disent apprécier le temps gagné pour explorer des idées avant de les figer. Reste à voir si cette prochaine mouture en sortira aussi stable, alors qu’iOS 27 avait mis en avant ses gains de stabilité pour justifier le petit nombre de nouveautés.

articles.title: Une start-up promet un million de dollars pour résoudre cinq problèmes scientifiques avec l'IA
articles.text:
Gagner jusqu'à 1 million de dollars en résolvant des problèmes scientifiques avec l'IA, ça vous tente ? Le challenge est très complexe, si bien que même ChatGPT ou Claude déraillent rapidement.
La jeune entreprise Discovered Materials, basée à San Francisco et issue de la promotion du printemps 2026 de l’accélérateur Y Combinator, a annoncé la création d’un concours pour remporter un total d’un million de dollars. La somme vise à récompenser la résolution, par des modèles d’intelligence artificielle, de cinq problèmes non résolus en science des matériaux.
Les IA encore à la traîne sur la physique des matériaux
Si les modèles d’IA les plus avancés ont obtenu des résultats très solides sur des questions mathématiques et permis des avancées dans les sciences du vivant, ils se heurtent encore à la complexité de la physique des matériaux. Contrairement aux mathématiques, où les énoncés reposent sur des critères précis menant à une réponse binaire, la science des matériaux impose un cadre plus difficile à formaliser et ne possède pas d’équivalent aux problèmes mathématiques plus classiques.
Pour définir ces enjeux, Discovered Materials a sollicité un groupe d’universitaires issus de plusieurs grandes institutions internationales.
« À travers la science des matériaux, il existe des phénomènes que nous observons mais que nous ne pouvons pas expliquer » - Felipe Jornada, professeur à Stanford
Un total de cinq sujets retenus
Les sujets retenus sont les suivants :
- L’élaboration d’une théorie pour expliquer la supraconductivité des cuprates, c’est-à-dire l’absence de résistance électrique de certains matériaux à très basse température.
- La mise au point d’une méthode numérique pour prédire la structure des interfaces entre le silicium et le dioxyde de silicium, une combinaison utilisée dans la quasi-totalité des semi-conducteurs.
- Une méthode numérique pour relier la structure des grains aux propriétés thermiques, afin de concevoir de meilleurs matériaux de dissipation de la chaleur.
- Une théorie expliquant pourquoi l’exposition à la lumière modifie le comportement des matériaux, particulièrement sur le plan de la supraconductivité.
- Une méthode numérique visant à améliorer la théorie de la fonctionnelle de la densité, une technique employée pour modéliser la structure des atomes et des molécules.
Mais avant d'officialiser le concours, la jeune start-up a testé ces sujets sur divers modèles avancés, avec un accès à internet et des ressources pour fonctionner en toute autonomie.
Après plusieurs jours de calcul sur chaque sujet, les IA se sont révélées peu convaincantes. Discovered Materials estime néanmoins que des acteurs comme OpenAI ou Anthropic pourraient tenter de les résoudre en mobilisant des modèles plus récents ou des capacités de calcul plus importantes.
Établir des repères scientifiques mesurables
Pour Advaith Sridhar, cofondateur de l’entreprise, l’intérêt réside dans la création de repères scientifiques mesurables. La démarche traduit également une évolution de la recherche assistée par l’IA : alors que la capacité de calcul facilite la recherche de solutions, la formulation des questions initiales devient capitale. L'entreprise a ainsi fait appel aux chercheurs pour définir les critères de validation et le cadre des problèmes en amont.
Créée il y a quelques mois, Discovered Materials axe principalement ses activités sur la recherche de nouveaux matériaux destinés aux puces électroniques. L'entreprise mène ses propres travaux, mais elle travaille aussi avec de grands fabricants de semi-conducteurs. Alors qu'elle annonçait une levée de fonds en août avec l'objectif de concevoir un matériau exploitable d'ici un an, la direction indique aujourd'hui une accélération de son calendrier de recherche.
Source : TechCrunch

articles.title: Desenvolvedor cria script que manda dados de RAM para Sam Altman • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Desenvolvedor cria script que manda dados de RAM para Sam Altman
Ferramenta para Linux transforma dados de memória disponível em mensagens irônicas ao CEO da OpenAI, em resposta a declarações sobre o uso de RAM em PCs.
Um desenvolvedor criou um script que monitora a memória RAM disponível em PCs com Linux e transforma os números em mensagens bem-humoradas direcionadas para o CEO da OpenAI, Sam Altman. Batizada de Ram-Altman, a ferramenta é uma sátira a comentários recentes do executivo sobre o uso de RAM em computadores pessoais.
Criado por Iain Kay e publicado no GitHub, o código verifica o sistema a cada cinco minutos. Quando mais de 10% da RAM está disponível, prepara uma mensagem com os números da máquina. Apesar da ironia no nome, o repositório não inclui o endereço de Altman. O usuário precisa informar remetente e destinatário manualmente.
Para evitar relatórios repetitivos, o Ram-Altman alterna entre oito assuntos, dez modelos de texto e seis despedidas. Um exemplo diz que há 8,6 GB de RAM disponíveis no computador, “sem nenhum plano para hoje”, e que poderiam estar em um data center.
O programa registra medições em um arquivo CSV e oferece um modo de simulação que permite visualizar o e-mail sem enviá-lo. O cálculo considera as estimativas do próprio Linux, que inclui memória livre e parte do cache que pode ser recuperada pelo sistema.
A brincadeira faz referência a uma fala de Altman no podcast Cheeky Pint. Ao discutir a oferta limitada de DRAM, o executivo afirmou que é “terrível” manter grandes quantidades de memória em computadores pessoais, já que ela seria usada “talvez 5% do tempo”. Na visão dele, parte dessa capacidade poderia ser aproveitada em data centers de IA.
A declaração gerou críticas em meio à alta dos preços da memória. O Tecnoblog já mostrou como a demanda de data centers de IA pressiona a oferta de DRAM e como a alta dos preços afeta o bolso consumidor.
Depois da repercussão, Altman afirmou no X que deseja que as pessoas ainda tenham bastante memória em seus computadores e que suas declarações foram tiradas de contexto. O executivo também mudou temporariamente seu nome de exibição na rede social para “Ram Altman”, inspiração para o nome do script.

articles.title: Windows 11 Will Finally Let You Silence the Sticky Keys Prompt for Good
articles.text:
Monday, November 9th 2026
Windows 11 Will Finally Let You Silence the Sticky Keys Prompt for Good
Pressing Shift five times in a row might soon stop summoning the Sticky Keys prompt on Windows 11. Microsoft is updating the dialogs that ask whether you want to turn on Sticky Keys or Filter Keys, adding a way to tell Windows not to ask again directly from the prompt. The change shows up in the release notes for Beta build 26320.9876 and Experimental build 26340.9882, both released to Windows Insiders on November 6. Right now, getting rid of the prompt for good means going into Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard and turning off the keyboard shortcut for each feature. The same Beta build also moves the channel to Windows 11 26H2 and brings Microsoft's rebuilt Windows Search.
This is a small tweak, though it fixes a long-running annoyance for gamers. Plenty of games use Shift to sprint or crouch, which makes it easy to trigger the Sticky Keys shortcut by accident, and the prompt can pull players out of full-screen games. Filter Keys has a similar shortcut that kicks in when the right Shift key is held down for eight seconds. Microsoft's notes don't mention games at all, saying only that it should mean fewer interruptions for people who don't use these features. It looks like another quality-of-life fix from Microsoft's internal push to clean up Windows 11. There's no word on when the updated prompts will reach regular Windows 11 PCs, and Microsoft notes that features in Insider builds may not always ship, so it's reasonable to expect a wait of at least a few weeks.

articles.title: A Sam Altman parody offers an amusing lesson in memory management
articles.text:
Sam Altman’s recent comments on the Cheeky Pint podcast inspired developer Iain Kay to create a satirical script that allows users to email the OpenAI CEO once per day if more than 10 percent of their system RAM is reported as available. Ram-Altman is described by its creator as a “parody project” launched in response to Altman’s viral remarks about RAM in your personal PC.
As reported by The Verge, on the October 29 episode recorded with Stripe President John Collison, Altman said, “A lot of people want local inference. And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center. But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5 percent of the time.”
Altman has since explained that his comments were taken out of context and briefly changed his display name to “RAM Altman” on X, which Kay calls on the project GitHub, “objectively excellent and where the project gets its name.”
In an email to Ars, Kay said, “Ram-Altman is a bash script that takes MemTotal minus MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo, so the figure includes page cache and reclaimable slab but leaves out tmpfs and shared memory.”
If the script only showed what Linux reports as “free” RAM, it would paint an incomplete picture. Linux often reports a surprisingly small amount of “free” RAM, as it doesn’t count memory that is currently claimable for use. Linux will fill available RAM caches with file data for quick access, but the kernel can reclaim that usage at a moment’s notice when needed. The MemAvailable figure is the kernel’s own estimate of how much memory it could hand over without swapping.
used = MemTotal - MemAvailable
Users can schedule the script to ask the kernel for a status update every five minutes, and if more than 10 percent of RAM is available, it triggers a joke email from one of several joke templates. The script limits outgoing emails to one per day.

articles.title: Meta AI age detection feature is going global
articles.text:
Meta’s AI age-estimations systems are heading global.
In the U.S., E.U. and Brazil, Instagram has been using tech to estimate a user’s age. If the system determines that the user is between 13-17 they’ll be funneled into a teen account even if they signed up with an adult account.
Teen accounts are more restrictive than a regular one and have age-appropriate protections. A teen account prevents strangers from messaging teens, their profiles and posts are private and there are both app time limits and parental controls. The company is also bringing AI age-estimation tech to Facebook as well, and then Threads later this year.
Meta is also using bone structure analysis of photos and your mentions of things like school grades or birthday celebrations to determine’s a person’s age. And if they are under 13 years old they will be removed from the platform.
Canada’s Bill C-34, Safe Social Media Act, has established an under-16 age limit for social media accounts and AI chatbots. Though company’s like Meta can prove that their platform meets child safety standards.

articles.title: Exclusive: FormAssembly overhauls its platform to expand into AI-powered process automation - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: FormAssembly overhauls its platform to expand into AI-powered process automation
FormAssembly Inc., a provider of online data collection and workflow automation software, today announced a complete platform overhaul that expands its capabilities beyond building forms to automating complex business processes using artificial intelligence.
The new platform, which the company said took seven months to develop, combines form creation, workflow automation, integrations and compliance management in a single no-code environment.
It also introduces conversational AI agents that can collect information through natural language interactions and support for the Model Context Protocol, enabling external AI agents to interact with FormAssembly’s software.
The launch marks a significant expansion for the 20-year-old company, which has traditionally focused on helping organizations collect structured information securely and integrate it into business applications. “We’re about how people share information with organizations and what happens after that,” said founder and Chief Executive Cedric Savarese.
The new platform builds on the AI assistant FormAssembly introduced last October, which enabled users to generate forms and configure workflows using natural language instructions. The latest release extends those capabilities to entire business processes, including approvals, document generation, electronic signatures and payments.
For example, a municipal government could describe an application process for obtaining a permit to hold an event in a public park. The platform’s assistant, called Fai, could then generate the necessary forms, approval workflows and documentation requirements.
“You can explain what you need in plain English to your agent, and the agent will build the entire process in a couple of minutes,” Savarese said.
FormAssembly claims the AI-assisted builder can reduce development time from days or weeks to minutes. Savarese said the company based those estimates on recreating existing customer workflows using the new platform.
Form conversations
A second major addition is conversational intake agents that replace traditional forms with interactive voice or text conversations. The agents use predefined data structures to guide conversations, answer questions and convert unstructured responses into information suitable for downstream systems.
The agents can also personalize interactions using previously collected information, although Savarese emphasized that access to that information is restricted by default.
“The default for us is privacy,” he said. “You only decide what information needs to be collected and what information is relevant for that particular task for the AI agent.”
FormAssembly uses frontier AI models, primarily from Anthropic PBC, rather than developing its own. Savarese said the company has zero-retention agreements with Anthropic and OpenAI Group PBC to protect customer information.
The revamped platform also adds governance capabilities that evaluate workflows against predefined compliance policies before publication. Organizations can use built-in rules or define their own requirements based on internal policies and applicable regulations. Potential violations are flagged for human review rather than automatically blocked.
MCP support and application programming interfaces enable customers to create and manage FormAssembly workflows through external systems without accessing the software’s traditional interface.
Savarese said this approach could protect established software companies from the risk that AI agents will make conventional software-as-a-service applications obsolete.
“People will use AI agents, but they use AI agents to drive software, not to replace it,” he said.
The company isn’t positioning itself as a comprehensive competitor to business process management vendors such as ServiceNow Inc. Instead, it intends to concentrate on processes that begin with collecting information from people.
Existing customers won’t be forced to migrate immediately. Savarese said migrations aren’t planned until January, and pricing for existing customers remains uncertain. More sophisticated automation capabilities could carry additional charges depending on customers’ current subscriptions.
FormAssembly, founded in 2006, raised its first outside funding of $10 million in 2019 after 13 years of bootstrapping. The company says it has thousands of customers, particularly in regulated industries such as healthcare, financial services, education and government.

articles.title: Hotel giant Wyndham exposed customer data after app security lapse | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Hotel and resort giant Wyndham has acknowledged a cybersecurity incident after a good-faith security researcher discovered a bug that allowed anyone to access customers’ personal information.
Security researcher Robert Wiggins at What Security exclusively told TechCrunch that he found a password inside the source code of Wyndham’s Android app, which granted access to an internal company database, hosted by tech company Salesforce.
Wiggins told TechCrunch that the credential exposed personal information including customer names, email addresses, and Wyndham member numbers. The database also stores customer login tokens (called JWTs) that keep customers logged-in to their apps without having to repeatedly enter their own passwords. The database also contained Wyndham files and documents.
According to Wiggins, the database had millions of entries, but he was unable to determine an accurate number of exposed customer records. Wyndham touts some 129 million enrolled rewards members.
The researcher said Wyndham has no way to report security flaws, and asked for TechCrunch’s help in alerting the company. Soon after TechCrunch made contact with Wyndham’s cybersecurity staff, the exposed credential was revoked, preventing any further access to the database.
“Our team has taken steps to address the issue,” a Wyndham spokesperson told TechCrunch. “Our security teams have no evidence of any unauthorized access,” the statement added, without providing any further details about the claim.
Wyndham’s spokesperson would not say, when asked, whether the company had the technical means, such as server logs, to determine if anyone had access to the customer database prior to Wiggins’ discovery.
TechCrunch also asked Wyndham whether it planned to notify customers whose information was exposed, or disclose the incident to U.S. regulators, such as filing a notice with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, as public companies are required to do for material cybersecurity incidents. Wyndham would not say.
Wyndham’s spokesperson also would not say for how long the password was embedded in its customer app, or how Wyndham plans to ship a long-term fix for the app.
App and software developers generally avoid including passwords or credentials in publicly released software and apps — a process known as “hardcoding” — as anyone with a copy of the software can extract the password and use it to access its associated server or database. Given the simplicity with which credentials can be abused by anyone, many cases of hardcoded credentials are automatically scored with a maximum vulnerability severity rating.
For Wiggins, this is his second public discovery of hardcoded credentials in two weeks, after finding a near-identical vulnerability in Applebee’s app that exposed customer data. Wiggins relied on AI tools for both discoveries, which make it easier to identify simple security weaknesses, such as hardcoded credentials, by scouring thousands of lines of decompiled app code every second.
When asked about Wyndham’s response, Wiggins told TechCrunch that he was glad the company fixed the issue, but noted that without visibility into any past activity, someone with malicious intent could have leaked large amounts of customers’ personal information.
The company would not say whether it planned to set up a vulnerability disclosure program to allow outside security researchers and hackers to privately report security vulnerabilities.
Michael Francess, Wyndham’s cybersecurity director who responded to the incident, told TechCrunch that researchers can alert [email protected] with details of potential security issues. The company’s spokesperson would not say whether it plans to change its website to allow researchers to alert the company.
This is the latest known security incident at Wyndham in recent years. In 2024, a security researcher found several Wyndham hotel check-in desks were running remote-access spyware that was leaking screenshots of guest records and booking information to the open web.
Soon after our reporting, the spyware app found on the hotel computers, called pcTattletale, was hacked and its banks of customer data stolen, forcing the company’s owner, Bryan Fleming, to shut down the company. Fleming, a former resident of Michigan, was later arrested by federal authorities and convicted of making, selling, and advertising unlawful spyware.

articles.title: Memory shortage spurs smartphone makers to melt used memory off old devices, then re-solder it onto new products — recycled memory to keep budget phones affordable; 'reballing' adoption to double by 2027
articles.text:
Memory shortage spurs smartphone makers to melt used memory off old devices, then re-solder it onto new products — recycled memory to keep budget phones affordable; 'reballing' adoption to double by 2027
Recycled chips gain momentum.
The smartphone industry is expected to see a spike in reballed memory adoption. According to a report by global market intelligence and research firm TrendForce, the current penetration rate is estimated at around 3–4%, with reballed memory primarily used in entry-level and budget smartphone models. However, this figure is expected to rise to 7–9% in 2027.
Reballed memory is recycled memory salvaged from older or discarded devices. The term reball comes from the process itself, in which the solder balls on a used memory chip are first melted so the chip can be removed from the old device, then re-soldered to a new device, thus allowing the component to be reused rather than discarded. You can see the process in action in the video below.
This offers manufacturers a cheaper alternative to sourcing new memory chips, potentially helping them keep production costs under control. Currently, reballed 4GB LPDDR4X memory modules make up the majority of such components on the market, and they are used in 4G smartphones priced below CNY 1,299 (approximately $200). 
This tactic is becoming increasingly important for smartphone makers, as customers are particularly sensitive to price increases in the budget segment. This leaves limited room to raise retail prices without affecting demand. Using reballed memory can help offset rising bill of materials (BOM) costs while allowing brands to keep entry-level devices affordable.
TrendForce expects DRAM prices to rise even further in the first quarter of 2027, which may put additional pressure on smartphone manufacturers. As a result, the use of recycled memory and other lower-specification components could gradually expand beyond the entry-level segment and into more premium smartphones. What is currently a cost-saving measure for budget devices could eventually become a broader strategy for manufacturers looking to manage expenses amid a prolonged period of high memory prices.
The rising cost of memory is also pushing PC enthusiasts and hardware hobbyists to explore unconventional ways to reuse existing DRAM chips. Recently, an electronics hobbyist converted a relatively inexpensive $120 DDR5 SO-DIMM kit into a desktop memory kit valued at around $1,000. The project involved salvaging an SK hynix 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM kit purchased from Facebook Marketplace and reballing the chips onto custom desktop DIMM PCBs, with the resulting modules reportedly capable of reaching DDR5-7800 speeds.
Converting laptop memory into desktop DIMMs is technically demanding and requires considerable expertise and specialized equipment. Similarly, reballing memory for use in smartphones is far from straightforward, particularly given the tiny solder connections in modern BGA (Ball Grid Array) packages. Nevertheless, both developments highlight how manufacturers, repair specialists, and hardware enthusiasts are exploring alternatives to reuse existing memory to offset rising costs and limited availability.

articles.title: Statt Endlager: Dresdner Forscher wollen Atommüll recyceln
articles.text:
Statt Endlagersuche: Dresdner Forscher wollen Atommüll recyceln
Rund 27.000 Kubikmeter Atommüll sind in Deutschland durch den jahrzehntelangen Betrieb von Atomkraftwerken angefallen. Die Bundesgesellschaft für Endlagerung (BGE) ist auf der Suche nach einem sogenannten Endlager. Nach eigenen Angaben verfolgt die Gesellschaft das Ziel, einen Standort zu ermitteln, der den Abfall für eine Million Jahre sicher einschließt – eine knifflige Aufgabe. Kürzlich wurde die Suche eingegrenzt und die infrage kommenden Gebiete für ein solches Endlager deutlich reduziert. Die Technische Universität Dresden arbeitet jetzt an einem Projekt, das die Endlagersuche überflüssig machen könnte.
Was die Forschenden der TU Dresden vor haben
Die TU Dresden plant den Bau des Experimentalrecyclingreaktors „DEMO“ in einem Forschungsprojekt unter Einsatz eines sogenannten Flüssigsalzreaktors. Dieser verwertet die hochradioaktiven Stoffe aus dem Leichtwasserreaktorbetrieb energetisch und stofflich.
Mit dem Einsatz von „DEMO“ wollen die Forschenden einen entscheidenden Machbarkeitsnachweis erbringen. Dabei sollen vorhandene abgebrannte Kernbrennstäbe und verglaste Materialien ohne die bisher nötige Aufbereitung direkt in emissionsarme Energie transformiert und zu größtenteils kurzlebigen Spaltprodukten umgewandelt werden. Durch dieses Verfahren würden lediglich Spaltprodukte als Reststoffe zurückbleiben und die Endlagerung der nuklearen Abfälle gemäß StandAG entfallen. Das Gesetz regelt das mehrstufige Verfahren für die Suche nach einem Endlager für langlebige, wärmeentwickelnde radioaktive Abfälle.
Ökonomisches und gesellschaftliches Potenzial des Reaktors
Die Forschenden erhoffen sich durch ihren Reaktor erhebliche Einsparungen von rund 50 Milliarden Euro. Ihre Schätzung beruht auf der Annahme, dass ein Atommüll-Endlager nicht mehr nötig sei. Zudem erschließe die Technologie Energie-Ressourcen, die dem 300-fachen jährlichen Stromverbrauch Deutschlands entsprechen. Konkrete Angaben zur methodischen Grundlage ihrer Schätzungen enthält die Pressemitteilung zum Projekt allerdings nicht.
Ob das Konzept tatsächlich funktioniert und auf politische Akzeptanz stößt, muss sich in weiteren Entwicklungsschritten unter Beweis stellen. In frühestens fünf Jahren ist mit ersten Erkenntnissen zu rechnen, heißt es in der Pressemitteilung. In dieser Zeit will das Forschungsteam der TU Dresden den Experimentalreaktor bauen. An Reaktoren, die aufgebrauchte Brennstäbe oder in Atomreaktoren entstehende Transurane nutzen können, wird seit Jahrzehnten geforscht. Die Idee der TU Dresden ist also nicht neu, muss sich allerdings noch in der Praxis bewähren.

articles.title: Rockstar announces Grand Theft Auto 6: The Festival, a special live event featuring music from GTA 6 — here's when you can get tickets

GTA 6 is coming to Miami with a live Grand Theft Auto 6: The Festival special event — here's how to secure your pre-sale tickets
The odds of being selected for pre-sale tickets "will depend on the number of eligible entries received"
- Rockstar Games announces Grand Theft Auto 6: The Festival for November 21
- The special live concert will feature music from artists in the game and on the official soundtrack
- A pre-sale lottery for tickets will be available on November 11
Rockstar Games has announced Grand Theft Auto 6: The Festival, a special live concert scheduled for after GTA 6's launch and featuring music from the game.
The Festival is set for November 21 at Mana Wynwood in Miami and will feature a star-studded lineup of artists from the game and the official soundtrack across two stages.
Those performances include: Cactus Jack presents Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, and Sofaygo; Cardi B; Ca7riel & Paco Amoroso; Justice (DJ set); Metro Boomin; Nick León B2B DJ Python; Prospa B2B Skream; Rauw & Friends; Suero; Tainy; The Dare B2B Fcukers (DJ set).
Rockstar has confirmed that a pre-sale lottery will be available for a chance to purchase tickets, beginning on Wednesday, November 11.
Tickets are limited to two per pre-sale lottery code, and the lottery closes at 4PM ET / 9PM GMT on Tuesday, November 10.
Fans can sign up for the GTA 6: The Festival lottery here, with entries limited to a maximum of one entry per person. Entries must also be from people aged 17+.
"Winners will be drawn at random from eligible entries and contacted by SMS with a code on Tuesday, November 10 by 7 P.M. ET," Rockstar said. "Odds of being selected will depend on the number of eligible entries received."

articles.title: Marcas de moda piden en borradores de contratos usar imágenes de modelos alteradas con IA sin pagar más
articles.text:
Marcas como Diesel, Calvin Klein y L’Oréal propusieron en borradores de contratos con modelos permisos para modificar sus imágenes con inteligencia artificial, crear copias digitales o entrenar programas con sus fotos, según una investigación de Reuters. En algunos casos, el texto no prevé un pago adicional por esos usos.
Reuters entrevistó a 15 directores de agencias de modelos y revisó más de una docena de contratos confidenciales de sesiones de fotos. Los documentos eran borradores sin firmar. Contienen frases como “incluyendo” o “sin limitarse a”, que los abogados suelen usar para obtener permisos no enumerados.
Melanie Howard, socia de la firma Loeb & Loeb de Los Ángeles, que representa tanto a marcas como a modelos, dijo que esa redacción “es peligrosa por su ambigüedad” y que vuelve muy difícil que una modelo reclame por un uso no autorizado.
Lo que piden los contratos
Un borrador de Calvin Klein pedía a la modelo que aceptara que la marca “puede usar imágenes razonablemente irreconocibles”, sin rostro ni cicatrices ni tatuajes, para entrenar herramientas de IA, sin pago extra. Un portavoz de la empresa respondió que prueba y aprende en un campo que cambia rápidamente y que respeta las normas.
Una hoja de casting de Diesel pedía aceptar la “alteración o reconstrucción de los rasgos faciales y las proporciones corporales”, el intercambio de rostros entre modelos y la colocación del rostro de una participante sobre el cuerpo de otra persona. OTB, dueña de Diesel, afirmó que el documento era para una sola campaña y que no refleja sus contratos habituales.
Un contrato de la marca de cuidado de la piel Reale Actives, fundada este año por la creadora de contenido Alix Earle, buscaba derechos para fabricar réplicas de modelos con IA y usarlas durante un año sin pagar más. La empresa dijo que contrata talento real, que no replicó a ninguna modelo y que el texto venía de un socio de producción.
L’Oréal pedía derecho a usar IA para retocar y adaptar productos, envases y tonos. La empresa no comentó esa cláusula y señaló que usa herramientas habituales en posproducción que no alteran la imagen de las modelos.
Estudios cerrados y trabajo en retroceso
Zalando, la mayor tienda de moda en línea de Europa, cerró el año pasado sus dos estudios de fotografía en Berlín, según Reuters. En total eliminó más de 340 puestos, aunque la empresa indicó que parte del personal fue reubicado. About You, portal de comercio que Zalando compró en julio del año pasado, también cerró su estudio.
About You ofrece ahora a otras tiendas un servicio llamado Scayle Studios, que genera imágenes con modelos de IA y promete reducir los costos más de un 90%. Un vocero dijo que tiene 130 marcas como clientes y que produjo 190.000 conjuntos de ropa en el último mes. “Estamos ahorrando muchísimo dinero”, afirmó Julian Jansen, vicepresidente de marketing de la firma.
Las agencias informan que las reservas caen, sobre todo en las sesiones para tiendas en línea. “Dentro de un año, incluso en seis meses, habrá menos trabajo para las modelos”, dijo Adot Gak, modelo con sede en Londres que trabajó para Balmain y H&M. La española Mango ya usa modelos generadas por computadora. Moncler probó una campaña con IA en 2023 y dijo que hoy no las usa.
La Ley de Trabajadores de la Moda del estado de Nueva York prohíbe desde junio de 2025 crear o modificar réplicas de modelos sin su consentimiento explícito. Sara Ziff, fundadora de la organización Model Alliance, que impulsó la norma, busca leyes similares en otros estados y a nivel federal.
En el Reino Unido, la asociación de agentes de modelos BFMA elaboró un código de buenas prácticas que exige consentimiento explícito y deja la propiedad del gemelo digital en manos de la modelo. Su director, John Horner, advirtió que sin una ley vinculante en el Reino Unido o Europa las modelos siguen expuestas a agencias abusivas.
“Firmar derechos de IA a los 20 años podría afectar a alguien diez años después”, dijo Patrick Staal, dueño de la agencia Uniko Models, de Barcelona.

articles.title: Google Localiser (Find Hub) : comment activer l'alerte en cas d'oubli d'un traqueur sur Android
articles.text:
Jusqu’ici, Localiser savait vous dire où vous aviez laissé vos clés, mais seulement après que vous aviez remarqué leur absence. La version 3.1.787-06 de l’application de Google change la donne. Selon 9to5Google, une option baptisée « Notify when left behind » permet désormais de recevoir une notification dès qu’un traqueur est séparé de votre téléphone. Le site l’a vue apparaître le 5 novembre sur des traqueurs Chipolo et sur le Moto Tag de Motorola, chez des utilisateurs américains comme européens.
Pour éviter une avalanche d’alertes chaque fois que vous sortez de chez vous en laissant votre sac, l’adresse de domicile enregistrée dans votre compte Google, celle de Google Maps, est exclue par défaut. L’option se règle traqueur par traqueur. Dans Localiser, choisissez le traqueur concerné, touchez l’icône en forme d’engrenage en haut à droite du panneau qui s’affiche en bas de l’écran, puis activez la nouvelle option dans la section dédiée. Le déploiement se fait progressivement et, si elle n’apparaît pas encore, une mise à jour de Localiser depuis le Play Store peut suffire.
Une fonction qu’Apple propose depuis 2021
Google arrive tard sur ce terrain et la concurrence a déjà fait du chemin. Apple a lancé ces alertes de séparation avec iOS 15, en 2021, pour ses AirTag, ses propres appareils et les accessoires tiers compatibles avec son réseau Localiser. La plupart des AirPods récents y ont droit aussi. Chez Samsung, l’option « Notify when left behind » de Samsung Find et de SmartThings Find couvre les Galaxy SmartTag, mais aussi les Galaxy Buds, les Galaxy Watch et le S Pen Pro.
Sur ce point, Google reste nettement en retrait. En effet, l’option n’apparaît pas pour les autres types d’appareils rattachés à Localiser, comme les écouteurs. Si vous oubliez vos écouteurs Bluetooth sur une table, votre smartphone Android ne vous dira rien, sauf si vous utilisez un modèle Samsung avec des Galaxy Buds.
D’autres nouveautés sont également à prévoir, si l’on en croit les notes de versions des services Google Play (version 26.39). Repérées en octobre par nos confrères, elles évoquent un nouveau parcours d’enregistrement des traqueurs. Il permettra de choisir une catégorie (vélo, bagage, portefeuille…), de renommer l’objet et de régler ces rappels d’oubli dès la première configuration. Google promet aussi la prise en charge du NFC, pour afficher les réglages d’un traqueur ou identifier un traqueur perdu en le touchant avec son téléphone. Cette fonction dépendra toutefois du matériel, sachant que le Pixel Tag de Google lui-même ne dispose pas de puce NFC.
