Garmin Forerunner 265 armazena músicas e surge em queda por 10x sem juros
Garmin Forerunner 265 (46 mm) armazena músicas localmente e tem ampla bateria; smartwatch sai 36% mais barato no prazo em oferta da Amazon no mês da Black Friday
O Forerunner 265 de 46 mm está saindo por R$ 2.877 em até 10x sem juros na Amazon. O smartwatch da Garmin, com 8 GB de espaço interno para guardar músicas e bateria de longa duração, sai 36% mais barato que o preço original de R$ 4.499 durante a Black November.
O Garmin Forerunner 265 possui 8 GB de memória interna, que o permite guardar quase 2 mil músicas localmente (MP3, qualidade de 192 kb/s) e reproduzi-las sem depender de um celular, oferecendo assim uma experiência de uso independente.
Seus sensores de ponta e seu software avançado suportam diversas atividades esportivas, como triatlo, cardio, força, corda, ciclismo, arco e flecha, remo, natação, tênis e basquete. Ele conta ainda com recursos de qualidade de vida, como eletrocardiograma, monitores do sono, do estresse e da saúde da mulher.
Sua bateria de lítio resiste a até 13 dias no modo smartwatch, segundo a Garmin, ou 20 horas com o GPS ativo, garantindo uma autonomia para pelo menos um dia inteiro. A construção inclui a resistência a 5 ATM, possibilitando o uso seguro em esportes aquáticos.
O Forerunner 265 também pode salvar a vida do usuário: em uma situação de risco, ele pode enviar mensagens para contatos pré-determinados, enviadas automaticamente ou pelo usuário ao segurar o botão Liga/Desliga por 6 segundos, desde que esteja pareado a um celular.
Sua tela AMOLED de 1,3″ possui brilho de até 2.000 nits, sendo capaz de reproduzir ótimas cores com visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar. O vidro Gorilla Glass 3 protege-a contra arranhões e pancadas.
O Garmin Forerunner 265 de 46 mm (R$ 2.877 em até 10x sem juros) possui conectividade Bluetooth, Wi-Fi e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição do usuário em tempo real.
A edição 2026 da Black Friday, a maior data do varejo brasileiro, será realizada no dia 27 de novembro. Durante todo o mês da Black November, a Amazon e outras lojas vão trazer ofertas com cupons e descontos exclusivos.

articles.title: Maono Launches the PD500W Hybrid Microphone for Modern Creators
articles.text:
Monday, November 9th 2026
Maono Launches the PD500W Hybrid Microphone for Modern Creators
Maono, a leading global professional microphone brand, today announced the availability of the PD500W Hybrid Microphone, a professional dynamic microphone system designed to support modern creators across podcasting, streaming, video production, interviews and live content creation. Combining 2.4 GHz wireless, USB-C and XLR connectivity with optional 32-bit float internal recording and safety-track backup, the PD500W offers a flexible audio solution for a range of production workflows. 
The retail launch follows a successful 60-day Kickstarter campaign, which concluded on August 30, 2026, with 279 backers pledging US$100,124—more than double its original US$50,000 funding goal. The PD500W was developed around a practical challenge facing modern creators: a single recording session may begin at a desk, move to an on-location interview and later transition to a mobile or studio setup. By combining three connection options—USB-C, XLR and compatible 2.4 GHz wireless—with internal recording, the PD500W gives creators the flexibility to adapt to different devices and production environments without switching microphones.Designed for Modern Production Environments
Professional dynamic microphones are widely valued for their ability to capture clear vocal recordings while minimizing unwanted background noise. However, conventional setups often require external audio interfaces, preamps, complex gain staging and separate backup recording solutions, which can make it challenging to move between different production environments.
The PD500W addresses these challenges with a hybrid connectivity platform that supports USB-C, XLR and 2.4 GHz wireless operation. USB-C enables direct connection to computers and mobile devices, while XLR integrates with existing audio interfaces and mixers. Wireless connectivity, through compatible USB-C or multi-output receivers, supports mobile recording and camera-based production. Beyond these connection options, the microphone also features internal recording, allowing creators to maintain a local copy of their audio while recording through a computer, camera or other compatible device.This versatility allows creators to use one microphone across a range of production environments, from desktop podcasting and livestreaming to mobile content creation, on-location interviews and professional studio recording, without having to rebuild their audio setup for each workflow.
Maono has also refined the product's industrial design to support cleaner production environments. The microphone integrates concealed cable routing through its U-shaped yoke system, while a dedicated rear I/O hub consolidates USB-C, headphone monitoring and XLR connections to create a streamlined workspace.
Integrated Recording Protection
A key feature of the PD500W is its focus on recording reliability. Interviews, podcasts and live recordings frequently contain moments that cannot be recreated, making redundancy increasingly important for professional content production.
To address this need, the PD500W features 32 GB of onboard storage and supports internal WAV recording in both 24-bit and 32-bit float formats. While 32-bit float provides greater flexibility for adjusting recording levels in post-production, internal recording creates an additional audio file directly within the microphone.The system also includes a selectable -9dB safety-track feature that generates a lower-level backup recording to help mitigate unexpected volume spikes. Together, these recording safeguards reduce reliance on a single recording path and provide added confidence when capturing important content.
Enhanced Production Workflows
Beyond audio capture, the PD500W has been developed to streamline post-production workflows. When paired with the multi-output wireless receiver, the PD500W supports timecode synchronization to simplify alignment between internal recordings and compatible camera footage.
The microphone also integrates with MaonoLink, Maono's companion software platform, which provides access to AI-powered transcription, translation and summarization capabilities. These tools are designed to accelerate content review, highlight key discussion points and assist with the creation of production notes, transcripts and supporting content assets.Developed with input from creators and beta testers, the PD500W has undergone refinements based on real-world feedback. Updates include an improved Mute Lock function to help prevent accidental muting, enhanced wireless stability, upgraded metal controls and an extension component for broader boom arm compatibility. These refinements reflect Maono's focus on making professional recording tools more practical and reliable in everyday production environments.
Pricing and Availability
The Maono PD500W is available globally via the Maono website and Amazon US with pricing starting at US$399 for the Basic Version and US$429 for the Desk Stand Bundle.

articles.title: Pentagon mulls placing fleet of military satellites around the Moon
articles.text:
The US military has published a Request for Information on a federal procurement website signaling interest in deploying a “proliferated cislunar constellation” consisting of an unspecified number of satellites performing an undisclosed mission in the vicinity of the Moon.
The announcement follows statements in recent months from the Space Force’s acquisitions chief for advanced programs, Maj. Gen. Stephen Purdy, that the military was getting serious about extending its reach to the Moon. The Space Force’s most distant satellites today are in geostationary orbit, some 22,000 miles (36,000 kilometers) over the equator, collecting routine surveillance and missile warning data.
Most recently, Purdy spoke of a shift in Pentagon leadership’s thinking about the Moon following an executive order signed by President Donald Trump last December. The order set out the Trump administration’s space policy. One section of the order deals with the US government’s ability to detect, characterize, and counter threats to US space interests from low-Earth orbit to cislunar space, the term of art for the region of space around the Moon.
Fighting for the Moon
“I’ve got the Secretary of War and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs full on stating in public: ‘This is a warfighting domain,’” Purdy said at Space Systems Command’s Industry Days event in October, according to a report in Air & Space Forces Magazine. “And so, I would ask you all, please jump on my cislunar bandwagon because I need some more friends here, along with our deep, passionate crew that have been working on this for years.”
Officials have emphasized the military’s role at the Moon is to protect US interests there as the United States and China ramp up their lunar programs, with a series of robotic missions culminating in crewed lunar landings in the next few years. Some US officials foresee a competition for real estate and resources at the Moon, where there are a finite number of safe landing zones that can access the Moon’s water ice at the south pole.

articles.title: Effect 4.0 Ships: Dependency-Free Rewrite with 5x Smaller Bundles and Long-Term Support
articles.text:
Effect, the TypeScript framework for building production-grade applications with typed errors, structured concurrency and dependency injection, has released Effect 4.0. Published on 30 September 2026, it is the first stable version of a line that spent eight months in beta and six weeks in release candidate.
Effect 4.0 is a from-scratch rewrite of the fiber runtime, aimed at smaller bundles, lower memory use and higher throughput. The team's own figures put a minimal program using Effect, Stream and Schema at 7.1 kB against 35.6 kB in 3.x, a 5x reduction. The heap used by 50,000 fibers drops from 157.5 MB to 21.8 MB, an 86% cut, and concurrent task throughput moves from 0.71 million to 4.57 million tasks per second, roughly 6.4x. The numbers are medians of nine fresh-process runs on identical source, and as noted by stork.ai, have not been independently reproduced.
Alongside the rewrite, the ecosystem has been consolidated. Core modules from @effect/platform, @effect/rpc and @effect/cluster now live inside the main effect package, every @effect/* package shares a single version, and the core ships with zero runtime dependencies after the final removal of pg (replaced by a native PgProtocol client) and MessagePack.
With 4.0, the team has introduced a long-term support policy. Effect 4.x receives bug fixes until September 2029, or one year after 5.0 ships, whichever is later. Security fixes run until September 2029 or two years after 5.0, again whichever is later.
Stork.ai points out that the 43.9 million weekly downloads cited at launch covers the whole ecosystem across beta and RC tags, while stable Effect 4.0 itself recorded "approximately 150,000 downloads on its first day".
On HackerNews, one commenter has been using the beta for some time and has had a very positive experience:
I’ve been using the beta on three separate projects for quite a while now and it has been totally pain-free. I mostly use the v3x core library (which has expanded to contain other libraries in v4) and Schema so I can’t speak to much outside of those, but I trust they’ve done a great job all around.
I don’t see it mentioned here, but 4 also comes with a much simpler API in some modules. Schema is much better. It’s an exceptional update. I followed many of the video logs on YouTube and was impressed by the team. This is one of my favourite software projects, period. This rebuild is incredibly well done, and I hope a lot of people are willing to try it out and adopt it, especially with the LTS.
The team's own Effect 4.0: The First Week post, published alongside patch releases 4.0.1 and 4.0.2 on 8 October, admitted that several modules intended to ship as unstable went out without a @stability tag, implicitly promising they were stable. The missing tags were added, and every exported API now declares its stability explicitly. The same window moved HTTP, SQL, RPC and AI spans to the OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
Effect 4.1 followed on 20 October 2026 with new effect/crypto modules covering randomness, hashing and signing, a Glob module backed by FileSystem.glob on Node, Bun and Deno, a streaming Csv module in effect/encoding, and support for RFC 9457 Problem Details in HttpApi.
For teams on 3.x, the v3 to v4 migration guide is the starting point, with the team suggesting coding agents can handle most of the mechanical work. Effect sits in similar territory to ZIO in the Scala world, alongside TypeScript libraries such as Effection 4.0 that target structured concurrency with a deliberately smaller surface.
Effect is an open-source TypeScript framework maintained by Effectful Technologies, providing typed error handling, structured concurrency, dependency injection and observability primitives for both frontend and backend applications.

articles.title: Bell and Virgin Plus customers get coverage boost across Canada
articles.text:
Bell is kicking off two new initiatives to improve connectivity for Canadians.
The first, Extended Coverage, is a new enhancement that helps Bell and Virgin Plus customers stay connected in more places across Canada, including areas in which coverage was previously limited or unavailable. This means that rural areas, highways and travel corridors will benefit from expanded wireless access.
Bell says Extended Coverage is included in existing plans with no extra roaming charges or hidden fees. This feature will automatically apply when customers are in relevant coverage areas, with devices displaying either Bell-EXT or Virgin-EXT to inform you when you’re connected. Bell has a map to show where Extended Coverage is currently available and where access will continue to expand.
Additionally, Bell says it’s rolling out another initiative at the end of this week called Priority Network Access, which is intended to provide eligible customers with a more consistent mobile experience during periods of network congestion. With this feature, customers on eligible rate plans will benefit from faster speeds and more reliable connectivity in heavily crowded places like downtown spaces, transit hubs, music festivals and packed stadiums. As with Extended Coverage, this feature will work automatically with no action needed on the customer’s end.

articles.title: The race is on to sue Nvidia | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia’s stock slid more than 4% on Monday, the first trading day after its board said it would investigate CEO Jensen Huang over his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive U.S. intelligence believes was spying for China.
Securities lawyers were already moving. At least four firms, including Schall, Brown & Schwartz and Levi & Korsinsky, announced investigations Monday into whether Nvidia misled investors. Robert Bartlett, a Stanford Law professor and securities law expert, expects them to have plenty of company.
“I would definitely wager that there’ll be a filing,” Bartlett said in an interview Monday morning, adding that he wouldn’t be surprised if a case had been filed by the end of the day. Plaintiffs’ lawyers have good reasons to be first in line; under federal securities law, the first complaint triggers a public notice, and investors then have 60 days to ask the court to be named lead plaintiff. A firm that files early gets a head start on signing up investors with large losses, as well as on shaping the story of the case. Bartlett was right, in fact. A case surfaced Monday afternoon in the Northern District of California, where Nvidia is headquartered.
Rosen Law Firm, a New York-based plaintiffs’ firm that specializes in securities class actions, filed it on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher, a retail investor who made seven purchases totaling roughly $20,500 this year, according to a schedule attached to the complaint. (Rosen was lead counsel in a $250 million settlement with Alibaba and ranks among the most active filers of such cases.) The proposed class covers anyone who bought Nvidia securities between Oct. 9, 2025, and Nov. 8, 2026, and the suit names both Nvidia and Huang.
The complaint accuses them of misleading investors about Huang’s ties to Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center outfit where Alice Huang was considered a top exec, and it points to three statements as proof: Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo’s late-October claim that Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual or unexpected,” the company’s even earlier claim that it found “no evidence of diversion” of its chips, and Jensen Huang’s Oct. 30 comment to Bloomberg that Nvidia’s dealings with Megaspeed were “normal and not unusual.”
All three were false or misleading, the suit says, because Huang was having an affair with Alice Huang. Kistenmacher is asking for unspecified damages, interest and attorneys’ fees, and he wants a jury trial.
While much remains unknown, the legal theory here doesn’t depend on anything the board’s investigation may turn up about Huang’s private life. When The New York Times first reported on Huang’s ties to Alice Huang last month, Rizzo really did tell the Times that the relationship was “not unusual or unexpected.” Rizzo separately told another outlet, The Hill, that “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.”
Of course, the world now knows that was not true. Worse, the Times reports that U.S. intelligence had been monitoring Alice Huang for more than a year.
From a securities perspective, Bartlett said, the company’s earlier statement was “clearly a misleading statement.” And because Huang is CEO, Bartlett said, “his knowledge gets imputed to the company.” In other words, Nvidia is treated as having known what its chief executive knew.
The Kistenmacher complaint makes the same argument.
Bartlett predicted a “classic fraud on the market” claim, in which investors argue they paid prices that reflected false or incomplete public information, and lost money when the truth emerged. This early lawsuit relies on that theory, and Monday’s drop of $7.97 per share, or 4.27%, gives the attorneys involved a lot to work with. Damages in such cases are tied to the stock’s decline, and Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world, so you can imagine a settlement could prove exceedingly expensive.
That means a large payment from the company and its directors-and-officers insurers, but typically no personal consequences for the CEO or the board. It is also a civil matter, so Huang isn’t facing prison over it. The irony, as Bartlett noted, is that the suit is brought in the name of Nvidia’s shareholders, and shareholders ultimately pay for the settlement, directly or through insurance premiums.
Bartlett sorted Nvidia’s wider exposure into buckets. The first is the securities fraud claim, which is the clearest immediate problem for the company and potentially for Huang. The second is governance: what the board knew and when. It’s possible directors were kept in the dark, but the board also has oversight duties, and once the Times began reporting on the Megaspeed connection, the company should have had reporting lines to bring a critical risk like this to directors. If it didn’t, or if directors didn’t act, board-level liability is possible.
A third category, one that would change everything, would arise only if the board’s investigation finds Huang knew about the intelligence connection. That would be “a whole other ball game,” as Bartlett said. (The board said in a statement to the public Sunday that it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.)
There’s also the question of government action. The SEC can seek an officer-and-director bar for intentional securities-fraud violations, which Bartlett said is technically on the table. But he doubts the current SEC under Chairman Paul Atkins would have the appetite, given President Trump’s support for Huang. A roughly two-year clock after discovery of the facts would leave room for a future administration to act, but the window would be tight, and Bartlett posited that’s pretty unlikely when asked about it.
It’s worth underscoring that neither law firm announcements nor this newly filed complaint is a sign of a strong case. Plaintiffs’ firms are quick to publish these notices when they see an opportunity. Which firm winds up leading the case is decided later by the court, and that decision usually depends on which investor has suffered the biggest loss. Kistenmacher said in his filing that he’s willing to serve as lead plaintiff, but the court will ultimately choose among the competing investors. No doubt they’ll materialize soon.

articles.title: China builds massive 800-megawatt AI data center campus to rival US Stargate project — Galaxy campus delivers first 120 megawatts in a year at one-fifth the cost
articles.text:
China builds massive 800-megawatt AI data center campus to rival US Stargate project — Galaxy campus delivers first 120 megawatts in a year at one-fifth the cost
China's 800MW AI campus takes on Stargate with wind power, batteries and 800V DC
China is building an 800MW AI data center campus in Inner Mongolia that could challenge the economics of America's Stargate project, according to a new report from SemiAnalysis. Envision has built the first 120 MW of Galaxy AI data center campus in less than a year, a cost the researchers put at just one-fifth of comparable US projects, after visiting the site in September.
But getting the buildings up is only half of the battle. AI data centers need enormous amounts of electricity, and Envision is taking an unusual route to secure it— building its own wind farms and battery storage alongside the computing facility.
While US developers are turning to on-site gas turbines to work around grid constraints, Envision is building its data center alongside wind farms, battery storage, and dedicated power infrastructure. Galaxy is located in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, and is being developed across four phases for two unnamed internet companies. The completed campus is planned to provide up to 800MW of IT capacity by the end of 2027, putting it closer to the approximately 820MW of critical IT capacity at the Stargate campus in Abilene, Texas.
Envision is building its own power supply for Galaxy rather than leaving everything to the local grid. So far, the company has installed more than 100GW of wind turbines and wants its wind farms to provide over 60% of the electricity needed by the campus’s first two phases. Those farms, located about 80 kilometers apart, have a combined capacity of 420MW. That's well above the 240MW load expected from the first two phases, although wind turbines rarely get to run flat out. Ulanqab’s wind capacity factor is between 355 and 40%, so Envision is adding four-hour battery storage to keep the electricity coming when the wind dies down.
Power equipment is proving rather hard to come by for some US data center builders. We have previously reported on turbine shortages that have pushed delivery estimates to 2030, while SpaceX is looking to manufacture its own turbine blades for its gas-powered AI facilities. Envision, meanwhile, is putting wind generation and battery storage right alongside its servers.
The power hardware inside the Galaxy is worth a look, too. Semianalyss visited a 5MW hall where solid-state transformers take 10kV AC electricity and convert it directly into 800V DC for the server racks. That's a fairly substantial departure from conventional data-center power distribution, which typically involves several intermediate conversion stages. “In one 5MW hall, we saw the 800V system at work,” the researchers wrote. They explained that “Solid-state transformers (SSTs) take 10kV AC from the grid and convert it straight to 800V DC for the racks.”
The design removes several intermediate components found in conventional data center power systems, including low voltage transformers, uninterruptible power supplies and rectifiers. Fewer conversion stages can reduce equipment requirements and energy losses, although SemiAnalysis did not provide a measured efficiency improvement for Galaxy’s pilot. The 5MW installation is only a small part of the campus, but it puts the technology into operation at a live facility. Envision, however, plans an even larger deployment in the next construction phases, a move that aligns with Nvidia's push for 800V DC distribution in future high-density AI systems.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Galaxy's campus uses a cooling arrangement in which liquid-cooled and air-cooled servers share a single water loop, eliminating the need for conventional central chiller plants. That matters as AI servers generate more heat and require increasingly sophisticated cooling systems. Removing central chillers can simplify infrastructure, although the design depends on local climate conditions and the facility's ability to reject heat through its water loop. China has previously experimented with other unconventional cooling methods, including a wind-powered underwater datacenter off Shanghai that uses surrounding seawater to help cool its servers.
That said, Galaxy is the first major project in Invision's wider Inner Mongolia datacentre plans, which Semianalysis says add up to 3GW, with the rest of the campus still a busy construction site. The surrounding Chahar High-tech Zone is also expanding rapidly, with nearly 30,000 construction workers spread across 22 data center projects, according to a local report cited by the researchers.
The wider Chinese expansion is also attracting some of the world's largest technology companies. Alibaba, Huawei and ByteDance are among the firms expanding infrastructure in the region, which benefits from relatively cheap electricity, available land and abundant wind resources. However access to electricity and datacenter buildings does not automatically translate to available AI computing power. China's access to advanced accelerators remains a separate constraint, particularly as US export restrictions limit its ability to acquire Nvidia’s most powerful chips.

articles.title: Black Friday: Warum uns die Händler schon jetzt mit Rabatten bombardieren
articles.text:
Black Friday: Warum der Handel schon Wochen vorher die Rabattschlacht eröffnet
Wir schauen auf den Kalender und reiben uns verwundert die Augen: Der Black Friday ist erst am 27. November – und doch wirbt gefühlt schon die halbe Branche mit dem Schnäppchen-Schlagwort, das die preisbewussten Kund:innen in Wallung bringen soll. Und die Geschäfte sind erfinderisch: Pre-Black-Friday-Angebote, Early-Black-Friday-Deals und Black Weeks sind nur ein paar der kreativen Wortschöpfungen, die allesamt nur eins suggerieren sollen: Billiger wird’s so schnell nicht mehr.
Man könnte fast glauben, der Handel hätte Angst, den Black Friday zu verpassen. Doch in Wahrheit laufen vor allem die Händler dem Geld ihrer Kund hinterher. Dass sie damit seit Jahren immer früher anfangen, hat einen Grund, der insbesondere in diesem Jahr eine große Rolle spielen könnte: Die Kund:innen können ihr Weihnachtsgeld, so sie es überhaupt noch bekommen, schließlich nur einmal ausgeben.
Und wer hier früher dran ist als die anderen, so das Kalkül, hat größere Chancen darauf. Wer also sein Budget bereits Anfang November bei Händler A gelassen hat, fällt Ende November womöglich als Kunde für Händler B aus.
Die Angst, zu früh gekauft zu haben
Doch gerade in wirtschaftlich angespannten Zeiten überlegen Verbraucher:innen genauer, wofür sie ihr Erspartes ausgeben. Schon länger beobachten Marktforscher:innen gar nicht mal so sehr eine Kaufzurückhaltung, wohl aber, dass die Verbraucher:innen bis zum November mit wichtigen Anschaffungen warten – wohl wissend, dass in dieser Zeit das Rennen um die Rabatte besonders ausgeprägt ist.
Eher neu ist hier aber neben der verlängerten Rückgabefrist bis in den Januar, mit der Amazon schon seit Jahren den Markt zum Mitziehen motiviert, ein weiterer Faktor: Immer mehr Händler:innen bieten automatisch oder auf Anfrage eine Bestpreis-Garantie für all jene, die sich jetzt für einen Kauf entscheiden. Die Idee dahinter: Wer heute kauft, soll sich in zwei Wochen nicht ärgern, wenn das gleiche Produkt am eigentlichen Black Friday plötzlich noch günstiger angeboten wird.
Dabei lohnt sich dennoch ein Blick ins Kleingedruckte, denn nicht bei allen Händlern bedeutet das, dass man automatisch davon profitiert. In einigen Fällen müssen Kund:innen selbst aktiv werden, den günstigeren Preis entdecken und die Differenz beim Kundenservice beantragen. Eine weitere Einschränkung: Während die Preisgarantie in vielen Fällen branchenweit gilt, bezieht sie sich manchmal auch lediglich auf die Preise beim selben Händler.
Aus Sicht der Logistik ein gutes Geschäft
Dass viele Händler:innen den Black Friday entzerren wollen, hat aber auch noch einen weiteren, durchaus vernünftigen Grund: die Logistik. Denn die letzten Jahre haben gezeigt, dass innerhalb weniger Tage Lager, Versanddienstleister und Kundenservice übermäßig strapaziert wurden. Auch können die Händler:innen so ihre Ads-Kampagnen über einen längeren Zeitraum ziehen, anstatt an einem einzigen Wochenende mit allen anderen um die Aufmerksamkeit der Kund:innen zu buhlen.
Aus dem Black Friday wird so eine Art vorweihnachtliche Dauerschleife der Kaufverführung. Noch sieht es nicht danach aus, dass die Händler:innen das Thema überreizt hätten, auch wenn das Risiko durchaus besteht, dass dabei die Aufmerksamkeit irgendwann auf der Strecke bleibt.
All das ist aus Sicht vieler Händler nachvollziehbar. Denn wer abwartet, bis die Mitbewerber ihre Rabattaktionen starten, muss nicht nur gegen deren Preise ankämpfen, sondern riskiert auch, dass viele potenzielle Kund:innen längst eingekauft haben und aus dem Rennen sind.

articles.title: French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa hit in cyberattack — up to $133 million stolen and systems shut down
articles.text:
French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa hit in cyberattack — up to $133 million stolen and systems shut down
Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed ballpark figure
- Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms cyberattack led to the theft of roughly $133 million from the bank itself
- Attackers reportedly converted stolen funds into cryptocurrency and laundered them across multiple services and blockchains
- Bank says customer assets were unaffected, while investigators continue probing the third-party compromise
Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, a major French banking and financial services group, has confirmed it recently suffered a cyberattack that resulted in the theft of around $133 million.
The stolen money apparently did not belong to customers, but rather to the bank itself, and was converted into cryptocurrency to be siphoned out more easily.
The attack was first spotted by ZachXBT, a cryptocurrency analyst and blockchain fraud investigator who issued an alert on November 2 2026. “An EU entity is suspected of losing $106M+ from multiple centralized exchange accounts yesterday (Nov 1),” he said at the time. “The suspected stolen funds were withdrawn as USDC & USDT by an illicit actor.”
Blockchain as the tech of choice for both sides
It appears the attackers converted fiat currency into different cryptos before sending them out. As ZachXBT explained, the threat actor was “aggressively swapping” USDC (a stablecoin currency, one whose value is pegged to that of the US dollar) for ETH (Ethereum) and transferring the tokens to instant exchanges such as WellWallet and Keyrex. Some of the funds were converted to XMR (Monero, a known privacy-first token whose transactions are notoriously difficult to track) via Wagyu, and later bridged “across multiple chains.”
The irony is pbvious - blockchain and cryptocurrencies are often perceived as the go-to platforms for financial fraud and while many defend it by saying the fraud conducted via fiat is magnitudes larger, the fact remains the crooks transferred dollars to cryptos during theft.
On the other hand, the attack was not even discovered (at least publicly) until it hit the public blockchain where analysts like ZachXBT were able to see it and report on it.
A day later, ZachXBT issued an update, saying he identified an additional $27M+ of withdrawals, bringing the total amount stolen to $133M+.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“My working theory is a large financial institution in Western Europe was exploited and it’s currently being covered up,” he said. “No proper incident disclosure has resulted in $30M+ being laundered away which could have been frozen by EU law enforcement,” he added, suggesting that Crédit Mutuel Arkéa handled the situation poorly.
In his reports, however, he never mentions the name of the organization targeted. Crédit Mutuel Arkéa released a brief statement on November 4, saying it suffered an attack which it later managed to contain.
“As soon as this attack was detected [...] the decision was made, as a precautionary measure, to temporarily suspend certain transactions in order to secure operations and prevent any further fraudulent movements,” the announcement reads.
“This incident is closed and is now under control. Operations are being gradually resumed over the course of the morning, after the group and its subsidiaries ensured that checks had been carried out and enhanced security measures had been put in place.”
Not Lazarus
In an FAQ published a day later, the company said the attackers “went through the platform of one of our service providers and thus reached Crédit Mutuel Arkéa directly.” It did not want to say which service provider that is, but ruled out Fortuneo since that name was apparently being mentioned in local press.
The attackers used Arkéa's own account to carry out transactions with other banking players, it said, confirming that customer funds are safe and unaffected.
“We would like to reassure all our customers that this incident has no consequences for their assets. It only led to a delayed execution of certain transfer operations,” the FAQ further states.
The bank did not want to confirm the amount of money that was stolen, but commenting on ZachXBT’s $133 million figure, said it can “simply validate the order of magnitude.” In other words - it’s a close estimate.
So far no threat actors claimed responsibility for this attack, and chances are none will. ZachXBT believes this was not the work of notorious North Korean actors Lazarus Group.

articles.title: Sony dévoile un nouveau PlayStation Portal, avec plus de mémoire
articles.text:
Autant dire que le PlayStation Portal ne nous avait pas spécialement enthousiasmés lors de sa sortie en novembre 2023. Cet appareil, vendu au prix de 219 euros à sa sortie et présenté comme portable, s’est révélé être un simple accessoire de la PS5. Autrement dit, le PlayStation Portal se présente comme une manette DualSense coupée en deux, avec un écran intégré au milieu, qui fonctionne en diffusant les jeux depuis une PS5.
Cet accessoire a tout de même ensuite gagné en intérêt lorsque Sony a ajouté en novembre 2025 la possibilité de jouer depuis le cloud. Plus besoin de PS5 : un abonnement au PlayStation Plus Premium suffit désormais pour utiliser le PlayStation Portal. Bonne nouvelle pour ceux qui seraient intéressés par l’appareil : Sony a dévoilé une nouvelle version, mais qui est pour l’instant limitée à deux marchés.
Sony dévoile une nouvelle version du PlayStation Portal
Baptisée PlayStation Portal Player, cette nouvelle version de l’appareil semble de prime abord identique en tout point. On retrouve ainsi un écran LCD de 8 pouces (1080p/60 ips), un son 3D, un retour haptique et des gâchettes adaptatives. Seule différence visible : sa couleur noire.
C’est plutôt à l’intérieur de l’appareil que se situe la vraie nouveauté. En effet, Sony y a intégré davantage de mémoire interne. La firme nippone explique : « en prévision de futures fonctionnalités, du stockage interne a été ajouté sur ce nouveau modèle. Les détails concernant ces futures fonctionnalités seront communiqués dès qu’ils seront finalisés ». Mais de quelles fonctionnalités est-il ici question ? Autant dire que nous n’avons aucune indication.
Sony annonce une amélioration, sans expliquer précisément en quoi celle-ci sera bénéfique pour les joueurs. Nous pouvons imaginer que cette mémoire interne supplémentaire permettra d’installer des applications (plateformes de streaming, services de streaming musical, etc.) ou des jeux relativement modestes, ce qui permettrait de jouer hors ligne. Cet espace pourrait également être mobilisé pour prendre en charge de nouvelles fonctionnalités.
Un lancement seulement sur deux marchés
La PlayStation Portal Player sera commercialisée au Japon ce 10 décembre au prix de 39 980 yens (environ 226 euros). Sony précise que la langue du système est uniquement en japonais et que l’appareil peut être utilisé seulement avec un compte enregistré au Japon. Inutile donc d’espérer pouvoir en commander une depuis l’Europe. À noter que l’appareil sera également commercialisé ce 10 décembre en Corée du Sud, avec les mêmes restrictions. À l’heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, Sony n’a fait aucune annonce concernant un lancement de la machine sur le marché européen. Il reste maintenant à voir si cela sera le cas dans les mois à venir. Sony continue donc d’améliorer le PlayStation Portal, tout en développant la PlayStation 6.

articles.title: Intel entend lancer Razor Lake-S courant 2028 et conserverait le socket LGA-1954
articles.text:
C'est un peu comme mettre la charrue avant les bœufs alors que Nova Lake n'est même pas présenté officiellement, mais des infos sur la suite des événements, c'est toujours utile.
Nous le savons depuis déjà plusieurs mois, Intel entend remplacer les processeurs Nova Lake par la génération Razor Lake dans un avenir plus ou moins proche. Un avenir qui se dessine aujourd'hui davantage grâce à quelques indiscrétions d'un informateur bien connu.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Razor Lake arriverait bien courant 2028
Pour le moment, l'avenir d'Intel s'écrit avec Nova Lake. La génération de processeurs – desktop et mobile – qui remplacera bientôt Arrow Lake est toujours attendue quelque part au cours du premier trimestre de l'année prochaine, en attendant qu'Intel confirme tout cela.
Toutefois, et vous le savez si vous lisez régulièrement nos actualités processeurs, Intel a déjà bien avancé sur la génération suivante qui porte le nom de code de Razor Lake et devrait notamment inclure un véritable monstre de puissance. Cho Min-sung – directeur exécutif chez Intel Corée – a déjà évoqué un processeur Razor Lake-AX qui sera en mesure d'atteindre 700 TOPS, et ce, à l'horizon 2028.
Notons au passage que cela confirme un certain retard de la part d'Intel car si on se réfère à de vieilles prévisions – pensez donc, 2024, c'est la préhistoire ! – Nova Lake devait sortir en fin d'année 2025 et Razor Lake devait suivre juste derrière avec une fenêtre de lancement prévue autour de la fin d'année 2026… Oui, en ce moment même. Nous sommes loin du compte.
Au moins trois générations en socket LGA-1954
Mais revenons-en à nos moutons et à ces précisions délivrées par Jaykihn sur la plateforme X. Bien connu et souvent plutôt juste dans ses commentaires, l'informateur indique d'emblée que rien de ceci n'est encore officiel.
On se doute qu'Intel ne va pas encore parler du lancement d'une génération future (Razor Lake) alors qu'il n'a même pas officialisé de manière claire celui de la toute prochaine architecture (Nova Lake). En revanche, Jaykihn souligne deux points intéressants. Le premier, c'est que Razor Lake est toujours considéré par Intel comme un « produit de 2028 ». Cette fois l'intervalle entre Nova Lake et Razor Lake semble d'ailleurs plus raisonnable.
Deuxième information, et non des moindres, Razor Lake garderait bien le même support que Nova Lake, le nouveau socket LGA-1954. Nous avions déjà évoqué une telle éventualité, mais il est toujours heureux d'avoir une confirmation supplémentaire, d'autant que celle-ci arrive avec une nouvelle hypothèse : que le socket LGA-1954 sera plusieurs générations et les bruits de couloir évoquent l'architecture post-Razor Lake, Hammer Lake.
Bien sûr, ce serait un agréable changement de stratégie de la part d'Intel alors qu'AMD insiste depuis des années sur le suivi à très long terme de ses propres plateformes avec un socket AM4 qui reste encore d'actualité dix ans après son lancement. Nous n'en sommes pas encore là chez Intel, mais le maintien du socket LGA-1954 sur au moins trois générations est déjà une bonne nouvelle.
Rappelons enfin que Razor Lake dans sa version desktop (Razor Lake-S) devrait intégrer de nouveaux cœurs performants, les Griffin Cove venant remplacer les Coyote Cove prévus pour Nova Lake. Des puces Razor Lake sont également prévues pour intégrer jusqu'à 12 cœurs GPU Xe3P. En revanche, toujours selon Jaykihn, le simultaneous multithreading ne serait pas au menu des cœurs Griffin Cove pour le marché client alors qu'il le serait sur les puces à destination des processeurs Xeon.
Source : VideoCardz

articles.title: enza attracts $6 million investment to expand its African payments network
articles.text:
enza attracts $6 million investment to expand its African payments network
- UAE-headquartered fintech enza has raised $6 million in a Seed+ funding round, led by 4DX Ventures, with participation from British International Investment (BII). Existing investors Quona Capital and Algebra Ventures, which co-led the company's $6.75 million seed round in March 2025, also increased their investments.
- Founded in 2023 by Hany Fekry and Hamish Houston, enza is headquartered in Abu Dhabi, with regional offices in Egypt, South Africa, Ghana and Nigeria. The company provides payment infrastructure that enables banks and fintechs to offer digital payment services through a single platform integration.
- enza currently serves banks and fintech companies across 12 African countries. Its technology supports payment acceptance, transaction processing, fraud detection and other payment services, allowing financial institutions to modernise their systems while retaining control of their customer relationships and data.
- The funding will support expansion into additional African markets, the acquisition of regulatory licences and further development of enza's payment technology and product portfolio.
Press release:
enza, the payments infrastructure provider to banks and fintechs across Africa, has closed a US$6 million Seed+ round led by 4DX Ventures. British International Investment (BII), the UK’s development finance institution, joins as a new investor. Quona Capital and Algebra Ventures, who co-led enza’s seed round in 2025, have both added to their positions.
The round is a vote of confidence from the people who know enza best. Its existing investors have watched the business up close since the seed and chose to invest more capital. BII joins after completing its own investment and ESG due diligence.
Why it matters to African stakeholders
One of the biggest decisions a bank can make is the choice of payments infrastructure partner. This decision shapes the propositions the bank can take to market, how it differentiates its services, and which markets it can serve profitably. Switching is costly and regulators scrutinise outsourcing, so the choice has a long tail. Until recently, banks had limited options and were largely tied to legacy providers. Now a new generation of payments infrastructure providers has emerged, built on modern architectures that bring speed, lower operating costs and faster time to market. enza is leading the way on the African continent and now serves bank and fintech clients across 12 countries.
The new capital goes into the areas that clients rely on most. enza will extend into new markets, particularly those where the digitisation of payments is both a major opportunity and a national priority, and secure the additional licences needed to serve more banks and fintechs there. Clients get locally relevant payment infrastructure, delivered in line with each market’s regulatory requirements, on leading technology built for scale. The funding also supports continued investment in expanding the enza product line and the value these services unlock for enza clients.
Hany Fekry, Group Chief Executive Officer at enza“
Since our launch, we have been building the payments infrastructure partner African banks and fintechs have been missing. Our existing investors have seen us deliver, and they have put more capital behind us to accelerate our growth,” said Hany Fekry, Group CEO of enza. “To have leading fintech investors and a development finance institution of BII’s standing back that, after looking hard at what we do, is a powerful endorsement. For our clients, it means a partner with the resources and stability to keep investing in their payment capabilities. It also reaffirms our commitment to the transformation of the continent, one payment at a time.“
Daniel Marlo, Managing Partner at 4DX Ventures“
Payments in Africa have moved well beyond cards and are truly omni-channel today, yet the infrastructure on which banks depend has not kept pace,” said Daniel Marlo, Managing Partner at 4DX Ventures. “enza enables banks to modernise via a single integration to enza’s platform while allowing banks to retain control of their merchants and their data. 4DX led this round because we see that enza addresses a key gap in the ecosystem and the founders have done this before. They helped build one of the continent’s leading payment processors, serving banks across more than 40 African markets, and subsequently led processing and regional operations for one of the region’s largest payments companies following its acquisition of their business. That record has earned them the trust of banks, schemes and regulators across Africa, which is ultimately what determines success in this industry. We believe enza can become the backbone of how money moves across the continent, connecting every bank, merchant and consumer on a single modern network, and we are proud to partner with the team to build it.”
Chirantan Patnaik, Head of Disruptive Ventures at BII
“enza provides banks and financial institutions with the modern payments infrastructure that they need to reduce costs, broaden payment options, and expand access to affordable and reliable financial services across developing markets.” said Chirantan Patnaik, Head of Disruptive Ventures at BII. “Our investment in enza reflects our focus on inclusive finance and supporting SMEs by tackling a major barrier: the high cost and complexity of digital payments infrastructure.”

articles.title: Benidorm pone freno a las sillas propulsadas y prohíbe la circulación de las que tengan más de una plaza
articles.text:
Las sillas autopropulsadas de más de una plaza serán eliminadas de las calles de Benidorm. El pleno municipal aprobó inicialmente este cambio con el consenso de todos los grupos. Se trata de la reforma de la Ordenanza de Movilidad que todavía debe completar su tramitación.
Son de aquellos vehículos eléctricos (también llamados “scooters”) de varios asientos. Estos son muy utilizados por los turistas británicos mayores que van a Benidorm. El objetivo de esta modificación es mejorar la seguridad de los peatones en aceras y zonas peatonales.
El concejal de Movilidad, Francis Muñoz, ha situado esta reforma en el contexto de actualización de las normas de movilidad del Ayuntamiento de cara a los nuevos sistemas de transporte que se están implementando. Por otro lado, en el ámbito de la movilidad urbana también han tenido que regular aspectos relacionados con el alquiler de los vehículos (como contamos nosotros al hablar de las autorizaciones de patinetes en Madrid).
Qué cambia para las sillas con varias plazas
En la modificación del título IX se añade explícitamente el veto a las sillas de más de una plaza. En el texto municipal que se publicó en 2021 ya estaba prohibido llevar ocupantes. Sin embargo, se exceptuaban los vehículos que por su propia construcción podían llevar un ocupante trasero. Esta excepción pasará a desaparecer.
Muñoz ha indicado que un 25 % de los accidentes de tráfico en entornos urbanos de Benidorm tienen algún vehículo de movilidad personal involucrado. Este dato hace referencia a todos los vehículos de movilidad personal, no solo a las sillas autopropulsadas o a los vehículos de dos plazas.
El cambio de movilidad necesita acabar de tramitarse
Antes de votarlo, se ha hecho una consulta pública de 15 días naturales. En ella no se han presentado alegaciones ni sugerencias. A continuación viene una exposición pública de 30 días hábiles. Tras ello se procederá a su aprobación definitiva y entrada en vigor. La votación en pleno es la aprobación inicial.
En esta revisión se recoge el texto original de la ordenanza junto con sus modificaciones posteriores. Muñoz ha explicado que se trata de clarificar las normas existentes.
Así pues, se aprovecha para aprobar todo en un único acto. Desde el Ayuntamiento se vincula esta reforma a la defensa de los usuarios vulnerables. También se habla de acciones para “tranquilizar” el tráfico y hacer más sostenible ambientalmente el casco urbano.

articles.title: Masahiro Sakurai (Super Smash Bros.) n'utilise pas l'IA générative, mais conseille aux studios de ne pas la rejeter — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les créateurs stars du jeu vidéo japonais passent l’un après l’autre devant la même question : que pensent-ils de l’IA générative, ces outils qui bouleversent la création artistiques, en particulier dans le jeu vidéo en générant texte, image, son et code ? Après Shigeru Miyamoto et Hideo Kojima, Masahiro Sakurai, le père de Kirby et de Super Smash Bros., a répondu le 7 novembre. Il était sur scène à Akihabara, à Tokyo, pour le festival des 40 ans du magazine Famitsu.
Sakurai n’utilise pas l’IA
Sur ce sujet, Sakurai indique qu’il ne s’en sert pas lui-même, mais il déconseille aux studios de la rejeter en bloc. Sakurai n’a utilisé l’IA générative dans aucun de ses jeux, y compris Kirby Air Riders, sorti le 20 novembre 2025 sur Switch 2.
Il ne s’en sert même pas pour chercher des idées, car d’après lui, on ne peut pas tout faire tenir dans un simple prompt, et une idée ne suffit pas sans un calendrier, une équipe capable de le tenir et un budget.
Jouez dans les meilleures conditions avec la TV TCL C79L : une expérience gaming fluide en 144 Hz et un son immersif signé Bang & Olufsen, actuellement en promotion !
Pour les graphismes, il estime que la technologie n’a « toujours pas gagné la confiance » des développeurs et qu’elle ne doit pas devenir une forme d’exploitation.
Pour Sakurai, on trouve de meilleures idées en réfléchissant soi-même.
Dix fois plus de travail qu’en 2003
Sakurai juge aussi que créer un jeu est devenu « beaucoup trop exigeant ».
Il raconte que Kirby Air Riders lui a demandé dix fois plus de travail que Kirby Air Ride, le jeu d’origine sorti sur GameCube en 2003, et il cite des jeux qui perdent de l’argent alors qu’ils se sont vendus à plusieurs millions d’exemplaires.
Il prévient donc que ceux qui rejettent l’IA parce qu’elle n’est pas fiable « risquent de prendre un retard de plus en plus important ». Selon lui, les studios qui s’en servent « sans aucune hésitation » sortiront davantage de jeux.
Sakurai dit qu’il serait mal venu de ne rien faire, qu’il est encore trop tôt pour dire où et comment l’utiliser, et que lui-même y va doucement.

articles.title: Pour le dernier jour du Black Friday 2026, ce robot tondeuse Dreame 5 étoiles perd 136 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 – La tondeuse à gazon Dreame A2 "5 étoiles" à 939,00 € (-13%)
La tondeuse à gazon Dreame A2 passe sous les 950 € chez Amazon soit une baisse d'environ 13% sur le prix habituellement constaté. C'est actuellement l'un des meilleurs produit de notre comparatif.
Après un premier robot de tonte très convaincant, Dreame revient à la charge avec l'A2. Ce modèle reprend la technologie LiDAR de son prédécesseur, mais y ajoute une caméra pour mieux appréhender son environnement. Il inaugure aussi un système de coupe amélioré, permettant de déplacer le disque jusqu'aux bordures.
Dreame A2
- 
                            Equipement et installation
                            
            
- 
                            Ergonomie et utilisation
                            
            
- 
                            Efficacité et qualité de tonte
                            
            
- 
                            Réparabilité
                            
            
Points forts
- Facilité d'installation et d'utilisation.
- Design très réussi.
- Fonctionnement sans fil et sans balise.
- App intuitive avec de nombreuses options de paramétrage.
Points faibles
- Détection d'obstacles qui manque parfois de fiabilité.
- Système EdgeMaster décevant.
- Tarif très élevé.
- Autonomie.
Le Dreame A2 marque une belle évolution par rapport à son prédécesseur, tout en reprenant ses principaux atouts : expérience d’utilisation simplifiée, design toujours aussi soigné et technologie de navigation inspirée des meilleurs aspirateurs-robots. L’installation sans fil, la cartographie précise, la connectivité avancée et l’interface intuitive en font un robot accessible, même pour les novices. Sur le terrain, il livre une tonte globalement homogène et soignée avec des trajectoires bien maîtrisées et un fonctionnement silencieux. On apprécie aussi les nombreuses options de personnalisation. Mais tout n’est pas parfait : le système EdgeMaster, censé améliorer la tonte des bordures, reste perfectible et la détection d’obstacles manque parfois de fiabilité. L’autonomie limitée pourrait aussi poser problème pour les très grandes surfaces, alors que le prix élevé place clairement le Dreame A2 dans la catégorie premium.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
En alternative

articles.title: La crisis de la memoria ya no encarece sólo los móviles baratos: los modelos 'Ultra' son los siguientes en el punto de mira
articles.text:
Ya lo dijo Carl Pei, fundador de Nothing, hace unos meses: la memoria RAM ya era el componente más caro de los nuevos teléfonos. Estamos metidos de lleno en una crisis de memoria sin precedentes y ya hemos contado cómo ese aumento de los costes ha tenido consecuencias para el móvil barato. Por un lado, haciendo que haya empresas que se bajen del carro. Por otro, encareciendo los precios del móvil de entrada, gama baja y media sin que las especificaciones mejoren respecto a la generación anterior.
Sin embargo, una filtración apunta a una nueva categoría de víctimas en todo este asunto: la de los móviles de gama más premium. Y el Oppo Find X10 Ultra estaría en el punto de mira.
En corto. Nuestros compañeros de Xataka Móvil se han hecho eco de Digital Chat Station, un filtrador que, en Weibo, ha dejado caer que un modelo "ultra" de un móvil de generación actual habría sido puesto en pausa debido a la situación de los componentes. No dijo marca ni modelo, pero desde Android Authority se ha señalado que ese modelo misterioso que se queda por el camino es el Oppo Find X10 Ultra.
Buque insignia. Los Find X10 y Find X10 Pro Max llegaron a nuestro territorio a finales de este octubre y, como ya hemos expuesto en nuestros análisis, se trata de dos móviles de lo más interesantes. El Pro Max en concreto tiene unas capacidades fotográficas espectaculares, pero se esperaba un modelo "superflagship". Siguiendo el patrón de la generación actual, Oppo tendría el modelo Ultra preparado para comienzos de 2027, listo para competir contra lo más ambicioso tanto de Xiaomi como, sobre todo, de Vivo.
Evidentemente, hablamos de filtraciones, pero el móvil apuntaba a tener una cámara principal de 200 megapíxeles, un gran angular de 200 megapíuxeles, un teleobjetivo 3x también de 200 megapíxeles y otro teleobjetivo óptico 10x de 50 megapíxeles. Vendría para competir por el reinado fotográfico en 2027, pero con un Find X10 Pro Max que ya parte de un precio bastante alto, subir un escalón en especificaciones haría que los precios aumentaran aún más.
El Find X9 Ultra llegó en abril de este año por 1.699 euros, mientras que el mencionado X10 Pro Max acaba de desembarcar por 1.799 euros. Esto obligaría a aumentar mucho el precio y es fácil que los márgenes no compensen llegados a cierto punto, sobre todo cuando las fuentes de la industria señalan que la crisis de memoria y el precio de los componentes no se va a relajar a medio plazo.
El caso 'Ultra'. De nuevo, se trata de una filtración, pero hay que recordar que llevamos meses con señales contradictorias en lo que respecta a los móviles 'Ultra'. En agosto, las filtraciones apuntaban que Xiaomi había cancelado los planes del Xiaomi 18 Ultra, mientras que Oppo y Vivo seguirían adelante, pero sin vender sus modelos fuera de China. La novedad aporta algo más de contexto sobre este escenario, pero, de nuevo, se trata de una filtración y las compañías no han confirmado nada.
Crisis que no deja de apretar. De la manera que sea, y termine llegando o no, es evidente que la situación ha puesto en jaque los planes de los fabricantes de smartphones. Samsung es uno de los responsables de esta situación debido a que ha movido sus fábricas hacia la producción de memoria HBM para los centros de datos, haciendo que quede menos RAM para los móviles. TM Roh, uno de los mandamases de la empresa surcoreana, ya advirtió que estábamos ante uno de los peores escenarios de precios de memoria de la historia y los análisis como los de Counterpoint e IDC apuntaban a unos envíos anuales con cifras que no veíamos desde 2013.
El móvil barato ha sido tocado de muerte, Asus se bajó pronto del carro, Nothing ya dijo que nada de un flagship para 2026 y la propia Samsung ha visto cómo su división de móviles está sufriendo las consecuencias. De hecho, se estima que recorte un 20% la producción de su gama Galaxy A en el próximo trimestre, por lo que da igual si al final termina llegando un Oppo Find X10 Ultra o no: la lectura es que nos esperan años de móviles cuyas especificaciones no mejorarán al ritmo que estábamos acostumbrados... a la vez que los precios se vuelven más inaccesibles.

articles.title: Terafab Wants to Become One of the Largest Memory Makers by 2032
articles.text:
Monday, November 9th 2026
Terafab Wants to Become One of the Largest Memory Makers by 2032
According to Nikkei, a procurement team from Terafab, the chip venture between Tesla and SpaceX, visited Japan and walked local equipment makers through what it plans to buy. The targets it reportedly shared are gigantic: 1 million wafers per month from 2032 onward, with around 700,000 of those going to memory chips and 300,000 to logic. Nikkei's headline puts that at 40 times the output of Japan's Rapidus. The same split first surfaced in a Jiji Press report last month, which said a single Texas plant would handle both memory and logic, with a pilot fab completed as early as July 2027. Intel is reportedly helping with logic using its 2 nm and 1.4 nm-class technology, while a Taiwanese company has been floated as a technology partner for memory. That could be Nanya, though nothing is confirmed. 
For context, Samsung's entire DRAM output was estimated at 650,000 to 700,000 wafers a month late last year, while SK hynix was at about 550,000 earlier this year and hopes to reach roughly 1 million by 2030 or 2031. It isn't clear whether Terafab's memory figure covers DRAM alone or also includes NAND, so the Samsung comparison is a loose one. Musk has also been careful with his own dates. On an October SpaceX call, he put "big error bars" on reaching volume production by Q3 2028, with a first SRAM test chip planned for mid-2027 at Terafab's Austin research lab.The project itself has moved fast on paper. Intel signed on in April, filings showed the full build-out could cost up to $119 billion, and TSMC held talks about joining as well. With SK hynix expecting memory demand to outpace supply through 2030, another large memory maker would sound like good news for PC buyers. However, 2032 is still six years away, and Terafab's chips seem to be meant for Musk's own robots, cars, and data centers first, so consumers probably shouldn't count on it easing DRAM prices anytime soon.
Sources:
				Nikkei, 				Jiji Press, 				via Jukan05 on X

articles.title: Linus Torvalds já vê "paz" entre Linux e ferramentas de IA que caçam bugs • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Linus Torvalds já vê “paz” entre Linux e ferramentas de IA que caçam bugs
Linus Torvalds relatou que, em alguns pontos do Linux, o número de correções começou a superar os relatórios de bugs gerados por IA.
Linus Torvalds afirma que as correções no Linux 7.4 começaram a superar os bugs reportados via IA em alguns pontos do projeto. O mantenedor destaca o avanço nas correções da área do eBPF.
Torvalds considera o uso de inteligência artificial no kernel como o novo normal do projeto. O volume excessivo de relatórios ainda pode gerar sobrecarga na equipe, porém.
Os desenvolvedores do sistema seguem se adaptando ao ritmo das falhas trazidas por ferramentas. O lançamento da nova versão (7.4) é esperado para dezembro de 2026.
Em mais de uma ocasião, Linus Torvalds relatou que os desenvolvedores do Linux estavam ficando sobrecarregados com a quantidade de falhas no kernel reportadas com o auxílio de ferramentas de IA que “caçam bugs”. Mas, no último fim de semana, Torvalds deu a entender que essa relação está ficando mais, digamos, harmoniosa.
É importante deixar claro desde já que Linus Torvalds não é contra o uso de inteligência artificial no desenvolvimento e manutenção do kernel. Ele próprio já declarou que o uso de IA para encontrar bugs é o “novo normal” no Linux.
O incômodo vem da percepção de que o volume de falhas reportadas é elevado e, muitas vezes, envolve problemas com baixa prioridade, que já estão na fila de correção ou até que já foram corrigidos, sendo esse cenário o motivo da sobrecarga dos desenvolvedores.
No fim de semana, Torvalds anunciou a segunda versão release candidate do Linux 7.4 (Linux 7.4-rc2). No mesmo anúncio, Torvalds deu a entender que, nessa versão, as correções estão entrando em equilíbrio com o número de bugs reportados:
E sim, boa parte disso [dos avanços no Linux 7.4] foi motivada por várias correções feitas com o auxílio da IA. Acho que vou parar de repetir isso, pois podemos simplesmente considerar esse fato [correções auxiliadas por IA] como algo já conhecido.
Mas, desta vez, Alexei afirma que, pelo menos na área do BPF, as correções estão chegando mais rapidamente do que os novos relatos de problemas. E isso seria ótimo, se for verdade.
Linus Torvalds, mantenedor do Linux
Na mensagem, Torvalds menciona Alexei Starovoitov, um dos responsáveis pelo eBPF. Por sua vez, o eBPF (Extended Berkeley Packet Filter) consiste em um mecanismo do Linux que permite a execução controlada de recursos de software dentro do próprio kernel. Torvalds escreve “BPF”, mas fazendo referência ao eBPF, que é uma versão mais moderna da tecnologia.
Como o eBPF permite execução de software de modo seguro, sem necessidade de alteração no código-fonte do kernel ou de acionamento de módulos adicionais, por exemplo, encontrar e corrigir vulnerabilidades nessa área é muito importante.
Pois bem, segundo Torvalds, pelo menos no BPF (ou eBPF), as correções estão chegando em ritmo mais acelerado do que os novos relatórios de problemas.
Isso não significa que a “enxurrada” de relatórios de falhas acabou ou diminuiu de modo significativo. O que a mensagem de Linus Torvalds sugere é que os desenvolvedores do kernel já estão conseguindo se adaptar à nova realidade e que isso já é perceptível, ainda que em uma área específica, no Linux 7.4.
Se tudo der certo, essa versão será lançada oficialmente em algum momento de dezembro de 2026.

articles.title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
articles.text:
Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That’s the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets, including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories.
The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the “Yes, and don’t ask again” option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local “.claude/settings.local.json” file on the user’s computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it.
This isn’t really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user’s local machine (assuming that machine doesn’t become compromised itself, of course). And Anthropic notes in its Claude Code documentation that this particular settings file gets added to the developer’s global .gitignore list, which usually prevents it from being shared publicly.
But that .gitignore setting isn’t reflected at the repo level, meaning the sensitive file can be uploaded accidentally if a repo is cloned to another machine or a folder becomes a repo later, for instance. In many cases, Claude Code itself will commit changes to the settings file without the user’s input, Apiiro writes.
Apiiro’s researchers found over 100,000 cases where Claude Code’s local settings file had been uploaded to a public GitHub repository. Of these, only about 1,100 from 63 different organizations contained secrets such as public API tokens, database passwords, or private keys. Even after these files are discovered and removed from a repository, the secrets can persist in forks of the original project if a GitHub user isn’t careful.

articles.title: Spoof program monitors and emails your RAM usage to Sam Altman if under 90% utilization — 'RAM-Altman' logs usage and ‘reports’ you for wasting memory
articles.text:
Spoof program monitors and emails your RAM usage to Sam Altman if under 90% utilization — 'RAM-Altman' logs usage and ‘reports’ you for wasting memory
Free Bash script files your details, rotating through eight subject lines, 10 humorous message boilerplates, and six signoffs.
A new GitHub repository dubbed ram-altman features a script to monitor your PC’s RAM usage and report back to the eponymous OpenAI boss. Sam Altman infamously described people having spare, underutilized DRAM in computers at home as “quite terrible” in a recent podcast. Thus, developer Iain Kay was inspired to write a bash script that emails the OpenAI boss once a day to report on any RAM that is underutilized. Clearly this is not a serious tool, or rather “The memory accounting is. The correspondence isn't,” says Kay.
ram-altman leans on the MemAvailable query, which returns the kernel's own estimate of how much memory programs can claim without swapping, explains the developer of this script. When installed, it checks every five minutes and emails Altman once a day if you are found to be wasting this precious resource.
The emails take the .CSV file logs of your RAM use throughout the day as the data source to compose a summary email. These script-generated messages rotate through eight subject lines, 10 humorous message boilerplates, and six signoffs. Sample emails can be seen on the ram-altman.lol website. Altman’s email address isn’t supplied as part of the script.
If your machine is using 90% or more of its RAM, then you won’t be reported to the OpenAI boss for wasting memory. Also, if you don’t want to disturb Altman, you can run the tests without emailing anyone with the terminal command: bash ram-altman.sh --dry-run
The developer isn’t too scathing of the OpenAI boss. Kay quotes Altman’s explanations that his remarks were taken out of context. Moreover, the dev doffs his cap to the artificial intelligence leader’s humorous display name change to ‘Ram Altman’ on X last week. That’s where the name for this script came from.
ram-altman is a free bash script available on GitHub. It runs natively on Linux. On Windows, you can use WSL to run it, but someone has ported it for PowerShell too. It won’t run on Mac, but Altman and his minions would find it inconvenient, at best, to remove your soldered-down Apple RAM.
