articles.title: Nigeria adopts hybrid cloud storage for postcode database
articles.text:
When Nigeria’s National Digital Addressing System (NDAPS) launched on October 1, it promised to replace informal, landmark-based navigation with precise 11-character alphanumeric codes. The system is designed to improve e-commerce deliveries, enable address verification for banking and identity services, and assign unique digital postcodes to addressable buildings nationwide.
Led by the Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST) under the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, the initiative is intended to provide a reliable digital addressing infrastructure for the country.
TechCabal reported that technical checks of postcode.gov.ng’s public domain name system (DNS) records pointed to Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure in the United States. The finding raised questions about whether a critical public digital asset was hosted abroad, just as Nigeria strengthens its push for data sovereignty.
“The system has distinct layers,” NIPOST spokesperson Ibrahim Musa told TechCabal in an email response. “Nigeria’s digital postcode infrastructure runs on both AWS and Galaxy Backbone—Nigeria’s official digital infrastructure and shared services provider—but they serve distinct functions.”
What AWS’s cloud services mean
AWS has infrastructure across 247 countries. It opened its first Nigerian office in Lagos in 2022 and has invested in an AWS Local Zone in Lagos to support customers and partners adopting its services locally.
The company told TechCabal that it does not disclose customer relationships without their permission.
“AWS is sovereign-by-design,” AWS Communications Manager for Sub-Saharan Africa, Sonwabise Mzinyathi, said in an email response. “We have infrastructure globally so organisations can run AWS services in their own facilities or in a location they specify, keeping data exactly where they need.”
AWS also points to its Nitro System, which uses specialised hardware and firmware to protect customer workloads running on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2). It is designed to prevent outside access to those workloads, including by AWS employees.
The global cloud services provider stated that customers can also encrypt their data and manage their own encryption keys. “Customers who need to store and use encryption keys outside the AWS Cloud can use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) external key store,” said Mzinyathi, “retaining exclusive control over cryptographic material.”
AWS argued that its infrastructure is designed to remain available during supply chain disruptions, network interruptions and natural disasters. “We’ve instilled cloud resilience into our infrastructure, service design and deployment, operational model, and mechanisms to build more resilient cloud architectures,” the company said.
These capabilities, the company said, support its Digital Sovereignty Pledge, which promises customers greater control over where their data resides, how it is accessed, and how workloads are managed. However, these controls do not automatically determine where customer data lives. That decision ultimately depends on how the customer builds and manages its system.
The website is not the database
NIPOST emphasised that the public-facing postcode.gov.ng uses AWS’s global content delivery and web-protection services. These help pages load faster and protect the website against distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, which overwhelm online platforms with traffic until they become unavailable.
“The public website, postcode.gov.ng, uses AWS’s global content delivery and web-protection services, a standard approach used by many government and financial platforms to keep public portals fast and protected,” NIPOST told TechCabal.
The agency said Galaxy Backbone hosts and manages the core database. It contains the records that make the addressing system work, including building locations, geographic coordinates, and administrative boundaries.
Its technical team and private partners support development and maintenance under its direction.
“The content-delivery provider serving the public website does not host or have administrative access to the core database,” NIPOST said.
AWS helps deliver and protect the public website but, according to NIPOST, does not hold or manage the master postcode records. The database and its backups remain within Nigeria.
What Nigeria’s cloud policy says
NIPOST’s arrangement is based on the National Digital Cloud Policy, released by Communications Minister Bosun Tijani in August 2026, and NITDA’s supporting National Cloud Computing and Cloud Technical Guidelines.
The policy distinguishes between public information and sensitive government data, with different hosting requirements for each.
NIPOST considers public postcode lookups to fall under the policy’s “Open” data category, which has no data residency restrictions. This allows the public-facing website to use global infrastructure such as AWS.
The core database is treated differently. NIPOST said it applies controls consistent with the policy’s “Highly Sensitive” (Level 3) requirements, including keeping records within Nigeria and maintaining domestic disaster-recovery capabilities.
Using Galaxy Backbone also reflects the policy’s direction for federal agencies to meet their cloud hosting needs through the government’s shared services model.
However, NIPOST said it will still engage the Sovereign Government Cloud Governance Committee and NITDA on the system’s formal classification as the policy’s sovereignty framework is implemented.
Formal classification is still part of the process, even though NIPOST says its current hosting arrangements follow the relevant Level 3 controls.
In July, TechCabal examined whether Nigeria’s domestic data centre industry could support the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) directive requiring banks, fintechs and payment companies to move their transactional data from foreign cloud servers to infrastructure within the country by January 1, 2027. The directive is expected to trigger one of Nigeria’s largest cloud migrations.
NIPOST’s arrangement reflects a wider push to keep sensitive information within Nigeria.
The agency added that its hosting decisions balance security, resilience, cost, scalability and data sovereignty, with core infrastructure provided by government-owned Nigerian provider, Galaxy Backbone. It said the hosting arrangements would be reviewed as the use of NDAPS expands. It, however, didn’t disclose the contract details of the current hybrid arrangement, arguing that they are subject to public procurement rules.
Who controls the postcode database?
With the core database hosted locally, the next question is who can access or control it.
NIPOST said it retains ownership of NDAPS data and controls administrative privileges alongside Galaxy Backbone. The two organisations also manage the encryption keys protecting the system.
Private contractors and technical partners, including Milsat Technologies, do not have unrestricted access. NIPOST said service providers access the system only when necessary to perform their duties, under contractual confidentiality and data-protection obligations, role-based access controls and audit logging.
Banks, logistics companies and government agencies will connect to NDAPS through application programming interfaces (APIs), allowing different software platforms to exchange information. These integrations could let a bank verify an address or a delivery company locate a customer’s building without relying on informal landmarks.
NIPOST said access will be governed by agreements and limited to the location information required for service delivery.
“Personal data is not shared through these interfaces,” it said.
Although the platform provides location information rather than personal identity records, how organisations combine that information with their existing customer databases will matter for privacy.
Can local infrastructure handle the demand?
Keeping the database in Nigeria addresses where the information lives, but not necessarily how reliably it can be accessed.
Galaxy Backbone will support the infrastructure behind a system expected to serve banks, logistics companies and government agencies through automated queries. As adoption grows, demand will increase.
Nigeria’s domestic hosting environment faces practical challenges, including unreliable power supply, fibre cuts and network disruptions. Local providers must demonstrate that they can maintain services and recover quickly when infrastructure fails.
NIPOST said NDAPS has primary databases, replicas, backups and disaster-recovery arrangements within Nigeria. It added that the system undergoes regular testing and continuous monitoring to restore services following cyber incidents, infrastructure failures or loss of access to a hosting environment.
But having backup arrangements is different from showing they can withstand a major disruption. The real test will be how quickly the system can recover when millions of users and businesses depend on it.
The outstanding data protection question
Another compliance question concerns the system’s data protection assessment.
NIPOST confirmed that its Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) is still in progress and that it is engaging the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) on the system’s data-processing arrangements.
A DPIA helps organisations identify privacy risks associated with systems that process personal information. NDAPS is designed to map buildings across Nigeria, creating a national location database that could become increasingly useful to banks, businesses and government agencies.
Although NIPOST said it doesn’t share personal data through its APIs, location information can become more revealing when combined with other datasets, particularly those held by financial institutions and government agencies.
While hosting the database on domestic servers satisfies data residency rules, location is only half the equation. The true test for NDAPS will be whether local infrastructure can deliver the uptime, automated query speeds, and disaster recovery that banks and logistics firms would need to make the system reliable.

articles.title: Coprocesado de contrabando de Super Micro se declara culpable de enviar chips de inteligencia artificial a China — el corredor admite haber violado las normas de control de exportaciones mientras el cofundador de la empresa niega los cargos
articles.text:
Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun (un intermediario vinculado a Super Micro) ha reconocido su participación en una trama para enviar servidores con chips de Nvidia a China ignorando las restricciones que Estados Unidos impone a la exportación de esta tecnología. Eso sí, no hablamos precisamente de cuatro ordenadores, ya que las autoridades estadounidenses calculan que la operación llegó a mover equipos valorados en unos 2.500 millones de dólares.
Según informa Bloomberg, Sun se ha declarado culpable como parte de un acuerdo con la Fiscalía, pero aún no han trascendido detalles de una posible colaboración con las autoridades. El intermediario estaba acusado junto a otras figuras como Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw (cofundador de Super Micro) y Ruei-Tsang "Steven" Chang (antiguo responsable de ventas en Taiwán). De hecho, como Liaw niega los cargos, el caso sigue abierto para los otros implicados.
Usaban servidores falsos y hasta secadores de pelo para ocultar los envíos
Lo más llamativo de la operación es cómo, presuntamente, funcionaba. Según la investigación del Departamento de Justicia estadounidense, los acusados enviaban los servidores a una empresa del sudeste asiático que figuraba como compradora, aunque su destino real era China. Para ocultarlo, preparaban documentación falsa y trasladaban los equipos en cajas sin identificar.
Pero el engaño no acababa ahí. Los investigadores sostienen que llegaron a preparar miles de servidores falsos para superar las inspecciones, utilizando incluso secadores de pelo para despegar etiquetas y números de serie y colocarlos en las réplicas. De esta forma, los inspectores podían encontrarse con equipos aparentemente auténticos cuando los originales ya habían salido hacia China. Las cámaras de vigilancia llegaron a grabar parte de los preparativos.
Sun se ha declarado culpable de cuatro cargos relacionados con el incumplimiento de los controles de exportación, el contrabando, el fraude al Gobierno estadounidense y la obstrucción a la justicia. Su sentencia está prevista para el 8 de septiembre de 2027, mientras que Liaw mantiene su declaración de inocencia.
Por ahora, Super Micro no figura como acusada en el procedimiento. La compañía, que fabrica los servidores utilizados en esta trama, ha asegurado que está colaborando con las autoridades para impedir que sus equipos terminen en mercados restringidos.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO's affair becomes a national security problem
articles.text:
Nvidia’s chief executive Jensen Huang has admitted having an affair two days after the FT reported his alleged romantic relationship with a woman the US intelligence community believes was working as a spy for China.
Huang revealed the affair in an internal message to employees on Sunday that was obtained by the FT.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang said in the message. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
In a separate statement, Nvidia said its board would open an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
Huang said he would fully cooperate. “My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust,” he said. “I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence.”
The FT reported on Friday that the US believed Huang had a romantic relationship with a Chinese woman who was recruited to spy for China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency.
American officials this year wrote a memo, based on information from US intelligence, which said the Nvidia boss had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of the chipmaker, according to people familiar with the document.
The affair is a damaging blow to the Nvidia chief, who in recent years has become the face of the AI boom, one of the technology’s loudest champions, and transformed the Silicon Valley group into the first $5 trillion company.

articles.title: Many PCs from '80s and '90s had keyhole locks, right next to the Turbo and Reset buttons. What was it for?
articles.text:
And now, for some context
An actual key: The 1980s answer to pressing "Win+L"
If you ever cracked open a beige 386 or 486 tower, you might remember a keyhole on the front panel, usually parked near the Turbo and Reset buttons. IBM called it the keylock. With the key turned to "locked," the PC stopped listening to the keyboard. It was a physical password.
The reason it existed is explained by the software of the time. Early IBM-compatible PCs ran MS-DOS, a single-user system with no accounts and no passwords. Anyone who sat down at your desk could browse your files (or delete them) with a keypress.
IBM had already used keylocks on its mainframes and servers, and in 1984 it brought the idea to the IBM PC AT (model 5170), an expensive 286-based machine that cost thousands of dollars (over $12,500 in today's money). The AT shipped with a tubular pin-tumbler lock, similar to the "Ace" locks found on vending machines, pinball tables, and alarm panels. PC Magazine described it as a way for executives to sleep at night.
On that IBM, the lock did several things: it blocked the keyboard at the controller level, so software couldn't work around it. If the machine was powered on while locked, the BIOS self-test halted, and a metal piece inside the case moved into place to stop the cover from being removed. IBM also sold a separate "Keylock Option" for the original PC and XT that went further and blocked the machine from powering on at all.
Compatibility was the selling point of PC clones, so clone makers copied the feature, but not faithfully. Most only disabled the keyboard, and the case-locking part was reserved for higher-end systems. Implementations varied by maker, with some locks cutting off the power supply or hard drive instead. In some cases, budget builders skipped the wiring altogether, so the lock was purely decorative.
The keylock is a passing memory these days. It faded in the early-to-mid '90s, along with the Turbo button, as passwords arrived in software. Windows NT, NetWare, and Linux had real user accounts, Windows 95 had profiles (though not real security), and BIOS passwords became a common feature.
The physical lock idea lives on in cable locks like Kensington's, in the lockable front panels of servers, and in the keyboard shortcut you now use to lock your screen.

articles.title: Cloudflare Develops Public Certificate Authority for Post-Quantum Web Security
articles.text:
Cloudflare has tested Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs) as an alternative to traditional certificate chains, reporting 9% faster median performance in a Chrome experiment. The approach batches certificate data into an append-only Merkle tree, letting clients verify certificates with compact inclusion proofs instead of transmitting a full certificate chain. Cloudflare attributed most of the measured improvement to eliminating intermediate certificates; the experiment used classical signatures rather than post-quantum signatures.
Building on the approach covered in InfoQ’s earlier report, Cloudflare describes how landmark-based verification and independent transparency log cosigners support certificate issuance and verification at scale.
The experiment served billions of MTCs to 50% of Chrome Beta 146 for selected domains on Cloudflare’s free plan. Cloudflare wound down the experiment in August 2026 and is developing a public certificate authority (CA) that supports MTC issuance, targeting inclusion in Chrome’s quantum-resistant Root Store in early 2027, subject to evaluation.
Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince, in a press release, said:
Upgrading the web's security before quantum computers can break it is one of the biggest coordination challenges in the history of the Internet.
Post-quantum cryptography creates scaling challenges for the Web Public Key Infrastructure (Web PKI). According to Cloudflare, post-quantum signatures can be approximately 40 times larger than classical signatures, increasing bandwidth and storage requirements.
MTCs combine certificate issuance with transparency logging. Instead of signing certificates individually, a certificate authority (CA) records certificate data in an append-only Merkle tree and signs a checkpoint. Clients verify certificate inclusion using cryptographic proofs.
Cloudflare uses the Automated Certificate Management Environment (ACME) protocol to validate domain ownership. An independent mirroring cosigner verifies and stores updated tree states, helping detect inconsistent log views and preserve issuance records if the original log becomes unavailable.
MTC issuance and independent log mirroring (Source: Cloudflare Blog Post)
Landmark relative certificates further reduce TLS handshake data. Cloudflare distributes authenticated landmarks to clients, which verify certificate inclusion using cryptographic proofs. Servers must still prove possession of their private keys. In the common case, the handshake transmits one public key, one signature, and an inclusion proof smaller than 1 KB.
Landmark relative certificate verification using pre-distributed tree landmarks. (Source: Cloudflare Blog Post)
Clients may be newly installed, offline, or missing the relevant landmark update. Servers must therefore retain a standalone MTC certificate as a fallback. Cloudflare identifies independent monitoring at production volume, a diverse ecosystem of CAs and cosigners, and browser support as remaining requirements for broader deployment.
Alicja Tendaj, Tier 2 Technical Support Specialist at SSL.com, raised questions about revocation and incident handling in response to Cloudflare’s announcement on LinkedIn:
With short validity and trust anchored in a tree head, a lot of the old OCSP and CRL playbook becomes a question of how quickly you can stop including a certificate
Cloudflare’s planned public CA will require evaluation before its MTC issuance can be trusted through Chrome’s quantum-resistant Root Store. The company says production deployment will help determine whether the approach can maintain transparency, interoperability, and availability at Internet scale.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pulled out of the ElevenLabs Summit scheduled for this Wednesday in New York, ElevenLabs, the voice AI company, confirmed Monday. He has also dropped out of other speaking engagements, including the Anthropic CEO Forum. Nvidia is an investor in ElevenLabs.

articles.title: Huawei develops 'entirely Chinese' homegrown desktop PC system — features 10-core, 20-thread Kirin X90 consumer CPU and Huawei's own HarmonyOS operating system, but Western supply chain lingers
articles.text:
Huawei develops 'entirely Chinese' homegrown desktop PC system — features 10-core, 20-thread Kirin X90 consumer CPU and Huawei's own HarmonyOS operating system, but Western supply chain lingers
Goodbye, Wintel? Software for Windows too?
Huawei has introduced its first desktop PCs powered by its own 10-core processor as well as proprietary HarmonyOS operating system, reports the Southern China Morning Post. The company claims that the CPU and the OS are built entirely of using 'components manufactured' in China, which matters when it comes national security and domestic supply chains inside the sanctioned country. But whether these machines are truly 'entirely domestic' is an open question.
The Huawei Qinyun HM650 and HM650g desktop PCs come with 16 GB of LPDDR5 memory (probably made by China's CXMT) and either a 256GB or 512GB SSD (probably made by Chinese flash maker YMTC) are powered by the company's Kirin X90 system-on-chip, which originally debuted in Huawei's consumer systems in 2025. The key ingedient of the system it its processor, which features 10 Huawei-designed Armv8-based Taishan CPU cores in a 4+4+2 configuration, with all cores supporting simultaneous multithreading (SMT) to execute up to 20 threads simultameusly. The chip also integrates Huawei's Maleoon graphics processing unit (Arm Mali-based) and a dedicated neural processing unit for AI workloads.
Although Huawei doesn't officially disclose the Kirin X90's manufacturing process, a teardown analysis by TechInsights confirmed that the CPU is manufactured by SMIC using its 7nm-class N+2 process technology. This makes the X90 an example of Huawei's ability to develop PC-class processors using domestically available semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, albeit on a process technology that trails leading-edge nodes from Intel, TSMC, and Samsung.
The most interesting aspect of the Qinyun HM650 series is certainly Huawei's claim that all of its new system's components, including the processor, memory, storage, power supply, and wireless connectivity are manufactured domestically. Such certification itself does not necessarily mean that the entire semiconductor supply chain behind the machine is Chinese. While the CPU, memory, and storage chips are fabricated domestically, they are still made using foreign manufacturing equipment (from the Netherlands, U.S., and Japan), materials (from Japan), intellectual property (from the UK), and electronic design automation (EDA software from the U.S. and partly from China) tools.
Meanwhile, the claim about the operating system developed in China sounds ambitious. The machines run Huawei's HarmonyOS Enterprise Edition, which certainly reduces their dependence on foreign technology suppliers. Unlike conventional PCs that rely on Microsoft's Windows operating system, Huawei's desktops use a software platform developed and maintained by a Chinese company. Furthermore, unlike earlier HarmonyOS versions that incorporated Linux components, the HarmonyOS Enterprise Edition uses Huawei's own kernel and software architecture. This indeed gives Huawei greater control over operating system development, security updates, and integration with its hardware, although compatibility with existing Windows applications could remain a limitation for enterprise customers that rely on software by multinational corporations for Windows.
Keeping all these things in mind, can we say that Huawei's Qinyun HM650 series relies entirely on components developed and made in China? Probably yes. Yet, with major caveats, including a semiconductor supply chain that relies on tools and software designed and produced elsewhere. Furthermore, incompatibility of the OS with software designed for Windows could be a limitation for some customers.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Samsung prepara una revolución en sus Galaxy más baratos: la pantalla se verá mejor que nunca
articles.text:
Samsung podría llevar las pantallas OLED a sus Galaxy más baratos. Según ZDNet Korea, varios fabricantes de paneles están considerando desarrollar pantallas OLED con resolución HD para dispositivos de bajo coste. De confirmarse el rumor, este movimiento podría significar el principio del fin para el LCD, una tecnología que ha acompañado a estos dispositivos durante años.
Si bien la industria de los móviles es en donde vemos una adopción mayor del OLED, la realidad es que estas pantallas están reservadas para ciertos terminales. En modelos de gama media o alta es común encontrarlos, pero en la gama de entrada no se integran bien, a veces por el coste o por la resolución. Un ejemplo es el Galaxy A18, uno de los móviles más asequibles con OLED y pantalla FullHD+, algo que no se ve en el Galaxy A07 con panel LCD y resolución HD+.
El nuevo planteamiento consistiría en desarrollar paneles OLED más sencillos que sean compatibles con resoluciones HD (720p), lo cual ayudaría a reducir costes. Según el reporte, fabricantes como Oppo y Vivo ya están en conversaciones con algunos proveedores para sustituir las pantallas LCD por OLED con características similares. Aunque esto suena atractivo, el principal desafío es el precio, puesto que desarrollar un panel OLED que pueda competir con el coste de los LCD actuales todavía no es posible.
El OLED es común en casi todos los móviles, excepto en la gama de entrada
Si los fabricantes y los proveedores logran un acuerdo, el impacto de esta implementación podría ser más grande de lo que pensábamos. Según los analistas, unos 100 millones de móviles con pantalla LCD podrían adoptar el OLED en el futuro. Los usuarios que tienen un presupuesto ajustado no tendrían que sufrir con una pantalla de baja calidad, con negros que parecen grises y con un consumo mayor de la batería.
Samsung, Oppo, Vivo y otras empresas consideran los nuevos paneles OLED HD como una forma de activar las líneas de producción, reduciendo la presión de costes fijos. La firma de análisis Omidia estima que los envíos mundiales caerán un 12% este año, lo que ha obligado a toda la cadena de suministro a buscar nuevas oportunidades de negocio. Contar con una móvil con pantalla OLED podría ayudar a revertir la caída y generar más ingresos por la venta de dispositivos de entrada.
Por el momento no existe una confirmación oficial sobre la fecha en la que podríamos ver estos móviles. Compañías como Apple dieron el salto al OLED en sus iPhones más baratos, pero en Android las cosas son distintas. Todavía existen líneas muy básicas en las que se venden teléfonos con pantalla LCD, como el Redmi A5 o el Moto G 2026, incluyendo sus variantes Play y Power.

articles.title: Another huge data breach hits a major Japanese company — Iris Ohyama attack exposes info of 7.7 million customers
articles.text:
Another huge data breach hits a major Japanese company — Iris Ohyama attack exposes info of 7.7 million customers
Iris Ohyama forced to temporarily shut an ecommerce site down
- Iris Ohyama discloses breach affecting 7.7 million individuals after attackers compromised its ecommerce platform
- Exposed data included personal details and some encrypted passwords, prompting password reset recommendations
- Company continues investigating the attack, with no ransom demand, attribution, or confirmed misuse reported
Major Japanese consumer goods manufacturer Iris Ohyama has confirmed suffering a cyberattack which saw it lose data on 7.7 million people.
The company first disclosed the breach on October 29, 2026 when it confirmed “unauthorized access on the e-commerce site” Iris Plaza. At the time, the company said its investigation was ongoing, and that it would temporarily suspend the site to ensure customer safety. While it was looking into possible data leaks, it stressed that credit card information was not taken.
A week later, Iris Ohyama came forward with a more detailed report, in which it said that on October 28, if found “suspicious files” on an external cloud service it used. The subsequently launched investigation confirmed that the attackers stole sensitive data on 7.7 million people, which included member data on approximately 5.8 million people, and non-member data on 1.9 million.
Member data included names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, genders, dates of birth, and encrypted passwords (for some users). The non-member data was limited to names, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses.
Hashed passwords and stolen credentials
The fact that the passwords were encrypted is good news, since it means the accounts cannot be accessed that easily. However, the company did not say which encryption or hashing method it used, so it is possible that the attackers could break some of them offline. It is thus no wonder the company warned users to update their login credentials, especially for those who use the same password for other services.
Those that do use the same passwords across various platforms are also at risk of having all of them compromised, since threat actors are known for trying out the stolen combinations across a multitude of services.
We don’t know who targeted Iris Ohyama, and to what end. No threat actors have yet claimed responsibility for this attack, the data has not yet leaked to the dark web, and we’ve found no evidence it was used in phishing or social engineering attacks.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
In a statement given to BleepingComputer, the company said it received no direct communication from the threat actors, no ransom demands, and did not know who they were.
We also don’t know which third-party cloud service Iris Ohyama used, which malware was used, or how it was planted there. In the meantime, the company notified the country’s data protection watchdog agency, as well as local law enforcement authorities.
Targeting Japanese organizations
Over the last few months, Japanese organizations have experienced a barrage of cyberattacks, targeting firms of different sizes and in different industries. Just last month, we reported on an attack on GMO, a data breach incident at Japanese Burger King, and a malware attack on Daiichi Kosho. The GMO attack was particularly worrisome, since the company urged its customers to “unplug any cords connected to your PC”.
Burger King Japan also recently lost sensitive data on 11.18 million customers, most of which were using the company’s official smartphone app, while a malware attack on Daiichi Kosho’s supply chain resulted in the compromise of 8.7 million of both customers and employees.
All of these are large organizations and major enterprises, and Iris Ohyama is no exception. The company is a large consumer goods manufacturer, known for household appliances and everyday products, and has been around for decades offering air conditioners, vacuum cleaners, kitchenware, lighting, pet food and accessories, as well as different food products like rice and water.
For the financial year 2025, the company reported an annual revenue of $1.53 billion, with a headcount of more than 6,300. It also has a substantial international presence, with manufacturing and distribution operations in the US, Europe, China, and South Korea.

articles.title: Windows 11: Microsoft arbeitet an neuer Recall-Funktion – was sich ändert
articles.text:
Windows 11: Microsoft arbeitet an neuer Recall-Funktion – was sich ändert
Fast kein anderes Feature von Windows 11 wurde so heiß und ausdauernd diskutiert wie die Recall-Funktion. Dabei handelt es sich um ein KI-Feature, das mittlerweile nur noch auf kompatiblen Copilot-Plus-Geräten nach ausdrücklicher Zustimmung aktiviert werden kann. Die KI nimmt in regelmäßigen Abständen Screenshots des Bildschirminhalts auf, um damit später arbeiten zu können. Suchst du etwa nach einer Datei, die du vor drei Wochen bearbeitet hast, kannst du Copilot danach fragen und die KI sucht dir den Speicherort anhand der Screenshots heraus.
Windows 11: Microsoft arbeitet an neuer Recall-Funktion
Diese Funktion hat Datenschützer:innen sogar dazu bewogen, Windows-11-User:innen zu einem Systemwechsel zu raten. Denn dadurch könnten ungewollt sensible Informationen in den Daten der KI landen, die anschließend zum Training genutzt werden können. Zudem fürchten Sicherheitsexpert:innen, dass eine durchgehende Screenshot-Funktion die KI für versteckte Prompt-Injektionen anfällig macht.
Wie Windows Latest berichtet, hat Microsoft den Traum einer beliebten Recall-Funktion unter Windows 11 aber noch nicht gänzlich aufgegeben. Demnach arbeitet das Unternehmen aktuell daran, das Feature in einer neuen Fassung aufzulegen. Die zugehörige KI-App trägt den Codenamen „Project Pantheon“ und baut sogenannte „Context Vaults“, also Kontexttresore, für Windows‑11‑Nutzer:innen auf.
Diese Kontexttresore bestehen im Grunde auch aus Screenshots des Bildschirms. Im Gegensatz zur aktuellen Recall-Funktion nimmt Windows 11 aber nur ein Bild auf, wenn die User:innen die KI explizit darum bitten. Dazu können Nutzer:innen auch Webseiten, Dateien, Text sowie Audio- und Videodateien in den Tresoren speichern, um sie als Kontext für KI-Anfragen nutzbar zu machen.
Integration mit anderen KI-Tools
Schon jetzt lassen sich in einer ersten Testversion der App solche „Erinnerungen“ über Browser-Erweiterungen, den Dateiexplorer von Windows 11 und das Teilen-Menü hinzufügen. Nutzer:innen müssen also nicht jedes Mal die „Project Pantheon“-App öffnen, um eine Erinnerung zu erstellen. Das Erstellen soll sich natürlich in die Nutzung von Windows 11 eingliedern.
Ebenfalls spannend ist, dass „Project Pantheon“ das Model Context Protocol nutzen kann, um die Erinnerungen für externe KI-Tools freizugeben. So könnten abseits von Copilot auch Claude und Cursor auf die gespeicherten Daten zurückgreifen, wenn die User:innen es wünschen. Um die Daten zu schützen, soll Microsoft zudem an einigen Sicherheitsfunktionen arbeiten. Dazu zählen etwa Verschlüsselungen, wenn die KI nicht auf die Daten zugreift, einzeln einstellbare Zugriffsrechte für Apps und Windows-Hello-Schutz. Noch ist aber offen, ob die neue Recall-Variante eines Tages erscheint und welche Windows-11-User:innen darauf zugreifen dürfen.

Put simply, if you pair this processor with a recent GPU, you won't see many bottlenecks. Pair it with a top-class option like the RTX 5080 or RTX 5090, and you'll be hitting high frame rates in any game you can throw at it. The 9800X3D and 9850X3D are formidable options for gaming, the 1-2 winners that sit above all others. The record-low $399 sale price for the 9800X3D is simply exceptional, while $419 for the 9850X3D is an $80 drop compared to its launch price. articles.title: YouTube streaming data returns to Billboard charts, ending major disagreement | TechCrunch
articles.text:
YouTube is officially returning to the Billboard charts, ending a disagreement over how music streams should count toward chart rankings.
Announced Monday, YouTube is set to resume sharing its streaming data with Billboard in 2027. The decision follows recent changes to Billboard’s chart formula, which now gives more weight to ad-supported streams.
The disagreement began in December 2025, when YouTube said it would stop sharing its streaming data with Billboard. The company argued that the chart formula favored paid subscriptions while not giving enough credit to fans who listen for free with ads.
At the time, Lyor Cohen, YouTube’s global head of music, criticized the system in a blog post, saying it didn’t reflect how people listen to music today.
“Billboard uses an outdated formula that weights subscription-supported streams higher than ad-supported. This doesn’t reflect how fans engage with music today and ignores the massive engagement from fans who don’t have a subscription. Streaming is the primary way people experience music, making up 84% of U.S. recorded music revenue,” Cohen wrote.
Under Billboard’s previous formula, 1,000 paid streams counted the same as 2,500 ad-supported streams. YouTube felt this gave too much importance to paid listening, especially when millions of fans discover and support artists through free streaming.
Billboard has now updated its formula, reducing the gap between the two types of streams. Under the new system, 1,000 paid streams will equal 1,500 ad-supported streams when calculating album consumption units, compared with 2,500 under the previous formula. Paid streams will still count for more, but free streams will now have a bigger impact on chart positions.
YouTube’s return could make a difference for many artists, especially independent musicians and those with large international fan bases. Music videos, live performances, lyric videos, and other content on the platform help artists reach new audiences. With YouTube’s data back in the mix, more of that activity will now count toward their Billboard performance.
For Billboard, getting YouTube’s data back also means having a more complete picture of how people listen to and discover music. With so many fans using the platform, leaving its streams out meant missing a major part of music consumption.

articles.title: ¿Quieres invertir en criptomonedas? Conoce su valor y cómo ha fluctuado en las últimas horas
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 74.460,54 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -0,166% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de 0,066% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 2.122,39 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de 0,02%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 682,62 dólares, con un cambio de -1,82%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 50.795 dólares, tras una variación de -2.5168023.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,07 dólares tras presentar un cambio de -3,18% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Criptomonedas en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: WhatsApp, Signal, Messenger... : la France renonce à forcer l’accès aux conversations chiffrées
articles.text:
En 2025, le gouvernement français a introduit une proposition de loi contre le narcotrafic. Celle-ci prévoyait notamment d’obliger les plateformes de messagerie, comme WhatsApp, Signal ou encore Messenger, à transmettre aux autorités les conversations, pourtant chiffrées, de certaines personnes surveillées. À la suite de nombreuses contestations, la mesure n’a pas été conservée dans la loi promulguée contre le narcotrafic. Le débat a ensuite été relancé avec l’introduction de l’article 16 bis dans le projet de loi sur la résilience des infrastructures critiques et le renforcement de la cybersécurité. Pour rappel, l’article 16 bis vise à interdire d’imposer aux plateformes de messagerie des portes dérobées permettant aux autorités d’accéder à certaines conversations pourtant chiffrées de bout en bout.
Accès à des conversations chiffrées : le gouvernement veut un compromis
Le conflit autour de l’article 16 bis est simple. D’un côté, les services de renseignement veulent son abolition pour pouvoir accéder à certaines discussions chiffrées, dans le cadre d’affaires sensibles ou criminelles. De l’autre côté, les plateformes de messagerie, mais aussi une bonne partie de leurs utilisateurs, veulent maintenir la promesse de discussions totalement confidentielles, inaccessibles à l’État. Toute la nuance de cette affaire réside dans la capacité des autorités à accéder aux conversations chiffrées. Où commence et où s’arrête la surveillance des individus ?
Justement, la Commission nationale de contrôle des techniques de renseignement (CNCTR) regrette que le recours au recueil de données informatiques soit devenu quasiment « automatique », alors que cette technique est censée être utilisée en dernier recours. La Commission estime également que les enquêteurs ont tendance à récolter un grand nombre d’informations, avant de ne conserver que celles qui les intéressent. À noter également que cette demande de supprimer les portes dérobées est directement liée aux cyberattaques qui ont ciblé la France ces derniers mois, les portes dérobées étant de potentielles failles à exploiter pour les pirates.
Quoi qu’il en soit, Florent Boudié, ancien député Renaissance et chargé d’une mission gouvernementale sur le chiffrement des messageries, a demandé au gouvernement de renoncer à la possibilité d’imposer des portes dérobées aux plateformes concernées, mais aussi de supprimer l’article 16 bis qu’il estime trop contraignant pour les services de renseignement. Le gouvernement a suivi ces deux recommandations : un compromis semble donc se dessiner.
Le projet de loi « résilience » doit encore être examiné à l’Assemblée nationale
Anne Le Hénanff, secrétaire d’État au numérique, a dénoncé l’« impact délétère pour les services [de renseignement] » de l’article 16 bis et annoncé que l’exécutif « soutiendra » sa suppression. Mais, en contrepartie, le gouvernement français a annoncé qu’il « s’engagera à ne pas réintroduire ni soutenir une réintroduction » des portes dérobées dans les plateformes de messagerie « jusqu’à la fin de la session parlementaire ».
De son côté, Florent Boudié, conseiller d’État et ancien député Renaissance, invite l’État à « identifier une solution technique permettant un accès ciblé aux contenus protégés sans compromettre l’intégrité du chiffrement ». Il reste maintenant à voir quelle pourrait être cette solution technique. Le projet de loi « résilience » sera examiné à l’Assemblée nationale à partir de ce 9 novembre 2026.

articles.title: L'univers cinématographique DC Comics de James Gunn est déjà mort
articles.text:
L’ère James Gunn au sein de DC Studios est déjà terminée. Débauché de l’écurie Marvel avec l’ambition de relancer l’univers cinématographique des super-héros DC Comics, il est écarté de la direction du studio, a révélé Variety ce lundi 9 novembre. Peter Safran, qui codirigeait DC Studios avec lui, subit le même sort. Jeremy Latcham les remplace à partir du 1er décembre.
Le départ surprend à Hollywood. En octobre, à la finalisation du rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery par Paramount (111 milliards de dollars), David Ellison avait gardé le duo dans l’équipe de direction du nouveau groupe, rebaptisé Skydance. Le flop de Supergirl a toutefois pu peser. Si son film Superman a plutôt bien fonctionné, Supergirl est un flop retentissant au box-office mondial, avec seulement 126 millions de dollars empochés (contre 618 millions pour Superman), pour un budget de 170 millions de dollars. Le bilan du duo est contrasté alors qu’il avait une mission bien plus ambitieuse : bâtir un vrai rival à l’univers Marvel de Disney.
James Gunn revient à un rôle créatif
James Gunn et Peter Safran vont revenir à des rôles 100 % créatifs. Ce qui ravit James Gunn, comme il l’a écrit sur sa page Instagram : « Ce que seules les personnes les plus proches de moi ont su au cours des quatre dernières années, c’est que mon passage chez DC Studios a été particulièrement éprouvant, c’est le moins qu’on puisse dire. Je n’aime pas le côté parfois corporate de ce travail (merci à Peter d’en avoir porté le plus gros fardeau). J’ai toujours été un très grand travailleur, mais en tant que réalisateur, je pouvais au moins m’accorder de courtes pauses pour décompresser, alors que ces quatre dernières années, j’ai volé ce temps précieux à la fois à moi-même et à mes proches. »
James Gunn indique par ailleurs qu’il n’en a pas terminé avec DC Comics. Man of Tomorrow, la suite de Superman qu’il a écrite et réalisée, sortira l’été prochain. Il est aussi sur un autre projet DC. « Et bien sûr, les personnages que nous avons créés continueront d’exister », se réjouit-il.
Le départ de James Gunn et Peter Safran prend effet le 1er décembre. Le duo reste attaché comme producteur à plusieurs projets en cours, dont Man of Tomorrow, la série The People v. Gorilla Grodd et The Batman : Partie II de Matt Reeves, attendu en 2028.
Skydance, le groupe né du rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery par Paramount, a donc choisi Jeremy Latcham pour diriger DC Studios. Comme James Gunn, il vient de Marvel Studios, où il est entré en 2004 avant d’en partir en 2017 pour fonder sa propre société de production. Il a à son crédit des films comme Iron Man, Iron Man 2, Les Gardiens de la Galaxie, Spider-Man: Homecoming, The Avengers ou encore Avengers : L’Ère d’Ultron. « Le panthéon des personnages de DC compte parmi les plus emblématiques de la culture populaire américaine. J’ai eu le privilège d’aider à donner vie sur grand écran à certaines des histoires de super-héros les plus célèbres, et je suis ravi et honoré d’avoir aujourd’hui l’opportunité de guider DC Studios vers sa prochaine ère », déclare-t-il. Sans doute aura-t-il une vision moins foutraque que celle de James Gunn, et moins tournée vers des personnages de second plan.

articles.title: SEGA newsletter data breach exposes 2.2 million email addresses
articles.text:
Japanese gaming giant SEGA has disclosed that a data breach at its third-party newsletter provider, ARARA, exposed the email addresses of 2.2 million newsletter subscribers.
The company says the exposed data also includes 92,300 records with additional information yet to be determined. The breach affects 11 newsletters linked to SEGA and SEGA Fave products and services.
The investigation found that the compromised data did not include customer names, dates of birth, gender, addresses, phone numbers, credit card details, or account passwords.
Also, email addresses registered with a “SEGA Account” are handled by a separate distribution system and were not affected by this incident.
The company is working with ARARA to determine what data was exposed and says it has no confirmed evidence of misuse.
“We are currently investigating the information associated with newsletter distribution in cooperation with ARARA,” SEGA stated.
ARARA service breached
ARARA disclosed on November 2 that it suffered a massive breach affecting its email distribution service, which compromised 77 million email addresses from nearly 380 corporate clients.
According to the company, a web server vulnerability and problems in its system environment contributed to the incident, but the exact intrusion method and timing remain under investigation.
ARARA previously estimated a smaller impact and assured SEGA on October 29 that no data compromise had occurred.
However, on November 3, after uncovering the full extent of the incident, ARARA notified the gaming company that data had been exposed and shared the full details between November 5 and 8.
ARARA also said the attackers abused their access to its service to send over 7 million emails impersonating credit card companies in late October.
Other notable victims of the same incident include MOS Burger, with 7.5 million email addresses exposed, Shochiku Multiplex Theatres, with 3.3 million records, TKC, with 2.3 million email addresses, and IIJmio, with nearly 1 million email addresses.
SEGA Arcade still down
SEGA Fave’s arcade game network services, which suffered a separate cybersecurity incident last week, are still offline, undergoing maintenance and safety checks.
On November 2, SEGA FAVE, SEGA's subsidiary responsible for toys, electronic gadgets, and arcade machine operations, disclosed unauthorized access to servers supporting its ALL.Net and Aime arcade gaming network services.
In response, it suspended all related services, including online gameplay, SEGA Lucky Kuji Online, and new SEGA ID registrations.
Its initial investigation found no evidence of customer or business partner data exfiltration, while payment information was unaffected because it was stored separately.
SEGA noted that the two incidents are unrelated.

articles.title: Suecia tiñe de magenta sus paneles solares y consigue cosechar debajo el mismo brócoli que a pleno sol, aunque tarda 25 días más en crecer
articles.text:
El brócoli que se ha desarrollado bajo estos paneles semitransparentes de color magenta ha sido similar en tamaño final al que se encuentra en pleno sol. Sin embargo, se han necesitado 25 días más para llegar a la madurez. Así lo han demostrado en un ensayo en Suecia (Universidad de Mälardalen).
Los paneles permiten que llegue cierta luz a las plantas. Con parte del resto se genera electricidad. Se han diseñado para que pasen las longitudes de onda en rojo y azul (que son las que absorben los pigmentos de la clorofila). De esta manera se trata de paliar el problema de la sombra que puede reducir la disponibilidad de luz.
Dos transparencias y una cosecha más tarde
Los investigadores han comparado el brócoli de una parcela sin cubrir con otros dos casos de brócoli bajo módulos con transparencia nominal del 50 % y un 70 %. Han medido variables ambientales y los resultados de rendimiento y composición nutricional e incluso han analizado la respuesta fotosintética.
Se obtuvo una eficiencia en el uso de la radiación 4,5 veces mayor que a pleno sol en el caso de los paneles del 50 % y 2,8 veces en el caso de los del 70 %. Este parámetro mide la relación entre la biomasa seca aérea obtenida y la radiación fotosintéticamente activa recibida. Se ha conseguido un resultado similar de cosecha con menor luz. Sin embargo, se ha tenido que esperar 25 días más.
Las plantas se comportan de forma similar en ambos casos, explica Ma Lu en el comunicado de los investigadores. Los resultados se limitan a las condiciones de ensayo. Es necesario validarlos en más temporadas y en otros casos.
También hay un límite a la generación de electricidad. En estos paneles se utilizan células de telururo de cadmio. Estas crean bandas opacas sobre el vidrio. Cuanto más densas son estas bandas, más luz pueden captar (y así generar electricidad), aunque dejan pasar menos luz a las plantas.
Ramesh Rayudu es experto en sistemas eléctricos (Universidad Victoria de Wellington). Explica que en el periodo de cultivo se genera una cantidad estimada de 224,7 megavatios hora por hectárea. Esto representa unos 100 megavatios hora por hectárea menos que la referencia convencional. Para compensar este valor, sería necesario obtener entre 1,2 y 3,2 toneladas adicionales de brócoli por hectárea (dependiendo de los precios de la electricidad y de la cosecha).
Ma Lu ve más cerca aplicaciones en huertos comunitarios o cubiertas de invernaderos. El equipo ya está probando paneles de distintos colores (magenta, rojo y azul) en condiciones controladas. De esta forma pueden separar el efecto que tienen las características espectrales de la luz de otras variables de ensayo.

articles.title: F1 in Brazil: You’ve got to keep your tires alive
articles.text:
In sports, a “dead rubber” is a match that takes place after the outcome of the series or championship has already been decided. The people in charge hate this*—if you wrap up a title two-thirds of the way through a season, the viewers evaporate, as there’s nothing left at stake. But anyone who decided to skip this year’s Brazilian Grand Prix this past weekend missed one of the year’s most entertaining races, as a combination of a mixed-up starting order, some very fast drivers at the back, and a wet track that dried and then saw rain again resulted in action aplenty.
A peculiarity of F1 is that even if you manage to win a championship, there’s no guarantee you’ll be in a position to defend it. Take McLaren’s Lando Norris, who took the crown in 2025 after a nail-biting fight with his teammate Oscar Piastri and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen. Sadly for Lando, McLaren did not start this year in a position to win races, and even with several upgrades, the team has produced a car that is still very tricky to drive. But this weekend in Brazil, Norris demonstrated the form that earned him the number 1.
Rain on Saturday during qualifying helped jumble the usual running order. It was heavy enough that drivers used the wet weather tire with deep treads, which usually generates so much spray that visibility disappears and running has to be suspended. But with fewer cars on track in the later knockout qualifying sessions, this was not a problem for once. More disruption came from grid penalties for Verstappen and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, both of whom needed to use extra power unit components outside of the season’s allowance.
Everyone’s mixed up
Norris claimed pole, with this year’s new champion, Kimi Antonelli, alongside in his Mercedes. Row two was filled with the unusual sight of Liam Lawson’s Racing Bull and Nico Hulkenberg’s Audi, followed by Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar and Oliver Bearman’s Haas. Next was George Russell in the other Mercedes, then the even more unusual sight of Fernando Alonso’s Aston Martin, normally found much farther back. One could say the same about William’s Alex Albon, who qualified ninth ahead of the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri.

articles.title: AWS Launches TorchNeuron to Run PyTorch Models on AWS Trainium Without Modifications
articles.text:
At the recent PyTorch Conference North America 2026, Amazon introduced TorchNeuron, a native PyTorch backend that enables developers to run existing PyTorch code on AWS Trainium AI chips with virtually no code modifications.
Beyond reducing engineering effort, TorchNeuron allows enterprises to share hardware capacity between training and inference workloads, reallocating resources from inference to training during off-peak hours.
Amazon says that a single configuration change is sufficient to switch hardware, eliminating the need to rewrite and revalidate models when moving to Trainium.
Today, 85% of AI researchers and developers write their code in PyTorch. Until now, the hardware that code could run on was far more limited than the code itself, and expanding to new chips meant rewriting and revalidating work that took months to perfect.
According to the TorchNeuron documentations, when leveraging PyTorch's automatic device detection through torch.accelerator, the only required change is replacing .to('cuda') to .to('neuron'). The backend also natively supports distributed training and PyTorch parallelism APIs, including DDP, FSDP2, DTensor, and others. In addition, TorchNeuron provides native support for Torch streams and events through torch_neuronx.Stream and torch_neuronx.Event.
Amazon Annapurna Labs vice president Colin Brace, who leads the team behind TorchNeuron, emphasized that his team validated the 100,000 most popular models and more than 800 ML architectures to ensure a smooth developer experience when adopting the new backend.
Additionally, TorchNeuron enables developers and researchers to use the Neuron Kernel Interface to develop, optimize, and execute custom operators:
Developers can obtain finer performance control beyond Adaptive Eager and torch.compile by calling performance critical NKI kernels directly in model code to replace sequences of standard PyTorch operations (ATen ops).
Commenting on Amazon's announcement on LinkedId, Liner Notes Consulting CEO Yasuo Maeda noted that:
The real test will be whether developers can achieve competitive performance and total cost of ownership in production. The AI infrastructure race is not just about who builds the best chips. It is also about who makes them easiest to use at scale.
Similarly, user Pratham pratham hightlighted that, while reducing migration friction is important to avoiding accelerator lock-in, the real test lies in workload-specific performance, cost per token, and reproducibility.
Amazon also emphasizes that TorchNeuron has already been adopted by several organizations, including Cartesia, which is using it for voice AI inference, and the Lieber Institute for Brain Development, which explores applications in drug target identification and drug discovery.
AWS TorchNeuron announcement comes on the heels of Google's launch of TorchTPU, its native PyTorch backend for Google's TPU hardware.

articles.title: David Ellison says AI could be the ‘biggest creative unlock in modern history’
articles.text:
During Paramount Skydance’s latest earnings call, CEO David Ellison said “it’s hard to imagine” AI won’t have a bigger impact on the film industry than CGI. In response to a question about the company’s outlook for AI, Ellison said:
David Ellison says AI could be the ‘biggest creative unlock in modern history’
Paramount Skydance’s CEO compared AI to CGI, but said it ‘will never be a replacement’ for artists.
“I think when you zoom out and look at production, AI really has the potential to be the biggest creative unlock in modern history. The last time we saw anything close to this was really the, you know, advent of CGI and digital composites in the early 90s. That technology gave birth to amazing stories like Jurassic Park and Terminator 2, and it’s hard to imagine that AI is not going to have a more significant impact than that. And I personally believe that’s going to be an incredible unlock on creativity.”
Ellison gave Terminator as an example, describing how it cost $4 million to make, but “if you wanted to make that picture today, shot for shot, it’s $60 to 70 million.” He went on to suggest AI might be able to help with that: “We think these tools will help unlock more original storytelling by being able to make the budgets more digestible to be able to take that amount of risk.”
Ellison said AI will “significantly” reshape Paramount Skydance’s business, saying the company has been developing its own AI tools. As a result of those tools, Ellison claims, “content will be easier to produce, projects across the organization will speed up, and how we work will transform.” He emphasized that “all of this makes the value of premium IP and live events more valuable, not less.”
Ellison also noted that “in a world of AI slop, we think there will always be a premium for truly hand-crafted storytelling.” He added, “We also continue to believe that artificial intelligence is a tool for artists and will never be a replacement for them.”

articles.title: Auf dem Trockenen? Wo es gravierende Datenlücken bei unserem Grundwasser gibt
articles.text:
Datenlücken beim Grundwasser: „Wir wissen mehr über die Mondoberfläche als über unser Trinkwasser“
Kein Plätschern, kein Rauschen, keine Ferienromantik: Unser Grundwasser ist der wohl unauffälligste Gewässertyp, dafür ein ausgesprochen mächtiger. Rund 23 Billionen Kubikmeter H₂O – eine Zahl mit 15 Nullen – schlummern unter der Oberfläche unseres Planeten. Das entspricht etwa 99 Prozent der flüssigen Süßwasservorräte weltweit. Der Wasserspeicher unter Tage gilt als eine der wichtigsten Ressourcen, um die Wasserversorgung in der Klimakrise zu sichern – auch in Deutschland.
Doch die Begehrlichkeiten sind groß. Unsere Wasserwerke gewinnen rund 70 Prozent des Trinkwassers aus der Tiefe. Auch die Industrie, der Bergbau, die Landwirtschaft und etliche Menschen mit Eigenheim und Garten nutzen Grundwasser. „Gerade sind die Entnahmen recht konstant, wir rechnen aber mit einer Steigerung in den nächsten Jahren“, sagt Bernd Kirschbaum vom Umweltbundesamt. Unter anderem, weil Rechenzentren und Wasserstoffproduzenten künftig zunehmend Grundwasser zapfen werden. Auch Pflanzen konsumieren immer mehr, denn bei höheren Temperaturen und längeren Vegetationsperioden steigt die Verdunstung über ihre Blätter.
Dieser Text erscheint in der Ausgabe 8/2026 von MIT Technology Review. Darin beschäftigen wir uns mit den Folgen des Klimawandels und wie wir uns an Hitze, Dürre und Überschwemmungen anpassen sollten. Das Heft ist seit dem 06.11.2026 im Zeitschriftenhandel und in unserem Online-Shop erhältlich.
Gleichzeitig sinken vielerorts die Pegel des Grundwassers, weil es im Winter weniger regnet und heftige Niederschläge im Sommer auf knochentrockenen Böden eher abfließen als einsickern. Auch die Qualität bereitet Fachleuten Kopfzerbrechen. „Wenn das Rohwasser stark verunreinigt ist und entweder gar nicht oder nur mit hohem Reinigungsaufwand nutzbar ist, dann scheiden diese Vorräte für viele Nutzungen schlicht aus“, gibt Kirschbaums Kollege Jörg Rechenberg zu bedenken. Gut ein Drittel des Grundwassers sei in einem schlechten Zustand. Ein Problem, das sich durch den Klimawandel noch verschärft.
Schlittern wir also gerade in eine Grundwasserkrise? Werden sich in 50 Jahren Salzberge an Deutschlands Küsten türmen, weil Trinkwasser aus dem Meer gewonnen werden muss? Müssen Getreide und Gemüse statt auf Feldern in Zukunft in mehrstöckigen Hochhäusern wachsen, um möglichst viel Wasser im System zu halten? Und können wir es uns in Zukunft immer noch leisten, wertvolles Trinkwasser buchstäblich durchs Klo zu spülen? Die Suche nach Antworten läuft gerade. Und sie fängt beim Ist-Zustand an.

articles.title: Mass Effect 1 and 2 composer has hopes that 'someone else can come in' and save BioWare following the studio's shutdown and Mass Effect 5 cancelation — 'Frankly, it’s sort of bananas to think of BioWare as just…gone'
articles.text:
'Frankly, it’s sort of bananas to think of BioWare as just…gone' — Original Mass Effect composer hopes 'someone else can come in and take it from here' following studio closure
Mass Effect Universe was canceled alongside the studio's shutdown
- Original Mass Effect composer Jack Wall hopes BioWare can be saved one day
- Wall says, "It’s sort of bananas to think of BioWare as just…gone"
- He adds, "I hope that someone else can come in and take it from here"
Original Mass Effect composer Jack Wall has reacted to EA shutting down BioWare and hopes the legendary studio can be saved one day.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming following the devastating news and cancelation of the next Mass Effect game, Mass Effect Universe, Wall said, "Frankly, it’s sort of bananas to think of BioWare as just…gone."
Wall worked on Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2 and agreed that the series is important enough to warrant saving, saying, "Mass Effect is such a wonderfully original universe. It feels like it should live on not only in games but TV and Film as well. The stories are so compelling."
The composer added, "Not sure where the Prime TV series sits at this time, but it would be really cool to see a show of this universe."
Following its closure, the studio released a statement saying that the "generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember." The shutdown came as part of EA's first major restructuring plan that led to 400 layoffs across the publisher's studios, including around 50 for the people remaining at BioWare.
Many creatives across the industry are urging someone, like another publisher, to save the developer before it's too late. Fans have also created a petition called "#SaveMassEffect" and wish to see BioWare's vision for the Mass Effect series continue.
Wall shared a similar sentiment about the studio, saying, "In short, I’m sad to see BioWare go. I hope that someone else can come in and take it from here."

articles.title: Wearable sleep trackers are using your brainwaves to train AI models without explicit user consent — tens of millions of hours of EEG data harvested
articles.text:
Wearable sleep trackers are using your brainwaves to train AI models without explicit user consent — tens of millions of hours of EEG data harvested
"We agree users should be explicitly informed"
Your sleep data might be doing double duty. While wearable headbands promise to help users understand their sleeping patterns, some of the companies behind them are also turning the electrical signals collected from their customers' brains into training material for artificial intelligence models. Science recently conducted an investigation alongside Pulitzer Center's AI Accountability Network and found that the customer neurology companies have accumulated tens of millions of hours of electroencephalography (EEG) recordings — a rather technical way of saying brain-wave data. As per the findings, several are using those recordings to develop so-called brain foundation models, despite initially failing to spell out that use in their privacy policies.
Interaxon, the Canadian firm behind the Muse sleep and meditation headband, is one of them. Its devices monitor electrical activity in the brain, alongside other physiological measurements, while users sleep. The recordings are processed into reports that help customers track their rest and identify changes in their sleeping patterns. But there is another use for that information. Interaxon has already trained an AI model using about 50,000 hours of EEG recording and says it removes identifying information, including names, email, and addresses, before using the data. “We aim to use as much of that eligible corpus as possible,” Nadia Kumentas, its Chief Marketing Officer, said.
That was not made particularly clear to customers, though. Prior to talking to Seince, Interaxon's privacy policy did not explicitly disclose that users' brain recordings could be used to train foundation models. The company has, however, updated the same with Kumentas acknowledging, "We agree users should be explicitly informed." For customers whose recordings had already been used, the classification came late, which likely exposes the company to potential lawsuits. Privacy, it seems, remains a major issue. As per Science, more than two-thirds of the companies studied explicitly allowed corporate transfers of data without user consent. That could be significant if a small neurotechnology firm is acquired, potentially putting its accumulated recordings in the hands of a new owner. Colorado and California, however, have amended their consumer privacy laws to cover neural data, although other states lag behind.
Interaxon isn’t the only company pushing this idea. Emotiv, another wearable EEG maker, is training its Large Brain model partly on recordings from customers using its high-end devices. It also updated its privacy policy following questions by Science, disclosing the use of de-identified neural data for model training subject to opt-in consent.
Notably, the idea behind these systems is particularly different from training a large language model. Instead of feeding AI an enormous amount of text, developers supply it with recordings of electrical activity in the brain. The model then learns recurring patterns that can be adapted to recognize different brain states or assist with specific research tasks. And there are already some interesting results. AI startup Piramidal has trained its model on more than 4 million hours of EEG data in partnership with Cleveland Clinic. The company developed a seizure-detection system that correctly identified nine out of 10 seizures in a pilot study after being fine-tuned on the clinic's recordings. That, however, doesn’t mean consumer headbands can suddenly read people's thoughts. Most wearable EEG devices use just one to six electrodes, considerably fewer than 19 to 25 typically found in clinical EEG systems. Also, their recordings are generally less comprehensive.
That said, the privacy implications of wearable brain technology aren't entirely new. In February, an engineer discovered he could access other people's brainwave recordings through a smart sleep mask he had purchased. He reportedly investigated the device after running into connection problems. By examining its Android application, he discovered hardcoded credentials that appeared to be shared across devices, which he later found were EEG readings belonging to other users.
The industry has also been gathering neural recordings on a considerable scale. Last December, we covered Coundit’s effort to collect 10,000 hours of neural data from thousands of patients. The San Francisco startup built its own headset system to capture brain activity alongside speech and text, with the aim of developing AI capable of translating signals into language. Meta has also been working on BrainQwerty, a non-invasive brain-computer interface that translates brain activity into keyboard inputs. Its second-generation system improved average word accuracy to 61% from 40% in the earlier version, although the technology remains a far cry from practical everyday use.
