articles.title: IFC says African firms pay 1.8% more to access credit
articles.text:
An analysis of over 330,000 corporate bonds across 50,000 firms over three decades reveals that African businesses face higher borrowing costs. However, pension reforms, capital market liberalisation, and stronger corporate governance could help reduce this premium.
African businesses pay significantly more to borrow in corporate bond markets than their counterparts in high-income economies, with firms on the continent facing a median real borrowing cost that is 180 basis points (1.8%) higher, according to research by the International Finance Corporation (IFC).
The findings, presented by Césaire A. Meh, Manager of Private Markets at the IFC during the Africa Financial Industry Summit (AFIS) in Luanda, Angola, examine the factors driving corporate borrowing costs across countries, currencies, and financial markets.
The analysis draws on more than 330,000 bonds issued by over 50,000 firms globally over 30 years.
Between 2015 and 2024, the median real yield on corporate bonds in African countries was 2.8%, compared with 1% in high-income countries. The 180-basis-point difference highlights the additional cost African businesses face when accessing debt financing through capital markets.
However, the research suggests that the problem extends beyond the cost of capital itself. Domestic fiscal conditions, exposure to global financial shocks, the depth of local investor markets, regulatory frameworks, and individual company characteristics all influence how much businesses pay to raise debt.
Borrowing costs differ significantly across African markets
The IFC’s analysis also shows that borrowing costs are not uniform across the continent.
Its comparison of selected African economies, including Nigeria, Morocco, South Africa, and Egypt, points to considerable differences in real corporate bond yields.
The figures presented for these selected markets include yields of 4.9% in Nigeria, 3.9% in Morocco, 4.7% in South Africa, and 2.1% in Egypt.
These differences suggest that businesses operate under varying financing conditions even within the same continent.
The cost of borrowing is influenced not only by a country’s broader classification as an emerging or developing economy but also by its domestic financial and fiscal environment.
For businesses seeking long-term financing, this distinction matters. Capital availability does not necessarily translate into affordable capital, particularly where domestic market conditions and investor confidence push up yields.
Fiscal credibility offers protection against global shocks
One of the more significant findings is the relationship between domestic fiscal conditions and corporate borrowing costs.
According to the IFC analysis, a one-percentage-point reduction in sovereign yields is associated with a 76-basis-point decline in corporate borrowing yields in domestic markets. In international markets, the corresponding decline is 46 basis points.
This relationship illustrates how improvements in a country’s sovereign borrowing conditions can extend to private businesses.
When government borrowing costs fall, companies also benefit from lower financing costs. This makes fiscal credibility relevant not only to governments managing public debt but also to businesses seeking affordable capital.
The research also examines the effect of movements in US monetary policy on corporate borrowing costs.
A one-percentage-point increase in the US policy rate is associated with a 10-basis-point increase in corporate borrowing yields in domestic markets.
The effect is considerably larger in international markets, where yields increase by 47 basis points.
This contrast points to the relative ability of domestic capital markets to absorb external financial shocks. While local markets are not insulated from global monetary conditions, the impact is less pronounced than in international markets.
For African businesses that depend on international bond markets, changes in US monetary policy can therefore have a more direct effect on financing costs.
Pension reforms could lower the cost of corporate debt
The IFC identifies expanding domestic investor bases as another way to improve access to affordable financing.
Its analysis finds that pension reforms that introduce mandatory or quasi-mandatory individually funded programmes can increase corporate bond issuance.
The effect becomes more pronounced over time. The presentation shows domestic corporate issuances increasing progressively in the years following reform, reaching approximately 4.6% by the fourth year.
More importantly, the reforms are associated with lower yields on corporate borrowing. The analysis finds that pension reforms can lower corporate bond yields by approximately 150 basis points in domestic markets among firms issuing bonds before and after the reforms. This suggests pension systems play a role beyond providing retirement savings.
By expanding the pool of institutional investors, pension reforms can deepen domestic capital markets and provide businesses with additional sources of long-term financing.
For African economies seeking to mobilise private investment, pension reform can contribute to both the supply of investable capital and the affordability of corporate debt.
Opening capital markets could reduce international borrowing costs
Capital account liberalisation is another policy intervention identified by the IFC. The measures considered include reducing capital controls, opening markets to foreign investors, and easing regulations.
According to the analysis, these reforms increase corporate bond issuances, particularly in international markets.
The presentation shows international issuances rising following liberalisation, while domestic issuances also increase over the period examined.
The reforms are also associated with lower yields on corporate borrowing in international markets. For firms issuing bonds before and after liberalisation, the IFC reports a 120-basis-point reduction in international corporate yields.
The findings suggest that removing barriers to foreign investment can expand the pool of investors available to companies and improve the conditions under which they raise debt.
However, the results also reinforce the importance of domestic market development. Liberalisation is presented alongside pension reform as part of a broader effort to expand the investor base and increase corporate access to capital.
Transparency and governance influence what companies pay
The cost of borrowing is not determined by government policy and macroeconomic conditions alone. The IFC’s research also identifies firm-level characteristics that influence the yields companies pay.
Stronger regulatory disclosure requirements correlate with lower corporate yields, according to the presentation’s comparison of corporate transparency and median real bond yields across income groups.
At the company level, the analysis finds that unlisted firms pay a premium when accessing bond markets. The premium is 22 basis points in domestic markets and 84 basis points internationally.
Prior access to loan and bond markets, however, is associated with lower borrowing costs. Firms with previous market access record reductions of 23 basis points in domestic markets and 31 basis points internationally.
The presentation also identifies state-owned enterprises as borrowing at lower yields, with reductions of 50 basis points domestically and 37 basis points internationally.
These findings point to the importance of a company’s market reputation, ownership structure, and track record when investors assess its creditworthiness. The IFC argues that businesses can improve their credibility through three broad areas of intervention: governance, disclosure and creditor protection.
On governance, the IFC notes that independent oversight, effective audit committees, and credible board monitoring can strengthen investor confidence in a company’s management and decision-making.
On disclosure, timely and detailed financial reporting, clear information about debt profiles and the use of proceeds, and regular communication with investors can reduce information gaps.
Covenants, collateral, guarantees, and credible enforcement venues can provide investors with greater protection when extending credit can help protect creditors.
These firm-level interventions are particularly valuable in environments where country-level institutions and disclosure frameworks are still developing.
The challenge of mobilising private investment
The IFC’s findings offer a broader perspective on the challenge of financing business growth in African economies. Reducing borrowing costs requires more than increasing the amount of capital available to businesses. It also requires improving the conditions under which that capital is mobilised and deployed.
The research identifies several connected interventions: strengthening fiscal credibility, expanding domestic institutional investor bases through pension reforms, opening capital markets to international investors, improving regulatory disclosure, and encouraging stronger corporate governance.
Together, these measures could help narrow the borrowing cost gap between African businesses and firms in high-income economies.
The 180-basis-point premium identified in the IFC analysis illustrates the scale of the financing disadvantage. However, the findings also suggest that the gap is influenced by factors that governments, regulators, and businesses can address.
For African companies, the implications are equally important. Access to capital markets is not simply about issuing bonds. A company’s transparency, governance, ownership structure, and borrowing history can influence the cost of financing.
The central issue, therefore, is not only how African economies mobilise more private investment, but how they create financial markets and corporate environments in which businesses can access that investment at a lower cost.

articles.title: Las Guerreras K-pop y los Saja Boys: cómo generar dibujos para colorear con Gemini
articles.text:
La IA de Google, Gemini, permite transformar descripciones de texto o imágenes de referencia en láminas de línea negra sobre fondo blanco, listas para imprimir y pintar. La herramienta interpreta las características visuales de personajes animados como las protagonistas de Las Guerreras K-pop (Rumi, Zoey y Mira) y sus antagonistas, los Saja Boys, para convertirlas en ilustraciones de contornos limpios sin sombras ni degradados.
El procedimiento combina instrucciones textuales precisas con, opcionalmente, una imagen de referencia. El resultado depende en gran medida de la claridad del prompt ingresado en el chat y de la calidad de la fotografía o captura que se utilice como base.
Cómo pedir a Gemini que genere dibujos para colorear en estilo line art
El estilo conocido como line art es la base de cualquier lámina para colorear funcional. Consiste en trazos negros uniformes sobre fondo blanco, sin sombreados, rellenos de color ni degradados de gris.
Para lograrlo, la orden dirigida a Gemini debe ser explícita. No basta con pedir una ilustración de los personajes: hay que especificar que se trata de una página de libro para colorear, con contornos cerrados y gruesos, pensada para imprimirse en formato vertical sobre hoja tamaño carta o A4.
Una pregunta frecuente entre quienes se inician en esta técnica es qué hace que un dibujo generado por IA sea apto para colorear. La respuesta es simple: una lámina lista para pintar debe tener líneas negras definidas, espacios interiores completamente en blanco y ausencia total de sombras o tramas de gris, de modo que los lápices, marcadores o témperas puedan aplicarse sin interferencias visuales.
En el caso de Las Guerreras K-pop, el prompt recomendado solicita a Rumi, Zoey y Mira en una pose heroica de cuerpo entero, con sus atuendos de concierto y peinados característicos, acompañadas de notas musicales y estrellas dispersas como elementos decorativos del fondo.
Para los Saja Boys, la instrucción cambia el enfoque hacia una composición grupal dinámica, con atuendos escénicos oscuros de estilo K-pop futurista, peinados puntiagudos y micrófonos, manteniendo siempre la misma exigencia de contornos definidos y fondo blanco.
Uso de imágenes de referencia para conservar la fidelidad de los personajes
Aunque es posible generar las láminas únicamente a partir de descripciones escritas, subir una captura de pantalla nítida de la película a Gemini mejora la precisión del resultado. La imagen de referencia ayuda a que el modelo conserve peinados, atuendos de escenario y accesorios originales con mayor exactitud que una descripción puramente textual.
Lo ideal es que la captura muestre una pose frontal o de tres cuartos, bien iluminada, sin elementos que oculten los rasgos de los personajes.
El procedimiento para adjuntar la imagen requiere acceder primero a gemini.google.com o a la aplicación móvil de Gemini, con una cuenta de Google iniciada. Desde la caja de texto, el botón de signo más o el ícono de imagen permite cargar la fotografía de referencia antes de escribir el prompt.
Cuando se parte de una imagen, la instrucción debe pedir que se mantengan los rasgos faciales, las poses y los atuendos originales, pero redibujados en line art tradicional: trazos negros uniformes, contornos bien delimitados y ausencia de rellenos oscuros o sombras volumétricas.
Composición recomendada para láminas infantiles
La complejidad visual de una lámina influye directamente en si resulta adecuada para niños o principiantes. Las composiciones simples, con personajes en primer plano y de cuerpo entero, facilitan la tarea de colorear sin que los detalles diminutos se conviertan en un obstáculo.
Los fondos deben mantenerse limpios, evitando elementos pequeños que compliquen el uso de lápices o marcadores gruesos, herramientas habituales entre los dibujantes más jóvenes.
Revisión, ajustes y descarga del resultado final
Una vez generada la imagen, conviene revisar que los bordes de los personajes no queden cortados y que no aparezcan zonas con tramas de puntos o sombras densas que puedan manchar la hoja durante la impresión.
Si el resultado inicial presenta sombreados o trazos incompletos, es posible corregirlo dentro del mismo chat con una instrucción adicional que pida líneas más gruesas, eliminación de cualquier sombreado de gris y relleno completamente blanco en el interior de las figuras.
La descarga final debe hacerse en resolución completa para conservar la nitidez del contorno. Para la impresión, se recomienda papel bond tradicional en el caso de lápices o marcadores, y cartulina o papel más grueso cuando se planea usar témperas u otros materiales húmedos.

articles.title: "Un lienzo en blanco": se vende una isla entera entre Galicia y Portugal en medio de quejas que tildan de disparate construir ahí
articles.text:
“Belleza, tranquilidad y libertad de desarrollo”. Así se promociona la venta de Boega, una isla que se abre entre Tomiño y Vila Nova de Cerveira, donde el río Miño raja su cauce como quien extiende los brazos. Este islote de un bosque de verde eléctrico, silencio y pureza no tiene dueño. Por eso ahora, y como documentaban desde La Voz de Galicia, la mayor isla del Miño se ofrece al mejor postor por seis millones de euros. Sale a unos 146.000 euros por hectárea, según mis cuentas.
Qué se vende. Según Galiciaé, son unas 41 hectáreas de terreno plano y arbolado, de 1,4 kilómetros de largo y 400 metros de ancho, sin edificios ni infraestructuras. No hay nada, así que puede haber de casi todo. Los anuncios, publicados en Private Islands Online, JamesEdition y Vladi Private Islands, hablan de un “lienzo en blanco”. Entre los usos que sugieren figuran una residencia de lujo, cabañas ecológicas autosuficientes o un santuario natural privado. Solo se llega por barco o helicóptero, y Vladi precisa que está a 45 minutos del aeropuerto de Oporto y a 40 del de Vigo.
¿Isla gallega? Aunque se divise desde Tomiño, A Boega es portuguesa: pertenece a Vila Nova de Cerveira, y su titularidad particular fue delimitada y reconocida en 1952. Una leyenda local, recogida por el ayuntamiento portugués, atribuye su nombre a un anciano llamado Ega y a su nieto, que lo llamaba Bô. Hoy la propiedad está ligada a una sociedad cuyo capital adquirió íntegramente el fondo BlueCrow Growth Fund I en noviembre de 2021.
Sueños sin construir. Hace años se planteó convertirla en campo de golf o en complejo hotelero, y en 2023 llegó el proyecto más ambicioso, Porto Boega, un parque de atracciones presentado en Orlando por la británica Storyland Studios (y ojo que contaba hasta con el respaldo de BlueCrow, uno de los mayores capitales de Portugal). Sin embargo, no se construyó nada; más bien se criticó su posible impacto ambiental sobre un tramo delicado del río.
Ser dueño, pero a medias. El anuncio presume de “total flexibilidad arquitectónica”, pero, como recuerda Galiciaé, levantar una vivienda, un hotel o un helipuerto exigiría autorizaciones urbanísticas, ambientales y, en el último caso, aeronáuticas que no vienen con la escritura.
En 2023, el fondo presentó un Pedido de Informação Prévia (PIP), el trámite portugués para comprobar si un proyecto es viable, orientado a un uso agrícola. En julio de 2025, los citados BlueCrow lo daban por pendiente, y un anuncio posterior de Vladi asegura que hay un PIP favorable para actividades agrícolas. Es decir, se pueden montar granjas y zonas de cultivo, pero nada de parques temáticos.
El rechazo en la orilla gallega. Tal y como han publicado desde COPE, la puesta a la venta ha provocado un fuerte rechazo entre alcaldes como los de Tui y Tomiño y entre los pescadores del río, aunque la crónica no detalla sus argumentos. El más explícito es el alcalde de Tui, Enrique Cabaleiro, que pide que el Estado portugués o el español la conviertan en propiedad pública.
Tiene razón de ser: las administraciones se enfrentan a requisitos ambientales muy estrictos incluso para autorizar una prueba deportiva, y ahora se plantearía dejar a un ente privado emprender una obra de un impacto enorme. Recuerda además que todo el espacio del río pertenece a la Red Natura, el sistema europeo de áreas protegidas, y concluye que “es un disparate hacer ahí un resort o cualquier otra actividad”.
Mercado de islas. No es una rareza gallega, aunque sí minoritaria. Ya hay islas privadas como Toralla, la Illa da Creba, las Sisargas u O Santo, este último, un islote de Marín, anunciado en su día por 300.000 euros. En cualquier caso, no consta ningún comprador y el precio es un redondeo que puede bajar o subir según avance el tiempo de la oferta. Quedan sin aclarar el estado real del PIP y la posición de la Câmara de Vila Nova de Cerveira y de la sociedad propietaria, que no figuran en lo publicado. Mientras tanto, la isla no se va a mover de sitio, acaso ganará o perderá unos metros según el caudal del Miño.

articles.title: Iris Plaza Breach May Have Exposed Data of 7.7 Million Customers
articles.text:
Hackers may have stolen the personal information of 7.7 million people from Japanese online shopping platform Iris Plaza.
The incident, says household products and appliance manufacturer Iris Ohyama, which operates the platform, was discovered on October 28.
The Japanese company immediately suspended Iris Plaza, disconnected related systems, and launched an investigation into the attack.
Of the 7.7 million individuals potentially affected, 5.8 million are current and former platform members who had their names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, gender information, and encrypted passwords compromised.
The remaining 1.9 million individuals are non-members who had their names, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses compromised. They include people who made purchases without registering on the platform.
Iris Ohyama says the hacked external cloud service does not store credit card information. No store operated by Iris Plaza has been affected.
The company says it has blocked the attackers’ access to the service, has notified law enforcement and the relevant authorities, and has retained external experts to aid with the investigation.
“At this time, there have been no reports of unauthorized use or financial damage resulting from this incident,” an automated translation of the company’s incident FAQ reads.
The Iris Plaza platform remains offline while the company investigates the cause of the incident and applies the necessary remediation measures.
Additionally, the manufacturer suspended its home fashion specialty store Simple Style, the Iris Group’s home appliance subscription and delivery and installation services, and new applications to the site, although it has no evidence these sites were compromised as well.

articles.title: Narwal V50 Cube review: minor button quirks aside, this lightweight stick vacuum delivers smart dirt detection and great cleaning, with a brilliant multi-tasking base station
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Narwal has launched its first stick vacuum, the V50, with an aqua headlight that magnifies dust, and smart features that automatically increase suction when dirt or carpet is detected. The vacuum performed well on most of our tests, despite poor front edge cleaning. At first glance, the battery life seems average, however, this vacuum comes with a second battery that always stays charged and ready in a compact dock that auto empties the dust cup, detangles the brush roll, and hides the two-in-one crevice tool away.
Reasons to buy
- + Good side edge cleaning
- + Lightweight and maneuverable
- + Wand extends to reach high places
- + Aqua headlight magnifies dust and dirt
- + AI dirt detection, eco, and turbo modes
- + Back-up battery stays charged in base
- + Base detangles brush roll, empties dust cup, and stores two-in-one crevice tool
Reasons to avoid
- - Poor front edge cleaning
- - Average turbo suction power
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Narwal V50 Cube: two-minute review
For its first stick vacuum, Narwal did a great job with the V50 Cube. It launched in November 2026 as an extremely lightweight and cordless stick vac with an extendable wand and a dock that does more than charge and auto empty. Over the course of two weeks, I used the vacuum to clean debris from my laminate and hardwood floors, the cobwebs in my windowsills, and dust from my ceiling.
Even with just a maximum 28,000 Pa suction (I’ve tested robovacs with more power), the V50 Cube did pretty well cleaning fine and thick materials, especially on my rugs. Most of the time, I used the AI or auto mode (and sometimes the turbo mode) as the eco mode wasn’t as effective.
The only time the vacuum struggled with a cleaning task was suctioning Cheerios from my hard floors. Other than that, I was very satisfied with its performance thanks to its dirt detecting capabilities which increased the suction power when debris was detected. I even appreciated the aqua headlight that showed me exactly where to clean as it magnifies dust more so than a regular white headlight. The front edge cleaning was poor, but at least the side edge cleaning was anywhere between zero and half an inch.
The charging dock auto empties the dust and debris and reverses the brush roll to prevent tangling. The two-in-one crevice tool is hidden away inside the dock when not in use. There, you’ll also find an extra battery that is always charged and ready to go. This is good since one battery only lasts seven minutes on turbo, 20 minutes on AI or auto mode, and 55 minutes on eco mode.
There are other little details about the design that’s amazing like how it automatically lowers a brush plate when cleaning a carpet to pull more dust and debris – or the way it’s outfitted with a manual scraper to pull off residue stuck in the dust cup. Sure, there are some drawbacks, like how the vacuum head and wand buttons sometimes stick or the crevice tool fell off a few times, but when weighing the pros and cons, I believe there is a lot of value in this vacuum and a promise from Narwal of more to come.
Narwal V50 Cube: price and availability
- List price: $649.99 (about £480 / AU$930)
- Launched: November 2026
- Available: US, Canada, China, and selected EU countries (Germany, France, Italy, Czech Republic, Hungary, and Belarus)
The Narwal V50 launched in November 2026 with a price tag of $649.99, becoming the brand’s first stick vacuum in the US. That works out at roughly £480 / AU$930, but it's not currently available in the UK or Australia. It is, however, being sold in Canada, China, and the EU.
You may also be able to find it more cheaply in one of Narwal's regular sales. Despite its recent release, at the time of writing it has received a $150 discount in Narwal's Black Friday deals, bringing its price down to $449.99.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The relatively high price tag comes from the fact that the vacuum has sensors that detect floor type and dirt. It’s also sold with a charging base with auto-empty features, and an extra battery that doubles your battery life. Considering these features, I’d say the price makes sense.
- Value score: 4 out of 5
Narwal V50 Cube: specs
| Weight | 3.1 lbs / 1.4 kg | 
| Bin size | 450ml for dust cup / 0.3L dustbin | 
| Max runtime | 20 min on Auto, 55 min on Eco, 7 min on turbo | 
| Charge time | About 2-3 hours | 
| Size (H x W x L) | Vacuum Cleaner (Default): 9.5 × 6.4 × 34.6 in Vacuum Cleaner (Extended): 9.5 × 6.4 × 41.3 in Dock: 10.6 × 7.5 × 24.8 in | 
| Modes | Hard floor mode, Carpet mode | 
| Cleaning path | 9.5 in | 
| Headlamps | Aqua light | 
Narwal V50 Cube: design
- Extremely lightweight cordless vacuum that maneuvers easily
- Aqua headlight magnifies dust, dirt, and debris
- AI capabilities sense floor types and dirt
As Narwal’s first stick vacuum, the V5 has a lot going for it in terms of its design. The black and gray vacuum is modern, sleek, and compact. After pulling it from the base, I have to extend the wand to make it more comfortable to use (I’m 5’5”). The buttons on the vacuum can stick when it comes to removing the vacuum head or the handheld from the wand, but I never had an issue with the extension button. Unfortunately, the vacuum can’t stand on its own, but it can lie 180 degrees flat.
At only 3lbs., the V50 is super lightweight, which made it easy for me to move the vacuum across my floors or hold it up high above my head to clean ceiling corners. The vacuum head is 9.5 inches wide and it’s maneuverable without being uncontrollable, allowing me to clean around chair legs easily.
The grip on the vacuum is very comfortable with the power button and mode switch button in easy reach. A small screen shows the mode and battery life displayed as an icon. When in AI auto mode, the display screen has a curved line to highlight the dirt level. Purple tells you that the floor is clean, while red indicates unseen dirt.
I’ve always been a fan of headlights on vacuums, but this one really takes the cake. The aqua light covers 145 degrees, magnifying every bit of dust on your floor. It works very well in tandem with the AI DirtSense technology which detects dust and dirt, thereby automatically increasing the suction power. The AI technology senses rugs or carpets and lowers a brush plate to create a seal to better pull dust from the fibers of the carpet.
The charging dock is one of the most compact ones I’ve seen — and definitely ever tested. In fact, the vacuum won’t fit on the dock unless you unextend the wand. The charging dock automatically removes dust and debris from the dust cup into a sealed bag that holds up to 100 days’ worth of dirt. Dual H13 HEPA filtration and UVC+ Silver Ion Sterilization ensure that the dust stays locked away.
Narwal also added an anti-tangle hand tool to the dust cup that scrapes away tough residue. There’s a scraping ring under the vacuum that prevents hair or thread wrapping. And when you place the vacuum on the dock, the brush roll undergoes reverse rotation to flush everything out into the dust bag.
Behind the front panel of the dock, there’s a compartment that holds the 2-in-1 crevice tool and another one that charges an extra battery. I really admire that Narwal created a space to hide the accessory and the battery in the dock — something that not enough brands do in my opinion. My only critique would be to have the front panel placed on a hinge in the future.
Setup took no time at all. I added the wand and the vacuum head to the handheld, charged it up, and started cleaning.
- Design score: 4 out of 5
Narwal V50 Cube: battery life
- 20 min on auto mode, 55 min on eco mode, and 7 min on turbo mode
- Extra battery stays charged in the charging base
- Took about two hours for the vacuum to fully recharge
The Narwal V50’s battery life differs depending on which mode you use and the dirt level of your floors. In my testing, the eco mode lasted the longest at 55 minutes, while the battery on turbo mode lasted only seven minutes.
The battery died on AI mode, or the dirt detection mode, after 20 minutes. In that time, I was able to clean about three quarters of the hardwood floors in my home, however, I was moving fast to achieve that. My floors were particularly dusty and dirty, so I’m not surprised that the battery lasted only 20 minutes. Each time the vacuum recognized dirt or dust, it increased the suction which used more power. To that effect, you may see the battery life adjust a bit depending on if you’re using the vacuum on carpet or hardwood floors, as carpet or rugs will cause the vacuum to increase the suction.
The battery life is quite average compared to others, and I wish it lasted a bit longer on the dirt detection mode. However, the cool thing about this vacuum is that it comes with a backup battery that always stays charged in the charging base. So whenever the battery dies, I can grab the other battery, fit it to the Narwal V50 and continue cleaning. It effectively doubles the battery life of the vacuum, allowing you to clean way more at once.
The vacuum took about two hours to recharge on the dock.
- Battery life score: 4 out of 5
Narwal V50 Cube: performance
- Powerful carpet suction, with decent edge cleaning
- Headlight and auto dirt detection work together to pick up dust and debris
- Very lightweight and nimble for cleaning floors or high spaces
The Narwal V50 is a fascinating vacuum. With a turbo suction power of only 28,000 Pa, it’s not the strongest vacuum I’ve tested, and yet, it performed surprisingly well in a lot of ways. I used the vacuum to clean my floors as I normally would, and ran a few tests to see how well it suctioned a variety of materials on different floor types.
One of my favorite aspects of this stick vacuum is its lightweight nature and the smaller vacuum head size. It’s so nimble and twists and turns easily so I could clean around a lot of my furniture without having to move it. The aqua headlight magnifies dust and debris considerably. (I was astounded by how much dust collects on my floors daily!) The ability to lie 180 degrees flat was a big bonus and because the vacuum head and the wand are so thin, I was able to clean under a dresser that I’ve never been able to reach with any other vacuum I’ve tested.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
I was very satisfied with how the vacuum picked up dust and debris on the turbo mode and AI or auto mode. I used the V50 most days to pick up food droppings in my kitchen or to clean up dirt I trekked into my mudroom. I was also very glad that I could break down this vacuum and use it as a handheld with the 2-in-1 crevice tool to clean cobwebs from my ceilings and windows or dust from my base boards. I should note that the crevice tool fell off the wand a few times. I even struggled to remove the handheld from the wand too.
The eco mode performed better with the vacuum head on the body of the vacuum (rather than as a handheld), but I doubt I will use that mode from herein out since the suction power was quite low.
Edge cleaning wasn’t as good as I hoped it would be. There was about an inch along the front edge of the vacuum. The side edge cleaning was better, ranging anywhere from 0.5 inches to no space along the side. Unfortunately, I never figured out why the side edge cleaning was not consistent.
To test the Narwal V50, I laid out Cheerios, rice, baking soda (on a rug), and flour (on hard floors) on my different floor types and used the AI dirt detect mode to see how well the vacuum picked up these materials. The vacuum performed perfectly on the rug, suctioning everything in a single go.
The hard floor results were not as good as the rug test. The Narwal V50 appeared to pick up all the flour from the hard floor, but there was a slight film of flour left behind that required the turbo mode to completely remove. While the vacuum picked up all the rice in a single pass, it struggled with the Cheerios. At first, it picked up some of the Cheerios, but after that, the vacuum just pushed the Cheerios forward. Even when I moved the vacuum head slower, I was only able to suction a few more Cheerios, which still left about five behind on the floor.
No matter what, I can’t praise the convenience of the charging base and its auto-empty capabilities. I love the ease of being able to put the vacuum on the base and going about my day, knowing that it suctions all the dirt and dust and keeps it fully contained until it needs to be replaced. The manual scraper tool inside the dust cup of the vacuum is also quite unique in that it removes stubborn residue that the suction power of the base might not be able to do on its own. I haven’t seen that with other vacuums so that’s a great maintenance feature.
I would by no means rely on the Narwal V50 to be your go-to vacuum to clean carpeted rooms. It’s great for cleaning rugs, but it doesn’t have the suction power to handle a house with mostly carpet. Instead, I’d utilize it as a quick-cleaning tool to pick up scraps of food, random bits of dirt, dust from your windowsills, or pet hair that clumps under furniture. It would also be a good choice for smaller homes or apartments.
- Performance: 3.5/5
Should you buy the Narwal V50 Cube?
| Narwal V50 Cube score card |  |  | 
|---|---|---|
| Attribute | Notes | Rating | 
|---|---|---|
| Value | Aptly priced, considering the extra battery, charging dock, and smart features. | 4 / 5 | 
| Design | A lightweight vacuum with an aqua headlight, dirt and floor sensing technologies, and a charging dock that does more than you expect. | 4 / 5 | 
| Performance | Very lightweight and maneuverable with a dust magnifying headlight. Side edge cleaning is good and picks up fine and large materials on rugs better than hard floors. | 3.5 / 5 | 
| Battery life | The battery life is average, lasting 7-55 minutes depending on the mode, dirt level, and floor type. However, an additional battery that stays charged in the base lets you double your use of the vacuum. | 4 / 5 | 
Buy it if
You want a vacuum that helps you to pick up dust you can and can’t see.
The aqua headlight magnifies dust so you know exactly where to vacuum in your house. And if you can’t see the dust or dirt? The Narwal V50’s AI DirtSense technology sees the dirt you cannot and increases the suction power automatically.
You want something lightweight to clean in all spaces.
The Narwal V50 is only 3lbs, making it easy to maneuver around your house. You can lay it flat to clean under beds or use it with the crevice tool to clean spider webs and dust above your head.
You hate doing vacuum maintenance.
Set the V50 on its base and the dock will not only charge the vacuum but detangle the brush roll and automatically empty the dust and dirt into a HEPA filter bag. Bonus: the base charges an extra battery and hides the two-in-one crevice tool away.
Don't buy it if
You have lots of carpet
The Narwal V50 did a great job during my rug test, however, a 28,000 Pa suction power isn’t high enough for deep cleaning of carpeted rooms. An upright vacuum will do a better job.
You want to clean the whole house on a single charge
Depending on which mode you choose, the charge of a single V50 battery lasts only 20 minutes on AI mode, which probably won’t clean a medium or large house. Thankfully, Narwal included a second battery that’s always charging in the dock, but if it feels like too much of a hassle to switch, then you’d do better to find a stick vacuum with a longer singular battery life.
You want superb edge cleaning
The front edge cleaning of the Narwal V50 is within an inch, which isn’t ideal for cleaning some areas of your house. The side edge cleaning is better but not consistent, resulting in a side edge cleaning within zero to half an inch.
Narwal V50 Cube: also consider
If the Narwal V50 Cube isn't the right vacuum for your home, here are two other options that you should consider:
Shark PowerDetect Cordless
This cordless vacuum auto-adjusts for use on carpet, and delivers outstanding cleaning. A better choice than the V50 Cube if you have more carpet than hard flooring.
Read our full Shark PowerDetect Cordless review
Dreame V20 Pro
If you want to get right up to baseboards and furniture, Dreame's V20 Pro is one of the best vacuums around for edge cleaning.
Read our full Dreame V20 Pro review
How I tested the Narwal V50 Cube
Over the course of a few weeks, I tested the Narwal V50 in my 1,600-square-foot house outfitted with historic hardwood and laminate floors and two large rugs. I used the vacuum to clean my floors, windowsills, baseboards, and ceilings, noting how it suctioned fine dust and large debris. After running multiple tests, I got a great sense of the battery life, maintenance required, and ease of use.
Read more about how we test vacuum cleaners.

articles.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS
Today, we are announcing the availability of Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic’s most capable generally available model for technical work that raises the bar in coding and the sciences. Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs for advanced work in cyber security and life sciences.
In this post, we cover what’s new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with the model on Amazon Bedrock.
Why Claude Fable 5.2
Fable 5.2 raises the bar on the hardest problems in coding, math, and science. It takes on ambiguous, multi-step work, verifies its own output, and can run unattended for hours to days. It interprets prompts, iterates, catches its own errors, and optimizes as it goes.
In Anthropic’s alignment testing, Mythos 5.2 hallucinates less, completes tasks more reliably, surfaces important information more consistently, and self-reports issues more honestly than Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1. Anthropic expects Fable 5.2 to behave similarly.
If a cyber security query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 4.8, and if a biology query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 5. On Amazon Bedrock, the retry is your code’s job, not an automatic switch. If the declined request hit the prompt cache, the refusal also includes a fallback credit token. Send that token with the retry and it’s billed as cache reads, so you don’t pay to write the same cache twice. Check the documentation for more information on fallback credit.
For authorized work in cyber security and life sciences, Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs.
Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 use cases
Where Fable 5.2 fits:
- Agentic coding across large, multi-repository codebases.
- Long-running agents for coordinating many subagents on multi-day work.
- Scientific research from new analytical methods to formal mathematical proofs.
- Financial analysis for quantitative research and forecasting.
- Design for 3D, hardware, and motion for generating environments, components, and simulations in code.
Mythos 5.2 covers two high-risk domains, available only through the verification programs noted earlier:
- Cyber security, for security engineering, red teaming, and penetration testing.
- Life sciences research, especially biomolecular design and research synthesis.
Data retention and Enterprise Frontier Safeguards
Anthropic designates Claude Fable 5.2 as a Covered Model. By default, its use requires retention for up to 30 days and human safety review. On Amazon Bedrock, Amazon personnel perform the review within the AWS boundary. Set the aws_review data retention mode on your account or project before you invoke the model. See Amazon Bedrock data retention for more details.
Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), built in collaboration with AWS, combines the privacy of zero data retention (ZDR) with state-of-the-art safeguards for detecting misuse. EFS works by storing data in cloud infrastructure controlled by the customer. Until EFS is available, eligible customers can use Fable 5.2 with zero data retention. This is available for internal use through at least June 30, 2027.
Getting started with Claude Fable 5.2 on Amazon Bedrock
To try Fable 5.2, open the Amazon Bedrock console, choose Test, Playground, and select Fable 5.2 as the model. From there, you can run a prompt directly against it.
Programmatically, you can call the model with the Anthropic Messages API against bedrock-runtime (through the Anthropic SDK). You can also stay on the Invoke and Converse APIs on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK.
Prerequisites
To follow along with the code examples in this post, you need the following:
- An active AWS account with Amazon Bedrock access.
- AWS CLI installed and configured with appropriate credentials.
- Python 3.9 or later.
- Boto3 (AWS SDK for Python) installed: pip install boto3.
- AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions: bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream.
Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3):
You can explore the Getting Started notebook for more examples.
Migrating to Claude Fable 5.2 with the claude-api skill in Claude Code
For teams already running Claude models on Amazon Bedrock, the claude-api skill in Claude Code helps you upgrade to Fable 5.2.
The claude-api skill is an open-source skill built into Claude Code that captures the details that make Claude API code work well. It covers which agent patterns fit a given job, what parameters change between model generations, and when to apply prompt caching. It stays current as Anthropic’s SDKs evolve: when a new model is released or the API gains a feature, the skill already knows.
What the skill does for Fable 5.2 migrations
When you ask Claude Code to upgrade your codebase to Fable 5.2, the skill reviews your code and walks you through:
- Updating model references swapping model IDs to the Fable 5.2 ID across your application code.
- Adjusting thinking settings moving manual thinking configurations to adaptive thinking where appropriate for the new model.
- Cleaning up outdated parameters removing deprecated beta headers, parameters, and settings that no longer apply.
- Suggesting effort levels recommending the right output_config.effort settings inline based on your use case.
The skill also detects your deployment platform including Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, and other environments and adjusts model ID formats and feature configurations accordingly. For example, it uses the Amazon Bedrock structured model ID format (global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-2).
How to use it
In Claude Code, run the migration directly:
/claude-api migrate
This scans your working directory (or a subdirectory or specific file list you confirm) and applies the migration changes in a single guided pass. You can also invoke it conversationally by telling Claude Code:
- “Upgrade me to Claude Fable 5.2” Claude reviews your code and walks through the necessary changes.
- “Improve my cache hit rate” the skill applies prompt caching rules that many developers miss, helping reduce costs on Bedrock.
- “Add context compaction to my agent” it walks you through compaction primitives and agent patterns for long-running Fable 5.2 sessions.
The claude-api skill is available in Claude Code and is also bundled into CodeRabbit, JetBrains IDEs (including Junie), Resolve AI, and Warp. It is open source at anthropics/skills on GitHub, so any coding agent can integrate it.
Availability
Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 are available today on Amazon Bedrock through US Geo CRIS and Global CRIS inference profiles. See the Bedrock documentation for the full list of supported Regions. For pricing information, see Amazon Bedrock pricing. Both models are also available through Claude Platform on AWS in every Region where the service is offered.
Give Claude Fable 5.2 a try in the Amazon Bedrock console, in Claude Platform on AWS, or explore the Getting Started notebook on GitHub.

articles.title: Grab 32 GB of RAM for just $209.99 thanks to the G.Skill Ripjaws V DDR4-3200 kit — rare sale on a quality kit from an enthusiast brand with a stellar reputation
articles.text:
Grab 32 GB of RAM for just $209.99 thanks to the G.Skill Ripjaws V DDR4-3200 kit — rare sale on a quality kit from an enthusiast brand with a stellar reputation
A soothing balm for these memory-troubled times.
Current-gen desktop builds are becoming rare due to memory and graphics card pricing, so many enthusiasts have taken to upgrading older machines, using previous-gen platforms, or buying used hardware. For any and all of those scenarios, the G.Skill Ripjaws V DDR4-3200 32 GB kit is just perfect, and it can be yours for $209.99 at Newegg with promo code BNWF83.
This dual-channel kit does exactly what it says on the tin, offering a roomy 32 GB that ought to be fine for many years to come, or until Altman finds your location. The rated speed is pretty good at 3200 MT/s, and latency is pretty good at 16 cycles. There's no onboard RGB, but that's a blessing in disguise, proven by the low asking price. The exact model is F4-3200C16D-32GVK, if you're curious.
This no-nonsense RAM kit offers just what the doctor ordered in these memory-starved times: high capacity, good speeds, and a low asking price.
With this kit in hand, you can conjure up a perfectly potent gaming rig using, say, a Ryzen 5800X3D CPU ($319.99 with promo code BFF43), an Asus TUF B550-Plus Wi-Fi motherboard ($119.99), and a Gigabyte Radeon RX 9070 graphics card ($729.99) and still come in under $1,500 for the baseline components.
As befits any quality memory kit, there are onboard XMP 2.0 profiles, and the maker offers a limited lifetime warranty. I've personally used the G.Skill memory for decades now, and have nothing but good things to say about the quality of the gear and the effectiveness of the company's RMA and support.

articles.title: Warum interessiert Klarna meine Miete?
articles.text:
Neue Regeln für Ratenkäufe: Klarna, Paypal und Co. fragen jetzt genauer nach
Kleidung zur Auswahl auf Rechnung mit 30 Tagen Zahlungsziel bestellen, das neue Smartphone in drei Raten finanzieren – all das ist im Rahmen von Buy now, pay later in den letzten Jahren für viele Kund:innen zum Standard geworden. Händler:innen setzen hier oftmals auf Dienste wie Klarna, Paypal, Stripe, Unzer oder Ratepay, die dafür sorgen, dass Kund:innen den gewünschten Zahlungsaufschub bekommen, die Shops aber dennoch sicher an ihr Geld kommen.
Doch was bisher oft mit wenigen Klicks umzusetzen ist, könnte in Zukunft unbequeme Fragen aufwerfen, etwa die nach dem monatlichen Einkommen, der Höhe der eigenen Miete oder weiteren bereits bestehenden Krediten. Der Grund dafür ist die neue EU-Verbraucherkreditrichtlinie, kurz CCD II. Die gilt in Deutschland ab dem 20. November und bezieht sich auch auf kleinere Finanzierungen, die bisher nicht unter die strengen Verbraucherkreditregeln fielen. Der Gesetzgeber zielt hier bewusst vor allem auf kleine, kurzfristige und zinsfreie Kredite sowie viele Angebote nach dem Prinzip „Buy now, pay later“ (BNPL) ab.
Warum interessiert Klarna meine Miete?
Die Neuregelung soll dazu beitragen, dass weniger Verbraucher:innen durch Verbraucherkredite in Zahlungsschwierigkeiten bis hin zur Überschuldung rutschen. Aufgabe der jeweiligen Zahlungsdienstleister ist es deshalb, genauer hinzuschauen und sich auch nicht nur auf bisherige bekannte Zahlungsausfälle zu verlassen. Die Richtlinie verlang „eine Prüfung auf Grundlage relevanter Informationen über Einkommen, Ausgaben und andere finanzielle Verpflichtungen“.
Hierzu zählt daher auch die Frage, wie viel Geld nach Abzug der monatlichen laufenden Kosten für zusätzliche Ratenzahlungen bereitsteht. Deshalb kann auch die Miethöhe zu den Daten gehören, die ein Zahlungsdienst abfragt. Einige Nutzer:innen in sozialen Medien berichten bereits jetzt von entsprechenden Anfragen gängiger Zahlungsdienstleister, die insbesondere auf die Miethöhe abzielen.
Zwar gibt es weder im Gesetz die zwingende Frage nach der Miethöhe, noch regelt die Direktive, welche Daten wie oft erhoben werden müssen. Doch sollen die erhobenen Informationen im angemessenen Verhältnis zu Kredithöhe, Laufzeit und Risiko stehen.
Das bringt die Zahlungsdienste in Zugzwang und in eine Zwickmühle, wie ein Experte aus dem Payment-Umfeld erklärt. Denn einerseits dürfen diese im Zusammenhang mit der DSGVO-spezifischen Datensparsamkeit nicht beliebig viel abfragen und wollen mit übermäßiger Fragerei natürlich auch Kund:innen nicht vor den Kopf stoßen, andererseits wird in Zukunft bei entsprechenden Zahlungsausfällen genauer nachgefragt werden, wie umsichtig der Anbieter vor Vergabe des Kredits – nichts anderes ist eine BNPL-Lösung ja – die Zahlungsfähigkeit geprüft hat.
Bonitätsprüfung auch bei niedrigen Beträgen
Anders als bisher sehen die Vorschriften aber vor, dass nicht mehr erst Finanzierungen ab 200 Euro derartig umfassend geprüft werden und dass auch jene Kurzläufer (die berühmte Zahlung nach 30 oder 45 Tagen) unter die Lupe genommen werden soll. Bislang waren diese weniger riskanten Fälle nicht Teil der Prüfungen.
Verbraucher:innen sollten sich daher – abgesehen von der möglicherweise damit verbundenen Schufa-Abfrage – genauer überlegen, ob sie bei überschaubaren Beträgen oder kurzen Laufzeiten eine solche Zahlungsart nutzen wollen.
Ganz neu sind solche Bonitätsprüfungen bei BNPL allerdings nicht, auch wenn die Kreditwürdigkeit bei kurzfristigen und zinsfreien Finanzierungen eher die Ausnahme als die Regel war. Anders sieht das übrigens aus, wenn der Händler selbst einen kurzfristigen, kostenlosen Zahlungsaufschub ohne Beteiligung eines Finanzierungsdienstleisters bietet. Dabei sind Zahlungsziele von bis zu 50 Tagen möglich.
Zahlungsdienste passen den Checkout an
Allerdings verweist, wie oben bereits genannt, die neue EU-Richtlinie ausdrücklich auch auf den Grundsatz der Datenminimierung aus der Datenschutz-Grundverordnung (DSGVO). Danach sollen Anbieter:innen nur jene Angaben für eine Kreditwürdigkeitsprüfung nutzen dürfen, die für den jeweiligen Zweck erforderlich und angemessen sind. Außerdem gilt, dass Verbraucher:innen eine verständliche Erklärung einfordern können, wenn die Kreditwürdigkeit mithilfe automatisierter Datenverarbeitung bewertet wird.
Das bedeutet, dass man eine Ablehnung in Zukunft nicht mehr kommentarlos hinnehmen muss, sondern Gründe erfragen kann, wenn man im Checkout von einer automatisierten Prüfung abgelehnt wird. Allerdings besteht weiterhin kein Anspruch darauf, den gewünschten Kredit tatsächlich zu bekommen.
Einige der großen Zahlungsdienstleister erklären daher schon jetzt im Checkout, dass vor Abschluss bestimmter BNPL-Zahlungen zusätzliche rechtliche Hinweise und Kreditbedingungen eingefordert werden. Andere stellen für die Kund:innen zusätzliche Informationen und Warnhinweise bereit. Doch in wie vielen Fällen Kund:innen nach zusätzlichen Informationen zu Einkommen, Miete und Haushaltsausgaben befragt werden, ist noch offen.

articles.title: Nvidia investiga CEO por relação com suposta espiã chinesa • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nvidia investiga CEO por relação com suposta espiã chinesa
Jensen Huang admitiu ter tido um relacionamento com executiva suspeita de espionagem industrial.
A Nvidia abriu uma investigação sobre seu CEO, Jensen Huang, após relatos de que ele teve um relacionamento amoroso com Alice Huang, ex-executiva da empresa singapurense Megaspeed, suspeita de trabalhar para o serviço de inteligência da China.
Segundo comunicado divulgado pelo conselho de administração da Nvidia neste domingo (08/11), a investigação será conduzida por membros independentes do órgão, com o apoio de advogados externos.
Huang reconheceu o relacionamento em uma mensagem enviada aos funcionários. Ele admitiu ter sido infiel à esposa, pediu desculpas à família e aos colegas e afirmou que vai colaborar com a investigação. O executivo também reconheceu ter falhado em suas responsabilidades com a companhia.
Autoridades suspeitam que Alice Huang tenha sido recrutada pelo Ministério da Segurança do Estado da China para obter informações sobre a Nvidia, de acordo com o jornal New York Times.
A Megaspeed, empresa da qual ela era executiva e cliente da fabricante de chips, é investigada pelo Departamento de Comércio dos EUA por suspeita de facilitar o envio de semicondutores de inteligência artificial ao mercado chinês.
Vale lembrar que Washington mantém restrições à venda dos modelos de chips mais avançados da Nvidia para empresas chinesas. O governo Trump também passou a exigir autorização para que determinadas companhias tenham acesso aos componentes.
Até o momento, porém, não há confirmação de que dados sigilosos tenham sido compartilhados. A Nvidia diz que não há “motivos para acreditar que segredos de segurança nacional” tenham sido comprometidos.

articles.title: Australia's internet restrictions could go even further, Gmail warns of ban for under-18s
articles.text:
A hot potato: Young people in Australia could soon face another restriction in the name of keeping them safe. Google has warned that the country's proposed Digital Duty of Care legislation could force it to block under-18s from Gmail. Having already banned under-16s from social media, Australia's push to make the internet safer for children could now affect something as ordinary as checking their email.
According to Reuters, YouTube's Australia and New Zealand policy head Rachel Lord raised the concern at a Senate hearing on November 9. She said provisions requiring age checks where children risk encountering pornography could affect email, messaging, and private file storage.
"We are talking about potentially intrusive monitoring within private communications or file storage," Lord said.
The bill has passed the House of Representatives but still needs cross-party backing in the Senate. Google's warning concerns what complying with the rule could require.
Unsurprisingly, Google wasn't the only company objecting to the proposal. Meta, TikTok, and Snap warned that giving regulators this type of broad discretion over harmful content could encourage platforms to remove too much material to avoid penalties.
The government's description of the legislation puts those penalties at up to AU$109.2 million ($75.40 million). Introduced on October 15, the law would require providers to take reasonable steps to keep Australians safe, with additional protections for under-18s.
The proposal also includes tools allowing users to choose whether algorithmically recommended content appears in their feeds. It would give the eSafety commissioner powers to issue removal notices for nudify apps and websites, shorten required responses to cyberbullying and abuse complaints to 24 hours, and set minimum standards for platform complaint processes.
Australia is already fighting over its existing restrictions for teens. It was reported last week that Reddit is challenging the country's under-16 social media ban, calling it "ill thought out" and "inept" while arguing that Reddit isn't a social media platform.
That social media ban for kids took effect on December 10, 2025, making Australia the first country in the world to introduce such a restriction. Reddit says it restricts political expression and argues that its lack of reliance on friend networks differentiates it from platforms such as Facebook.

articles.title: Investidor alertou sobre relação de CEO da Nvidia com suspeita de espionagem meses antes
articles.text:
Seis meses antes de o caso envolvendo Jensen Huang e uma suposta espiã chinesa ganhar repercussão, uma empresa de investimentos de Nova York já havia levantado suspeitas sobre a proximidade entre o CEO da Nvidia e Alice Huang, executiva de uma companhia de Singapura que compra chips da fabricante.
O alerta foi publicado em 13 de maio pela Culper Research, empresa especializada em operações de venda a descoberto (short selling). Na ocasião, a companhia afirmou que a Nvidia tinha problema significativo relacionado à China e questionou a relação entre os dois executivos.
O relatório voltou a circular nesta segunda-feira (9), depois que Huang admitiu ter tido relacionamento extraconjugal com Alice Huang e a Nvidia anunciou investigação formal sobre o caso.
Segundo informações atribuídas a autoridades de inteligência dos Estados Unidos, Alice Huang é suspeita de ter sido recrutada pelo governo chinês para coletar informações sobre o CEO e influenciar sua posição em relação às restrições estadunidenses à exportação de chips avançados de inteligência artificial (IA).
Os dois compartilham o sobrenome, mas não têm parentesco.
Relatório apontou proximidade entre os executivos
- No documento publicado em maio, a Culper Research classificou a relação entre Jensen Huang e Alice Huang como “desconfortavelmente próxima”;
- A empresa afirmou que os dois foram vistos socializando e participando de festas em diversas ocasiões. O relatório também mencionou que alguns funcionários da Nvidia teriam questionado se existia um relacionamento especial entre eles;
- Na época, a investigação da Culper tinha como foco principal as relações comerciais da Megaspeed, empresa de data centers sediada em Singapura, com a Nvidia;
- O relatório levantou a hipótese de que negócios da fabricante estadunidense com a China, prejudicados pelas restrições de exportação dos Estados Unidos, estariam sendo redirecionados por meio de países do Sudeste Asiático;
- A Culper também afirmou que a Megaspeed poderia estar recebendo financiamento indireto do grupo chinês Alibaba por meio de empresas intermediárias.
Leia mais:
- Internet não perdoa CEO da Nvidia após revelação de traição
- Trump diz que CEO da Nvidia não sabia que mulher com quem teve caso seria espiã
- Nvidia e Jensen Huang são processados por caso envolvendo suposta espiã chinesa
Megaspeed teve crescimento expressivo de passivos e patrimônio
Um dos pontos destacados no relatório envolve a evolução financeira da Megaspeed. Segundo registros citados pela Culper, o total de passivos e patrimônio líquido da companhia passou de US$ 33 milhões (cerca de R$ 176 milhões) no fim de 2023 para aproximadamente US$ 3 bilhões (R$ 16 bilhões) no encerramento de 2024. Grande parte desse crescimento estaria relacionada a depósitos reembolsáveis de fonte não identificada.
Nesta segunda-feira, o Financial Times também publicou reportagem afirmando que documentos indicam que a Alibaba emprestou dinheiro à Megaspeed por meio de subsidiárias.
Empresa tinha interesse financeiro na queda da Nvidia
A Culper Research é uma investidora que aposta na desvalorização de ações. Isso significa que a empresa poderia obter ganhos financeiros caso os papéis da Nvidia caíssem após a divulgação de suas acusações.
A própria companhia declarou em maio que estava apostando contra as ações da fabricante de chips.
O TechCrunch ressalta que as alegações sobre um possível desvio ilegal de chips para a China não foram verificadas de forma independente. Portanto, o relatório deve ser tratado como uma investigação conduzida por uma empresa com interesse financeiro na queda da Nvidia, e não como comprovação das suspeitas levantadas.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: CIBC’s security chief on how AI is changing cybersecurity | BetaKit
articles.text:
Joe LoBianco has a fairly expansive definition of what it means to protect a bank.
As Executive Vice-President and Chief Information Security Officer at CIBC, LoBianco’s mandate stretches from the bank’s mission-critical systems and client data to third-party providers plugged into its infrastructure.
It is a significant scope, considering that CIBC serves more than 15 million clients in Canada and around the world. How it manages that already-wide remit continues to evolve as cyber threats become faster-moving and more sophisticated across the industry. Over the past year, AI has accelerated trends that cybersecurity teams were already watching, according to LoBianco.
“We’ve seen an increasing pace and sophistication of threats over time,” LoBianco said. “I would say AI is supercharging those.”
AI is changing the threat landscape
The threat landscape has changed, and so have the weak points that large enterprises need to watch. Historically, security teams could concentrate resources on the weaknesses judged to pose the greatest immediate risk, leaving lower-severity problems further down the remediation queue. LoBianco said AI is making that approach no longer viable.
“AI is particularly adept at chaining these lower-severity issues together into a much more high-risk weakness,” he said.
LoBianco said the industry has so far done a reasonably good job of keeping the most advanced tools out of malicious hands. Still, companies are beginning to see more AI-enabled attacks, giving threat actors greater ability to operate at speed and scale.
How banks are shifting their defences
Like many institutions, CIBC is looking beyond the highest-risk vulnerabilities and addressing lower-severity issues more quickly. The bank is also adjusting where it directs its cybersecurity attention and investment.
“We’ve seen an increasing pace and sophistication of threats over time. I would say AI is supercharging those.”
Joe LoBianco, CIBC
LoBianco pointed to several priorities, including embedding security earlier in the design of new products, increasing automated testing throughout the software development lifecycle, and strengthening how the bank manages risk across third-party providers. CIBC is also using AI to improve its security testing and defences, alongside core security practices such as patching, identity management, and data protection.
The pressure to respond to threats faster is also impacting the role security teams play inside large organizations. “We have to be building our defences to deal with this year’s and next year’s threats,” LoBianco added.
In addition to proactive threat monitoring, LoBianco said CIBC watches attacks and breaches affecting other organizations, examines which controls failed, and then asks how its systems would fare under similar circumstances.
These learnings also get applied to technology solutions that are built in-house.
“Within my team, our job is to figure out how we can help the business manage its risk, so what that means in practice is finding alternatives,” he said.
The bar for vendors is rising
No bank can solve every security problem in-house. Technology vendors enter the picture when banks can benefit from outside expertise, or when building a bespoke solution would make little sense. For high-growth companies hoping to fill those gaps, strong tech alone will not close the deal, according to LoBianco.
A security product might generate useful alerts, for example, but those alerts still have to feed into the systems and workflows a bank already uses to investigate and remediate issues. High-growth companies that understand those integration requirements early, LoBianco said, make adoption much easier for large enterprise customers.
“Do your homework,” LoBianco said. “Understand your customer and how they work.”
In fact, seamless integration often outweighs marginal gains in product performance. “If it’s hard for us to integrate into our security practices, then it doesn’t matter if it’s two percent better than the other solution,” LoBianco added. “Our time to market is going to be impacted.”
Sean Duffy, Managing Director at CIBC Innovation Banking in the UK and Europe, sees the same challenge from the market side. Selling technology into a major financial institution can be a long process, Duffy said, because purchasing decisions involve more stakeholders and considerably more complexity than they might at a smaller organization.
“It can take years to sell some of these solutions,” Duffy said, adding that technology founders need to account for those timelines when thinking about funding and go-to-market strategy.
Duffy said buyers also want to know how a product will evolve with AI, who else is already using it, and—echoing LoBianco—how difficult it will be to integrate. LoBianco said the bar rises considerably when a bank’s data moves to a vendor’s systems. Companies need to prove they can maintain the required level of protection throughout the relationship.
Expectations around vulnerability remediation are accelerating, too. LoBianco feels that the new expectation is for “near real-time turnaround” when weaknesses are discovered in technology running in sensitive environments.
“That’s a very different bar than I think we had in the past, where we could wait days, if not weeks, for fixes from technology founders,” LoBianco said. “Now, it’s going to be a 24-hour-or-less turnaround. We need to have confidence that a provider is going to be able to do that for us today, during the sales cycle, but a few years down the road as well.”
Still, higher expectations have not diminished the role of outside technology founders. For many large enterprises, Duffy said, building software is simply not their core business.
“Companies are born to fill customer needs. And the vast majority focus on needs that are completely unrelated to software development. They have their hands full managing their own mandates; becoming a software development shop on top of that is not realistic and represents a diversion from core business focus.” Duffy added.
LoBianco said trying to develop every product internally at CIBC would not be practical from either a time or cost perspective. Outside technology founders remain an important part of CIBC’s ecosystem, and the bank is looking for a collaborative relationship with them.
“What’s changing is that I’m looking for more co-development, probably, than we used to,” LoBianco said. “We’re looking for design and development partners, as opposed to a series of vendors that I’m just buying shrink-wrapped, off-the-shelf software from.”
LoBianco and Duffy landed on much the same advice for founders: understand your customer, solve a real problem, adapt as the needs of your customers change, and be prepared for multiple go-to-market motions.
“If you have use cases for your product set that can suit other industries or other areas of [financial services], don’t neglect that,” Duffy said. “Don’t disregard that, because if you win a contract with a large bank like CIBC, that’s great, but it can take two, three years to get that.”
The broader point, Duffy said, is that patience should be part of the strategy, rather than a reason to narrow the opportunity.
“Selling into financial institutions and large banks can be challenging,” he added. “So be ready for the journey.”
But the journey is often well worth it. Winning the trust of a financial institution gives a young technology company credibility that carries well beyond a single contract. Banks also invest considerable time and resources into evaluating and integrating new technology, and those relationships tend to last.
CIBC sees its technology providers as long-term partners, rather than vendors it can easily swap out. For those willing to play the long game, the payoff can be years of reliable business. Few sectors offer companies the same combination of customer scale, spending power, and long-term demand.

articles.title: Anthropic joins AI’s natural gas frenzy, buys $3.4B worth of turbines | TechCrunch
articles.text:
AI’s power crunch has become so acute that Anthropic, a company that has generally avoided buying physical infrastructure, is spending $3.4 billion on natural gas turbines.
The AI company, which is planning to go public this year, is buying Caterpillar generators that equipment supplier OnePWR had originally ordered, according to a Financial Times report. The generators are capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts of electricity.
Historically, Anthropic has preferred to rent rather than buy. The company disclosed in its S-1 filing in May that it is paying SpaceX subsidiary xAI $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 to use xAI’s computing power.
“We expect to enter into additional similar services contracts,” Anthropic stated in the filing, meaning more deals to rent computing power.
But as demand for compute ramps up, the market for power has also grown increasingly uncertain, which may have forced its hand. The backlog for natural gas turbines stretches into the early 2030s, and queues to connect to the electrical grid can be just as long.
Anthropic’s purchase looks like a last resort.
According to the report, OnePWR ordered the turbines a couple years ago but couldn’t find financing to complete the purchase. Anthropic had planned to buy them from OnePWR but instead went directly to Caterpillar, the manufacturer.
It’s not clear why OnePWR was unable to secure financing despite Anthropic’s apparent interest as a customer. Whatever the case, Anthropic likely wanted to keep the generating capacity to itself rather than give a competitor an opportunity to snap it up.
AI companies have been ramping up their purchases of natural gas equipment and supplies in recent years. Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta have all announced plans to build massive natural gas power plants to power their data centers on-site, rather than drawing from the public grid.
The binge has given a second wind to fracking, the drilling method used to extract natural gas from underground rock. And if the buildout proceeds as planned, U.S. data centers alone could consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined by 2035. The reliance on natural gas also exposes hyperscalers to price fluctuations. One analyst expects that prices could more than triple by the end of the decade in some markets. If that happens, Anthropic might have a serious case of buyer’s remorse.

articles.title: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
articles.text:
Anthropic is announcing two new models today: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it says are designed to take on “daunting” technical challenges. The company claims the new models show improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision, and can generate outputs faster than the 5.1 versions of the Fable and Mythos models.
Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
Claude Fable 5.2 is designed to take on big technical challenges, and it’s available today.
Claude Fable 5.2 is good at challenging software engineering problems, Anthropic says, and can orchestrate agent teams and tackle long-running projects. The new model has also solved some complex scientific problems, including two open theoretical physics problems.
During prerelease testing, the two models have “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours,” Anthropic says.
Claude Fable 5.2 is launching today. As for Claude Mythos 5.2, only vetted organizations will have access to start. The new 5.2 models follow the release of Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 in September.

LPDDR6 becomes an essential ingredient as intelligence moves into autonomous and mobile edge systems.
								November 9th, 2026 - 
								By: Ed Sperling
								
							
Humanoid robots, autonomous vehicles, and drones all share one thing in common — they can only function as long as the battery lasts. After that, they need to return to a charger. Today, in the case of humanoid robots, usefulness may only last a few hours per charge. So how can that time be extended? There’s no simple answer because no single component will solve all problems, but the underlying basics remain the same — efficient processing, denser and faster memory, and optimized data movement between processors and memories. Frank Ferro, group director for product management at Cadence, explains why data hierarchies are so critical for physical AI, what can be done on the memory side to speed up read/write times, and how to maximize performance while keeping costs down.
