articles.title: DeepX Tapes Out Chip With Claimed 6.7× Gain - EE Times
articles.text:
South Korean edge AI chip startup DeepX has taped out its second-generation AI accelerator with access to custom processor-in-memory (PIM) technology from Samsung. The DX-M2 is designed to bring generative AI to robots, drones, and other edge devices, enabling inference of models with up to 100 billion parameters at less than 5 W.
DeepX’s first-generation chip, the DX-M1, is now in mass production, targeting vision applications. The newly taped-out DX-M2 aims to make local AI a practical choice for devices with tight power and thermal budgets. The chip is designed to run models with 20 billion to 100 billion parameters (approximately 3 billion to 20 billion active parameters) at 10 to 30 tokens per second, depending on the model. This is achieved within the same power budget as the M1—just 5 W.
“The most important change [between M1 and M2] is the memory bandwidth,” DeepX founder and CEO Lokwon Kim told EE Times.
Memory bandwidth has tripled from 50 to 150 GB/s, but there are several other efficiencies. DeepX said its NPU has doubled its power efficiency thanks to design improvements, and moving to a 2-nm process node doubled it again. 80 TOPS can now be achieved.
“This is important because with 5 W power consumption we can go everywhere, drones or any other battery-powered device,” Kim said. “Our goal is to enable deployment of sophisticated AI in all devices.”
The M2 can handle large mixture-of-experts LLMs and supports new techniques, including speculative decoding and TurboQuant.
Processor-in-memory
Most types of AI inference operations are constrained by moving weights between memory and compute, especially GEMV (general matrix-vector multiplication), during which random memory accesses are required, slowing down computation. Memory makers have come up with PIM schemes in which memory-bound operations such as GEMV can be computed inside the memory chip. Doing operations within memory increases the effective memory bandwidth and reduces time-consuming memory access times.
PIM is set to become a JEDEC standard for LPDDR6. However, DeepX has been working with Samsung on integrating the DX-M2 with Samsung’s LPDDR5x-PIM.
“We have spent one and a half years on this technology, collaborating with Samsung Memory, as they already have their custom PIM for LPDDR5x,” Kim said. “We already received LPDDR5x PIM samples and we are testing the operations and performance in-house.”
DeepX’s simulations show that offloading GEMV operations from the DX-M2 into LPDDR5x-PIM will result in 6.7× the tokens per second for Llama3.1-8B versus the DX-M2 alone.
“DX-M2 with LPDDR5x-PIM is close to optimal,” Kim said. “But our next generation, the DX-M3, will support official LPDDR6 PIM technology; then we can get the full theoretical performance advancement, which is 5× to 8× higher performance.”
The only drawback, Kim explained, is that the extra compute doesn’t come for free—6.7× the performance needs 2.7× the power consumption overall. That said, DeepX thinks it can get a 2× performance uplift within the same power envelope as non-PIM operation.
“Substantial manual effort” is required in the compiler to support this mode of operation, Kim said, noting DeepX currently has a prototype compiler running, based on a simulation of the PIM-enabled LPDDR5x. “We are now making the hardware modules so that we can test that in the physical environment, so we couldn’t finish the compiler yet, but we are actively working on it.”
Key markets
The DX-M2 will target several key sectors. DeepX is working with Taiwanese OEMs to find the right sweet spot for AI PCs, including laptops and workstations. Robotics companies, currently prototyping on GPUs such as Nvidia Thor, want lower power and more compute on-device, and automotive companies are looking for a low-power chip that can run agents in-vehicle, Tim Park, director of strategic marketing at DeepX, told EE Times. For IoT devices, DeepX is already working with Samsung on a next-generation smart hub. The company is also joining the AWS IoT ecosystem so it can use Greengrass to support remote model updates.
Robotics customers typically begin development on GPUs but have to look for alternatives due to thermal and power consumption considerations, Park said. DeepX is working hard to enable transitions from the Nvidia Isaac robotics platform to its in-house equivalent, Newton.
“Robotics customers ask us about our hardware, but also about how they can migrate from Nvidia to DeepX,” he said. “This is the answer—customers change their APIs to call Newton instead of Isaac and then they can run the exact same pipeline on the DeepX system.”
DeepX has 17 compatible libraries up and running, Park said. The company has demonstrated M1-based robots using the same source code as an Nvidia Jetson-based robot, but calling the DeepX libraries.
“The actual outcome for the customer is they can enjoy 20 times longer battery life and [lower cost] when they switch from Nvidia to DeepX,” Kim said. “At the same time, the switching time can be under a second. They just need to change the API name from Isaac to Newton. That’s it.”
A full robotics stack for DeepX hardware is currently under development.
DeepX is engaging with robotics customers in the U.S., China, Vietnam, and Korea, while Hyundai Motor Group Robotics Lab is already using the DX-M1 in its robotics platform.
Meanwhile, the company is building out its ecosystem, adding Taiwanese OEMs, vertical champions in various markets and, lately, a collaboration with Intel.
DeepX is working with Intel to integrate OpenVINO with the DeepX SDK in order to tap into Intel’s x86 customer base. The DX-M1 can complement integrated NPUs in Intel Core Ultra CPUs and enable AI for other Intel edge CPUs that don’t have an NPU, offloading some or all of the AI workload.
The company recently met with AMD to discuss jointly developing a robotics platform based on DeepX accelerators combined with AMD’s Kria reference board, in particular for the Korean ecosystem, Kim said. This is part of DeepX’s drive to collaborate with other heterogeneous ecosystems, including Raspberry Pi and Baidu’s PaddlePaddle ecosystem.
Commercial traction
DeepX has more than 100 purchase orders for the DX-M1 so far, from all major global markets across all physical AI industries (including drones, robots, smart factory, surveillance camera, aerospace and defense, healthcare, and IoT), Kim said. The M1 is now in mass production.
The most active market for physical AI was previously China, Kim said, but Japan has emerged this year as a major market, with a strong willingness to pioneer humanoid robots.
“All the large Japanese companies are evaluating our chips, more than 10 leading companies in Japan right now, and their feedback is very encouraging,” he said. “At the same time, the U.S. market [is strong]; we have several big names there, and their feedback is really good.”
DeepX is also engaged in smart city projects in South Korea, Vietnam, and Singapore.
“Our long-term view is that AI compute will become more distributed as efficiency improves,” Park said. “The PC and smartphone eras showed how computing can spread into many products. AI will follow its own path, but local inference has clear value when an application needs immediate access to sensor data or operation without continuous connectivity.”
DeepX considers edge AI to be a substantial opportunity for its chips, Park said, especially at a time when the amount of power available for new data centers is limited.
Kim’s belief is that just as only a quarter of the CPU market is in the data center today, the AI processor market will also shift to the edge in the next five to 10 years.
At a time when many AI data center projects are delayed, the AI capacity issue can’t be solved with investment alone, he added. AI chips that consume just 5 W can enable migration of AI to the device.
“If we deploy models up to 100 billion parameters in devices, we can reduce AI data center traffic by more than 80%,” Kim said. “That means we could have five times larger infrastructure without adding any AI servers. This is our vision.”
On the roadmap for DeepX’s third generation is the DX-M3, coming in 2028. The M3 will be chiplet-based and will target 1 ePOPS (INT8) using LPDDR6-PIM. The main target markets for this are automotive OEMs and humanoid robotics companies, whose demands will require multi-chiplet designs.
In the meantime, samples of the M2 are expected in March 2027, with mass production targeted for fall 2027.

articles.title: El Gobierno se plantea paralizar los servicios de TikTok en España por permitir abuso sexual infantil
articles.text:
El Gobierno se plantea paralizar los servicios de TikTok en España por permitir abuso sexual infantil
La ministra de Juventud e Infancia, Sira Rego, pide a la Fiscalía la apertura de una investigación contra la red social por dejar que pederastas usen abiertamente su plataforma
La ministra de Juventud e Infancia, Sira Rego, ha anunciado este lunes que su ministerio ha solicitado a Fiscalía que abra una investigación contra TikTok por permitir en su plataforma miles de vídeos de abuso sexual infantil y la comunicación entre pederastas.
El ministerio se plantea también la posibilidad de paralizar los servicios de la plataforma en España. La decisión de la ministra ha sido provocada por una investigación española que ha documentado vídeos, directos y mensajes en TikTok que prueban que la red social permite abuso sexual infantil sin apenas control. Maldita.es, la organización autora del trabajo y que ha estado 35 días reuniendo evidencias, también ha denunciado a TikTok ante la Fiscalía.
En su escrito para la Fiscalía, el Gobierno traslada la información conocida para que adopte las medidas necesarias para garantizar la protección integral de los niños, niñas y adolescentes que puedan estar afectados. Según fuentes del ministerio, “los hechos documentados por Maldita.es son de extrema gravedad y requieren una respuesta inmediata y coordinada de todas las administraciones competentes, tanto en el ámbito nacional como en el europeo. Además, ponen de relieve graves deficiencias en los mecanismos de detección y moderación de contenidos, así como en el papel de los sistemas de recomendación de TikTok en su difusión”.
La ministra Rego ha pedido también una reunión urgente con los representantes de la red social en España para conocer sus explicaciones y las medidas y actuaciones previstas.
Maldita.es ha encontrado en TikTok 1.183 vídeos de abuso sexual infantil explícito con 48 millones de visualizaciones y más de 26.000 perfiles de potenciales pederastas que comentan y comparten ese material. “No se puede ni comparar a TikTok con el resto de plataformas en lo que abuso sexual infantil se refiere”, dice Clara Jiménez Cruz, directora de la organización española de lucha contra la desinformación Maldita.es, que ha hecho la investigación. TikTok ha eliminado algunos de esos vídeos, pero la mayoría de las cuentas que los cuelgan siguen activas.
Gracias a un caso judicial en Estados Unidos, en 2022 surgieron informes internos de TikTok, red social de vídeos cortos de origen chino, donde admitían que tenían un problema de pedofilia en la plataforma. Maldita.es ya había publicado dos investigaciones anteriores sobre explotación sexual infantil en TikTok. Esta vez llaman a la red social el “hogar del pederasta”. Han denunciado una muestra de 50 vídeos de abuso sexual infantil por el canal que ofrece TikTok y la compañía solo ha retirado cinco de ellos, un 10%, y bloqueó otros 13 solo en España. Tres días después de la denuncia, el 40% de las cuentas que publicaron esos vídeos seguían activas.
Maldita.es ha contactado con TikTok, que se ha limitado a pedir más información sin responder a consultas sobre sus mecanismos de protección de menores, los fallos detectados y el contenido ilegal en su plataforma.

articles.title: The Optical Superhighway For AI
articles.text:
Exponentially increasing AI compute performance requires exponential interconnect speeds.
There is much disagreement on the timing of the transition from copper interconnects to optical interconnects, but almost everyone agrees we are moving to all-optical interconnects over the next five years.
Optical interconnects already dominate scale-out. Optical interconnects will next move into scale-up by connecting racks in very large pods of hundreds to thousands of XPUs (AI compute units), then optical scale-up will replace copper within the rack.
Today, optical is dominated by pluggable transceivers mostly using single wavelengths (DR) with 2 or 4 fibers. Increasing performance using pluggables would require power-hungry, higher-speed PHYs (physical layer interfaces) and/or more fibers, which will drive up costs because connectors cost more than fibers.
To reduce power and cost while increasing bandwidth, the industry consensus is shifting toward multi-wavelengths per fiber with bidirectionality, using NPO (near-packaged optics), then CPO (co-packaged optics). Alternatives may develop, but the emerging consensus for the future of optical interconnect appears to be OCI-MSA.
OCI-MSA (Optical Compute Interconnect Multi-Source Agreement) is an industry consortium recently formed for an open, interoperable optical interconnect spec for AI scale-up. Founding members include AMD, Broadcom, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and OpenAI. In that mix are both GPU giants, the largest maker of custom AI compute, two of the hyperscalers, and one of the two Frontier Model companies. This is a big bandwagon. Of these, AMD, Broadcom, Meta, and Microsoft have made presentations on their plans for OCI-MSA at recent industry conferences.
The stated objectives for the OCI-MSA are:
Drew Alduino (Meta’s director of optical infrastructure), Near Margalit (VP & GM of Broadcom’s Optical Systems Division) & Matthew Streshinsky (AMD senior director for photonics) were on a panel in September at the AI Infra Summit. “We want AMD GPUs talking to Broadcom switches,” Alduino said. “We want all of our compute and switches to be interoperable.”
Alduino went on to say:
As Near Margalit noted, what matters for interoperability is what appears on the fiber.
The spec for Gen 1 of OCI-MSA can be found at oci-msa.org.
OCI is workable for pluggables, NPO, CPO in the package, or CPO on the interposer.
Fig. 1: OCI-MSA Gen 1 has 8 channels per fiber, 4 in each direction. Source: oci-msa.org
The OCI-MSA spec is 24 pages. The Optical specification provides for 8 wavelengths per fiber, with 4 in each direction. Each wavelength is 53.125Gbps NRZ. The wavelengths in the groups are spaced slightly more than 2nm apart. The reference optical fiber link model is based on 500m SMF-28 fiber with 2.5 dB total insertion loss, mainly driven by the connector losses in the link between transceivers. (The effective data rate is 50Gbps per wavelength after error correction and miscellaneous signaling.)
At OCP (Open Compute Project) in October, Rajiv Pancholy, director of hyperscale strategy & products for Broadcom, talked about how OCI-MSA compares at equal bandwidths to alternatives. (See figure 2, below)
Fig. 2: Comparison of OCI power/reach versus alternatives. Source: Broadcom @ OCP
As the table above shows, for a 200G aggregate bandwidth (one direction), OCI in CPO format is the best combination of low link power per bit and long reach. OCI has the reach of pluggables at 1/3 the power of a pluggable transceiver. And OCI has a scalable bandwidth roadmap.
At PECC (Photonic Enabled Cloud Computing) 2026 in October, AMD explained that there are numerous ways to increase OCI bandwidth for future generations:
The combination of all of these gives a scaling up of over 100×. If OCI doubles every 1 to 2 years, this gives decades of scalable runway. This is just the bandwidth per fiber. The number of fibers can increase, as well.
Fig. 3: OCI has numerous ways to continue to scale bandwidth. Source: AMD
Microsoft at PECC also discussed its plans for OCI and the need for a common standard.
Fig. 4: Microsoft will use OCI in CPO+NPO, then just CPO. Source: Microsoft
Microsoft’s first wave of scale-up optical will use CPO on the switch and NPO with the accelerator. In the second wave, both ends will use CPO in scale-up.
So far, OCI-MSA is the only optical scale-up standard published and frequently discussed at multiple conferences (AI Infra/OCP/PECC) by multiple champions (AMD/Broadcom/Meta/Microsoft).
It seems likely that in 2027, we will see the first fully functional OCI Gen 1 implementations and perhaps interoperability demos between suppliers. If a “bandwagon” forms and multiple suppliers exist, OCI can become the Ethernet of optical interconnects, as Drew Alduino envisioned at AI Infra Summit.
Other standards could develop, or some players might choose to do a proprietary optical interconnect. But as of today, OCI-MSA is the frontrunner for the optical super highway for AI scale-up.

articles.title: "On est allés trop loin” : Mercedes reconnaît que ses voitures ont perdu trop de boutons et veut faire marche arrière
articles.text:
"On est allés trop loin” : Mercedes reconnaît que ses voitures ont perdu trop de boutons et veut faire marche arrière
Les boutons reprennent du service
C'est donc officiel : Ola Källenius, PDG de Mercedes-Benz, admet que la suppression des boutons physiques au profit des dalles tactiles géantes était une erreur. Le constructeur promet d'en réintroduire dans ses prochains modèles.
*Cet article a été initialement publié en août 2026. Nous le republions aujourd'hui car le débat autour du "tout tactile" dans les habitacles et le retour salutaire aux commandes physiques restent des sujets de discussion brûlants (et souvent sources de frustration !) au sein de nos lecteurs.
*
Régler la climatisation à 22 °C, monter le volume d'un cran, basculer les essuie-glaces en intermittent : des gestes autrefois mécaniques, accomplis sans quitter la route des yeux. Mais depuis quelques années, il faut pour cela naviguer dans des sous-menus enfouis derrière un écran. Dans une interview accordée au magazine britannique Autocar, paru le 31 juillet 2026, le PDG de Mercedes-Benz a reconnu publiquement que cette course au tout-numérique avait dépassé les bornes.
	
Parfois, on se laisse emporter et l’on développe de la technologie pour la technologie, en oubliant quelque peu le client. Dans certains domaines, on est allés trop loin. Désormais, vous nous verrez réintroduire les boutons les plus pertinents.
Mercedes fait marche arrière : quels boutons reviennent dans ses voitures ?
Le virage est déjà amorcé, puisque sur la nouvelle CLA, Mercedes a remplacé le curseur capacitif du volant par une vraie molette de volume, physique et crantée. Le GLC With EQ Technology et le CLA Shooting Brake héritent du même volant repensé, avec des commandes tangibles en lieu et place des surfaces tactiles. Källenius promet que d'autres contrôles "sensés" suivront, sans pour autant renoncer à l'Hyperscreen MBUX, cette dalle tri-écran de 142 cm qui tapisse le tableau de bord d'un montant A à l'autre. Les grands affichages restent. Ce sont les commandes critiques qui retrouvent une existence physique.
Volkswagen a déjà réintroduit des boutons physiques sur le volant de la Golf Mk8.5 après les critiques visant ses commandes tactiles. Hyundai a remis des boutons et molettes dans le Tucson restylé, tandis que Ferrari a annoncé le retour de commandes physiques sur ses futurs modèles après les plaintes de ses clients. Porsche adopte une approche hybride, en conservant des commandes tactiles tout en réintroduisant certains contrôles physiques.
Pourquoi l'Europe et la Chine imposent le retour des boutons en voiture
La pression réglementaire accélère le mouvement car depuis janvier 2026, Euro NCAP pénalise les voitures dépourvues de commandes physiques pour les fonctions critiques : clignotants, feux de détresse, essuie-glaces, klaxon, appel d'urgence. Sans ces contrôles, impossible de décrocher les cinq étoiles. Or, selon Euro NCAP, environ 90 % des acheteurs européens consultent cette note avant de signer un bon de commande. La Chine prépare un cadre similaire via le ministère de l'Industrie (MIIT), applicable à tous les véhicules neufs produits après juillet 2027.
	
Les nouvelles évaluations de l’interface homme-machine examineront notamment la disposition, la clarté et la facilité d’utilisation des commandes essentielles, y compris la présence de boutons physiques pour les fonctions couramment utilisées, dont les retours des consommateurs montrent qu’ils peuvent réduire la distraction.
La Tesla Model S, lancée en 2012, a popularisé l’idée d’un habitacle piloté par un grand écran central. Depuis, de nombreux constructeurs ont suivi cette voie, parfois jusqu’à enfouir des fonctions essentielles dans des menus numériques. Mercedes redécouvre aujourd’hui une règle très simple : certaines commandes doivent rester accessibles immédiatement, sans détourner le regard de la route.

articles.title: Google TPU 8tx Pairs AMD EPYC Turin Hosts with Confidential Computing while TPU 8i Max Doubles Memory Bandwidth
articles.text:
Google is expanding its eighth-generation TPU portfolio with two new offerings, the TPU 8tx and the TPU 8i Max. This marks the first time Google has introduced four distinct system configurations in a single year, though it is not four new chip designs. The 8tx builds on existing silicon for confidential computing, marking a notable win for AMD, while the 8i Max combines two 8i chips into one package to tackle massive context windows.
Google TPU 8x
When we covered the TPU v8s at Hot Chips 2026, we highlighted how Google specialized networking for different workloads. The inference-focused TPU 8i uses a Boardfly topology with a maximum network-hop diameter of seven, compared to sixteen hops in the training-oriented torus design. This structural difference reduces latency for real-time reasoning, helping explain why Google continues to tailor interconnects rather than rely on a single fabric.
The TPU 8tx is the third system in the generation and targets regulated enterprises and governments running frontier or proprietary models alongside sensitive data. It uses the same silicon as the training-focused TPU 8t, but Google has paired it with custom 5th Gen AMD EPYC “Turin” hosts to build security directly into the hardware layer. Normally, data is encrypted at rest and in transit but must be unlocked in memory while a computer processes it. The 8tx keeps that active data protected through confidential computing, which encrypts data in use inside an isolated trusted execution environment.
Here is Google’s rendering of the TPU 8tx board. The illustration shows four accelerator chips with heat sinks and connector ports along one edge, giving a sense of the tray layout that pairs these accelerators with their Turin host CPUs.
For the 8tx host CPU, Google selected 5th Gen AMD EPYC Turin to match the TPU 8t’s PCIe Gen5 x16 interface. A dual-socket Turin configuration provides 128 Gen5 lanes, ensuring zero I/O oversubscription across four TPUs and high-speed NICs. Google noted that a Gen6 host like AMD EPYC Venice (stay tuned for more on that) would step down to Gen5 speeds without adding accelerator bandwidth, aligning with their 2027 hardware qualification schedule.
The 8tx also adopts the Boardfly network from the inference-oriented TPU 8i rather than the training-optimized torus. That topology reduces the maximum hops between chips, which matters for multi-step agents that make many sequential inference calls. Google claims up to 2x lower latency than TPU 8t with a near-zero performance penalty.
Google TPU 8i Max Packs Two Chips and More Memory
The fourth system, TPU 8i Max, attacks the memory wall from a different angle. When many agents work across an entire codebase or hours of video simultaneously, memory bandwidth becomes the bottleneck before compute does. Google combined two low-latency TPU 8i chips into a single multi-chip package.
That gives the 8i Max double the compute, double the SRAM, and double the HBM bandwidth of a single TPU 8i. Specifically, it offers 384 GB of high-bandwidth memory, about a third more than the TPU 8i, while HBM bandwidth doubles to 17.2TB/s and on-chip SRAM doubles to 768 MB. The TPU 8i Max doubles HBM bandwidth to 17.2 TB/s and on-chip SRAM to 768 MB, directly addressing the memory wall that bottlenecks large-context agentic workloads.
We asked and Google told us that if data must remain within the confidential computing domain, users should stick with TPU 8tx for inference and serving. This system retains the same low-latency Boardfly topology optimized for real-time tasks.
Final Words
Probably the key message here is that Google is tailoring its TPU offerings for different parts of the AI stack, and really even different customers. The TPU 8tx seems to be more of a customized product for confidential computing, while the TPU 8i Max is designed for inference. For AMD, this is probably not going to drive a 10% server CPU market share gain overnight. Instead, it is a big win because AMD is notching both a win for EPYC in a non-AMD accelerator system, and it is showing its confidential computing chops by winning a socket at a major hyperscaler.

articles.title: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum
articles.text:
Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX.
Ryu Je-myung, vice minister of science and ICT, joined NVIDIA leaders to meet with over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI semiconductors.
NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2, with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD and Upstage.
Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure.
Motif Technologies, a Seoul-based AI lab, develops foundation models for building AI agents that carry out complex tasks, including Motif-3, a large language model released with open weights.
RLWRLD, a physical AI startup based in San Francisco, Seoul and Tokyo, develops robotics foundation models that enable humanoid and industrial robots to perform complex real-world tasks that require five-finger dexterity, such as precisely inserting components, threading nuts onto bolts and kitting parts from moving conveyors.
Upstage, a Korean enterprise AI company, develops Solar language models and document AI tools that help businesses extract information from complex documents, streamline workflows and build AI applications for everyday operations.
The companies represent work across the full AI stack, from infrastructure to models to robotics applications.
The planned investments build on NVIDIA’s work with Korea’s startup and venture community, including more than 1,000 Korea-based members of NVIDIA Inception, a program that helps startups grow with access to preferred pricing, technical expertise and opportunities for investor introductions.

articles.title: Hackers Exploiting ‘SSHole’ Authentication Bypass in OpenSSH
articles.text:
Threat actors have started exploiting SSHole, a recently patched high-severity authentication bypass vulnerability in OpenSSH.
Tracked as CVE-2026-123158, the flaw is “related to misinterpretation of whether a string is intended to be a password hash” and could let attackers access certain accounts by supplying any password between 257 and 1024 characters.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to access accounts such as root, which should never accept a password.
On certain Linux distributions that use the musl libc implementation with the Pluggable Authentication Module (PAM) disabled, such as Alpine, Buildroot, OpenWrt, Yocto, and others, these accounts do accept a password.
This happens because the OpenSSH server (sshd) checks the supplied password by hashing it against a stored password hash associated with the username.
When an account has no password hash, as with root on Alpine (where the field is ‘*’), sshd borrows the salt from another account’s hash to process the login attempt. For passwords longer than 256 bytes, musl’s crypt() function fails and, instead of returning NULL, returns ‘*’. Because that matches the ‘*’ stored for the target account, sshd treats the password as correct.
In Alpine, affected accounts include root, any key-only user created with adduser without a password, the Alpine user in the official tiny-cloud images, and any user coming from a directory service through musl-nscd.
Last week, OpenSSH rushed patches for the bug, and Alpine urged users to apply them and restart sshd as soon as possible.
Over the weekend, both WatchTowr and Previdian warned that hackers had started exploiting SSHole in the wild. According to WatchTowr, only botnets and crypto miners have picked it up so far.
“Previdian sensors have observed 20 exploitation attempts, 13 unique attacker IPs, and 9 countries targeting CVE-2026-123158. First observed Nov 06, 2026; last observed Nov 08, 2026,” Previdian said.
Exploitation attempts have also been reported by GreyNoise and Defused.
Users are advised to update to OpenSSH version 10.6p2 as soon as possible. As a mitigation, they can disable password authentication (on by default in OpenSSH) or disable SSH. They should also check logs for unusual requests to identify exploitation attempts.

articles.title: Lentejas de Canadá y alubias argentinas: la realidad detrás de platos tradicionales como las fabes asturianas
articles.text:
Un buen cocido madrileño, un potaje de vigilia, una fabada asturiana o un plato de judiones de La Granja. Todo suena tradicional y muy típico de la gastronomía patria, pero la realidad es que gran parte de las legumbres que usamos en algunos de nuestros potajes más emblemáticos tienen poco que ver con el campo español: llegan de cientos (o incluso miles) de kilómetros de distancia, de plantaciones de Norteamérica u otras zonas de Europa. De hecho, cuando hablamos de ciertas legumbres lo más fácil es encontrarse con género extranjero, no autóctono.
La razón es muy sencilla: costes.
¿Te gustan las legumbres? Si la respuesta es sí y sueles preparar en casa (o comer en el bar) potajes y cocidos es probable que tu dieta sea más internacional de lo que piensas. Aunque las leguminosas son un ingrediente esencial de algunos de los platos más tradicionales de la cocina española, la realidad, en el siglo XXI, es que gran parte de las que se comercializan llegan del extranjero.
Lo reconoce el propio Ministerio de Agricultura y Alimentación, que explica que “tanto España como la UE son importadoras netas de leguminosas grano”. Se cultivan. Se exportan. Pero sobre todo se importan de otros países.
¿Qué dicen las cifras? Que si hablamos de legumbres y balanza comercial debemos utilizar el signo negativo. Así lo muestra la plataforma de análisis COTEC, que registró en 2025 exportaciones por valor de 67,5 millones de euros y un flujo de importaciones valorado en 174 millones. La ‘foto’ de OEC es algo distinta, pero la lectura se repite: la balanza comercial global es negativa, con más mercancía entrando que saliendo, al menos en términos de valor.
En su último informe sobre leguminosas en grano, correspondiente a la campaña 2025-2026, el Ministerio de Agricultura muestra que se importan muchos más guisantes, habas, lentejas, garbanzos y judías de las que se exportan. De hecho, y más allá de la balanza comercial, hay casos en los que el volumen de importación supera con creces la producción y resulta clave para cubrir el consumo interno.
¿Hay más datos? Sí. Una fuente valiosa es Mercados Centrales de Abastecimiento (Mercasa), que ha publicado un informe en el que analiza cuestiones como la evolución de la demanda en España, la producción nacional o el enorme peso que tiene en el mercado doméstico la mercancía extranjera. Sus estadísticas se basan en datos de 2024, pero aún así resultan elocuentes.
Como recordaba hace poco El Confidencial, las tablas de Mercasa sugieren que el 74% de las alubias o judías secas, el 64% de las lentejas y el 38% de los garbanzos que llegan a nuestras mesas se cultivan en otras naciones. En general, alrededor de dos tercios de las legumbres que consumimos son importadas.
¿De dónde vienen? En ocasiones, de plantaciones situadas a miles de kilómetros. Según Agricultura, Canadá y EEUU son la principal fuente de lentejas importadas. Si hablamos de garbanzos la referencia es EEUU y México y en el caso de las judías secas, Argentina. Rusia ha sido tradicionalmente el origen de los guisantes secos, Reino Unido de las habas secas y Australia del altramuz.
Hay casos en los que el peso de las importaciones es aplastante: algunos analistas advierten desde hace años que la mayoría de lentejas que consumimos (en 2018 se habla de entre el 65% y 80%) vienen de fuera, sobre todo de Norteamérica.
Garbanzos ‘made in USA’. Esa diversidad de orígenes la constataba hace unos años la OCU en un análisis en el que reveló, por ejemplo, que el 71% de los garbanzos importados llegan de EEUU y el 15% procede de México. En el balance de las importaciones de lentejas destaca Canadá, con el 58% de los envíos, y en el de las alubias Argentina, con el 74% de la mercancía foránea. Canadá y Polonia aportan otro 14% y el resto desembarca desde EEUU, Austria, Perú y Turquía.
“A pesar de que en España tenemos una gran tradición de cultivo de legumbres de buena calidad, la mayoría de las que consumimos son de importación”.
Y eso, ¿por qué? Básicamente, por costes. “España es el mayor productor y consumidor de legumbres de la UE, pero aun así no somos capaces de producir de una forma económica ni siquiera para satisfacer la demanda interna”, explica a El Confidencial Diego Rubiales, de la Asociación Española de Leguminosas.
Una idea similar transmite Nicolás Armentero, de la Asociación Legumbres de Calidad: pese a la huella de carbono que implica mover la mercancía, “en un mundo interconectado el coste real de traer 40 contenedores en un barco que ha hecho 7.000 km es muy inferior al de cultivar esas legumbres aquí en España”.
¿Consumimos muchas legumbres? Consumimos algo más que en los últimos años, aunque menos que hace unas décadas. Según las estadísticas de Agricultura, en 2025 la ingesta media per cápita (persona y año) en los hogares fue de 3,47 kilos, por encima de los 3,36 del año anterior o 3,06 de 2015.
Si echamos la vista más atrás, hay fuentes que aseguran que el consumo en la década de los 60 era muy superior. En cuanto a las explotaciones, la superficie media cultivada de leguminosas grano en España ronda las 400.000 hectáreas, casi un tercio dedicadas a guisantes secos. El resto se lo reparten vezas, yeros, garbanzos, habas, judías, altramuces y lentejas, que acaparan el 10%.
A la hora de competir, el producto español dispone de sus propios recursos, como apostar por la calidad frente a los precios (la brecha entre lo que cuestan las fabes asturianas y las alubias polacas es considerable) y distinguirse claramente en los comercios. Para ello cuenta con sellos oficiales que acreditan su origen.

articles.title: Plafonné depuis 2016, le Bluetooth va presque quadrupler ses débits en 2027
articles.text:
Le Bluetooth SIG, consortium de plus de 43 000 entreprises qui pilote la norme, a officialisé le 4 novembre le Bluetooth High Data Throughput, ou HDT. Cette fonction optionnelle de la nouvelle spécification Bluetooth Core 7.0 porte le débit maximal du Bluetooth basse consommation à 7,5 Mbit/s. Ce plafond était resté fixé à 2 Mbit/s depuis Bluetooth 5, présenté fin 2016, qui avait déjà doublé la vitesse de cette déclinaison économe en énergie.
Jusqu’à 7,5 Mbit/s, avec l’audio sans perte en ligne de mire
Pour y parvenir, HDT introduit une nouvelle couche physique, la partie de la norme qui décide comment les bits voyagent sur l’onde radio. Des modulations plus denses font transporter davantage de données à chaque signal. Le débit s’ajuste paquet par paquet entre cinq paliers, de 2 à 7,5 Mbit/s, et un paquet peut dépasser 8 000 octets. Les données perdues sont renvoyées par blocs, avec un mécanisme de correction d’erreurs. Le code qui vérifie l’intégrité des données grimpe par ailleurs de 32 à 64 ou 128 bits.
Les meilleurs écouteurs sans fil en 2026
Le premier usage visé est l’audio haut de gamme, attendu en 2027 : son sans perte et haute résolution, multicanal et spatial. À titre de comparaison, un CD audio débite environ 1,41 Mbit/s, et le SBC, qui transporte la musique en Bluetooth classique, plafonne à 328 kbit/s. HDT pourrait ainsi transporter nativement un son haute résolution et sans perte, là où il faut aujourd’hui passer par des codecs propriétaires comme LDAC ou aptX.
HDT vise aussi les montres, les appareils de santé et de sport, la maison connectée, la réalité étendue et les appareils dotés d’IA. Une montre pourrait synchroniser ses données d’entraînement en quelques secondes, et le transfert d’un fichier de plusieurs mégaoctets passerait d’environ 16 à 4 secondes. Des lunettes connectées pourraient déléguer le traitement de leurs données à un autre appareil, et les mises à jour de micrologiciel se feraient presque sans interruption.
Vos écouteurs actuels resteront à 2 Mbit/s
HDT modifie le matériel radio lui-même, et aucune mise à jour logicielle ne pourra l’ajouter à un appareil existant. Le téléphone comme les écouteurs devront embarquer une puce compatible, faute de quoi la liaison ne pourra pas en profiter. La fonction étant optionnelle dans la norme, rien n’oblige d’ailleurs les fabricants à l’adopter sur tous leurs modèles. La plupart des écouteurs diffusent encore la musique en Bluetooth classique, dont le débit utile tourne autour de 2,1 Mbit/s. L’audio en basse consommation, sur lequel repose HDT, ne se répand que depuis 2024.
Une version préliminaire de la norme circulait depuis un an parmi les fabricants. Côté puces, Realtek a présenté avec Rohde & Schwarz un premier banc de test HDT dès mars 2026 et prévoit des composants compatibles. Qualcomm annonce la prise en charge sur sa puce FastConnect 8800, et Nordic Semiconductor se positionne aussi. Les premières puces et les premiers écouteurs pourraient être montrés au CES, en janvier 2027. Avec plus de 5 milliards de produits Bluetooth livrés chaque année par les membres du SIG, anciens et nouveaux appareils risquent de cohabiter longtemps.
Pour les mélomanes, rien ne change donc sur les écouteurs actuels. L’audio sans perte en Bluetooth, réservé à des codecs propriétaires comme l’aptX Lossless annoncé par Qualcomm en 2021, attendra 2027 pour devenir standard, et il faudra renouveler le téléphone en même temps que le casque.

articles.title: Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus review - effortless and effective chemical-free cleaning - Tech Guide
articles.text:
- RATING
The Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus is built for the modern home and offers chemical-free cleaning that’s effortless and effective.
The battle to clean your floor is heating up – literally. The new Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus now uses 230-degree Celsius HyperSteam to make your floors spotless without the need for any chemicals.
It turns steam into a natural disinfectant to clean and kill germs and keep your home safe for your kids and pets.
Tech Guide took the Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus for a spin in our home.
Our place is perfectly suited for a product like this because 90 per cent of our living area is covered in large tiles.
It has a sleek modern look and, thanks to the SmoothDrive Technology, it’s self-propelled and easy to move in all directions. It’s effortless cleaning.
The first thing you need to do is fill up the clean water tank that sits on top of the cleaner head.
There’s a small display at the top of the handle that allows you to control the Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus and access the various cleaning modes – Auto, Max Steam Suction and Quiet.
Naturally we went for the Steam mode first up and we were presented with a progress indicator on the display.
About a minute later steam was available and we could see it coming from the roller.
Now our tiles are a light beige colour and dirt shows up easily so it didn’t take too long to see just how effective the steam mode was.
Usually small stains and dirt lifted straight off with one sweep.
On board is an iLoop Smart Sensor, which can detect dirt and adjust the amount of water and power needed to remove it.
But the Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus also has a ReverseScrub Technology which activates a 14-second reverse brush rotation so you can concentrate the scrubbing on a particular area.
We used this a couple of times on a couple of stubborn stains and seconds later they were gone.
The Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus has triple-sided cleaning, which means it can clean along skirting boards and corners right up to the edge.
It’s also easy to manoeuvre around furniture so there’s no need to lift chairs and can lie flat to fit under low furniture to get into all those hard to reach places.
The other modes can be used depending on how much and how intensely you’d like to clean.
The Suction mode was great to pick up visible dirt and debris on the floor before running the steam clean mode.
And Quiet mode really speaks for itself. It took the noise levels right down so it’s ideal for those times when you need to clean but don’t want to wake other people in your household or a sleeping baby.
Now all the while, clean water is being applied to the brush and dirty water is removed at high speed to prevent streaking and deliver a more hygienic residue-free clean.
But the system managed that all very well and there was never any excess water on the floor.
There was the odd streak here and there but that’s not a deal breaker. Overall it did a terrific job.
Battery life was impressive with up to 110 minutes when used in Quiet mode.
In Max and Steam mode that runtime can go between 45 minutes and an hour, which is still plenty of time to get through even a larger home.
But it’s not the end of the story when you finish your clean.
When you’re done the Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus can then run through its self-cleaning system.
Simply place the unit back on its charging stand and hit the self-clean button on the top of the handle.
From here the FlashDry Self-Cleaning with Silent Dry mode kicks in to clean the brush roller and the internals to ensure it’s ready to go the next time you need it but also ensure there are no nasty smells either.
The Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus is available now exclusively through Amazon and is priced at $1,499.
VERDICT
The Tineco Floor One S9 Artist Steam Plus is built for the modern home and offers chemical-free cleaning that’s effortless and effective.

articles.title: US bans MEXC crypto exchange over sanctions evasion, cybercrime links
articles.text:
The US Department of the Treasury has cut off the MEXC Global crypto exchange from the US financial system over sanctions evasion and links with cybercrime gangs.
Founded in 2018, the Seychelles-based MEXC is one of the world's largest crypto exchanges, giving more than 40 million users from more than 170 countries access to 3,000 cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets.
According to a Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) order, MEXC has allowed illicit transactions of at least $16 billion linked to cybercrime operations and Iranian, North Korean, and Russian sanctions evasion between May 2021 and May 2026.
The Treasury Department said that, as recently as June 2026, MEXC was still processing transactions with sanctioned Russian entities Garantex and Grinex, and it also facilitated or processed at least $226 million in transactions benefiting or connected to the Russia-based, OFAC-sanctioned A7 sanctions evasion network.
"MEXC Global has not only facilitated Russian illicit finance but has also served as a hub for other types of illicit financial activity, including Iranian and DPRK sanctions evasion, ransomware and scam payments, and Russian and other darknet market activity," the Treasury Department said.
"Between May 2021 and May 2026, MEXC Global had sent or received approximately $1 billion in direct transactions with more than 40 identified Iranian CVC exchangers, some of which are subject to U.S. and international sanctions."
FinCEN has blamed this on deficiencies in the crypto exchange's anti-money laundering (AML) and customer identification and verification policies.
The ban exposes US financial institutions and individuals to secondary sanctions or enforcement actions for transfers of funds to or from the MEXC Global crypto exchange.
In response to FinCEN's ban order, MEXC said that its legal and compliance teams have launched a review of its sanctions and AML controls.
"MEXC is aware of the order issued by the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) on November 6, 2026, and is reviewing it closely in coordination with our legal and compliance teams. MEXC is operating normally, and user assets remain secure," MEXC said.
"We take the concerns raised seriously and intend to engage constructively with FinCEN, as well as other relevant regulators and competent authorities worldwide. We have also begun an independent review of our AML and sanctions controls."

articles.title: Sony annonce un nouveau PlayStation Portal, avec une nouveauté qui intrigue
articles.text:
Sony dévoile un nouveau PlayStation Portal, équipé cette fois d’un stockage interne. Problème : le constructeur n’a pas précisé à quoi il allait servir.
Le PlayStation Portal n’est pas mort. Cela fait déjà trois ans que Sony propose cet écran déporté permettant aux joueurs de profiter de leurs titres PS5 en streaming via le Wi-Fi de la maison, puis depuis 2025 à l’extérieur en utilisant le service de cloud gaming du constructeur. Dans un post de blog, Sony annonce aujourd’hui le lancement d’une nouvelle version du PlayStation Portal, avec une vraie nouveauté matérielle : l’ajout d’un mystérieux stockage interne, sur lequel la marque japonaise reste particulièrement discrète.
Du stockage en plus, mais pour faire quoi ?
La capacité du stockage reste pour le moment inconnue, mais aussi les fonctionnalités qui en profiteront. Sony ne confirme ni l’installation de jeux, ni leur exécution directement sur la machine. « Par ailleurs, en prévision de futures fonctionnalités, du stockage interne a été ajouté sur ce nouveau modèle. Les détails concernant ces futures fonctionnalités seront communiqués dès qu’ils seront finalisés », indique tout juste Sony dans son communiqué.
Les acheteurs du PlayStation Portal de deuxième génération devront faire une confiance aveugle à Sony, et attendre plusieurs mois avant de savoir à quoi sert la mémoire installée.
Pour le reste, le constructeur conserve une formule connue. On retrouve un écran LCD de 8 pouces, affichant les jeux en 1080p jusqu’à 60 images par seconde, ainsi que le retour haptique et les gâchettes adaptatives hérités de la DualSense.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Une petite subtilité sur la boîte qui en dit long sur la stratégie de Sony
L’autre changement se lit sur la boîte : le PlayStation Portal abandonne la mention « Remote Player » au profit de « Player ». Sony entend ainsi mieux refléter ses usages, qui dépassent désormais la seule lecture à distance depuis une PS5.
Pour profiter du jeu en mobilité, il est indispensable de posséder un abonnement PlayStation Plus Premium, facturé 18,99 € par mois, ou 151,99 € pour une année complète, sans compter le prix des jeux compatibles.
Preuve que Sony souhaite miser un peu plus sur le cloud gaming, un mois d’abonnement au PlayStation Plus Premium est offert pour tout achat de l’appareil. Un « cadeau » qui permettra aux joueurs de tester en conditions réelles le jeu à distance, avant pourquoi pas de passer à la caisse.
Cette version Midnight Black sera commercialisée au Japon à 39 980 yens, avec des précommandes ouvertes le 13 novembre. La sortie est prévue pour le 10 décembre au Japon, ainsi qu’en Corée du Sud. Pour le moment, Sony n’a pas communiqué sur une disponibilité en Europe.

articles.title: Pluggable Agentic AI Framework: A seven-layer composable enterprise agentic AI reference architecture on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Pluggable Agentic AI Framework: A seven-layer composable enterprise agentic AI reference architecture on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
“How do we run our AI agents in production at scale?” is the question every customer eventually asks. It comes bundled with several questions. How do we handle thousands of concurrent user requests securely and confidently? How do we make sure the agents stay reliable under real traffic instead of failing silently? How do we know if an agent still meets the quality and safety standards it passed during testing? What are agent security best practices? Should that be deterministic or non-deterministic? And many more. A proof-of-concept answers none of these, because it is built to show the agent model can do the task, not to survive production traffic, cost pressure, and security review.
That gap between a working prototype and a system that runs reliably, securely, frugally and responsibly at scale, is where most agentic AI initiatives stall, and it is rarely the model’s fault. Every team building an agent tends to rebuild the same scaffolding from scratch: its own routing logic, its own guardrails, its own observability, all applied after the fact rather than built in from the start. The teams need a shared, production-ready architecture that every agent can build on.
This post walks through a seven-layer composable reference architecture designed to take multi-agent AI applications from prototype to production scale.
Composable architecture
The Pluggable Agentic AI Framework is a reference architecture for multi-agent applications organized into seven layers, each with a distinct responsibility and a stable contract. The services and technologies shown in each layer reflect the reference implementation, not mandatory choices. Organizations can substitute alternatives that align with their existing infrastructure and requirements. Together, these layers offer a blueprint for building, securing, and operating agentic AI applications at production scale.
Data and Knowledge is the foundation of Agentic AI. An agent is only as good as the data it can access. Whether an agent is checking out a healthcare formulary, tracking inventory, or interpreting a compliance rule, it needs relevant, up-to-date information to answer correctly. This layer owns retrieval, embeddings, and access to structured and unstructured data through a clear contract and protocol: accept a query and return the most relevant information that acts as context for an agent. Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base, Vector Engine for Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, Amazon S3 Vectors and Amazon DynamoDB are example building blocks for this foundation.
Model and Inference choices should be driven by configuration, not hardwired into agent or application logic. Use smaller, faster models for simple tasks and larger models for requests that require more nuanced reasoning. It is important to conduct a thorough model evaluation for the use case you are building with realistic and representative business data. A model routing layer keeps AI agents decoupled from the model hosting environment and provider-specific APIs by relying on a consistent request-and-response contract. A proxy such as LiteLLM provides a common interface across providers, so you can switch models based on your evaluations without rewriting application logic.
Orchestration determines how work is distributed, and choosing the right approach is critical. For straightforward tasks, use a single agent to handle the work from end to end. For complex, cross-domain workflows, use a supervisor to delegate specialist agents, each scoped to a specific capability and tied to a specific set of tools. Avoid building one agent that does everything. As tools, instructions, and context accumulate, the context window grows, latency increases, and accuracy can suffer. Tool sprawl sets in, which can push agents beyond their intended boundaries, leading to unintended actions and security breaches. Splitting responsibilities keeps each agent’s context focused and makes latency more predictable. You can also test each agent’s behavior, scale it, and define its security model independently. Enforce bounded autonomy: specialists should execute strictly within the tools they have been granted, and nothing more.
In addition to decomposing into specific specialists and setting its boundary, decouple the specialist agents from the supervisor agents. Allow the supervisor to discover the specialists from a centralized agent registry and invoke them through a standardized protocol like MCP (Model Context Protocol) and A2A (Agent to Agent). Maintain a centralized agent registry that catalogs every agent’s tools, skills, and owner. This gives your organization the visibility it needs for governance at scale, increases the velocity of AI agent implementation through reusability, and avoids the cost of repetitive development. Consider using Strands Agents for specialists, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness for the orchestrator, AWS Agent Registry and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway for centralized discovery and routing.
Security and Guardrails should be a primary concern, built into the design from day one. Agentic AI exposes organizations to a new class of risks that conventional security frameworks were not built to address, from prompt injection and tool misuse to memory and data poisoning. Treat all external content as untrusted by default. Authenticate every request, whether it comes from a user, another agent, or an automated workflow, through a service like Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity. Then use fine-grained access control to determine whether each tool call is permitted before execution. Grant agents temporary, scoped credentials instead of persistent secrets. On the data-protection side, mask sensitive data like PHI (Personal Health Information) and PII (Personally Identifiable Information) in agent and tool requests and responses, so that sensitive customer information does not appear in agent outputs or lingers in memory. For accountability, capture every significant decision in a tamper-evident audit trail, route high-impact actions through a human approval gate, and deploy circuit breakers to halt anomalous behavior before it can escalate. Consider using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails for user inputs, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity and Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for authentication and access control, along with AWS Security and governance controls to bring defense-in-depth security.
Application is where the end-user experience lives, whether that is a chat interface, an API surface, or an embedded widget. Keep this layer intentionally thin. Its only responsibilities should be presenting the conversation and passing requests to the orchestration layer beneath it. Resist the urge to embed business logic here. The cleaner the separation, the more easily you can iterate on the user experience without destabilizing the backend. A decision model can sit at this boundary as a fast, inexpensive check: in one call it scores whether a request is in scope, needs a human, or is urgent, returning probabilities instead of free text. Your code acts on those scores with simple thresholds, answering off-topic requests directly and flagging escalations, so the full agentic loop runs only when it adds value. When building the application layer, think about what would be needed for another AI agent to consume and interact with your AI agents along with humans. Build your external interfaces accordingly.
Observability should watch every layer from day one, not after the first incident. Along with the logs and metrics, end-to-end agent traces are critical to measure whether the agent performed its task correctly. Along with the trace, collect cost and token usage per request, time to first token, whether the call is secure, and surface dashboards for latency, error rates, and spend before you go live. Proactive monitoring is cheaper than reactive firefighting. Consider using Amazon CloudWatch with OpenTelemetry along with Amazon CloudWatch Omni for tracing and metrics to get comprehensive visibility across your stack.
Agentic Operations closes the loop with continuous evaluation, so set it up from day one. Score every production session for groundedness, accuracy, and safety, and put a regression gate in place to catch quality drops before they reach customers. Without this, you only know the agent worked at launch. With it, you can prove it still works after every subsequent release. Consider using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations for scoring and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore optimization for continuous performance tuning.
Reference implementation for a retail customer support agent
To bring the architecture to life, the framework includes a ready-to-run reference implementation based on a retail customer support scenario covering order status and refund eligibility. We chose this use case because it exercises every layer of the stack while remaining intuitive enough for a team to follow and adapt to their own needs.
A supervisor agent receives a customer’s refund request and delegates to an Order agent and a Refund agent, each a specialist with a scoped set of tools. The Order agent looks up delivery and purchase details from Amazon DynamoDB. The Refund agent retrieves tier-based policy rules from a knowledge base and calculates eligibility using the delivery date, the current date, and the customer’s loyalty tier. Every one of these calls passes through the AgentCore Gateway, which enforces fine-grained access control before a tool executes with Policy in AgentCore, and every call is traced end-to-end through the observability layer, so when a calculation goes wrong, the trace shows exactly which layer and which decision point caused it.
Anyone building a similar supervisor-and-specialist pattern can clone the reference implementation and swap in their own domain logic layer by layer.
Why pluggability matters as much as the layers themselves
The value of a seven-layer architecture lies not only in how it separates responsibilities, but in how quickly each layer can evolve. Pluggability makes that possible. Stable contracts at layer boundaries, from identity checks and access policies to telemetry interfaces, let you change the underlying technology without redesigning the rest of the stack. Essentially, take an architecture-first approach to building agentic AI systems rather than a technology-driven approach.
The framework puts this into practice by demonstrating pluggability through integrations with third-party providers across the layers: model and hosting providers at the inference layer, search capabilities at the orchestration layer, decision APIs at the application layer, guardrails at the security layer, and agent tracing and monitoring solutions at the observability layer alongside business value and cost tracking. It supports industry-standard providers at each layer, so you can compose solutions that meet your specific requirements.
For enterprises, flexibility protects existing investments. Teams can retain the observability, security, and inference tools they already trust, fill gaps where needed, and adopt new capabilities incrementally. The architecture provides a consistent foundation without requiring every technology decision to come from the same vendor.
Conclusion
A working prototype proves what an agent can do. A well-designed architecture determines whether your enterprise can depend on it. Moving to AI operations means designing security, governance, visibility, cost controls, reliability, and adaptability into the design from day one, not adding them after the system is built.
The Pluggable Agentic AI Framework brings those concerns into an architecture with a clear principle: build a stable foundation without locking every technology choice in place. Models will change. Tools will evolve. Business requirements will shift. Your architecture should make those changes manageable, not turn each one into a rebuild.
Put that principle into practice. Start with the Workshop Studio experience, explore the public sample repository, and use the hands-on implementation as a starting point for your own architecture. It is not a substitute for production security hardening, testing, and review.
Build the capabilities you need today and the flexibility you will need tomorrow.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday, Decathlon fait -400 € sur ce VTT électrique Rockrider E-EXPL 700 qui n'a pas peur de l'aventure — Frandroid
articles.text:
Si vous avez une envie soudaine d’aventure et d’exploration de chemins forestiers, qui sont très charmants en cette période automnale, il va vous falloir un sacré allié. Pour le Black Friday, Decathlon pose sa candidature avec le Rockrider E-EXPL 700, un VTT électrique semi-rigide doté d’éléments pensés pour améliorer le confort sur des terrains accidentés. Il n’est pas destiné aux pratiques extrêmes comme l’enduro ou le downhill, mais si vous aimez la randonnée sportive, il est déjà plus adapté. Avec une réduction de 400 euros sur le site de la marque, sans compter les aides régionales, vous pouvez vous faire plaisir.
Les atouts du Rockrider E-EXPL 700
- Son moteur central Brose de 70 Nm avec assistance progressive
- La batterie de 630 Wh avec 100 km d’autonomie annoncée
- Il est pensé pour les chemins avec la fourche X-Fusion de 130 mm, les pneus de 29 pouces et les freins hydrauliques
Le Rockrider E-EXPL 700 coûte normalement 2 499,99 euros. Chez Decathlon, il est vendu 2 099,99 euros pour le pré-Black Friday. Pensez aussi à vérifier les aides à l’achat de votre région ou de votre commune, qui peuvent faire baisser la note.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Rockrider E-EXPL 700. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un moteur et une batterie pour avaler les kilomètres
Pour son Rockrider E-EXPL 700, Decathlon a choisi une motorisation centrale Brose Drive T de 250 watts (460 watts en pointe) qui développe jusqu’à 70 Nm de couple. Un choix cohérent sur un VTT électrique pensé pour la randonnée sur terrains variés. Contrairement à des motorisations qui privilégient des accélérations franches, ici on a une assistance progressive et continue. Le capteur de couple adapte l’aide électrique à l’effort fourni pour garder des sensations de pédalage naturelles. Il y a plusieurs niveaux d’assistance disponibles, dont un mode Boost utile pour les montées difficiles. Le moteur est suffisamment puissant pour franchir les dénivelés d’une sortie loisir, mais les vététistes les plus avertis pourront trouver ses 70 Nm un peu trop justes.
L’autre argument de ce Rockrider est sa batterie intégrée de 630 Wh, avec laquelle Decathlon annonce jusqu’à 100 km d’autonomie à faible dénivelé. Une valeur qui, comme à chaque fois, dépend du relief, du poids, de la météo et du niveau d’assistance utilisé. Bon point, elle peut être complétée par une extension de 360 Wh qui se fixe à la place du porte-bidon et ajoute environ 44 km selon Decathlon. Comptez quand même 499,99 euros de plus. Petit bémol, il faut une clé Allen pour extraire la batterie, ce qui est moins pratique qu’un système de verrouillage rapide.
Un équipement confortable pour les randonnées
Le Rockrider E-EXPL 700 est bien équipé pour la randonnée. Il repose sur un cadre en aluminium et des roues de 29 pouces avec de larges pneus Rockrider Grip 500 de 2,4 pouces. Ils offrent une bonne accroche sur les terrains meubles et irréguliers. À l’avant, la fourche X-Fusion RC32 apporte 130 mm de débattement pour absorber les aspérités. Sa position de conduite relevée contribue au confort sur les longues distances et la tige de selle télescopique permet d’abaisser rapidement la selle pour les descentes plus techniques. Le freinage est confié à un système hydraulique Tektro M530 à quatre pistons avec des disques de 180 mm. Un ensemble rassurant pour contrôler les 24 kg (en taille M, sans pédales) de ce VTT électrique.
Sur le guidon, on retrouve un écran couleur bien pratique, qui affiche de nombreuses informations sur votre sortie. Il peut même être associé à l’application Decathlon Ride pour suivre vos performances. Tout n’est pas parfait, cependant, parce que l’écran est sensible aux reflets et certains textes, les plus petits, manquent de lisibilité. Un sabot de protection devant le moteur n’aurait pas été de trop non plus, parce qu’il est pas mal exposé aux chocs. Si vous comptez faire de la randonnée sportive ou des promenades en forêt, c’est un bon choix. Si vous êtes plutôt All Mountain ou enduro, il vous faudra un modèle plus costaud.
Si vous avez une autre idée du vélo électrique, vous pouvez explorer notre guide d’achat dédié pour découvrir des modèles adaptés à votre pratique de la discipline.
