articles.title: Can We Trust AI Agents When Zero Trust Isn’t Really Zero
articles.text:
This article is brought to you by Queen’s University Belfast.
Several teams around the globe are leveraging AI by creating a task force of agents managed by an orchestrator and creating applications to support risk assessment, client profiling, match making, and information yield with a slight overview of decision making. One of the important components for these agents is to ensure that the logs are managed and historic relevance is not being used to avoid skewing towards same decision making. Thus, the system is expected to keep checkpoints in place where agents are prompted to delete such historic relevance.
However, despite such methodology in place, a future prompt could make the agents bring forward the information that was supposed to be deleted and can be tricked into revealing more information, which is a classic case of context recovery attack. So, the question raised here is: How can we trust that our instructions have been followed? And where is the proof?
There is an element of utilizing zero-trust architectures (ZTA) for orchestrating and managing agentic activity, which simply means all agentic interactions use the core principle of “never trust,” “always verify.” ZTA components include a policy enforcement point (PEP) that has to be trusted to maintain trust across the system, so the question that remains is where is the component of zero-trust, and shall we trust the policies enforced by PEP?
Having a pro-agentic approach and utilizing agents could be helpful with the right guardrails in place. Opening our systems to random agents that are being trained on off-the-shelf models and blindly relying on them can pose significant cyber risks. For example, vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.
Vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.
This opens critical discussions towards how vibe coding could interfere with the positioning and implementation of trusted execution of the agentic queries. Consider an autonomous web of agents that relies on agents’ inputs to drive the operations. When the system is operating under low tolerance of failure and with non-tracking based agentic workflows, it could be computationally expensive to trust and verify each query in real-time that leads to the common trade-offs of memory vs execution.
Another risk to consider is the zero-day attack. When it happens, how will the system react? Would such an event be manageable without a total infrastructure breakdown? The scale of impact can be observed from over reliance on agentic ecosystems with only one trusted layer. This could mean that when failure occurs, the entire ecosystem could be exposed, just like there will be no autonomy if the backbone network is not available, which essentially means no layer to place trust.
How quickly can de-authentication attacks occur?
An in-house experiment done at Queen’s University Belfast (QUB) provided an initial understanding of how the scale of agentic attacks could mean a lower window of vulnerability. The team focused on very popular de-authentication attacks and with agentic orchestration, the swift rate to do de-authentication attacks could go as low as 2 to 3 seconds. This gives little to no time to react and decide on patching the system.
There is another aspect of the large-scale agentic system, which establishes trust under asynchronous autonomy. Trust serves as a critical foundation for traceability. How would you ensure that all the agents operating towards a common goal are aligned and understand the delays associated with their goals?
Our team worked around this space, which at first involved demonstrating that the problem exists, and its impact and scale can be huge when you must prove trust under boundaries of asynchronous autonomy. Solutions towards such problems can be simplified by keeping things like AI-bill of material or leveraging distributed ledger technology that can provide underlying infrastructure of trust via traceability and immutability and keep the agentic activity and associated trust vectors agnostic to the platform.
Within trust, another factor that is not well explored but needs a thorough investigation is the concept of horizontal anomalies. It defines how agents interact differently with various sources under different settings. As agents behave correctly and align themselves with the architectural expectations for one specific task or application, that does not necessarily mean these can be trusted for their operations across all associated components. How to identify such anomalies and what methods can be employed without complying with such agents remain open questions and topics for further exploration.
The critical aspect is that utility of agents with semi to low trust governance offer short-term high benefits, but the cost of recovery when the system fails is yet to be explored, and this will not be a contained issue. We are looking into the system where agents are already sweeping into different entities and may not allow complete recovery. For example, a mere supply chain issue because an agent going rogue is now not a containable small task but needs sweeping across all the touch points of those affected agents. This essentially means despite the number of agents and their ability to trigger proxy-agents, which may not be directly linked to the wider ecosystem, there is a need to ensure that computationally expensive trackers are in place for all the agents.
Other relevant PhD works carried out in our research group are towards sovereignty of AI, exploring aspects of trust and accountability. Our hypothesis is that sovereignty and trust need to be governed together as onus of provenance is high on the host of agents. Thus, it needs understanding of laws governing trust-based executions of AI. The important challenge here is that there is a vital difference between missed information and missed instructions, and both have different impacts when it comes to trusted accountability.
Does true zero-trust architecture exist?
The real-world issue with these systems lies in the failure to adopt approaches that historically have relied on state-based modeling when governing trust. In stateless systems where agentic autonomy is high, the convergence and reliability towards trust-provenance decreases significantly. Thus, it brings us back to the original question – does a true zero-trust even exist?
Can policies be trusted? If so, how should these be managed without falling into the trap of policy-based accessibility and control issues? Despite the argument that PEP can help manage access between the agents, placing a single entity and expecting it to scale towards all agentic interactions is underestimating the problem space.
Formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models.
To build our case and settle around the challenges of trust embeddings in Agentic AI, within Cyber AI hub, we are exploring opportunities to help companies scale up as well as build their pipeline of agentic applications for commercial viability. However, the element that governs our regular work and decision making are scale of problem and number of agentic deployments, anomaly detection across the agentic workflows, continuous evaluation of the attack surfaces and vulnerability assessment, exploring differences in the pure agentic AI and task-driven multi-agent system.
We are working with industries where trust is a pre-requisite, and these organizations put trust as a guardrail managed via internal policies with a pure focus on securing the systems through policies rather than trusting the third-party agentic service providers. Additionally, trust in services is presented by ensuring constraints around their service models where agentic activities are tracked and managed via logs including management of their token revocation list to avoid replay attacks depending on the type of application. Formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models. Things like balancing the adversarial accuracy along with certified adversarial robustness can help to determine how much the model can be trusted.
But the question is, can we settle for anything less than foolproof when it comes to deployment of agents in the real world? And if so, how much impact can be controlled, and who is responsible for the remaining component?
References
Wickremasinghe G, Sandjaja FR, Rafferty K, Sharma V. State-verification in asynchronous blockchain-driven agentic AI systems. 40th International Conference on Information Networking (ICOIN) 2026 Jan 14 (pp. 139-144). IEEE.
Sandjaja, F. R., Abdul Majeed, A., Abdullah, A., Wickremasinghe, G., Rafferty, K., & Sharma, V. (Accepted/In press). Policy design in zero-trust distributed networks: challenges and solutions. In Industrial Networks and Intelligent Systems: 12th EAI International Conference, INISCOM 2026: (to appear in proceedings).
Melis M, Del Rincon JM, Sharma V. Improving Certified Robustness via Adversarial Distillation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.31653. 2026 Jun 30 (Accepted to appear in BMVC’26).
Vishal Sharma is a Reader in the School of Electronics, Electrical Engineering, and Computer Science (EEECS) at Queen's University Belfast (QUB), Northern Ireland, United Kingdom. Before arriving at QUB, he was a Research Fellow in the Information Systems Technology and Design (ISTD) Pillar at the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), Singapore.

articles.title: The $75 million Nigeria could make from taxing crypto
articles.text:
This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
Nigeria’s crypto market received $38.1 billion in value between July 2025 and June 2026, according to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis, highlighting the scale of a market the government hopes to tap to expand its tax base in 2027.
Governments are increasingly taxing crypto, but most focus on profits made when investors sell or exchange digital assets. India, for instance, imposes a 30% tax on income from crypto transfers.
Nigeria is taking a blanket approach, combining taxes at both ends of a crypto transaction life cycle. In July, the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) issued new rules setting out the tax obligations for cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and other virtual assets. The framework introduces a 1.5% stamp duty on fiat-to-token and token-to-fiat conversions, a 1% withholding tax on gross disposal proceeds for certain virtual assets, and a 7.5% value-added tax (VAT) on taxable services provided by virtual asset service providers (VASPs).
The stamp duty is particularly significant because it can apply at both ends of a crypto transaction, meaning the government can collect revenue when users buy and sell, regardless of whether they make a profit.
After doubling revenue from the Electronic Money Transfer Levy (EMTL) through tighter compliance across fintechs, the government has extended the renamed stamp duty to crypto transactions. Its medium-term projections show the levy’s growing importance to government finances.
Stamp duty collections are projected to rise from ₦456.07 billion ($334.72 million) in 2026 to ₦579.82 billion ($425.54 million) in 2027. These projections cover stamp duty across the economy, not crypto transactions alone.
The Crypto Tax Observatory
Follow the money. Discover how much of Nigeria’s $38.1 billion crypto economy the government can actually reach, and exactly where the new stamp duty applies.
Nigeria’s crypto market is vast but highly fragmented. Explore the network below to see what happens at each node, what regulatory obligations exist, and where visibility breaks down.
Trace a single illustrative $100 transaction journey. The new framework applies a blanket 1.5% stamp duty at both ends of a fiat-crypto lifecycle, capturing revenue regardless of investor profit.
Fiat Enters the Ecosystem
A Nigerian buyer starts with fiat currency in their bank account, preparing to purchase a digital asset (like Bitcoin) through a regulated domestic VASP.
Conversion 1: Fiat-to-Token
The platform is obligated to deduct a 1.5% stamp duty on the originating fiat value during the purchase.
Asset Held in Wallet
The buyer holds the crypto asset. This holding phase does not trigger another stamp-duty event.
Conversion 2: Token-to-Fiat
Selling the crypto back to naira triggers a second 1.5% stamp duty deduction on the remaining transaction value.
A $38.1 billion market does not equal a $38.1 billion tax base. Explore the data disparities and the path to the theoretical $75M revenue scenario.
Domestic Exchanges
Subject to stringent NRS guidelines. Must register for tax purposes, maintain transaction records, and deduct taxes.
P2P Marketplaces
New CBN rules mandate platform-facilitated operators to identify customers and link crypto activity to corresponding naira settlement.
Private Wallets & Offshore
Transfers between private wallets and offshore DEXs create immense enforcement challenges and fall outside automated infrastructure.
Applied to qualifying fiat-to-token and token-to-fiat conversions. It captures revenue regardless of profit.
Applied specifically to the gross disposal proceeds for certain virtual assets when sold or exchanged.
Applied strictly to the taxable services and fees provided by VASPs, not the crypto asset itself.
This is an illustrative scenario representing an assumed two-conversion cycle, rather than a forecast of actual collections. Potential collections remain distinct from actual revenue due to compliance gaps, offshore routing, and private wallet evasion.
How much can Nigeria actually collect from stamp duty?
When a Nigerian buyer buys a crypto asset such as Bitcoin, they expect to get the full value, but Nigeria’s new rule takes 1.5%, leaving them with 98.5%. When the new buyer sells the crypto, they pay another 1.5%, leaving them with 97% of the original asset. Nigeria gets its stamp duty on the originating digital asset.
So what does that mean when placed against the scale of Nigeria’s crypto market?
Between July 2025 and June 2026, Nigeria recorded $38.1 billion in cryptocurrency activity, according to Chainalysis. But the more relevant figure for understanding the government’s potential reach may be the $25.2 billion that Nigerian users sent to crypto services during the period.
Because the new rules place tax collection and reporting obligations on crypto service providers, activity passing through these platforms gives the government identifiable points from which to collect taxes.
If just 10% of the $25.2 billion involved qualifying conversions between fiat currency and crypto assets, Nigeria would have a potential stamp-duty tax base of $2.52 billion. Applying the 1.5% rate would generate approximately $37.8 million in stamp-duty revenue from the initial purchases, leaving buyers with $2.48 billion worth of crypto assets.
If those same assets were sold within the year, and the next buyers were charged another 1.5% on the remaining value, the government could collect an additional $37.23 million in stamp duty. The new buyers would receive approximately $2.45 billion worth of crypto assets.
Across the two rounds of transactions, Nigeria could collect approximately $75.03 million in stamp duty from an initial $2.52 billion pool of crypto purchases. This translates to 17.63% of potential stamp duty in 2027.
This is an illustrative scenario rather than a forecast of actual collections. As more qualifying transactions fall within the tax net, potential stamp-duty revenue increases. This calculation only accounts for stamp duty, excluding withholding tax, income tax, and VAT on applicable services.
The initial $38.1 billion in crypto activity recorded in Nigeria cannot be treated as a potential tax base since it includes different types of transactions, not all of which involve taxable conversions between fiat currency and crypto assets. Some activity also happens through private wallets, offshore exchanges, and other channels that Nigerian tax authorities may find harder to monitor and collect from.
Crypto Tax Revenue Engine
Test how Nigeria’s new double-ended 1.5% crypto stamp duty impacts government revenue and erodes trader capital across multiple transaction cycles.
| Compliance | Base | Rev (1R) | Rev (2R) | 
|---|---|---|---|
A $38 billion crypto market
Nigeria’s $38.1 billion in cryptocurrency activity made it Sub-Saharan Africa’s second-largest crypto market, behind South Africa, which recorded $39.3 billion over the same period.
Nigeria’s figure, however, is a 3% decline year-on-year. The country also continues to have a significant peer-to-peer crypto market, where individuals exchange digital assets directly or through marketplace intermediaries.
Chainalysis found that Bitcoin accounted for $923 million of the $1 billion in small domestic wallet transfers below $10,000 recorded in Nigeria during the period.
Transactions conducted through regulated exchanges may be easier to identify and report, but transfers between private wallets, decentralised exchanges, and offshore platforms create different visibility and enforcement challenges.
A new Central Bank of Nigeria rule could improve visibility into a portion of this activity. Its new regulation requires platform-facilitated P2P operators to maintain records linking each virtual-asset transaction to its corresponding naira payment or settlement. They must also identify customers and counterparties and route naira payments through permitted banking and payment channels.
The rules could give regulators a clearer picture of transactions on P2P platforms. However, they do not automatically bring every private wallet transfer within the banking system’s visibility.
The NRS rule already requires taxpayers to keep records of their virtual-asset activities and requires VASPs to report certain large or suspicious transactions.
The NRS guidelines also require VASPs to register for tax purposes, maintain transaction records, and comply with reporting obligations. They must deduct and remit applicable taxes, while P2P marketplace operators face their own compliance requirements.
Domestic exchanges could become particularly important to this collection effort. Chainalysis found that they received $6.22 billion during the reporting period, accounting for half of Nigeria’s centralised exchange inflows, with their share rising from 7% in 2022 to 27% in 2025 and 50% in 2026.
The growth of domestic exchanges means most centralised exchange activity passes through platforms that Nigerian authorities can potentially reach. These platforms can identify customers, retain transaction histories, and deduct applicable taxes at qualifying conversion points.
But the $6.22 billion flowing into domestic exchanges is not itself taxable income or a confirmed stamp-duty base. It indicates the volume of activity passing through platforms where collection may be more practical.
The government’s ability to collect will depend on how much of that activity represents qualifying taxable transactions, whether exchanges can accurately identify the relevant tax events, and how effectively the NRS enforces compliance.
In January, the NRS taxed exchanges to log customer trades daily into a government e-reporting portal.
However, the numbers suggest that crypto could become another contributor to Nigeria’s growing stamp-duty revenue. A 10% scenario based on crypto-service flows points to approximately $75.03 million in potential stamp-duty collections in 2027 if crypto activity remains unchanged in the country.
But the same tax also introduces another cost to crypto transactions. As stamp duty is deducted from the tokens credited to buyers, repeated conversions reduce the amount of crypto users receive at each qualifying transaction.
For the government, the opportunity is to expand a revenue stream that already generates hundreds of billions of naira. For traders, the question is how much of their transaction value will be lost to taxes as they move in and out of the crypto market.

articles.title: CPU-Z data reveals impact of the memory crisis: 32GB and 64GB PCs decline, DDR4 makes a comeback
articles.text:
Winners & losers: In what will come as a surprise to nobody, the latest CPU-Z hardware survey has illustrated how having more than 16GB of RAM in a PC is increasingly becoming a luxury. With the AI-driven memory crisis continuing to push DRAM prices through the roof, the number of people with 32GB and 64GB configurations is falling, while DDR4 is making a comeback.
The latest CPU-Z Validator statistics come from hardware configurations users submit to CPU-Z's online Validator database, so it doesn't represent retail sales or all PCs. However, it gives us an idea of what the landscape looks like.
The headline takeaway is that, for the first time ever, RAM capacity on PCs has declined year-over-year. Over the last 3 months, the number of systems with 32GB of RAM is down 2.5%, while the number with 64GB of RAM is down 18%.
During the same period, there's been an increase in PCs with smaller amounts of memory. 16GB was up 12.9%, 8GB jumped 5.5%, and 24GB was up 19.7%. Although 32GB remains the most popular capacity (37.2%), 16GB is now just 4.2 points behind the leader.
Another sign of the times is the RAM Generation chart. The number of PCs with last-generation DDR4 increased 6% YoY to 54.4%, cementing its place at the top. The current-gen DDR5, in second place, was down 2.9% to 32.9%. Both RAM generations have shot up in price, but DDR4 is still the cheaper of the two.
It's a similar story on the Steam survey. Participants with 32GB of RAM declined 5.1% last month, while those with 16GB, the most common configuration, increased 3.6%.
While there are an increasing number of signs that the AI bubble is looking shaky, companies continue to warn that the situation could get even worse.
Last week, RAM maker TeamGroup CEO Chen Ching-wen said RAM prices will keep climbing for many months, and that the IT industry will endure its worst chip shortage from the final quarter of 2026 through the end of the second quarter next year.
We're seeing the impact of this RAM crisis everywhere. From the 16GB Raspberry Pi 5 now costing triple its launch price to a Nintendo chip supplier quitting the ROM business, the situation is a depressing sight for consumers. It's also why Microsoft keeps improving the performance of 8GB PCs. Elsewhere, AMD has decided it's no longer a gaming-focused firm but a data center-first company, according to CEO Lisa Su.

articles.text:
Dona da 99 teve número “insignificante” de corridas solicitadas por agentes de IA
Na semana passada, Uber revelou que apenas quatro viagens por IA foram registradas.
Uma das maiores empresas de mobilidade do mundo, a chinesa DiDi, dona da 99 no Brasil, registrou um número “insignificante” de viagens a partir de agentes de inteligência artificial, como os presentes no ChatGPT ou Claude. A informação foi compartilhada com o Tecnoblog pelo vice-presidente sênior Stephen Zhu durante uma visita de jornalistas à sede da companhia, em Pequim.
Na semana passada, a Uber revelou, na divulgação de resultados do terceiro trimestre, que apenas quatro viagens foram solicitadas da mesma forma. Veículos da imprensa estrangeira entenderam que era uma cifra modesta diante de todo o burburinho em torno dos agentes de IA – já se fala em uma economia “agêntica” no exterior.
Durante o encontro realizado nesta segunda-feira (09/11), Zhu refletiu sobre o valor agregado de uma tecnologia assim. “Temos que nos perguntar: qual valor adicional é criado por um agente de IA? Traz mais conveniência, por exemplo?” Ele acrescentou que os clientes já estão acostumados com o funcionamento do app da DiDi (99 no Brasil). Na visão do executivo, é preciso avaliar se o cliente hesita em mudar de hábito.
O mercado chinês tem uma dinâmica própria. O app da DiDi traz funções mais avançadas, inclusive uma inteligência artificial própria, a assistente de viagens Xiao Di. Ela aceita comandos por voz ou texto e escolhe entre 90 opções de serviço diferentes, o que permite atender a solicitações mais sofisticadas. O consumidor pode pedir “um carro em que caiba o meu cachorro”, e a IA consegue realizar este cálculo. Corridas assim já estão ocorrendo, mas ele não as classificou como de agentes de IA externos.
Fundada em 2012, a DiDi opera hoje em 15 países, entre eles Brasil, México, Chile e Japão. Segundo dados oficiais da empresa, são mais de 749 milhões de usuários ativos anuais no mundo, mais de 100 milhões deles fora da China. No segundo trimestre de 2026, a companhia registrou 55 milhões de transações por dia, número que soma todos os serviços da plataforma, e não apenas as corridas.

articles.title: Chinese AI firms want Silicon Valley’s top minds. Poaching them won’t be easy
articles.text:
Chinese AI companies are hiring Silicon Valley-based engineers to work on their models, potentially tapping into the talent at American labs like OpenAI and Anthropic.
MiniMax, the Hong Kong-listed Chinese AI startup, currently has around 16 San Francisco-based job openings listed on its website, including for a research lead focused on developing its core AI model. The company is also recruiting specialists in finance, law, life sciences, and cybersecurity, as well as a lead recruiter to attract top AI talent in Silicon Valley and Seattle.
Moonshot AI, the Chinese company behind the Kimi AI model, is looking for U.S.-based “solutions architects,” who will “help enterprise customers integrate its AI models into their businesses.”
American AI companies, with their deep pockets, have attracted global talent, including many Chinese engineers, by offering high compensation and opportunities to work on the world’s best models. In comparison, Chinese companies have so far largely relied on homegrown talent. Hiring in the U.S. reflects a strategic shift by Chinese companies as they look to compete and stay close to one of their most lucrative markets, experts said.
“Wanting to establish research teams in Silicon Valley makes perfect sense for Chinese AI companies seeking access to talent and the latest developments in the industry,” Cheryl Wu, a researcher in the economics of AI at Yale University and global think tank GovAI, told Rest of World.
Good Work and $$$
More than half of the world’s top AI researchers complete their undergraduate studies in China, a September study by research center Carnegie China said, based on the educational backgrounds of people who published papers at NeurIPS, one of the world’s leading AI conferences.
Yet the U.S. remains a global magnet for AI talent, the study concluded.
In 2025, the U.S. saw a net gain of 2,145 researchers while China recorded a net loss of 1,729, according to the analysis.
China’s AI companies have been trying to lure top Chinese researchers at American AI labs to return home. One high-profile example is Tencent, which recruited former OpenAI researcher Yao Shunyu to lead its AI research.
Chinese companies are seeking “little geniuses” who have worked at companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, a headhunter recruiting for Chinese labs in the Bay Area told Rest of World, requesting anonymity as she is not authorized to speak to the media.
These attempts, however, have not had much success because Chinese companies often struggle to match the salaries paid by their Silicon Valley peers.
“It’s money. Chinese companies simply don’t have enough of it to offer competitive wages for talent,” said Wu, who published a report examining Chinese AI companies’ financing with research institute Epoch AI. “They have only recently begun raising more substantial funding and still lag far behind their U.S. competitors.”
There is a stark gap between what Chinese and American AI companies pay employees.
MiniMax spent $84.3 million on employee remuneration in 2025, equivalent to roughly $203,000 per person, based on its year-end head count of 415, according to its financial filings. The annualized remuneration costs of Z.AI, another Hong Kong-listed Chinese AI lab, in the first half of 2026 amounted to $140,000 per employee. Neither company disclosed a breakdown of pay for engineers or researchers, and both figures include share-based compensation and staff across all departments.
In comparison, OpenAI advertises annual base salaries of $250,000 to $445,000 for research engineers in San Francisco, before equity awards. Three Chinese researchers working in Silicon Valley say it’s common for their peers to get an annual compensation package worth more than $1 million.
As of September, China’s six leading AI firms collectively generated only about 10% of the combined AI-related revenue of OpenAI and Anthropic, according to Wu’s research.
“Career prospects are another factor. Even senior Meta engineers might accept a lower-ranking position to join Anthropic because of its work on frontier AI,” Wu said. “That makes it even harder to persuade top talent to join a lab whose models are just not at the cutting edge.”
Chinese tech companies are now ramping up their salary game. If an AI researcher had offers from OpenAI or Anthropic, ByteDance’s frontier model division Seed would try to lure them with a competing offer that’s 1.5 times higher, according to a person familiar with the team.
Wu Yonghui, a veteran AI researcher who worked at Google for 17 years, joined Seed as the head of research in early 2025. Seed currently lists 71 positions in San Jose, San Diego, and Seattle.
But even with matching pay, three Chinese researchers working in the U.S. told Rest of World they preferred American companies for better work-life balance and the chance to work on frontier models.
“I think most of the top Chinese talent would feel pretty comfortable in Silicon Valley; it’s the only other place where “996” isn’t really frowned upon,” Damien Ma, director of Carnegie China, told Rest of World, referring to the demanding work culture common in China’s tech industry, where employees work from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., six days a week.
Extension of the U.S.-China AI war
Washington has spent years restricting Chinese companies’ access to advanced Nvidia chips, and is scrutinizing their use of overseas data centers and cloud services. But no comparable restrictions prevent Chinese AI companies from establishing U.S. operations and hiring engineers there.
Both Washington and Beijing are increasingly seeking to protect their most advanced AI technologies from each other.
The Chinese government proposed export controls on some of the country’s most advanced AI models, particularly those trained using the country’s “important data,” despite specifications.
U.S. officials and American AI companies, meanwhile, have accused Chinese AI labs of using unauthorized distillation techniques to replicate their models’ capabilities. On other sensitive tech fronts, like the semiconductor industry, the U.S. has already restricted some American engineers from working in Chinese facilities without a license.
While neither country has imposed a blanket ban on AI companies hiring researchers across borders, the growing competition over advanced technology could make talent recruitment another flashpoint.
“Given it is already so competitive, it doesn’t take much to imagine U.S. companies at some point capitalizing on U.S.-China competition and making national security arguments that will make it more difficult for Chinese labs to operate or to attract the best talent. Conversely, it’d be a similar dynamic if U.S. labs were operating in China,” Ma said. “This elite talent is by definition scarce; we are talking [about] like the top 5%–10% of people. Who wouldn’t want to hoard the best and the brightest for themselves?”
Chinese tech companies have previously faced U.S. restrictions that disrupted their American research operations. In 2019, telecom giant Huawei cut more than 600 jobs at its U.S. research arm, Futurewei, after Washington placed the company on a trade blacklist.
Not all Chinese AI companies want to hire in the U.S. China’s AI poster child, DeepSeek, continues to advertise research and engineering positions in China. It recently announced about 150 positions for engineers who would expand AI agentic and back-end infrastructure. In a 2024 interview, DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng said he hired mostly Chinese-educated people and believed the company itself could cultivate elite AI researchers.
Yale researcher Wu is skeptical that Chinese startups could attract enough top researchers to compete with America’s leading AI labs. “They may have plans to hire, but that doesn’t necessarily mean they’ll be able to find the people,” she said.

articles.title: Meta expands Instagram's AI age-guessing tech globally | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Meta announced on Monday that it’s expanding its AI-powered age-estimation technology on Instagram worldwide to identify more teens and place them under its Teen Account protections, as it faces numerous lawsuits accusing its platforms of harming teens.
The social media giant says it will use the AI technology to find people it suspects to be teens, even if they use an adult birthday.
Teen Accounts place users into a stricter account experience with additional safeguards, such as receiving direct messages only from people they follow or are already connected to, hiding harmful comments, and setting accounts to private by default.
Meta’s age-guessing tools use AI to analyze entire profiles for contextual clues, such as birthday celebrations or mentions of school grades. Meta also looks for these signals across different formats, such as posts, comments, bios, captions, and more. The company also looks at visual cues from photos and videos, including a person’s height or bone structure.
Meta said it’s continuing to roll out the technology on Facebook, with a similar global rollout planned for Threads later this year.
The global expansion comes as Meta reached settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every U.S. state and territory in August to resolve lawsuits alleging its platforms harm teens. As part of the settlements, Meta agreed to improve how it identifies teens and children under 13.
“We’ll continue to do our part to proactively ensure teens are in age-appropriate experiences on our apps,” Meta wrote in a blog post. “That’s why as part of our agreement with 52 bipartisan attorneys general across US states, territories, and the District of Columbia, we’re investing in even stronger technology to proactively catch accounts that may belong to children under 13. We’re also strengthening the technology we use to identify accounts that may belong to teens between the ages of 13 and 17 so we can ensure those accounts are placed in experiences designed for teens, even if they give us an adult birthday.”
Meta said parents in the U.S. will start seeing an in-feed video on Instagram explaining its approach to ensuring their teens are in age-appropriate protections.

articles.title: Why Boson AI’s Toronto office is growing faster than its Silicon Valley HQ | BetaKit
articles.text:
Silicon Valley-based Boson AI has been quietly building a presence in Canada since late 2023.
Over the past couple of years, the well-funded AI research lab has opened an office in Toronto that now houses approximately 20 of its 40 staff, established a relationship with the Master of Science in Applied Computing Program at the University of Toronto (U of T), and begun purchasing most of its computing power from eStruxture’s Barrie, Ontario data centre.
Boson chose to set up shop in Toronto because it offered access to the compute, talent, and the predictability the startup needed to advance its plans to build foundation models to power voice agents, Boson co-founder and CEO Alex Smola told BetaKit in an interview.
Alex Smola argues that US actions to curb immigration present a “massive” opportunity for Canada that “will not last forever.”
Ahead of the last federal election in the United States, Smola said Boson thought it prudent to develop a “Plan B” in case the US began acting erratically and making conducting business in the country more difficult. That has since happened after US President Donald Trump implemented steep tariffs and drastically restricted immigration.
Boson’s decision to build a presence in Toronto “has turned out to be a really good thing because, so far, Canada has been a lot more predictable,” and provided the compute and talent the company requires, Smola said.
The German-born AI leader, who previously served as a vice-president and distinguished scientist at Amazon Web Services, co-launched Boson in 2023, and the company has since closed $70 million USD ($98 million CAD) to take on OpenAI and Meta in the voice AI model race.
During Boson’s early days, the CEO said he ran the numbers and quickly realized that renting computing capacity from a big cloud provider or neocloud was simply “not sustainable.”
RELATED: Superwhisper partners with Cohere for all-Canadian voice-to-text AI
When Boson shopped around for alternative options, Smola said the startup got connected with Montréal-based eStruxture and initially considered setting up in that city, which also possesses a deep AI talent pool thanks to the strength of its local research institutions.
Boson ultimately landed in Toronto after it found suitable power and a compelling offer from eStruxture’s Barrie facility. While the startup had a competing offer from a US provider at the time, Smola said eStruxture was “just a lot nicer” to work with compared to the other company, which he claimed tried to walk back their initial quote and tack on extra fees.
While Boson’s Canadian operations have allowed the firm to bypass tariffs and access equipment and products it needs for cheaper, some of which are not currently available in the US, Smola said access to talent has been the bigger boon thus far.
Today, Boson’s Toronto office offers staff a lower cost of living compared to Silicon Valley. The hub is a short walk down the street from U of T’s downtown campus, from which the startup regularly sources interns. It also houses, among others, two Iranians who Smola said are “excellent” staff members but who are unable to travel to the US at the moment.
Right now, Smola said Boson is growing faster in Toronto than Santa Clara because it remains easier to access the work permits and navigate the associated requirements, timelines, and fees necessary to hire AI talent from abroad in Canada.
“This is starting to become a real issue in the US,” Smola said, adding that in many cases it has become “very difficult” for the firm to bring prospective staff to California.
Smola said he didn’t even open a current machine learning engineer position in the US, citing work permitting challenges, as well as the higher cost of living and turnover characteristic of Silicon Valley compared to Toronto.
The Boson CEO believes the actions the Trump administration has taken to steeply curb US immigration present a “massive” opportunity for Canada to recruit talented folks who might have otherwise moved to the US, and argued that this opening “will not last forever.”
But Smola also highlighted that securing the work permits it needs could soon become an issue for the company in Canada.
“We’ve been told that the requirements have gone up by our immigration advisers and we’re about to find out for a candidate we’re bringing in from Europe,” Smola said. “We have high hopes that it will work out, but ultimately this is in the hands of the appropriate authorities. Overall, I hope that Canada can be (and remain) a place that will continue to attract and retain talent from all around the world.”
Feature image courtesy Boson AI.

articles.title: Instagram’s Effect Builder makes new filters from AI prompts
articles.text:
After expanding its Edits app to macOS last week, Instagram’s next move is launching this Effect Builder that generates custom filters for your Stories posts with AI. Available now for US residents who are over 18, it has a prompt box for describing your filter idea to the chatbot, with an option to attach style reference images.
Instagram’s Effect Builder makes new filters from AI prompts
The Effect Builder bot is available on the web to build whatever new Instagram filters you can think of.
Then you can upload your own photos to preview the AI-generating effects, and ask for changes in follow-up prompts. There’s also an option to allow Instagram’s AI to rewrite your prompt, which turned my one-line test prompt “Make a filter that turns photos into comic book pages” into several AI-generated paragraphs of detailed style requests on everything from color palette to lighting. The filter Effect Builder generated as a result still looked nearly identical to its output for my original one-liner.
You can submit your filters to Instagram directly from Effect Builder, but effects have to pass a safety review before they’ll be available to other users. Instagram says after an effect is approved, it “shows up in Instagram Stories for anyone to use, and whenever someone uses your effect we’ll link back to your profile so that it’s easy for others to find your work.”

articles.title: Diese Helikopterdrohne fliegt zum Saturnmond Titan – und dein Name könnte mit an Bord sein
articles.text:
Diese Helikopterdrohne fliegt zum Saturnmond Titan – und dein Name könnte mit an Bord sein
2028 soll die Helikopterdrohne Dragonfly auf ihre Reise in Richtung Titan starten. Ab 2034 soll sie dann den größten Mond des Saturn erforschen.
Virtuelle Bordkarte und dein Name auf deinem Chip
Du kannst bei der Mission dabei sein – zumindest virtuell. Die Nasa hat eine Homepage aktiviert, auf der du deinen Namen hinterlassen kannst. Der wird dann auf einen Chip an Bord der Dragonfly eingraviert.
Wenn du auf der Seite Vor-, Nachname und deine E‑Mail-Adresse eingibst, erhältst du außerdem eine personalisierte Bordkarte für den Trip. Du bekommst dann laut Nasa Updates zu der Mission geschickt und nimmst teil an einem virtuellen Gastprogramm.
Name bis Mitte Januar 2027 hinterlassen
Wer dabei sein will, hat noch gut zwei Monate Zeit, um seinen Namen verewigen zu lassen. Die Frist endet am 15. Januar 2027.
Die Publicity-Aktion ist Ende Oktober dieses Jahres gestartet. Bis jetzt haben sich schon über 350 000 Menschen registriert (Stand: 9. November 2026).
Standortwechsel alle ein-zwei Titan-Tage
Die Nasa hat die Mission von Dragonfly im Sommer 2019 angekündigt. Damals war von einem Launch im Jahr 2026 die Rede, später verschob die US-Raumfahrtbehörde den Start um zwei Jahre.
Der Helikopter soll an Bord einer Falcon Heavy von SpaceX zum Titan fliegen. Auf dem zweitgrößten Mond des Sonnensystems soll er innerhalb von drei Jahren an mehreren Orten landen und Bodenproben sammeln.
Geplant sind Standortwechsel alle ein bis zwei Titan-Tage. Ein Tag auf dem Saturnmond entspricht 16 Tagen auf der Erde. In der Zeit dazwischen muss die Drohne ihre Batterien aufladen.
Dragonfly: 450 Kilo in 4000 Metern Höhe
Dragonfly ist etwa so groß wie ein SUV. Er besitzt acht Rotoren, die das fast 450 Kilogramm schwere Gefährt auf eine Flughöhe von bis zu 4000 Metern bringen können.
Die Kameras der Drohne wurden bereits auf dem Mars getestet. Betrieben wird Dragonfly nuklear und verwendet dabei ein System, das dem der Marsrover sehr ähnlich ist: den Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator.
Das verspricht sich die Nasa von der Titan-Mission
Warum ausgerechnet Titan? Der Mond verfügt über eine Atmosphäre, Flüsse und Seen, Jahreszeiten und eine Landschaft, die reich an organischem Material ist.
Titan ähnelt laut dem Stand der Forschung der ursprünglichen, methanreichen Erde. Seine Erforschung könnte also Aufschlüsse dafür liefern, wie auf unserem Planeten Leben entstanden ist.

articles.title: Korea Advances Physical AI Across Industries With NVIDIA
articles.text:
Tapping into the country’s strengths in manufacturing and engineering, NVIDIA is helping advance Korea’s physical AI ecosystem.
The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles.
These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production.
Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics
Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering.
In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST. Samsung is also exploring NVIDIA cuEquivariance to speed up tensor operations used in training and inference for atomistic AI models.
Samsung is developing chip-scale thermal and mechanical analysis workflows with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo. In one AI homogenization case, combining AI-predicted effective material properties, coarser grids and GPU acceleration resulted in a roughly 1,600x speedup. Simulation time fell from about 18 hours for a fine-grid solve on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds for a GPU-accelerated coarse-grid solve.
Looking ahead, NVIDIA Agent Toolkit could connect these simulation tools and AI models, helping future engineering agents run analyses and compare design options.
Kakao Mobility Collaborates With NVIDIA to Advance Autonomous Driving Development
Kakao Mobility plans to build on NVIDIA’s autonomous vehicle computing and safety technologies to advance development of a level 4 autonomous driving system. The work combines Kakao Mobility’s proprietary driving software and experience operating in Seoul’s Gangnam district with NVIDIA’s vehicle computing platform.
Kakao Mobility plans to use NVIDIA Hyperion, a reference platform for vehicle sensors and compute, powered by NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor. It also plans to use NVIDIA Halos to support safety across the development and validation of its autonomous driving technology.
Initial development is planned around Kia purpose-built vehicles, integrating Kakao Mobility’s autonomous driving software with NVIDIA technologies. The effort aims to support future level 4 mobility services in Korea.
LG Electronics Advances Robot Learning and Factory Simulation
NVIDIA and LG Electronics successfully demonstrated NVIDIA Isaac GR00T-powered robotic manipulation and manufacturing tasks using LG’s CLOiD robot in an actual manufacturing environment.
The collaboration implemented a physical AI data flywheel connecting real-world data collection, NVIDIA Cosmos-based data augmentation, GR00T model training, NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor onboard computing and simulation-based evaluation, establishing reusable workflows for continued development and validation of CLOiD’s robotic capabilities.
The teams are using this work to refine a repeatable process for training, evaluating and improving robots for manufacturing.

articles.title: Una investigación española descubre miles de nuevos vídeos y perfiles pedófilos en TikTok
articles.text:
Una investigación española descubre miles de nuevos vídeos y perfiles pedófilos en TikTok
La organización ‘Maldita.es’, autora del trabajo, ha denunciado ante la Fiscalía a la red social por su inacción ante las cuentas que crean este contenido con millones de visualizaciones
TikTok está lleno de pedofilia y pederastas. Una nueva investigación hecha en España ha encontrado en esta red 1.183 vídeos de abuso sexual infantil explícito con 48 millones de visualizaciones y más de 26.000 perfiles de potenciales pederastas que comentan y comparten ese material. “No se puede ni comparar a TikTok con el resto de plataformas en lo que abuso sexual infantil se refiere”, dice Clara Jiménez Cruz, directora de la organización española de lucha contra la desinformación Maldita.es, que ha hecho la investigación. TikTok ha eliminado algunos de esos vídeos, pero la mayoría de las cuentas que los cuelgan siguen activas. A falta de nuevas acciones de la red social, Maldita.es ha denunciado a TikTok ante la Fiscalía española con capturas de imágenes y vídeos como pruebas.
Gracias a un caso judicial en Estados Unidos, en 2022 surgieron informes internos de TikTok, red social de vídeos cortos de origen chino, donde admitían que tenían un problema de pedofilia en la plataforma. Maldita.es ya había publicado dos investigaciones anteriores sobre explotación sexual infantil en TikTok. Esta vez llaman a la red social el “hogar del pederasta”. Han denunciado una muestra de 50 vídeos de abuso sexual infantil por el canal que ofrece TikTok y la compañía solo ha retirado cinco de ellos, un 10%, y bloqueó otros 13 solo en España. Tres días después de la denuncia, el 40% de las cuentas que publicaron esos vídeos seguían activas.
Maldita.es ha contactado con TikTok, que se ha limitado a pedir más información sin responder a consultas sobre sus mecanismos de protección de menores, los fallos detectados y el contenido ilegal en su plataforma. Horas después de que esta historia fuera publicada, la compañía ha respondido a este diario lo siguiente: “Mantener TikTok como un lugar seguro para nuestra comunidad es nuestra máxima prioridad. El contenido sexualmente explícito con menores (CSAM por sus siglas en inglés) está categóricamente prohibido, y desplegamos tecnologías de detección avanzadas y mecanismos de cumplimiento para identificar y eliminar de forma contundente este contenido de nuestra plataforma. Dado que los actores malintencionados evolucionan continuamente sus métodos para evadir la detección, una respuesta colectiva es vital”. La compañía dice que insta a Maldita “a compartir sus hallazgos de forma completa”.
EL PAÍS ha probado algunos de los hashtags o palabras clave que usan en estas comunidades para encontrar nuevo material. Es extremadamente fácil dar con él. Algunas de las búsquedas con esas mismas palabras en Instagram, una red de Meta, reciben esta advertencia: “El abuso sexual infantil es ilegal. Creemos que tu búsqueda puede estar asociada con abuso sexual infantil” y redirige “confidencialmente” a un centro de ayuda.
Más allá de los problemas obvios de permitir en su plataforma y difundir con su algoritmo este material, TikTok está incumpliendo la regulación europea. La Ley de Servicios Digitales dice que las plataformas deben limitar los riesgos para la infancia y actuar “con prontitud” para retirar o bloquear el acceso a este tipo de contenidos.
También en España
Para encontrar este tipo de mensajes nocivos para los menores, no es necesario hacer una investigación exhaustiva. Basta detenerse en vídeos de TikTok de directos de adolescentes o jóvenes que hablan con la cámara desde distintos lugares de España, incluso desde sus aulas. En la mayoría hay apenas unas cuantas docenas de personas reunidas viéndolas. Ante la solicitud de algún usuario, algunas jóvenes comparten incluso su nombre de Instagram con una enorme ligereza. En apenas un rato, llegan mensajes de acoso al chat público: “¿Alguna lo engulle entero con todo y huevos?”, “menuda paja”, “la de gafas a cuatro”.
TikTok advierte en todos sus directos de que son solo para adultos: “¡Te damos la bienvenida a TikTok Live! Diviértete interactuando con otros espectadores en tiempo real. Los creadores deben ser mayores de 18 años para poder emitir un Live, mientras que los espectadores deben ser mayores de 18 años para recargar y enviar regalos”. Esos regalos pueden ser en algunos casos a cambio de detalles sexuales que alguna chica pueda hacer en el vídeo. Pero muchas de ellas no tienen 18 años. Y la red se queda con una comisión de los “regalos” que reciben. TikTok se enriquece, por tanto, con mensajes sexuales de desconocidos a adolescentes españolas.
Todo esto ocurre en España, no en algún rincón oscuro del planeta. Maldita.es ha encontrado que, de los 26.000 perfiles de pederastas potenciales, al menos 7.700 hablan en español y muchos de ellos son españoles.
Pero el problema es global. TikTok sirve para dar a conocer este material y llevar a los más interesados a otras plataformas, sobre todo Telegram y Zangi, una aplicación de mensajería con más garantías de privacidad. Maldita.es ha contactado con algunos y sus vendedores han ofrecido directamente el contenido de abuso sexual de menores. También lo han visto en grupos automatizados con bots en Telegram con miles de seguidores.
La investigación ha detectado trucos digitales que usan estas cuentas para intentar evitar los controles de TikTok, pero no es nada tan sofisticado: textos largos superpuestos a imágenes, fotos de menores con un pequeño recuadro donde se reproduce parte del material de abuso o grandes emoticonos que tapan las partes más delicadas del menor.
Maldita.es ha encontrado incluso una comunidad llamada “Team 94″ con unos 2.000 seguidores de un violador de bebés estadounidense ahora en la cárcel. Son usuarios que emplean la red para compartir sus vídeos e intercambiar material personal. El 94 es un número que usaba el pedófilo. Una búsqueda simple en TikTok lleva a docenas de comentarios en español en una de esas cuentas: “Quiero que mi sobrinito de 8 aprenda a jugar, alguien de Perú”, “yo quiero entrar”, “larga vida a perver” o “yo quiero ver ese bello contenido”. Alguien preguntaba este mes de octubre qué es todo eso y el propietario de la cuenta respondía: “Eres muy inocente para saber el contexto”, y lo redirigía a un canal de Telegram.

articles.title: STF encerra inquérito das fake news, mas investigações derivadas continuam
articles.text:
O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), ministro Edson Fachin, determinou, nesta segunda-feira (9), o arquivamento do inquérito das fake news, aberto em março de 2019 para investigar ataques e ameaças contra integrantes da Corte. A decisão encerra o procedimento original, mas não interrompe automaticamente as investigações e os processos derivados que ainda estejam em andamento.
Fachin atendeu a pedido da Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), que considerou esgotado o objeto específico da apuração. Os desdobramentos que permanecerem abertos continuarão sendo analisados individualmente pelo Supremo.
Na decisão, o ministro afirmou que o encerramento do chamado inquérito-mãe não invalida as razões que levaram à sua abertura nem os resultados institucionais alcançados durante a investigação.
“O que ora se encerra é o procedimento investigatório matriz. Não se apaga sua história, não se infirmam as razões institucionais que determinaram sua instauração, nem se desconhece a relevância que teve para a proteção desta Corte e da ordem constitucional”, escreveu.
O ministro também ressaltou que o arquivamento não afeta condenações, absolvições, acordos, recebimentos de denúncias ou outras decisões tomadas em processos autônomos.
Sigilo do inquérito será retirado após análise dos documentos
- O material reunido ao longo da investigação soma mais de 12 mil páginas e 50 volumes. Antes de liberar o acesso aos autos, Fachin determinou a separação de informações protegidas pelo direito à intimidade, incluindo dados bancários, fiscais, telefônicos e pessoais;
- A medida atende à manifestação da própria PGR. Depois da triagem e da criação de apenso específico com os documentos sensíveis, o sigilo do restante do inquérito será levantado;
- O levantamento feito pelo STF identificou 104 procedimentos vinculados à investigação. Também foram encontradas diligências sem cumprimento há 22 meses, entre elas a tomada de depoimentos;
- Fachin afirmou que investigações precisam ter prazo de encerramento e que a proteção das instituições democráticas deve respeitar garantias constitucionais, como a liberdade, o devido processo legal e a duração razoável dos processos.
Leia mais:
- AGU muda de ideia e pede ao STF que derrube marco legal das bets
- Rumble volta a funcionar no Brasil mesmo com bloqueio do STF em vigor
- Justiça volta atrás e derruba autorização para três bets funcionarem no Brasil
Inquérito foi aberto em 2019 por Dias Toffoli
O inquérito das fake news foi instaurado em março de 2019 por iniciativa do então presidente do STF, ministro Dias Toffoli. Na ocasião, Alexandre de Moraes foi designado relator.
A investigação começou com o objetivo de apurar a existência de notícias fraudulentas, denunciações caluniosas e ameaças contra o Supremo, seus ministros e familiares. Com o passar dos anos, porém, seu escopo foi ampliado e chegou a envolver até mesmo um integrante da Corte, o ministro André Mendonça.
Ao longo de mais de sete anos, a apuração resultou em operações policiais, bloqueios de perfis em redes sociais, prisões e denúncias apresentadas pela PGR. Também provocou críticas de entidades, como a Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil (OAB), e atritos com setores da oposição no Congresso, além de controvérsias no meio jurídico.
A possibilidade de encerrar o inquérito já vinha sendo discutida internamente durante a presidência de Luís Roberto Barroso. Com a saída do ministro, Fachin assumiu as tratativas e defendeu a necessidade de estabelecer prazo razoável para a conclusão da investigação.
PGR defendeu a investigação, mas pediu seu encerramento
No pedido encaminhado ao STF, o procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet, defendeu a importância do inquérito para proteger a independência do Judiciário e a ordem constitucional.
Segundo Gonet, a duração da investigação acompanhou a sucessão de ameaças identificadas ao longo dos anos contra o livre exercício da função jurisdicional dos ministros.
Apesar de sustentar a legitimidade da apuração, a PGR avaliou que seu objetivo específico havia sido esgotado e pediu o arquivamento.
A Procuradoria também se posicionou contra a divulgação indiscriminada de todo o material reunido. Para o órgão, a abertura dos autos poderia expor dados pessoais de pessoas que passaram pela investigação sem que fossem identificados indícios suficientes para justificar suspeitas contra elas.
Por isso, defendeu análise individual dos documentos antes da retirada do sigilo, posição acolhida por Fachin.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Il n'a pas l'argent pour bâtir sa maison, sa solution : des briques géantes en plastique recyclé qui s'assemblent comme des LEGO pour créer un logement de 40m²
articles.text:
Il n'a pas l'argent pour bâtir sa maison, sa solution : des briques géantes en plastique recyclé qui s'assemblent comme des LEGO pour créer un logement de 40m²
Fernando Llanos n’avait pas les moyens de bâtir sa maison sur son terrain. La raison : des routes beaucoup trop compliquées pour transporter les matériaux, mais surtout un coût énorme. Sa solution fut radicale puisqu’il a créé de grands blocs en plastique recyclé qui s’emboîtent comme des Lego pour monter une maison de 40 mètres² en cinq jours.
Cet article a été initialement publié en octobre 2026. Nous le republions aujourd'hui car l'ingéniosité des solutions alternatives de construction et le recyclage intelligent du plastique continuent de susciter un vif intérêt au sein de notre communauté.
Nous en avions déjà parlé dans nos colonnes : le plastique recyclé peut être une très bonne solution en termes de coût pour construire des logements habitables. Fernando Llanos fait partie de ceux qui ont utilisé cette solution pour bâtir une maison sur son terrain à Cundinamarca, en Colombie.
Des blocs en plastique qui s'emboîtent comme des LEGO
Et pour cause, faire venir des matériaux depuis Bogotá était trop compliqué et coûteux. Alors quoi de mieux que de grands blocs en plastique recyclé qui s’emboîtent comme des Lego ?Pourtant, Fernando n’a aucune formation dans le bâtiment, lui qui est musicien.
Puisque le trajet depuis Bogotá prenait jusqu’à sept heures, l’homme n’avait d’autre choix que d’opter pour un matériau léger et facile à transporter. D’abord, il pensa à du plastique neuf, puis a découvert que sous forme recyclée, son prix est jusqu’à treize fois moins cher. Fernando Llanos a alors suivi des formations pour apprendre à travailler le plastique et la construction.
Les premiers essais l’ont mené à une rencontre avec Óscar Andrés Méndez, un architecte qui travaillait sur le même sujet à l’université. L’architecte a même lancé le projet Conceptos Plásticos à Bogotá, qui transforme des sacs, des emballages alimentaires ou des flacons de shampoing en blocs et colonnes composés à près de 95 % de plastique.
Mais alors comment ça marche ? D’abord le plastique est trié, broyé, fondu puis placé dans des moules. Les briques ont alors des formes qui s’emboîtent entre elles comme des pièces de Lego. Les murs se montent à sec, sans même besoin de colle entre les blocs.
Le toit, les fenêtres et les autres équipements sont ajoutés séparément. Un procédé qui réduit donc le temps de chantier mais facilite aussi le transport vers les zones où les matériaux arrivent difficilement, comme dans le cas de Fernando Llanos.
Pour une maison type avec ces blocs de plastique recyclé, on trouve deux chambres, une salle de bain, un salon, une salle à manger, une cuisine. Le temps de montage est d’environ cinq jours avec cinq tonnes de plastique utilisées et un prix entre 3 900 et 6 800 €. Les blocs résistent aux séismes, au feu, mais réduisent aussi les échanges de chaleur. Óscar Andrés Méndez estime que la durée de vie de ces bâtiments est d’environ 200 ans.
Une solution exportée dans le monde
Mais il n’y a pas que Fernando Llanos qui a profité de cette solution. Conceptos Plásticos a participé à bâtir un refuge à Guapi pour 42 familles déplacées par les violences en Colombie, avec 200 tonnes de plastique utilisées. Le chantier fut beaucoup plus long puisqu’il a demandé 28 jours.
Mais cette durée de 28 jours reste en deçà du temps habituel pour construire une maison à l'ancienne pour 42 familles. L’autre avantage, c’est que ces blocs sont démontables et permettent donc de déplacer les abris si la situation l’exige. Depuis, le projet a voyagé jusqu’en Côte d’Ivoire.
L’an dernier, plus de 3 500 tonnes de plastique ont permis de bâtir plus de 550 salles de classe pour un coût qui représentait environ 60 % de celui d’une construction classique. Conceptos Plásticos a aussi imaginé une unité de production miniaturisée qui tient dans un conteneur de 12 mètres pour les régions où une grande usine est difficile à installer.
Notons que la technologie a quelquefois des limites. Selon l’UNICEF, les briques ne sont pas adaptées aux salles de bain, puisque leur surface poreuse complique le nettoyage. Depuis, le projet a prévu d’autres matériaux ou encore un revêtement dans ces espaces.
Fernando Llanos cherchait d’abord une manière abordable de bâtir une maison sur un terrain presque inaccessible, mais sa petite histoire a débouché sur une méthode qui permet désormais de bâtir des murs avec plusieurs tonnes de déchets. L’autre avantage, c’est aussi de réduire le temps de construction ou encore de faire naître des écoles dans les zones plus défavorisées. Désormais, cette solution est utilisée bien au-delà de la frontière de la Colombie.

articles.title: Amplifon Americas Data Breach Impacts 1.3 Million
articles.text:
Amplifon Hearing Health Care has disclosed a data breach impacting the information of more than 1.3 million individuals in the US.
The incident involves Amplifon Americas, the Minneapolis-based arm of the Italian hearing healthcare giant Amplifon, which claims to serve over 80 million members through a nationwide network of thousands of clinics.
According to Amplifon Americas’ data breach notice, hackers broke into its internal systems in January 2026 and copied files from certain systems between January 18 and February 8.
Although it immediately contained the incident and launched an investigation into the attack, Amplifon needed eight months to review the stolen data and determine that personal information was potentially affected.
The review concluded that names, contact information, driver’s license numbers, other government ID numbers, dates of birth, hearing and medical information, dates of service, other health information, and health insurance information were compromised.
For some individuals, Social Security numbers and financial information were also stolen, the company says.
“We are not aware of any fraudulent use of personal information as a result of this incident,” Amplifon notes.
Amplifon’s filing with the Texas Attorney General’s Office reportedly mentions a total of 1,332,826 people being affected nationwide.
SecurityWeek has emailed Amplifon for additional information on the data breach and confirmation on impact and will update this article if the company responds.

articles.title: Cette marque américaine cherche à séduire en Europe : son nouveau système de conduite autonome peut-il l'aider ?
articles.text:
Quand on pense voitures électriques, positionnement premium et technologies embarquées, les premiers noms qui viennent en tête sont BMW, Mercedes ou encore Audi, mais pas celui de Cadillac. Pourtant, le constructeur américain exerce bien en France et en Europe et tente de séduire une clientèle qui a toujours résisté aux marques venues d’outre-Atlantique. Pour tenter de convaincre, Cadillac annonce le lancement de son système de conduite autonome SuperCruise sur les véhicules électriques distribués en Europe.
Conduire sans les mains jusqu’à 130 km/h
Si presque tous les constructeurs, ou presque, se vantent d’avoir des systèmes de conduite semi-autonome, rares sont ceux qui permettent réellement de lâcher les mains du volant. Ford avait fait fort dès 2023 avec le système BlueCruise. Il a fallu attendre 2026 pour que BMW fasse mieux avec le Highway Assist, permettant de rouler sans les mains, mais aussi de changer de voie sans toucher au volant sur autoroute.
C’est désormais Cadillac qui lance son système SuperCruise en Europe. Ce système permettra au conducteur de lâcher les mains du volant sur autoroute et jusqu’à 130 km/h sur 180 000 km d’autoroute dans 16 pays différents. L’attention du conducteur doit encore rester sur la route, une caméra dotée d’un système de surveillance y veillera. Il s’agit donc d’un système de conduite autonome de niveau 2, pas encore d’une conduite totalement autonome comme Xpeng et Denza (BYD) l’ont présentée en marge du Mondial de l’Auto 2026.
Pour fonctionner, le système de Cadillac s’appuie sur un LiDAR ayant scanné les cartes. Si certains constructeurs comme Volvo reviennent sur l’utilité du LiDAR, Cadillac l’utilise pour le système SuperCruise. Cadillac annonce aussi dans son communiqué de presse utiliser des caméras fonctionnant en temps réel, des capteurs radar, des données GPS et un régulateur de vitesse adaptatif.
Trois ans offerts
Alors que BMW et Ford font payer la fonctionnalité, soit sous la forme d’une mensualité de 24,90 euros ou de 280 euros par an pour Ford, et de 1 100 euros pour 4 ans chez BMW, Cadillac offre 3 ans de fonctionnalité à compter de la date de mise en circulation du véhicule ou de la mise à jour s’il s’agit d’un modèle circulant déjà.
Cadillac annonce trois modèles électriques compatibles en Europe. Les SUV Optiq, à partir de l’année-modèle 2025, les Lyriq, à partir de l’année-modèle 2026, et le Vistiq pourront profiter de cette nouvelle fonctionnalité. Pour les modèles déjà vendus, un passage par un partenaire Cadillac est nécessaire pour déclencher la technologie SuperCruise. Une fois les 3 ans écoulés, la fonctionnalité deviendra payante, mais Cadillac n’a pas encore annoncé les tarifs. La marque américaine a trois ans pour les fixer, cela dit.
Cette actualité arrive dans un moment de creux pour Cadillac. La marque est de retour en Europe depuis 2024. Elle était d’ailleurs présente au Mondial de l’Auto cette année-là. Mais depuis, les actualités produits ne sont pas si nombreuses. Le constructeur américain a lancé fin 2025 le Cadillac Optiq, mais depuis… peu de nouveautés ont animé la marque en France. Et c’est dommage, car cela se ressent sur les ventes : seulement un peu plus de 200 modèles Cadillac ont été immatriculés en France. Les ventes restent donc confidentielles pour une marque ayant pourtant un nom connu des Français (Cadillac tire son nom d’une commune française) et une gamme déjà fournie de trois modèles électriques.

Le blender chauffant Moulinex Multisoup est à 49,99 € (-38 %)
Six programmes automatiques et un moteur de 850 W pour les soupes, veloutés, compotes et smoothies : le blender chauffant Moulinex Multisoup passe à 49,99 € chez Amazon.
Vendu et expédié par Amazon, ce modèle (LM5629F0) affiche 49,99 € contre 79,99 € pour le prix conseillé, soit une remise de 38 %. Il passe aussi près de 25 € sous son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours (74,32 €).
Des soupes maison sans surveiller la casserole
Ce blender chauffant cuit et mixe dans le même bol : il suffit d'y mettre les légumes et l'eau, puis de choisir l'un des six programmes automatiques. Il prépare aussi bien des soupes et des veloutés que des compotes ou des smoothies, et une fonction maintient la préparation au chaud.
Ses six lames, entraînées par un moteur de 850 W, permettent d'ajuster la consistance des préparations.
Une capacité familiale et une paroi qui reste froide
Le bol de 1,2 litre (1 litre pour les recettes chaudes) prépare jusqu'à quatre portions. Sa double paroi garde l'extérieur froid pendant la cuisson, ce qui limite le risque de brûlure.
Moulinex s'engage aussi sur la réparabilité de l'appareil pendant 15 ans, via son réseau de centres de réparation. Pour une famille plus nombreuse, sa capacité pourra en revanche sembler juste. Il est noté 4,4/5 sur Amazon.

articles.title: Over 3 Million People Hit by Frontline Education Data Breach
articles.text:
Frontline Education has informed the Indiana Attorney General’s Office that a data breach it suffered in August affected more than 3 million people.
The K-12 school administration software provider puts the total number of affected individuals at 3,085,266. That is well over twice the figure from the company’s earlier filings with several other states, which added up to roughly 1.3 million.
Frontline says the attackers got into part of its environment by exploiting a vulnerability in a third-party software product. The company detected the intrusion on August 14 and says the attack was fully contained the next day.
The hackers stole the personal information of school district employees and students from two Frontline products: Frontline Central and School Health Management.
The compromised information varies from person to person. It may include names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, driver’s license numbers, passport and other government ID numbers, health insurance information such as Medicaid IDs, and student IDs.
Affected adults in the US are getting two years of free credit monitoring and identity theft protection. Eligible minors are getting free dark web monitoring.
Frontline has not named the exploited third-party product or said who was behind the attack.
No known cybercrime group appears to have taken credit for an attack on the company.

articles.title: Can Carney execute on the ‘entrepreneur budget’? | BetaKit
articles.text:
Prime Minister Mark Carney’s second federal budget makes clear the PM remains solely focused on driving “ambitious” economic growth, with a whole lot of levers his government plans to pull to deliver. BetaKit published a nearly 3,500-word budget overview for Canadian tech, as well as features on some of the biggest line items (all of our Budget 2026 coverage can be found here).
While some of these levers are net new, like the Canada Growth Initiative and US QSBS-style capital gains tax cut, others detail how previously committed capital will be spent, or continue past pledges. There are plans to anchor quantum companies in Canada, develop dual-use tech, forge sovereign space launch capability, provide AI compute, expand cleantech tax credits, and support homegrown IP. As Munk School senior fellow Jaxson Khan said on The BetaKit Podcast, “it’s pretty clear the government has gone down a lot of the laundry lists from businesses and entrepreneurs and just said, ‘OK, well, what if we do all of the above?’”
It’s a lot of new and past commitments to execute on, especially since this government’s record on execution has a few black marks.
Take one pullout: open banking. Since the government first announced it would be studied in 2018, BetaKit has tracked a series of missed launch dates and a narrowed scope of delivery (recently introduced regulations include read-only access, not write access, one of the key asks from FinTechs). Budget 2026 featured no open banking movement beyond teasing an expanded scope for consumer data portability to telecom and transportation—despite the feds not yet enabling it in the financial industry. Canada’s Start-up Visa program is another example: applications remain indefinitely paused, with no replacement, despite promises an update would come before the end of this year.
Some changes will need to be executed smoothly to avoid gumming up the works. Take the proposed BDC-EDC merger. The combined Crown corporations will need to bring together more than 5,000 employees and $120 billion in assets, with very different cultures and structures, all while ensuring that committed capital (including $4 billion for defence and $1.75 billion in the government’s Venture and Growth Capital Plan) starts flowing. BDC is already a capital bottleneck for Canadian tech; more delays could be disastrous.
The real test of this budget’s ability to kickstart growth won’t be found in the size and breadth of its commitments, but in how fast (and well) Ottawa can execute. The government is pulling many levers—BetaKit will be watching to see what they’re connected to.
Sarah Rieger,
Managing Editor
